## Phase 140 (2026-07-23 — adversarial-review compound-claim hardening + the review-family borrows)

**Why this phase.** Resolves the highest-value not-yet-a-phase feedback from the 2026-07 cross-model review comparison (confound-4): a same-family adversarial reviewer systematically under-catches **compound findings** — a finding asserting multiple independent clauses or citing multiple `file:line` sites gets *partially refuted* (one clause disproved, the rest silently dropped), and the whole finding is dismissed. The mechanism is directional — it only ever turns a **real** finding into an apparent false positive, never the reverse — and the in-family adversarial re-check ratified every such dismissal; of the six audited dismissals, half concealed a real finding, one of them a High-severity security issue. What recovered the dropped clauses was a re-adjudication constrained to **trace every cited site** rather than judge the finding as a unit, fresh-context. Sysop's adversarial review (`_shared/adversarial-review.md`, consumed by `/claim-task`, `/plan-review`, `/auto-build`) and the Phase-138 fan-out merge (`_shared/fanout-evidence.md`, consumed by both review skills) are exactly the mechanism class this attacks — a reviewer/merge step empowered to dismiss findings, feeding the convention-promotion loop.

**The rule, at every dismissal site.** (1) *Classification Rubric*: decompose before rejecting — refuting one clause does not reject the finding; surviving clauses classify on their own merits; a rejection rationale must name every clause. High/security rejections get a second, independent pass (fresh context required; cross-family sharpens but is never assumed — portability), **with a no-spawn fallback**: where the shape can't spawn one (the reviewer-executor leaf; a no-nesting consumer agent), the rejection is never silently absorbed — the sealed report/plan carries the per-clause rationale to the next independent reader. (2) *Prompt template*: reviewers enumerate each claim/site explicitly (terse), so an unlisted clause can't be silently dropped downstream. (3) *Fan-out merge* (partial + both review skills' Step 3c/3b): drops are clause-by-clause and the rule **binds on downgrades too** (a High→Low on one refuted clause is the same laundering as a drop), covering single-site multi-claim findings (adjudicate remaining clauses, not just other sites). (4) *Step 4 dedup* in both skills — a reviewer-caught uncovered drop path — dedups clause-by-clause.

**The review-family borrows (ride-alongs).** From the official plugins' source read (`tools/REVIEW_FAMILY_PLUGIN_NOTES.md`; headline: the catalog's whole review family is diff-scoped and memoryless, so no head-to-head exists — only the source-read leg): **(1)** silent-failure checklist depth — a dedicated `Silent failures` group in `/codebase-review` 3a (broad-catch enumeration, unjustified fallbacks incl. mock-in-production, retry exhaustion, optional-chaining silent skips, propagation check) + the same items enriching adversarial dimension #3; **(2)** verify-the-cited-rule — a merge-time re-read of any convention bullet a finding cites, in both review skills; **(3)** a dispatch-side do-not-report FP taxonomy in both review skills (executed-pre-scan-covered / silenced-with-rationale / map-Skip-listed / pre-existing-on-incremental-rounds-only / recorded-decisions / sub-severity nitpicks); **(4)** name-the-regression on Tier-1 recommendations in `test-assessment-rubric.md`, symmetrizing Tier 2b's named-evidence demand. Borrow (5), the git-blame re-introduction lens, stays evidence-gated (parked — build only if a real round shows re-introduced un-promoted fixes).

**Adversarial review (house practice — two independent fresh-context Opus reviewers; evidence-fidelity + mechanism-coherence lenses; 10 findings, all absorbed).** The evidence reviewer verified every cited claim against the primary records and found zero de-identification leaks, but killed a "dismissed on its weakest clause" gloss (the record shows the refuted clause was itself shaky — the honest phrasing is "refuted one clause while the clause carrying the vulnerability was silently dropped") and a "fan-out findings" over-attachment (the measurement was a graded review pool; the generalization is sanctioned, the wording isn't). The mechanism reviewer broke the first draft in two load-bearing places: the second-pass mandate was **unsatisfiable** exactly where it matters (the self-classifying reviewer-executor leaf; no-nesting consumers) → the loud-record fallback; and the pre-scan suppression list keyed on `checks.yml` **membership** instead of the Step 2b accounting's **executed** set — telling agents to suppress patterns a silently-skipped scanner never checked, the precise silent-degradation shape Phase 135 built the accounting to surface. It also caught the dedup/downgrade/single-site laundering gaps folded into the rule above, a false fire-ledger rationale on verify-the-cited-rule (the 5e ledger is fed only by mechanical stale-verdicts — the drift test had pinned the false premise), and the incremental exclusion's unactionability (agents get whole files; the orchestrator now states the last-round date so agents can diff). One stale-reference fix rode along: `/codebase-review`'s legacy "(3a–3g)" range → "(3a)", drift-guarded. A discovered pre-existing mirror hazard was also fixed: the Phase-139 mirror-push note named the dogfood target in its Pass-1c parenthetical — in this shipping file, which that very pass hard-fails on — reworded de-identified.

**Gate.** +19 tests (`tests/test_compound_claim_hardening.py`, from the 1098 baseline → 1117): the decompose-before-reject rule + directional evidence + every-clause rationale + no-spawn fallback, clause-only drops/downgrades in the partial and both mirrors, clause-by-clause dedup, the corrected verify-the-cited-rule rationale, executed-set suppression keying, incremental-exclusion actionability, the whole-repo carve-out ("whole-repo rounds exist to find pre-existing issues" — the falsehood-shaped hazard of borrow 3), the silenced-issue flip, the 3a silent-failure group, dimension #3 enrichment, and Tier-1 name-the-regression. Full suite green. Prose + tests only; no production code touched. Inline close-out (meta-repo convention); the compound-claim item and the review-family steal-list item move to `REVIEW_ARCHIVE.md`, with borrow (5) re-parked evidence-gated under § Decisions to revisit later.

## Phase 141 (2026-07-23 — `/security-audit` coverage + adjudication bundle)

**Why this phase.** Executes the re-ranked steal list from a head-to-head against Anthropic's `claude-security` plugin (announced 2026-07-22) on a real production codebase. The comparison's sharpest result was not about model quality: **the audit's misses were a map problem, not a reasoning problem.** Three of the six findings only the plugin found sat in top-level subtrees the security map does not cover *at all*, and because the map is **authored rather than derived**, an unmapped subtree is never flagged as unmapped — it is silently invisible on every round, forever, and its silence is indistinguishable from a clean result. The plugin's one structural advantage was an **inventory completeness invariant** (every top-level directory in a component or in an explicit skip ledger with a reason). That invariant was not on the filed steal list; the data promoted it to #1 and demoted the list's expensive candidate (a severity-gated verification panel) to last, because the FP data went the *other* way from the hypothesis — our refuted findings failed on bad reachability triage, not on weak verification of novel claims.

**Deliverable 1 — Step 2a-0, top-level inventory completeness (both review skills).** 2a-1/2a-2 derive their enumeration roots *from the maps' own section globs*, so they can only ever report gaps inside territory some section already names. 2a-0 enumerates the repo independently (`git ls-files | awk -F/ '{print $1}' | sort -u`) and asserts every top-level entry holding tracked code is **covered**, **excluded with a stated one-line reason**, or **unlocalized** (a placeholder section plausibly covers it — the fix there is localizing that section, never a duplicate). Directories and root-level files are judged differently (a section glob may *name* a root file rather than resolve beneath it). Each skill asserts against the map that keys **its own** dispatch. Reasonless exclusions are surfaced, never blocking. The check composes with 2a-1 rather than replacing it: 2a-0 finds subtrees no section reaches, 2a-1 finds files no section matches inside subtrees sections do reach.

**Deliverable 2 — § Adjudication, evidence in both directions (`_shared/fanout-evidence.md`, universal).** Every finding the audit filed and later had refuted failed on an *unexamined assumption*, so the rule binds symmetrically: a falsified premise refutes outright (the ordinary death); beyond that, kill or downgrade only on a mitigation **located and read** at a `file:line`, keep or escalate only on a path actually traced, and when neither can be established **the finding survives** with the gap recorded. The survival default deliberately **inverts** the plugin verifier's default-to-FALSE_POSITIVE, and the reason is specific to this loop: a filed task gets another reader — the fixer, the reviewer, `/review-close` — while a dismissal gets none. An unverified finding costs a review cycle; an unverified dismissal is silent and permanent.

**Deliverable 3 — dependency reachability triage (Agent 6).** An advisory says a vulnerable version is *installed*, not *reachable*. Three of that round's five dependency narratives were materially wrong — two inflating severity by asserting reachability that did not exist, one understating affected call sites. So: trace the chain and cite it, or file `Reachability: unassessed` at the advisory's own severity (still file it — only the *asserted* chain is the defect). Paired with a remediation-blast-radius rule, because one refuted finding would have caused a **production outage** had its fix been applied as filed — via an ignore-file change, not a version bump.

**Two deliberate deviations from the item as filed, recorded so the close-out doesn't read "shipped as filed".** (1) The filing put the skeptical-verifier framing at "Steps 3/3b"; it ships at **adjudication sites only**, never at hunter dispatch — a skeptical hunter reports less, suppressing real findings before anyone can adjudicate them, and the plugin's own architecture separates researcher from verifier for exactly this reason. A drift guard now pins the dispatch paste *with* its not-a-licence-to-report-less disclaimer. (2) The filing said to ship the located-and-read rule "plus a default-to-false-positive stance"; the stance is **rejected** for the queue-asymmetry reason above.

**Adversarial review (house practice — two independent fresh-context Opus reviewers; evidence-fidelity + mechanism-coherence lenses). It changed the phase substantially, and both reviewers independently found the same structural defect.** The evidence reviewer verified de-identification clean and confirmed both shipped empirical claims came from the one experiment arm that completed — but killed **a falsehood in the shipped prose**: the first draft asserted the dependency errors "ran one way", which the primary record contradicts (it contains a finding that *understated* blast radius), and the draft had *pinned that falsehood with a drift guard*, blocking a future author from correcting it. It also caught the test docstring overstating two counts (a "majority" of misses that is three of six; "every" refuted finding that is two of three) and the outage example being a container-config finding presented under a dependency heading. The mechanism reviewer broke the build in four load-bearing places: **the adjudication rule as written protected fabricated findings** (a finding could die only on a *located mitigation*, but a hallucinated finding has no mitigation to locate — and it directly contradicted the sample-re-read bullet immediately above it) → the falsified-premise branch; **"full scans only" made 2a-0 unreachable** (Step 1 auto-detects incremental at ≤7 days, so a weekly-cadence project never reaches a full scan) → runs every round, with scope-narrowing and repeat-compression instead of skipping; **the invariant false-flagged root-level files** the shipped map keys sections on, and would have emitted false gaps on the shipping default day one; and **the rule claimed three binding sites it had no delivery mechanism for** (sub-agents never read the partial, Step 4 dedup never cited it, and `/test-audit`'s own text said only Tier 1 applied) → all three wired. **Both reviewers converged on the exclusion-class defect:** 2a-0 inherited 2a-1's per-file exclusions, which exempted config-only and docs-only *subtrees* — so the check built to end subtree invisibility was blind to exactly the highest-value classes (`.github/` CI integrity, `migrations/` privilege grants). Smaller folds: a dedup reconciliation (`when in doubt, skip` is not a dismissal — the finding survives as the matched task), the compound-findings rule's **second** leg restored to the composition claim, an unsourced frequency comparative dropped from the universal contract, the severity block hoisted out of Agent 6 and its Low tier closed as an evidence bypass, and a root-less-glob (`**/*.py`) ambiguity resolved. Two rider fixes: the three `<project>/CLAUDE.md` stub comments dropped a stale "(loop mode)" label (they have seeded in both modes since Phase 131), and the head-to-head archive entry's two superseded sentences were corrected in the same commit.

**Gate.** +36 tests (`tests/test_audit_coverage_adjudication.py`, from the 1117 baseline → 1153), including a **mirror-equivalence guard** so the two skills' 2a-0 blocks cannot be hardened one at a time, and a replacement for a first-draft test that asserted the absence of a phrase nobody had written (it passed against the pre-change tree *and* would have failed the correct fix). 17 mutations run across both rounds, all killed. Full suite green. Prose + tests only; no production code touched. Inline close-out (meta-repo convention); the steal-list item moves to `REVIEW_ARCHIVE.md` **partially** — its threat-model-step candidate stays filed and unranked, because the head-to-head traced the plugin's unique finds to coverage, not to threat modelling, so that candidate's hypothesis never fired.

## Phase 142 (2026-07-23 — Codex-native skill links)

**Why this phase.** The portability claim has always been architectural intent with one honest caveat attached: designed for any capable agent, never actually integrated with one. The cross-harness work turned that from an absence of evidence into a mixed but *real* record, and the Codex leg produced something buildable — a standalone workspace (`~/Projects/codex-sysop-integration/`, mechanism-neutral by design) whose deliverables 01+02 finalized 2026-07-22. This phase executes [`tools/CODEX_INTEGRATION_SPEC.md`](./tools/CODEX_INTEGRATION_SPEC.md), the spec authored from that evidence and adversarially reviewed the same day. It is the build half of the announce tease "natively supporting Codex in an upcoming version."

**The decision, adopted not re-argued.** Two relative symlinks, no `AGENTS.md` emission:

```
.agents/skills/codebase-review -> ../../.claude/skills/codebase-review
.agents/skills/security-audit  -> ../../.claude/skills/security-audit
```

Links, not copies or conversions — **one source of truth per skill, zero drift surface**, and the native `$`-selectors that no instruction-file prose can provide. Deliverable 01 verified that a fresh isolated Codex session, given only an ordinary request with no Sysop filename or kickoff, selected the right installed workflow. The ownership boundary is the cleanest available: Sysop owns two directory entries, and the consumer's root `AGENTS.md`, other `.agents/` content, and sibling skills survive the whole lifecycle. Three `[amended]` departures from deliverable 02 carried over from the spec: both install modes (not loop-only), probe failure warns and continues (rather than stopping before mutation), and the collision escape hatch is *persisted* rather than re-typed forever.

**Deliverable 1 — `preflight_codex_links`, pinned before every target mutation.** Placed after the T7 guard and strictly before the Phase-128 migration block, which puts it ahead of `_ns_precompute_and_derive`'s hidden DRY_RUN pipeline, the pre-update snapshot commit, the namespace moves, and the runtime migration. It is the sole owner of the collision hard-error, because `ensure_relative_symlink` runs in three DRY_RUN contexts where an error would be invisible or fatal. Hard-fail is deliberate: a consumer-owned `.agents/skills/codebase-review` routes ordinary Codex requests to *their* workflow while a skipped install claims Sysop is set up — the silent-divergence shape Phases 135–141 exist to kill.

**Deliverable 2 — `ensure_relative_symlink`, and the never-exit rule.** Under `DRY_RUN` it classifies and records only: no creation, no verification, **no error**. That is a correctness requirement, not tidiness — it runs inside `cmd_adopt`'s managed-paths computation and inside `run_install_pipeline >/dev/null 2>&1`, where a bash `exit` kills `--update` with zero output despite the `|| true`. A path Sysop does not own is never recorded, which is what makes `--adopt` of a real Codex user safe: adopt records reality and moves on, and the collision surfaces later as an error rather than as consumer data inside the sweep's blast radius.

**Deliverable 3 — lock, flags, sweep.** `codex_links` joins `mode` and `packs` as a re-read field, so `--no-codex-links` survives a bare `sysop-update.sh`. The obsolete sweep gains `-e || -L` (a broken managed link fails `-e` and would be stranded) plus a raw-target ownership guard. **Identity is the raw `readlink` value everywhere, never resolved content** — a link the consumer repointed is their data even when it resolves to the same bytes.

**A payload consequence the spec did not call out.** The install gained a top-level directory, which silently invalidated every documented `git add … CLAUDE.md` line — the exact Phase-131 drift class two cold readers hit. Fixed at all five doc sites, plus the two loop→full upgrade lines (a *pre-Codex* loop install gains `.agents/` for the first time on that upgrade), and pinned by a guard test. The trap handled explicitly rather than papered over: `git add .agents/` itself fatals for opt-out and probe-failure consumers, so the quickstart documents the default path and both degradation paths say to drop it.

**Adversarial review (house practice — two independent fresh-context reviewers; installer-mechanics + evidence-fidelity lenses). It changed the phase substantially, and both reviewers landed findings the build session had missed entirely.** The mechanics reviewer found the worst one: the sweep guard's own comment said "never a path further down" while the code did the opposite, so a corrupt lock naming `.agents/skills/codebase-review/SKILL.md` would have been resolved by `-e` *through* the link and removed by `rm -f`, deleting the real skill body — reproduced, exit 0, 85 KB gone. It also found that the preflight checked only the two *leaf* paths, so a consumer file at `.agents` or an unwritable parent died as a bare `mkdir`/`ln` failure mid-pipeline: under `--update` that lands *after* the snapshot commit and the skill overwrite, leaving a split-version install with a stale lock. Both are now guarded, with the guard defaulting to deny for the whole `.agents/` namespace. Two smaller ones: the lock re-read was `--update`-scoped, so a plain re-install would resurrect the links or hard-error on an already-acknowledged collision; and the capability probe wrote into the target *before* the `Proceed?` confirmation, so a declined run had already touched the repo — the probe is now split out and runs after consent.

The evidence reviewer caught the phase's own dishonesty. The shipped `AGENTS.md` fallback recipe was a paraphrase, not deliverable 02's verified block, and the sentence it dropped is load-bearing (resolve `_shared/*.md`, run the deterministic pre-scan via `run_checks.sh` — the Phase-136 failure class, 24 tasks vs a reference 372); the verbatim block now ships. It found "Claude Code is unaffected either way" reinstated in shipped prose and installer output — the exact unverified "ignores" claim the *spec's own* adversarial pass had struck. It found full-mode registration stated as fact where the spec tags it **derived, untested**. And it found a false universal in the README: the pre-existing "every real run so far has been Claude Code" is no longer true after the cross-harness cells, and this phase's added Codex clause made the contradiction sharper — the new wording keeps the honest limit (including the measured security-audit refusal) without sizing any gap or naming the dogfood target.

**Test theater, found twice.** The build session's own mutation pass caught one test that proved nothing: it broke both links by deleting their targets, except `--update` reinstalls the skills before the sweep runs, healing them before the assertion. The evidence reviewer then found a second in the same family — the probe-failure-during-`--update` test never invoked the probe at all, because the probe is gated on "something needs creating" and both links were already correct, so the mutation it claimed to guard survived. Both are rebuilt around the state that actually reaches the branch, and both now die under their mutation.

**Gate.** +41 tests (`tests/test_install_codex_links.py`, 1153 → 1194 collected), every review-driven fix mutation-verified (5/5 killed) on top of the build session's own round (9 killed, 1 equivalent). **The phase is not done at green tests:** spec § 7 requires the Task-5 acceptance run — a fresh scratch install driven by an ordinary request in an isolated Codex session, filed as `deliverables/05-shipped-mechanism-validation.md` — and that is what closes the checklist item's build half.

## Phase 143 (2026-07-23 — review-round refusal/abandonment loudness)

**Why this phase.** A review round that dies partway leaves nothing behind: no `review_tasks.md` entries, no error, no trace. It is byte-identical to a clean round that found nothing. The provenance is measured, not hypothetical — in the cross-harness comparison, one frontier non-Claude model refused `/security-audit` 2/2 on identical prompts, once before doing any work and once *after* ~1 minute of genuine effort (reading the prior round, running the pre-scan, dispatching four OWASP-scoped sub-agents) before declining. This executes item (2) of that checklist entry, from [`tools/AUDIT_REFUSAL_LOUDNESS_SPEC.md`](./tools/AUDIT_REFUSAL_LOUDNESS_SPEC.md). Items (1) and (3) are docs and stay naming-unlock-gated.

**The honest limit is the design's first premise, not a footnote.** A skill cannot detect a refusal that *precedes* compliance — nothing running inside the refused round can. So the mechanism is two layers with different reach: an in-skill marker that catches mid-run death, and outer checks that run independently of the round and can therefore see a round that never started. Nothing here attempts a refusal *workaround*: rephrasing past a model's safety refusal is out of scope on principle, and a prompt engineered to slip past one would no longer be measuring the skill.

**Layer 1 — the round marker.** Both review skills gain a `## Pre-flight: Round Marker` step and a pinned `### 5f. Clear the round marker`. The marker is a nonce-keyed file under `sysop/runtime/pending-rounds/`, anchored to the **main checkout** via `--git-common-dir` (the Phase 32 lock precedent, reaffirmed by Phase 65a — a marker written inside a worktree is invisible to every reader and destroyed by `git worktree remove`). Both operations are a single plain `python3 - <<'PY'` heredoc, the Phase-126 idiom, so they ride the already-shipped `Bash(python3 -:*)` rule: **zero new permission rules**. Removal is pinned immediately after the `review_tasks.md` write and *before* the summary and promotion steps — a death during Steps 6–9b strands a marker, which is correct, because the round's results are already durably written; removing at the true final step would strand a marker on every unattended loop run that skips interactive promotion.

**Layer 2 — absence surfacing.** `self_check.sh` gains probe 6 (stale markers with their recorded start times; last completed round per skill). The round parse reads `review_tasks.md` **and** `review_tasks_archive.md` and matches by **substring**, because Step 5b merges same-day rounds into a combined `— Code Quality Review + OWASP Security Audit` header that a suffix-keyed parse would report as a round that never ran. The `run_checks` pre-scan summary appends a stale-marker line — that is the surface a loop-mode consumer actually re-reads every round, where `self_check.sh` is a one-shot probe nothing re-runs during operation. `/sitrep` gains an `abandoned review round` discrepancy for the full-lifecycle path.

**Four deviations from the spec, all corrections rather than preferences.**

1. **The listing moved into the write step, ahead of the write.** The spec put the marker write before Step 1 and the listing *in* Step 1 — which would make every round detect its own marker and report a phantom "concurrent session" on the first run of any single-session repo. Folded into one heredoc that reports priors and then writes, so a round structurally cannot see itself.
2. **Asymmetric round history is advisory, not a failure.** The spec had the bad-line fire on asymmetry. But "the model refuses this task class" and "the human hasn't run it yet" leave *exactly the same trace*, and round history cannot separate them. Failing there would redden every adopter still working through the loop — the cry-wolf failure this phase is otherwise careful to avoid. The check now names both readings and stays advisory; only a stale marker fails, because that one is unambiguous evidence a round started and never finished.
3. **A clean round still clears its marker.** Neither skill stated Step 5 was unconditional, so a model with zero findings could reasonably jump to the summary and strand a marker — turning every healthy review into a reported abandonment. Not in the spec; found by walking the zero-findings path.
4. **The marker is best-effort and deliberately absent from the hard-stop permission guard.** A hard requirement would convert a missing allow-rule into "you cannot run a review at all," which is strictly worse than a missing marker. A drift-guard test pins this against a future author tidying the dependency into the guard list.

**A spec claim that was true for the wrong reason.** The spec justified "zero new permission rules" by asserting that "the review skills' existing heredocs prove the rule ships in both" templates. Neither review skill had a `python3 -` heredoc — the evidence did not exist. The conclusion survives independent verification (`core/companion/.claude/settings.json:33` and the 14-rule `LOOP_ALLOW` subset at `install.sh:2500`), and a test now pins the loop-subset membership so layer 1 cannot silently disarm in the install mode the public docs route newcomers to.

**Gate.** +33 tests (1194 → 1227 collected): `tests/test_round_markers.py` extracts both heredocs from the shipped SKILL.md prose and executes them — write, owner-checked removal, nonce-mismatch refusal, `git check-ignore` fail-safe, worktree-anchoring, self-detection — so the tested artifact is the one that ships (the `test_review_close_close_heredoc.py` pattern); plus probe-6 fixtures in `tests/test_self_check_sh.py` for combined same-day headers, archive-only consumers, and symmetric-vs-asymmetric absence. **Honest scope, stated rather than papered over:** the abandon→surface lifecycle is model-executed prose and is not automatable end-to-end; the heredoc unit tests and the drift guards are the testable surface. The ~2h live/stale threshold is a first guess to tune on real use.

**Adversarial pass (run 2026-07-23, after the first commit `fb60ce5`; two independent fresh-context reviewers — mechanics lens + evidence-fidelity lens, per house practice).** Both landed on the **same** #1 defect independently, and both reproduced it: `self_check.sh` probe 6 anchored to `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (the *worktree* root) while the two other outer surfaces — the pre-scan note and `/sitrep` — resolve `--git-common-dir` (the *main* root) where markers actually live. Run from inside a worktree, probe 6 read the empty worktree copy and reported a false all-clear on a stale marker in main — the exact silent under-report this phase exists to close, in the one surface with no worktree test. Fixed: probe 6 now resolves `MAIN_ROOT` via `--git-common-dir` (matching the other two) and bases both the marker-dir glob and the round-history reads on it; +2 worktree regression tests (`test_stale_marker_in_main_is_seen_from_a_worktree`, `test_round_history_read_from_main_when_run_from_a_worktree`). Three lower findings also applied: the removal heredoc's "owner check" comment overstated its guarantee (the nonce cross-check only catches an internally-inconsistent file — real ownership is passing your own captured `ROUND_MARKER=` path; comment corrected in both skills), the "clean round still clears its marker" guard lived only inside Step 5f where a zero-finding model that skips Step 5 never reads it (hoisted a plain "do not skip this step, even with zero findings" line to the Step 5 heading ahead of 5a, pinned by `test_zero_finding_guard_is_at_the_step5_heading_not_only_in_5f`), and `docs/loop-mode.md` implied the every-round pre-scan surface covers the refuse-*before-start* case (it doesn't — that shape writes no marker; only `self_check.sh`'s asymmetry line catches it, so the copy now splits the two refusal shapes and names the surface for each). **What the pass confirmed sound** (both reviewers, verified against the code, drift guards mutation-tested): the "zero new permission rules" claim (`Bash(python3 -:*)` ships in both `settings.json` and the `LOOP_ALLOW` subset; both drift guards bite under mutation), git-common-dir parity between the two heredoc implementations, the gitignore fail-safe on a non-existent probe path, no-raise pre-scan, bash 3.2 compatibility, the archiver/combined-header parse, non-interference with `/review-close`'s dirty-worktree classification, and — the design decision most worth scrutinizing — the **advisory-asymmetry call is correct** (the one disambiguator, a previously-completed-now-archived security round, *is* read and suppresses the alarm; making it fatal would cry wolf on every mid-adoption consumer). Two undisclosed-but-defensible minor deviations noted: the pre-scan note fires on *stale* markers only (not all pending — the correct age-split behavior, consistent with the asymmetry deviation) and the marker omits the spec's optional "harness+model (when known)" content field. **One residual, filed not fixed:** an armed CI running `run_checks --fail-on-blocking` does not fail on an abandoned round (the pre-scan note is advisory, doesn't touch the gate) — only an operator running `self_check.sh` (exit 1) or reading the pre-scan output catches it; this is intentional (the gate is for findings, not orchestration health) but means CI is not a catch-net for this signal. **Gate after the pass:** +36 tests over the phase (1194 → 1230 collected), full suite green.

## Phase 144 (2026-07-24 — `claude-security` detect-and-ingest for `/security-audit`)

**Why this phase.** The filed detect-and-ingest item (checklist § Medium), strengthened by the 2026-07-23 head-to-head that measured **zero overlapping findings** between Anthropic's `claude-security` plugin and Sysop's `/security-audit` on the same commit: six of the audit's nine were pass-through of already-promoted deterministic machinery, while all six of the plugin's were novel code reasoning that *no promoted rule would have caught at commit time*. That is the feeder thesis measured, not asserted — the plugin finds what the loop's deterministic layer structurally can't. This phase lets `/security-audit` fold a `claude-security` report into `review_tasks.md` as tracked `[reported]` tasks, so those findings enter the queue instead of evaporating with the plugin's (nondeterministic, session-eating) run.

**Two decisions were locked before building, both survived the adversarial pass.** (1) **Passive-ingest only, no `--deep` flag.** Sysop *cannot* launch the plugin: a `claude-code-guide` probe (corroborated by an independent reviewer) established that the `Workflow` tool is stripped from every sub-agent with no override, so spawning the `claude-security` orchestrator agent would fail the instant it invoked `Workflow(claude-security:scan)`. Reading the report off disk needs nothing special and is harness-neutral — which also sidesteps introducing Sysop's first runtime harness-detection check. The human runs `/claude-security` on their own cadence (a documented quarterly-sweep recipe); the audit ingests whatever report is present. (2) **Ingest-and-flag-stale** for reports scanned at an older commit — union across all present reports, never drop a finding.

**What shipped.** A tested parser `sysop/scripts/ingest_security_report.py` (the read-and-sanitize boundary) + a new `/security-audit` **Step 3c** (always-on, best-effort) that folds in-scope findings under their own `Ingested — claude-security` batch, buckets out-of-scope findings visibly, and surfaces a truncated scan loudly. Plus the loop-mode permission wiring: the ingest CLI's allow-rule in the master `settings.json` template and the `LOOP_ALLOW` subset (14 → 16 rules).

**The two-reviewer adversarial pass (run on the plan, before any code) reshaped the wiring — the corrections are the substance of this phase.** The first-draft plan leaked in ways green tests would never have caught; each was verified against the plugin source and folded in:

1. **Loop-mode dead-on-arrival (the reviewers' most serious finding).** The loop-mode `settings.json` is a hard-coded 14-rule *allowlist*, not a denylist complement — so the ingest CLI matched no rule and would have *silently halted* under `auto` + `skipAutoPermissionPrompt`, in the exact mode Sysop ships to. Fixed by adding the allow-rule to both the master template and `LOOP_ALLOW`, guarded by the existing exact-set loop-mode test (now 16).
2. **The parser was inverting the plugin's stability contract.** The plugin promises only filenames + JSONL field order + `verification.status`/`reason` stable; the stamp's `run_shape`/`verification` sub-key *sets* are variable (3 keys coverage-absent, ~14 present). The draft pinned the variable thing (would have raised on valid low-effort reports) and ignored the stable one. The parser now keys trust off `verification.status`/`reason`, reads the stamp defensively, and **warns-and-skips on drift rather than raising** — a drifted leftover report must not brick the audit. `verified` != coverage: a truncated run still stamps `verified`, so coverage caveats are surfaced separately (and `skipped_components` / `completeness_check_outcome`, which are normal disclosure, are deliberately *not* alarm-triggers, to avoid cry-wolf).
3. **Untrusted-input injection.** Finding text is a model summary of scanned code and may carry adversarial markup; the raw JSONL escapes only its own line separators, not markdown. Written verbatim it could forge a `[verified]` provenance tag or inject a command `/auto-fix` re-runs. The parser is now the sanitization boundary (collapse newlines, neutralize backticks and brackets, cap length); the skill writes only the parser's emitted fields, never the raw report; `snippet` (attacker-controlled source) is never emitted.
4. **Provenance stays `[reported]`.** No third "externally-verified" marker (the item asked for one; the binary `_shared/fanout-evidence.md` contract forbids it). The plugin's panel verification is recorded in the row annotation as data, never promoted onto the tag — and placing ingest *after* Step 3b keeps ingested findings structurally out of the 3b sample-re-read that upgrades to `[verified]`.
5. **Conservative union + honest staleness.** Cross-report merge collapses only exact `(file, line, category, title)` duplicates and never drops a distinct finding (a lossy identity key would itself be the "supersede" the rule forbids; line drift between nondeterministic runs is left for the skill's ±5-line dedup + the human). Staleness is best-effort git — unversioned/dirty/absent-commit → `unknown`, never dropped; paths rebased from the stamp's `scan_root`.
6. **Re-ingest + accumulation.** A fold-once marker (`sysop/runtime/ingested-security-reports`) stops a persistent gitignored report re-surfacing every round; ingested findings dedup against closed/dismissed tasks so a human-rejected finding doesn't reappear from a fresh scan.
7. **Honest value, per the reviewers.** The item's headline — "Sysop turns any scanner's findings into permanent `checks.yml` rules" — is unreachable for the plugin's code-reasoning findings (they fail Step 8's systemic-pattern gate and Step 9's cross-round recurrence gate, landing as prose at best). The reachable, measured value is the tracked `review_tasks.md` tasks; the docs and archive note say so rather than sell the unreachable half. Also recorded (checklist `:50`, the nested-spawn item): Claude Code v2.1.217 flipped nested agent-spawning off by default, so that item's "on by default, no config surface" premise is now stale in both clauses.

**Second adversarial pass (on the built code, before merge; two independent fresh-context reviewers — a parser lens and a wiring lens).** The wiring reviewer confirmed the load-bearing security properties clean (permission match, provenance non-laundering, hard-stop isolation, loop-mode discoverability, no "permanent checks" overclaim); the parser reviewer found **two HIGH bugs, both fixed**. (1) `trust()` raised `AttributeError` on a non-dict `verification`/`run_shape` — a truthy non-dict slips the `or {}` coercion — so one junk stamp would abort ingestion of every other report and break the never-raise/exit-0 contract; fixed with `isinstance` coercion (matching `revision`) plus a per-report skip wrapper. (2) `sanitize()` covered per-finding text but **not the stamp channel** — `generated_at` (uncapped), `commit`, `mode`, `reason`, caveat dir-names reached the row annotation and trust block raw, so a crafted stamp could forge the exact `[verified]` `TASK-` row the sanitizer exists to stop; fixed by routing every stamp-derived string through `sanitize()`. Lower findings also applied: the union key now uses the *raw* (untruncated, unsanitized) title so a display-title collision cannot merge-and-drop a distinct finding (the never-supersede invariant, previously only asserted); non-ASCII staleness (`-c core.quotePath=false -z`); commit hex-validation + `--` guard; negative-line clamp; the `..prefix` rebase over-rejection; and the stale loop-mode count strings this phase introduced (dry-run "14"→16, now count-guarded). The wiring reviewer's two executability gaps were closed too: a hard "non-`--full` rounds MUST pass `--scope-file`" imperative (was caller-discipline-only → could flood an incremental round) with a concrete `sysop/runtime/audit-scope.txt` home, and the dedup-against-closed rule now searches `review_tasks_archive.md` and distinguishes a rejected finding (suppress) from a re-surfaced *fixed* site (keep — a regression signal, since `[x]` conflates the two).

**Gate.** +56 tests (1230 → 1286 collected), full suite green. `tests/test_ingest_security_report.py` (43) exercises the parser against real fixtures — tolerant parse of both stamp shapes and non-dict fields, trust off status/reason, the finding-*and*-stamp injection repros, conservative union across the collision cases, best-effort staleness in a real git repo (ASCII + non-ASCII), the fold-once marker; `tests/test_audit_ingest_skill.py` (13) pins the Step 3c wording, the scope-file imperative, the archive-aware closed dedup, and the full-mode allow-rule; the loop-mode suite's exact-set + count assertions now cover the ingest rule. **Honest scope:** the ingest→file→promote lifecycle is model-executed prose; the parser's behavior and the drift guards are the testable surface.

## Phase 145 (2026-07-24 — pre-push doc-currency bundle: evidence-claim softening + § 8.4 scripts-table backfill + drift guard)

**Why this phase.** A pre-mirror-push gate turned up two things worth fixing before the snapshot rather than after. Neither is a bug in shipped machinery; both are the documentation half of work already done, which is exactly the class the promotion loop keeps proving goes silently stale.

**(1) An unscoped evidence claim in shipped prose.** Phase 144 shipped "the head-to-head measured **zero overlap** between the two tools' findings" at three sites — `/security-audit` Step 3c, `WORKFLOW.md` § 6, and the `ingest_security_report.py` module docstring — stated flatly, with no n and no codebase. It is one run, on one production codebase, at one pinned commit. Everything around it is carefully hedged (`[reported]` never promotes to `[verified]`; "a floor, not a coverage claim"), which made the one unscoped sentence the outlier against the honest-limits discipline Phases 98/140/141 exist to enforce. All three now read "one head-to-head (2026-07-23, a single production codebase at one pinned commit) measured **zero overlapping findings** … one run, not a general property." The fact is unchanged; its scope is now stated. Verified first that no drift guard pinned the old phrasing — Phase 141's lesson was a guard that had pinned a *falsehood* in place, so "is this claim load-bearing for a test?" is now a pre-edit check.

**(2) `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.4 had fallen eight rows behind the shipping tree.** Missing: `next_task.py` (45a), `pr_dependabot.py` (53), `sitrep_survey.py` (82), `self_check.sh` (133), `ingest_security_report.py` (144), plus `validate_tasks.py`, `backfill_completed_dates.py`, and `_log.py`. `self_check.sh` is the shape of the defect: the install footer and the quickstart both tell a consumer to run it, while the canonical table did not list it at all. Phase 144 was itself half-documented by its own convention — § 6 prose, no table row. Each new row was written from the script's actual contract (docstring + flags + exit codes), not inferred from its name.

**The durable half.** `tests/test_workflow_scripts_table.py` (+3) makes the absence mechanical, because an absent row is silent by construction — it looks exactly like a script that doesn't exist. Same failure shape as an unmapped subtree in the security map, so the same fix at smaller scope: every non-underscore script in `core/companion/scripts/` must have a § 8.4 row; the backward direction catches dead referents (a row for a deleted script); and the private-helper exemption is asserted as an exact set, so a new `_helper.py` forces a deliberate call instead of inheriting the exemption silently. Two scope calls are deliberate and stated in the module docstring: the guard is top-level-only (`run_checks/` is a package, not entry points), and a renumbered section fails loudly rather than passing vacuously — mutation-verified, along with the three real failure modes (4 mutations, all killed; baseline green on clean input).

**Gate.** +3 tests (1286 → 1289 collected), full suite green. Docs, prose, and one new test file; no production code touched. Inline close-out (meta-repo convention). Also filed, not built: a **monograph + public-docs currency pass for Phases 134–144** (checklist § Medium) — `docs/workflow.html` has zero hits for `claude-security`, `Codex`, attestation, pre-scan accounting, adjudication, or round markers, and the public `docs/` tree has no surface at all for the ingest, which the announce beat sheet's Beat 1 hook depends on. That is phase-sized and announce-gating, so it is queued rather than folded in here.

## Phase 146 (2026-07-24 — monograph + public-docs currency pass for Phases 134–144, and the first public surface for the ingest)

**Why this phase.** Executes the item Phase 145 filed rather than folded in (checklist § Medium). Two legs. **(a)** `docs/workflow.html` was eleven phases stale — the last real currency pass was Phase 109 (covering 97–108), and 128/129/133 touched it only incidentally. Measured before touching anything: zero hits for `claude-security`, `Codex`, attestation, pre-scan accounting, adjudication, `self_check`, inventory completeness, or round markers. The monograph described a Sysop that predated the entire 134–144 hardening arc, and it is the deep-read surface the announce points at. **(b)** The public `docs/` tree had no surface at all for the Phase-144 ingest, while Beat 1 of the announce beat sheet hooks on the `claude-security` plugin launch — a hook with no page to land on.

**The organizing choice, and why it isn't eleven paragraphs.** A phase-by-phase absorption would have produced a changelog, which is what `PHASE_LOG.md` already is. Instead the arc was re-read for what it actually argues, and it argues one thing: **a review that didn't happen is indistinguishable from a review that found nothing.** Four phases are four shapes of exactly that failure — a stage that died (135), a runner that never started (136), a round that never finished (143), and a subtree no map section names (141, deliverable 1) — so they ship as one § III subsection, *The failure that looks like a clean result*, with each shape stated as the concrete failure that produced it. A second subsection takes the provenance/adjudication trio (138 attestation, 140 decompose-before-reject, 141 deliverable 2) under *What it takes to file a finding — and to kill one*, because those three are one argument about evidence in both directions. A third, *Folding in an outside scanner*, is leg (b).

**Leg (b) sites.** The ingest section in § III plus a paragraph in `docs/loop-mode.md` § "Day one" — loop mode ships the parser and both allow-rules, and after the Phase-132 funnel inversion that page is where a newcomer lands. Both carry the Phase-145 scoping verbatim in substance (one head-to-head, a single production codebase at one pinned commit, zero overlapping findings, *one run, not a general property*) and the honest ceiling the Phase-144 reviewers insisted on: these are code-reasoning findings that mostly fail § IV's systemic-pattern and cross-round recurrence gates, so what the ingest buys is *tracked work*, not permanent checks. A first draft of the loop-mode paragraph linked `claude-security` to a GitHub URL that was never verified and appears in no shipped doc; removed rather than guessed — the shipped surfaces name the plugin without linking it, and this one now matches.

**Smaller absorptions.** `/test-audit`'s glossary entry gains the Phase-137 pair: `security_map.md` as the second "audit this hardest" signal (the rubric had cited it since Phase 80 while the skill never opened the file), and the de-overclaimed read-only guard — the frontmatter fires on skill *invocation*, so an agent merely told to read `SKILL.md` is held by the contract, not the guard. § VI gains *One concrete step off Claude Code* for Phase 142 (the two relative symlinks, the narrow ownership boundary, the persisted opt-out) with the README's honest-limits wording as its floor, not a softer paraphrase. The consumer-layout listing gains `.agents/skills/`, `sysop/runtime/pending-rounds/`, `self_check.sh`, `ingest_security_report.py`, and `accounting.py` on the `run_checks/` line.

**Two deliberate non-absorptions, recorded so a later reader doesn't read them as misses.** Phase 134 (`/review-close` Step 3b `mkdir -p` + parked-marker removal) is a data-loss bug fix in mechanics the monograph describes one altitude up; there is no claim it falsifies. Phase 139 (`## Map coverage exclusions` scope) is a consumer-`CLAUDE.md` schema detail the monograph has never described, at `WORKFLOW.md` § 6.1's altitude rather than this document's — its own thesis (a schema section two capable agents read differently makes cross-run comparison unreliable before any model-quality question is reached) is about authoring a consumer's config, not about how the review works. Everything else in 134–144 is absorbed, including Phase 135's follow-up, whose trust-anchor *prevention* rides as a closing clause on the stage-death paragraph — the crash is not merely made visible, it stops happening.

**Stamps.** Hero stat and both colophon stamps 113 → 146 · 2026-07-24, moved together as `tests/test_doc_currency.py` requires. Verified current rather than assumed: 23 skills (matches `core/skills/`), 78 promoted conventions, 2 install paths, and the 71-round / 3,298-finding evidence corpus (the Phase-94 July snapshot) all still hold. Render-verified in a browser at both themes, per the Phase-115 precedent.

**Adversarial review (house practice — two independent fresh-context Opus reviewers, not forks; evidence-fidelity + completeness/coherence lenses). It earned its keep twice over: between them they landed one HIGH, thirteen MEDIUM, and eight LOW, and the build session had missed every one.**

The evidence reviewer's HIGH was a corpus misattribution: the compound-claim result was credited to "this project's own review data" when the primary record is a blind grading pass over a *pooled cross-model finding set from an outside codebase*. The document already cites two other corpora (the cross-harness trial, and § IV's 71-round upstream archive), so the draft collapsed three distinct evidence bases into a claim about one. It also killed a claim that all three ingest properties were adversarial-pass corrections — the first was locked before any code and merely *survived* the pass; "the runner bootstraps itself", which reinstates the exact phrasing Phase 136's own review struck (PyYAML is the runner's one hard dependency, so it does not bootstrap *that*); an unscoped Codex selection claim (measured on loop mode, *expected* for full — the same defect Phase 142's evidence reviewer caught); "most verifiers take", the unsourced frequency comparative Phase 141's pass had already removed once; a `/test-audit` guard description that dropped the partiality half (`Bash` stays allowed, so a shell redirect writes); "the ingest behaves identically under any agent", a mechanism property stated as an agent-behavior one eighty-five lines below a measured refusal; a "Both review skills now open with" that contradicted § III's own lede; a § IV cross-reference to a gate § IV does not state; and a `security_map.md` signal presented without its post-localization caveat.

The completeness reviewer produced the per-phase absorption table this phase should have produced itself, and it found **two silent misses and one silent inversion**. (1) **Phase 141's deliverable 3 was simply absent** — dependency reachability triage plus the remediation-blast-radius rule, which carries the most concrete fact in the whole arc (a refuted finding whose fix, applied as filed, would have caused a production outage). Now a paragraph in the adjudication subsection, where it belongs: an asserted call chain is an unverified premise. (2) **Phase 135's follow-up** (trust-anchor prevention) was neither absorbed nor declared; it now closes the stage-death paragraph. (3) **The Phase-138 tiers were inverted** — the draft opened "Both generators fan out… *So* every finding carries its provenance," making the universal Tier-1 marker read as a consequence of fan-out. That is precisely the collapse Phase 138's *own* plan reviewer caught and reverted; it had crept back in. Rewritten so the marker is stated as universal (single-agent `/test-audit` included, now said in that skill's entry too) before the fan-out tier is introduced. It further found Phase 140 half-absorbed and homed wrong — the rule's primary home is `_shared/adversarial-review.md`, § I/§ II territory, so `/plan-review`'s entry now carries decompose-before-reject *and* the second-independent-pass rule with its no-spawn sealed-rationale fallback; that the § VI framing was backwards (the companion layer was always harness-neutral — the *skills* were the Claude-Code-shaped part); that neither public surface told a reader **how to produce a report** (`/claude-security` → `CLAUDE-SECURITY-<timestamp>/` → `/security-audit`, now in `loop-mode.md`); that `docs/index.html` — where the announce's own CTA lands — had zero trace of the hook, now a sentence deep-linking the new `#outside-scanner` anchor; and that the new guard's leg-(b) assertion was **near-vacuous** (`"[reported]" in text or "reported" in text` — the second disjunct is satisfied by the word "reported" in ordinary prose, so it could never fail). Also folded: an undefined "the older forward coverage audit" back-reference, `[reported]` glossed on first use in loop-mode, deep-link `id`s on the three new headings, and a stale `Fig. 4`/`Fig. 5` source comment.

**Gate.** +4 tests (1289 → 1293 collected), full suite green. `tests/test_ingest_claim_scoping.py` promotes the no-overlap claim's scoping to a deterministic check — the second occurrence of the same claim-scoping defect (Phase 144 shipped it unscoped at three sites, Phase 145 rescoped all three, nothing pinned the fix), which is the same recurrence rule the convention loop applies to review findings. Keyed on the *claim* rather than one phrasing, because the five sites already word it two ways and a phrase-exact guard would have missed the two this phase added. Four legs: the `not a general property` disclaimer at every site, a concrete scope detail at every site, an exact-set completeness sweep so a sixth site is a deliberate call, and a leg-(b) guard so a future rewrite can't silently drop the ingest's public surface. Five mutations run, all killed; baseline green. Two scope calls stated in the module docstring: consumer-facing surfaces only (the history files restate the claim as history, not as a claim to a reader), and the exact site set. Docs, prose, and one new test file; no production code touched. Inline close-out (meta-repo convention); the currency-pass item moves to `REVIEW_ARCHIVE.md`.

**Mirror note.** This pass is in-tree only. The public monograph still reads "as of Phase 113" until the next mirror push, which is now the actual remaining pre-announce dependency — recorded in the checklist's § Before announce status line rather than as a bullet, since the item itself is resolved.

## Phase 147 (2026-07-24 — the give-back family's target repo becomes a first-class consumer config)

**Why this phase.** GDP's first consumer run of the reporting family, the day before, surfaced the item verbatim (checklist § Medium, filed 2026-07-24). All three GitHub-touching give-back skills — `/report-issues`, `/contribute-convention`, `/share-wins` — hardcoded `getsysop/sysop` and accepted only a per-invocation `--repo`. Two consequences, and the second is what makes the first structural. **(1) The shipped default is a disclosure trap.** `SYSOP_ISSUES.md` friction entries routinely quote the security context that *produced* the friction — GDP's ISSUE-0008 names an unfixed PII-scrub coverage gap and the contents of open security-review batches — and the default files them to a **public** repo. Per-entry consent showed *what* was being filed; the destination was one plain line in the plan output and nothing flagged entry sensitivity. **(2) There was deliberately no durable override.** Skills sit outside the customization-preservation scope (§ 8.2c, Phase 24b: standard overwrite, no silent prompt-forks — an unchanged and correct call), so a consumer could not persistently redirect the family. GDP's workaround was a consumer-side `CLAUDE.md § Sysop upstream repo` section (gdp `e742a077`) that binds the model at runtime but that the skills' own prose knew nothing about. This phase promotes that workaround into a config the skills actually read.

**Resolution, single-sourced.** New `core/skills/_shared/upstream-repo.md`, cited (never duplicated) by all three skills at Step 0.6 — the first `_shared` partial written *for* the give-back family (all three already cite `permission-guard.md`), and the same "consumer declares its shape" pattern as `§ Merge policy` and `§ Pre-merge verification`. Precedence: `--repo` › `CLAUDE.md § Sysop upstream repo` › `getsysop/sysop`. The parser takes the first non-empty line under the header and strips surrounding backticks, because the *documented template* is the backticked form and GDP's live section is written that way — a bare-word-only parser would have failed the one real consumer on day one.

**The load-bearing safety property is what happens when the section is malformed.** A present-but-unparseable section is a **hard stop**, not a fall-back to the default. This inverts the usual "absent or broken → default" reflex on purpose: a consumer who wrote that section did so to keep something *off* the public repo, so routing them back to it because their line had a typo or a full URL in it is precisely the disclosure the config exists to prevent. An *absent* section stays the ordinary case and is not an error — fail-closed on malformed, unchanged on absent.

**Visibility, primary-with-fallback (Wade's call).** The nudge could fire on a cheap local heuristic ("target is the shipped default") or on the authoritative answer. Ratified: authoritative primary, heuristic fallback. A read-only `gh repo view <target> --json visibility` probe answers `PUBLIC`/`PRIVATE`/`INTERNAL`; when it fails — offline, unauthenticated, rate-limited, or a target the token cannot see — the shipped default resolves to PUBLIC *by definition, not by inference*, and **anything else resolves to UNKNOWN, never to private**. That asymmetry is the whole design: assuming public costs a redundant warning, assuming private costs a disclosure. Every line reporting visibility carries `[verified]` or `[assumed]` — the *bracket-marker convention* of Phase 138's `fanout-evidence.md`, deliberately **not** its vocabulary (that pair is `[verified]`/`[reported]`, and its `[verified]` means "I opened the cited `file:line`", where this one means "GitHub answered"). The partial states the distinction so the two are never read as interchangeable. The probe is advisory and non-fatal throughout — notably, a 404 from it does **not** prove the target is missing, since a private repo you lack access to 404s identically, so it never triggers the skills' existing not-found stop.

**Sensitivity nudge.** A local scan of the bodies about to be filed — not of the source file — fired when visibility is `PUBLIC`, `INTERNAL`, or `UNKNOWN`. It names which items matched and on which term. Bare `HIGH`/`CRITICAL` are deliberately **not** triggers: they fire on ordinary bug reports, and a nudge that fires every run trains the human to skim past it. It is a warning, never a filter — it drops nothing, redacts nothing, and changes nothing about what per-entry consent offers. Fired at *both* ends in all three skills: declared at Step 0.6 and re-stated at the consent gate, because Step 0.6 runs long before the human approves anything and a long run would otherwise lose it. `/contribute-convention` gets the sharpest framing of it — generalization strips *fingerprints*, not *subject matter*, so a perfectly placeholder-ized rule can still tell a reader which class of vulnerability this project keeps having.

**Permission call, made against an unverified claim rather than on top of one.** Two of the three skills already asserted that `gh repo view` is "read-only and auto-approved under `auto` mode" — prose that predates this work and that nothing has ever verified (the Phase-126 class of defect: an assumed harness idiom shipped as fact). With agent probes off the table this session, the design was made not to depend on the answer: `Bash(gh repo view:*)` now ships in the template allow-list *and* the loop subset (16 → 17 rules), so the primary path works under a restricted set; and the rule is deliberately **not** added to any skill's permission-guard required list, because a missing read-only probe must degrade per § B, never halt. The stale auto-approval assertions were reworded to stop claiming a classifier behavior nobody checked. `/report-issues` and `/contribute-convention` both ship in loop mode, so without the loop-subset entry the probe would have degraded to the fallback on every loop-mode run.

**Rider, verified independent of the above: a live Phase-128 miss in the same two skills.** `/report-issues` and `/share-wins` located the friction log at "`SYSOP_ISSUES.md` at the **consumer-repo root**". Phase 128 moved it to `sysop/SYSOP_ISSUES.md`; neither skill had been touched since before Phase 128 (`/report-issues` at `df35007`, Phase 99.1; `/share-wins` at `aff195b`, Phase 107), and the installer has seeded the vendor-dir path since. So on a post-128 full install, where the installer seeds the vendor-dir path, both skills instructed the agent to look somewhere the file is not — the likely outcome being "not present — nothing to report", a silent no-op (the skills are prose, so the failure is a strong tendency rather than a certainty; a diligent agent might have searched). In loop mode the log stays lazily created, so the same instruction merely pointed at the wrong place to create it — the same drift class as the round-4 cold read's `CONTRIBUTING.md:28` finding, one tree over and functional rather than cosmetic. Fixed at the locating instruction in both, with an explicit pre-128 fall-back so a consumer who has not re-run the installer keeps working, and guarded. Also fixed while in the same paragraphs: `/contribute-convention`'s consent reminder hardcoded "filed **publicly** on `<target>`", which becomes a false claim for exactly the consumer this config exists for.

**Docs.** `WORKFLOW.md` § 6.1 gains a required-sections row and a template block modelled on `## Merge policy`'s, stating the § 8.2c reason the config lives in `CLAUDE.md` at all. `docs/configuration.md` § "Behavior — `CLAUDE.md` prose" gains a two-row table for the two sections that are read as *configuration* rather than prose — previously that page named only `## Guided mode` as an example and never listed `## Merge policy` either.

**Gate.** +50 tests (1293 → 1343 collected) after the adversarial pass; full suite green at 1339 passed / 4 skipped. `tests/test_upstream_repo_config.py` pins the load-bearing wording: the three precedence tiers, the hard-stop-not-fallback rule, the never-assume-private fallback, the provenance markers, the not-a-filter property, the non-trigger rule for bare severity words, the consent-gate firing, the absence of any hardcoded public destination, the `/pr-dependabot` boundary (it operates on the consumer's own repo and must not grow an upstream target), and both halves of the friction-log path rider. The include-directive guard uses the same citation idiom `test_install_loop_mode.py` greps for when it checks that no loop skill *includes* an excluded partial — matching it keeps one idiom across both files. It does **not** gate shipping: loop mode ships `_shared/*` by an exclude list (`LOOP_EXCLUDE_SHARED`), so this partial ships regardless of how it is cited.

**Adversarial review (house practice — three independent fresh-context Opus reviewers, not forks; evidence-fidelity, completeness/coherence, and defeat-the-mechanism lenses). It earned its keep decisively: the build session had missed every finding, including two defects it had introduced *and then pinned with a passing test*.**

**The mechanism defects.** The sensitivity nudge's keyword list was **unbounded**, and the defeat reviewer measured it against the real GDP friction log rather than arguing about it: 6 of 10 entries fired, and 4 fired only because `RCE` matches *source*, *force*, and *porcelain* (`PHI` matches *graphics*; `PII` and `token` behave the same). The one true positive was indistinguishable from the noise — precisely the alarm fatigue the same section invoked three lines later to justify excluding bare `HIGH`/`CRITICAL`. Now bounded, with the false friends named concretely in the prose (an abstract "use word boundaries" reads as optional) and a mutation-verified guard. The completeness reviewer independently reached the same section from the other side: for `/contribute-convention --include-security` the corpus is a *security map*, whose subject **is** that vocabulary, so the keyword pass matches every item and warns about nothing. That corpus now gets a **substituted question** — generalization strips fingerprints, not subject matter, so scan for what survived it (real paths, hostnames, env var names, person or customer names, incident ids). Three further mechanism holes: **titles were never scanned** though the title is the most-read field and is composed separately; **`INTERNAL` was self-contradictory** (§ B said "no loud nudge", § C listed it as a trigger); and **near-miss headings failed open** — the exact-match rule made `## Upstream repo` or the rename-era `## Jig upstream repo` indistinguishable from *absent*, routing straight to the public default, so the hard-stop protected only an exact heading with a bad value.

**Two defects the build introduced and then pinned.** (1) `/contribute-convention`'s consent reminder previously said "filed **publicly**"; the rewrite dropped the word in the name of not hardcoding a destination — and the new `test_no_skill_hardcodes_a_public_destination` then *forbade restoring it*. On the default (public) path the skill warned **less** than before the phase. Fixed by putting the resolved visibility on the mandated target line (a healthy `[verified] PRIVATE` run and a degraded `[assumed] UNKNOWN` run were otherwise byte-identical on screen) and re-scoping the guard to require that line rather than merely forbidding the old wording. (2) The nudge was **ordered before its own input exists** in two skills — declared at Step 0.6, which runs before generalization (Step 4/6) and rendering (Step 2) — and `/report-issues` never got the Step 0.6 declaration at all, making the record's "fired at both ends in all three skills" false for the skill with the most sensitive corpus. Its guard passed anyway, because the skill's second "mention" was an inert Design-notes bullet. Step 0.6 is now an explicit forward pointer in all three; the guard anchors on the two *instruction* forms and asserts their order.

**False premises in the phase's own record, all three now corrected.** `[assumed]` was claimed as "the Phase-138 marker vocabulary" — it is not: `fanout-evidence.md`'s pair is `[verified]`/`[reported]`, and its `[verified]` means "I opened the cited `file:line`" where this one means "GitHub answered." The partial now states the borrowing (bracket-marker *convention*, not vocabulary) and the semantic collision, with a guard that fires if `fanout-evidence.md` ever adopts `[assumed]`. The loop-mode claim was two false clauses: `test_install_loop_mode.py` has no closure *detector* (only hardcoded sets), and loop mode ships `_shared/*` by an **exclude** list, so citation form never gated shipping. "Both skills were last touched at `df35007`" was true only of `/report-issues` (`/share-wins` is `aff195b`, Phase 107) — the conclusion survived, the cited evidence did not. "The first `_shared` partial in the give-back family" was false (all three already cite `permission-guard.md`). And the test counts were wrong in three places and in three directions — **1323 collected, 1319 passed / 4 skipped** as measured at the pass, with 1319 originally mislabelled as the collected count; the pass's own fixes then added the 20 guards that bring the shipped figure to the 1343/1339 the Gate paragraph states.

**Three guards were near-vacuous, each demonstrated by a surviving mutation** rather than asserted: the firing rule could be replaced with "nudge on every run" and stay green (the three state words survived elsewhere in the file); `/share-wins`' probe instruction could be deleted entirely (satisfied by the permission-guard paragraph naming the same command); and the fallback asymmetry — the thing this phase calls "the whole design" — could be **inverted** and stay green, because the guard asserted only the rationale phrase "Not a guess". All three are now scoped to the sentence that carries the property. The include-directive regex was also case-blind and matched none of the actual `Follow \`_shared/...\`` citations; it passed only via an unrelated sentence in the permission-guard paragraph.

**Doc drift, including one this phase caused.** `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.3 read "Nine partials are present" with ten on disk and this one unlisted — the same failure shape as the § 8.4 script table Phase 145 backfilled (an absent row looks exactly like a partial that doesn't exist), so it gets the same mechanical guard, both directions plus the count word. `install.sh`'s "57-rule allow-list" comment missed the 16 → 17 bump's fourth site and the full-mode count had no guard at all; `install.sh`'s `LOOP_EXCLUDE_SHARED` "Kept:" comment had been stale since Phase 138. `docs/configuration.md`'s "Two sections are read as configuration rather than prose" was contradicted two lines above it and by § 6.1's own tables. And the completeness reviewer caught a real hole: **loop mode ships two of the three give-back skills but deliberately does not ship `WORKFLOW.md`**, so § 6.1 — the config's only home — was unreadable to exactly the consumers who have the skills. `docs/loop-mode.md` now carries the config, and says `/share-wins` is full-mode only so the shipped partial's third skill isn't a dangling reference there.

**One finding routed to the checklist rather than fixed here, because it is not a code change.** The defeat reviewer verified that **GDP's installed skills predate this build** — `/report-issues --execute` there today still defaults to the public repo, and GDP's own `§ Sysop upstream repo` holds only because the model reads `CLAUDE.md`, not because the installed skill consults it. The fix is `sysop-update.sh` on GDP; the general question (does a *safety* property shipped as skill prose deserve a version assertion, an update nag, or an accepted-limitation note?) is filed with it.

**Not done, and stated rather than assumed.** The `gh repo view` auto-approval question is routed *around*, not answered — and the evidence reviewer noted the replacement prose ("the probe works under a restricted set") is itself an unverified prefix-matching claim, so one `claude-code-guide` probe should settle both and prune the rule if redundant. Filed. Inline close-out (meta-repo convention). GDP picks the feature up on its next `sysop-update.sh`; its existing section parses as-is, no consumer edit required. Mirror note: the new test file's docstring names GDP as the filing consumer — an accepted Pass-2 provenance class, not a Pass-1a leak, but it will show as a new site on the next cut's diff.

## Phase 148 (2026-07-25 — lock timestamps become content-anchored; a no-op install stops dirtying a clean consumer tree)

**Why this phase.** Found by the Codex-native integration evaluation, which ran the shipped installer through seven lifecycle cells against never-reused scratch consumers. Six matched their contracts exactly; cell D5 did not. A plain re-install and a `--update` over an already-current install both preserved link inodes, targets, and a deduplicated `managed_paths` — the *content* was right — but each still produced a working-tree diff, and the diff was nothing but a clock reading:

```diff
-  "installed_at": "2026-07-25T23:38:16Z",
-  "updated_at": "2026-07-25T23:38:16Z",
+  "installed_at": "2026-07-25T23:38:29Z",
+  "updated_at": "2026-07-25T23:38:29Z",
```

That is a small thing that behaves like a large one. A consumer who re-runs the installer to check they are current is handed a modified tracked file and a decide-or-revert; the documented `--update` flow ends with "do not auto-commit — leave it uncommitted so the consumer reviews", which is sound advice that becomes noise when the only thing to review is a timestamp. It also trains the exact reflex the flow depends on the consumer *not* having: commit the lock without reading the diff.

**The `installed_at` half was not a design tradeoff, it was code disagreeing with its own doc.** `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.2b has said since Phase 7 that downstream consumers should read `installed_at` as *"first time this lock existed," not "first time Sysop files landed"* — but `install.sh` wrote `write_lock_file "$now" "$now"` on every non-update path, so a re-install silently restarted it and the field meant "most recent plain install" instead. The `--update` path already preserved it correctly (it read the old value into a bash local first), which is why the divergence survived this long: the flow consumers use most had the right behavior, and only the re-install path — the one nobody runs deliberately — carried the bug.

**Resolution: anchor both stamps to lock content, in the serializer.** Rather than fix the one branch, both rules moved into `write_lock_file`'s Python heredoc, where they hold for every caller — plain install, `--update`, and `--adopt` alike — with no bash-side cooperation and no new call-site argument:

- `installed_at` — any readable existing lock's value is carried forward. Only a lock that is not there yet gets today's date. This is now true on the re-adopt recovery path too (Phase 125), which previously reset it.
- `updated_at` — advances only when some *other* field actually changed. A run that resolves to an identical lock rewrites it byte-for-byte.

The second rule is a real semantic choice and worth naming: `updated_at` now means "when this lock's content last changed", not "when the installer last ran". Nothing in the tree reads the field programmatically (only `WORKFLOW.md` documents it), and the content reading is the one that makes idempotence observable. Its one edge is honest and narrow: installing twice from a *dirty* source clone at the same commit produces identical lock fields with different file content, so the stamp holds — `sysop_commit` is the content anchor there, and it is already the field that would be wrong.

**A pre-existing crash surfaced by the tests, fixed here because it makes the new guard reachable.** The write path now parses any existing lock defensively. The read path did not: `lock_field()` called `json.load` unguarded and then `.get` on whatever came back, so a truncated or hand-mangled lock aborted the entire install with a raw `AttributeError` traceback — and did so *before* the new write-side guard could ever run, making that guard dead code for exactly the inputs it was written for. `lock_field()` now treats an unreadable or non-object lock the way the installer already treats an absent one: yield nothing, warn to stderr, let the callers' existing guards decide. That keeps `--update` fail-closed rather than loosening it — an empty `sysop_commit` still trips the ISSUE-0047 no-anchor check (Phase 125) instead of silently overwriting managed paths.

**Gate.** +15 tests (1343 → 1358 collected; 1354 passed / 4 skipped, full suite green). `tests/test_install_lock_timestamps.py` **mutation-verified against the pre-fix installer**: 9 of the 15 fail on `HEAD~`, and the 6 that pass in both states are the ones deliberately written to (fresh install stamping, `--update` preserving `installed_at` via the bash path that already worked, and both `updated_at`-advances cases). Preservation is pinned in both directions on purpose — a serializer that simply froze `updated_at` would satisfy a preservation-only suite while making the field meaningless, so every hold assertion is paired with a change assertion. Timestamps are forced to a 2020 sentinel rather than slept past, because `iso_now` has one-second granularity and a same-second re-run would let the pre-fix behavior pass by luck.

**Rider filed, not fixed.** Writing the fixture surfaced that `ensure_runtime_gitignore()` covers `sysop/runtime/` but not `sysop/scripts/__pycache__/`, so a consumer whose repo does not already ignore bytecode commits Sysop's `.pyc` files and then gets a dirty tree from every install *and* every `run_checks.sh` — the same friction class this phase closes, one directory over. Independently corroborated by the evaluation's own transcripts, where a session spent a command restoring "tracked Python bytecode cache files" it had just dirtied. Filed to the checklist; the test fixture ships the ordinary `__pycache__/` ignore a real Python consumer has, so it measures the lock property rather than that one.

**Close-out.** Inline (meta-repo convention). Docs: `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.2b step 8 and the adopt paragraph both state the content-anchored rule. No consumer action required — the next `sysop-update.sh` picks it up, and an existing lock's `installed_at` is preserved from that run forward rather than corrected retroactively (the original install date is not recoverable, which § 8.2b already tells readers).
