## Phase 160 (executed 2026-07-28 — the pre-push bundle: the leak gate that only existed at cut time, plus doc currency for Phases 147–159b)

**Why this phase.** The public mirror sat at Phase 146 (`f684224`, snapshot of private `8621f5f`, pushed 2026-07-24) while `main` had reached 159b — 37 commits, Phases 147–159b (13 phase numbers, 14 log entries: 159 shipped as `a` and `b`), 13,917 added lines, and six fixes to defects a public installer gets today (150 hooks, 151 `pr`-policy, 152 permissions, 156 batch lock, 157 failed-closes-as-done, 158 diff basis). The question asked was whether to build more before pushing. The answer was to push, after two things: a leak-gate violation, and a doc-currency pass.

**The gate was real, but it only existed at cut time.** `tools/make_public_mirror.sh` *prints* three MUST-be-empty greps (Passes 1a/1b/1c); `tools/cut_public_release.sh` reuses that builder and runs the same three as **blocking `hard()` checks**. So the checks do gate a push — what they never did was run between pushes. Nothing in `tests/`, the pre-scan or `/review-close` had ever looked at them, so for the entire span between two cuts a blocked identifier could sit in a shipping file with the tree green. (An earlier draft of this entry said "printing was the entire enforcement." That was false, the round caught it, and the correction matters because it relocates the defect from *no gate* to *no gate between cuts* — and because the enforcing copy needed the same fix the printed one got.)

- **Pass 1c.** Phase 149 named the leg-5 dogfood target in `PHASE_LOG.md`, which ships. It sat there three days across eleven subsequent phases (150–159b) and their adversarial rounds. The de-identified vocabulary it should have used was established by Phase 130, whose heading names *the dogfood-naming mirror gate*.
- **Pass 1a, and this one is already public.** `PHASE_LOG.md:1121` has carried a blocked internal identifier — the extraction source's client name — since the 2026-07-13 public cut, and **every cut since reported Pass 1a clean**. Both scripts filtered with `grep -vi 'wade@gdpquery.ai'`, which drops the whole *line*, so any line carrying the one allowlisted public address was invisible to every other Pass-1a identifier. Reproduced against the published tree both ways: the old pipeline returns empty, the token-scoped one returns the leak.

**The fix.** `tests/test_mirror_leak_gate.py` (+13) runs all three passes over the exact shipped file set — `git ls-files` minus the mirror's own exclusion list — on every phase, with the allowlist narrowed from line-scoped to **token-scoped**, which is the single change that surfaced the live leak. Both scripts were corrected to the token-scoped form, `cut_public_release.sh` included: it is the copy that actually blocks a push, and fixing only the printed one would have left the enforcing one broken.

**Most of that file is positive controls, and the round is why.** The first version was all negative assertions — `assert not hits` over a tree expected to be clean — which passes *exactly as well when the scanner is broken as when the tree is clean*. The guard-binding reviewer ran 29 mutations against it and **22 survived**: empty the file list, return no hits, read only the first line of each file, delete a pattern, widen an exclusion to `*` — all green, against clean trees and against planted canaries alike. That is this repo's recurring decorative-guard failure (Phases 155–159b), reproduced inside the guard written to fix a different instance of the same thing. The module now plants a canary for every leak shape and asserts each is **found**, plus a negative control that the allowlisted address alone is not a leak. Three further holes the same reviewer demonstrated end-to-end are closed: `fnmatch`'s `*` crosses `/` while the shell's `rm -f "$TARGET"/*_HANDOFF.md` does not, so a nested `docs/internal/X_HANDOFF.md` shipped *and* was excluded from the scan; `git ls-files` was split on whitespace, so a tracked path containing a space was silently skipped; and the scan was content-only, so an embargoed name in a *filename* — publicly visible in the URL — was invisible. The pattern drift guard was itself vacuous for three tokens, satisfied by their appearance in *comment prose* this very phase had added, and now reads only lines that actually run a grep.

Guards, all mutation-checked: the exclusion set must match what the builder removes; the scanned set must still contain a representative file from every shipped area (the widening direction the script-reading guard structurally cannot see); the pattern list must match **both** scripts; neither script may revert to the line-scoped filter; all three passes must stay wired to `cut_public_release.sh`'s blocking `hard()` (a pass rewired to a non-blocking call keeps its grep and reads exactly like a working gate); and every shipped file must be readable, failing with one named file rather than three tracebacks.

**Remediation decision (Wade, at the gate): scrub the tree, leave the history.** The name is gone from the live files at the next push; it remains in the public repo's snapshot history, which would cost a force-push of a protected public repo to remove. Recorded because a future reader will find it in `git log` and should know it was a decision.

**The round found the guard red on arrival, and the mechanism is worth keeping.** The first commit of this phase (`3b34222`) shipped **three of its own six tests failing**, and the `**Gate.** 1802 passed` line in that commit's record was false. Cause: `_shipped_files()` reads `git ls-files`, so while the new test file was untracked it was excluded from its own scan; `git add` put it in, and its pattern literals — which it must contain — trip all three passes. The pre-commit verification ran in the one window where the file was invisible to itself. **Two things follow, and the second is the real one.** First, the file is now excluded from the mirror and from the scan, which is correct on its own terms: it guards *this repo's publication process*, which no consumer has, and shipping it would put every blocked identifier in the public tree permanently and make the cut-time greps report hits forever — the phase had otherwise been about to replace two scrubbed leaks with two fresh ones in a newly-shipped file. Second, the honest reading is that **the guard behaved correctly and the verification around it did not** — a new file is invisible to this scan until the commit that adds it, which is exactly the class of failure the rest of this phase is about, landing on the phase's own headline artifact. That limit is now stated in the module docstring rather than discovered again.

**Doc currency — eight shipped docs, three audits, and the agents were not taken at their word.** Three fresh-context `general-purpose` agents ran read-only in parallel: one digesting 147–159b for consumer-visible surfaces, one auditing the monograph, one auditing the public markdown. Every load-bearing finding was re-verified against the tree, and **two did not survive**: an audit claimed ≥16 skills consume `permission-guard.md` (15 — `/review-close` was already inside its own grep), and one reported the wrong direction on Phase 158's mutation score. Shipped:

- **Four false monograph claims. All four date to the file's original commit (`1d38b49`, 2026-05-22)**, so all four predate the last snapshot and have been live on the public site since the cut on 2026-07-13 — fifteen days publicly, not the "months" an earlier draft claimed. `/next-task` described as sorted by effort (unblocker-first since Phase 74, with a collision tier ahead of that since 103); the convention-map pre-implementation read attributed to `/claim-task` Step 2 (it is Step 6 — Step 2 reads neither map); `/claim-task` credited with running the adversarial review (the sub-agent does); and Fig. 6's *"fall back to regex if race lost"* (retired in Phase 54 — the parser says so four screens from the figure that contradicted it). The same retired race framing was found still live at `claim-task/SKILL.md:562` and fixed there too.
- **`WORKFLOW.md`:** pre-scan documented as five stages when coverage runs in the same `main()` — six, with (f) written out; `permission-guard.md` "consumed by 8 skills" → 15, with the four explicit non-consumers characterized individually (`/roadmap` does shell out and *deliberately declines the hard stop*, which the first draft of this fix got wrong by asserting all fifteen were "every skill that shells out"); `--entry-state` added to § 4.3 incl. the closed-wins-over-a-stale-lock precedence; `## Post-deploy verification` and `## Pending documentation routing` added to § 6.1; `adversarial-review.md`'s § *Running more than one reviewer* named in § 8.3.
- **`WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md`, the stalest shipping doc:** its "most recent addition is Phase 59" claim replaced with a list that says outright it will date; `## Merge policy` — absent from the file entirely — added to the Merge Process; both claim kinds' locks and both `--release` paths; the give-back skills' hardcoded "the Sysop repo" replaced with the resolved target; `SYSOP_ISSUES.md` → `sysop/SYSOP_ISSUES.md`.
- **`configuration.md`:** `## Pre-merge verification` was listed as a section the review/audit skills read — it is a `/review-close` input; plus the two missing config sections.
- **`README.md` + `install-and-update.md`:** the review-batch un-claim (`batch_work.sh --release`). It was documented in `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.4 all along — an earlier draft of this entry claimed "zero mentions in any public doc", which the round falsified; the true gap was README, `install-and-update.md` and `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md`, i.e. every surface a consumer reads before the spec. README's removal recipe also omitted the two `.agents/` symlinks its own quickstart stages.
- **`getting-started.md`:** where `/report-issues` actually files, and the entry-state check. **`history.md`:** the test count.
- **Monograph currency:** stamps 146 → 159 at all three sites plus the masthead date, which had contradicted the colophon by seventeen days; `round-receipts/` added to the runtime tree and to `self_check.sh`'s attribution; the envelope filename's phase key; the `BATCH-<N>.lock`; `/auto-judge`'s `> Failed:`; merge policy in the `/review-close` entry; a give-back-targeting clause in § *The differentiator*.

**Three argument-level additions.** § III enumerated four shapes of *a review that didn't run looking like one that found nothing*; it now has a fifth — the round gate that failed three times, twice by **firing correctly** and then waiting for permission it had already been given, which is why the fix was authority rather than a reminder. § III also gains the Tier-0 coverage ledger, the tier that exists because Tier 1 and Tier 2 both measure work *inside* the dispatch path, so a round that never dispatched produces a *cleaner*-looking provenance split than an honest one. And § I's *"the record is verified, not trusted"* now carries what it doesn't buy: six consecutive phase records where independent reviewers found the phase's own new guards weaker than it had just claimed (41 of 53 surviving; 28 of a reviewer's 83 against a build reporting 33 of 33 killed; 32 of 80; 28 across two reviewers' 67 with 22 of 32 tests still passing against blanked files), with the transferable finding that an author-chosen mutation set measures the author's model of the code, not the tests.

**A record falsehood caught in passing, in the always-loaded file.** `CLAUDE.md`'s Phase 158 row read "killed 28 of 43 mutations". `PHASE_LOG.md` says 43 + 24 were run and **28 survived**. Corrected.

**Round.** Commit `3b34222`, three independent fresh-context `general-purpose` reviewers in isolated worktrees, each given the SHA, told to reach it via `git show <sha>:<path>`, and required to open its report with the SHA it actually read — the practice Phase 159a's round filed, applied here for the first time; all three echoed the correct SHA. Lenses: claim verification, guard binding, record truth. **It is the most consequential round this project has run, and it did not merely find defects in the work — it found the work's headline artifact non-binding and its record false about its own result.**

- **The commit was red.** Three of its six tests failed at `3b34222`, and the `**Gate.** 1802 passed` line in that commit's record was false. Two reviewers found this independently.
- **The guard did not bind.** 22 of 29 mutations survived (above).
- **`cut_public_release.sh` runs the passes as blocking checks** with the unfixed line-scoped filter — falsifying this entry's original "printing was the entire enforcement" framing *and* leaving the copy that actually stops a push broken. This phase would have "fixed" the gate while the real gate stayed broken.
- **Record falsehoods killed, all mine:** `batch_work.sh --release` "zero mentions in any public doc" (it is documented in `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.4; the true gap was the three surfaces a consumer reads first); "publicly wrong for months" (fifteen days publicly); "three of four predate the snapshot" (all four do); "four subsequent phases" (eleven shipped); "read clean at four consecutive cuts" — an unverified number I had already written into a shipped script comment; a "seventh check" that was the sixth; and a justification for the undecodable-file check that described a silent skip the code does not perform.
- **Three undisclosed changes** this entry had omitted from its own file list, including a whole argument-level monograph addition and `docs/history.md`.

Every finding was re-verified against the tree before being applied; none was taken on a reviewer's word, and one claim from an earlier audit (`permission-guard.md` "≥16 skills") did not survive that check. Reported per convention as **survivors**: `tools/phase160_mutations.py` is committed so the number is checkable by someone else — **20 mutations, 0 survivors**, the set derived from the reviewer's findings rather than author-chosen, which is the property Phases 159a and 159b established as the one that matters. 0 survivors means *these* are killed, not that the guard is complete.

**Gate.** 1809 passed, 4 skipped. All three leak passes empty over a **reconstructed snapshot** (tracked files minus the mirror's exclusions), not merely over the working tree. Monograph tag balance verified unchanged against `HEAD` rather than in the absolute. Both scripts syntax-checked; the printed Pass 1a pipeline was run verbatim against a built mirror by a reviewer and behaves.

**Mirror-cut follow-up (2026-07-29) — the cut found a defect the phase could not have.** Running `cut_public_release.sh` for the Phase-160 push turned up two things no amount of dev-tree testing would have. **(1) The sterilized tree failed three tests.** `tests/test_adversarial_review_gate.py` (Phase 154) reads `CLAUDE.md`, which the mirror deliberately removes, so it `FileNotFoundError`-ed rather than skipping — and since public `main` requires the `pytest` check, **the snapshot PR would have gone red on CI**. Unseen until now because Phase 154 landed two days after the last cut and nothing runs the suite against the sterilized tree except a cut. Fixed at the single read site with an explicit, reasoned `pytest.skip`, not a blanket exclusion: most of that module guards the shipped `_shared/adversarial-review.md` and must keep running for consumers (dev tree still 12 passed / 0 skipped). The general form — *any test asserting on a mirror-excluded path is invisible until a cut, and the feedback arrives in public* — is filed in § Medium. **(2) The rename-residue check went red on three intentional back-compat sites** (`_shared/upstream-repo.md:38-39` and its drift guard), where Phase 147 names the pre-rename spellings so a consumer whose heading is one word off is caught rather than silently defaulted to the *public* repo. Verified at the cut: five residue lines total, all intentional, **zero genuine missed renames**. The gate did its job — it surfaced new residue for a human — and Wade ratified pushing on that verified basis with the exemption filed (§ Low) rather than weakening the check under push pressure. Everything else was green: Passes 1a/1b/1c/3/4 empty, **Pass 2 zero new provenance sites**, Pass 2b five new BeanRider lines across five files (the "191 vs ~125" gap is the stale ratification-era baseline the script itself warns rots, not a swing).

**Mirror push (2026-07-29 — Phases 147–160 shipped).** First public/tester refresh since `f684224` (Phase 146); the snapshot of `ade2e1e` carries fourteen phases, the largest inter-cut delta the project has had. Public `2294456` via `getsysop/sysop` PR #22 (required `pytest` check green in 6m43s); tester `e207d4c` force-pushed to `wade-cms/sysop-tester` after confirming the repo is still **private**. Full gate on the exact pushed tree: Passes 1a/1b/1c/3/4 empty; **Pass 2 zero new provenance sites** against the published tree and Pass 2b five; sterilized-tree suite **1771 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed**; Pages rebuilt, `getsysop.com` and `/workflow.html` both 200, and the live monograph verified to carry the Phase-159 stamps with both corrected claims gone. **The cut went red twice before it went green and both were real**, which is the argument for running it rather than trusting the dev tree: the sterilized tree failed three tests that would have reddened the public PR's own required check (fixed in #261 — a test asserting on a mirror-excluded file), and the rename-residue check flagged three intentional back-compat sites, verified as zero genuine missed renames and pushed on that basis with the exemption filed rather than the check weakened under push pressure.

## Phase 161 (executed 2026-07-29 — the doc-truth pass: a five-lens audit of every public surface, and the fixes for what it verified false)

**Why this phase.** The Phase-160 doc-currency pass had fixed *staleness*; Wade asked for the complementary question — is anything **misrepresented**, and does the story have gaps — plus a positioning check: Sysop should read as a Claude Code tool first, with Codex support present but not the focus. Five independent fresh-context `general-purpose` auditors ran read-only in parallel, one lens each: public-markdown accuracy (README + the seven `docs/*.md` pages, ~90 claims checked against the tree), monograph + landing page (both files read in full), a cold-reader narrative pass over the whole funnel, a Codex/portability positioning sweep over every shipped surface, and WORKFLOW.md/WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md spec accuracy. Every load-bearing finding was re-verified against the tree before being acted on — none was taken on an auditor's word.

**The positioning verdict first, because it changes no files: the Codex story needed no demotion.** The sweep classified every portability/Codex mention on every shipped surface and found **zero overclaims and zero misweighted placements** — the landing hero says "Claude Code," Codex is never named on the landing page, README mentions it only under "Probably not for you," and the monograph's "one step is not a track record" section is the model paragraph. No public surface promises the gated `using-with-other-agents.md` or capability table. `install.sh`'s codex-links behavior matches its docs on every load-bearing point. What the sweep did find was **missing caveats**, fixed below.

**Three false monograph claims, live on the public site (all verified before fixing) — the first two since the 2026-07-13 cut; the third entered the file at Phase 146 and has been public since that snapshot's 2026-07-24 push (`git log -S`; this phase's own round corrected an earlier all-three-since-the-cut blanket here, and the phase's commit message still carries the uncorrected form):**

- **The centerpiece attributed the loop to the wrong skill.** The § IV lede and Fig. 5's top node said findings from `/review-close` get promoted — the retired promote-at-merge design (`WORKFLOW.md:352`: "Convention promotion is NOT a `/review-close` step"; `review-close/SKILL.md:930` carries the removal comment). The file even contradicted itself — § III and the landing page both had it right. Lede and node now name `/codebase-review` / `/security-audit` (whose Step 9 owns promotion), and the lede's "promoted into the relevant *pack's* map" also became "the *project's* map" (pack promotion is the separate downstream step the adjacent pullquote already described correctly).
- **A labeled excerpt was fabricated.** § "What's in a map entry" showed a listing labeled `excerpt · packs/python/companion/convention_map.md` whose four bullets exist nowhere in that file, in a format the file doesn't use, carrying "(Round N)" tags no shipped map has (`grep -rn "(Round" packs/*/companion/convention_map.md` → 0). The claim it illustrated is true of the *consumer's own* map — the recurrence gate reads round-attributed local entries (`codebase-review/SKILL.md:954`) — so the rewrite relocates the round-attribution story to that layer and replaces the listing with a genuinely verbatim, elision-marked excerpt (the CLI-scripts section: env-var validation, logger formatting, YAML safe-load, and the `> AST-backed equivalents:` line). Same false-premise class Phases 120/137 fixed elsewhere; the monograph never got that fix.
- **"No shipped security check is blocking" was false.** `grant-sensitive-table` (postgres, **critical**) and `window-open-noopener` (nextjs-react, medium) are `category: security` + `blocking: true`. The narrower claim the argument needed is true — every shipped *semgrep* check is advisory, and the crashed stage that motivated the passage was semgrep — so the sentence now says that, with the three blocking grep checks named. The same false clause sat in this file's own Phase-135 record (its "Blocking semantics" paragraph) beside its correct half ("three pack grep checks ship `blocking: true`"); corrected there with a dated note rather than silently.

Also in the monograph: the `/sitrep`+`/next-task` glossary entry claimed the `disallowed-tools` guard means "neither can mutate state even when asked" — the surviving instance of the overclaim class Phase 137 fixed, contradicted by both skills' own frontmatter notes; now states the partial-by-design truth. Plus the LOWs: hero "Issue 86" (a currency marker abandoned at Phase 86 while the colophon advanced to 159 — realigned), "78 conventions across two codebases" (the dataset attributes all of it to one project), Fig. 7's March label unified to 11% (data: 10.5%; the landing chart already rounded half-up), and the bash-installer card's "works with any agent" scoped to the installer/companion layer, deferring to the named-limits section below it — that section gained an `id`, and it is the *landing page's* new phrasing that carries the actual link.

**WORKFLOW.md was still documenting three retired behaviors** — the worst class, since §1 tells non-Claude agents the spec is the design source of truth:

- **The pending-docs schema was pre-Phase-23a** at all three sites (`task_ids:` in §2.4, §6.6, and the routing table) while `/document-work` writes `roadmap_ids:`/`review_task_ids:` and `/review-close` reads `task_ids` only through a compat shim slated for removal — the spec contradicted its own guide (WORKFLOW_GUIDE had the rename). Both schema blocks now carry the two-namespace fields, §6.6 gains the namespace semantics paragraph (including "do not author the legacy key"), and the Roadmap column left the routing table entirely: **the round-trip is type-independent** (`review-close/SKILL.md:819`), and the table's `feature`/`infrastructure`-only reading was exactly the pre-fix behavior of BeanRider ISSUE-0034 — documented as the design. §2.8 step 7 fixed to match.
- **"`validate_tasks.py` enforces schema invariants on every commit"** (two verbatim sites, plus §8.4's same-claim "Runs from pre-commit" row) — nothing shipped wires it into commits: the shipped pre-commit is a skeleton whose active code computes file lists and evaluates flags no check ever sets, the wiring exists only in `git-hooks/examples/`, and `install.sh`'s copy loop (`[[ -f "$f" ]] || continue`) never delivers that directory to any consumer. All five claim/pointer sites rewritten to on-demand + opt-in-wiring, with the examples located honestly in the Sysop source repo. Whether `examples/` *should* ship is now a filed decision (§ Low), not an accident.

WORKFLOW.md LOWs: two leftover four-stage pre-scan lists (Phase 160 fixed the others), the `disallowed-tools` inventory (2 skills → the current 5), §2.6 cross-reference numbering unified to the condensed list, the literal-`frontend/` PATH-prepend nuance stated, and the repointed-Codex-link "reported" claim narrowed to the `--update` path (the plain re-install opt-out skips silently — verified at `install.sh:2137` vs `:4719`).

**The markdown funnel was nearly clean** — README, packs, and history verified accuracy-clean, and getting-started passed the accuracy lens too (its portability *staleness* was the positioning sweep's catch — fixed below); the survivors, fixed: `install-and-update.md:109`'s "`/sysop:pr-dependabot` — the only skill that shells out to `gh`" (a Phase-53 fossil; **seven** skills invoke `gh`, and the sentence sits where a consumer audits GitHub egress); `one-rule.md`'s "through Round 74" now reconciles itself with the "71 rounds" every other surface counts (both true — numbering runs to 74, 71 rounds on record, per `docs/analysis/REPORT.md`) and its "check it yourself" pointer moved to `grep.py:190` where the nosemgrep suppression actually lives; `loop-mode.md`'s "one of two shapes" heading a three-bullet list; `configuration.md`'s `best` one-key aside (only `fable` is truly one-key — anything else must also be listed under `served:`).

**The Codex caveats, both halves of the filed §72(b) doc fix:** `install-and-update.md § Codex` now states where the default `workspace-write` sandbox stops the loop (the round writes findings, the commit is denied; `danger-full-access` closes it and is appropriate only in an already-isolated environment — the honesty the checklist entry ratified on 2026-07-25 and the docs never shipped), plus the open-acceptance-run disclosure. `_shared/permission-guard.md` now opens with a Claude-Code-only scoping paragraph telling other harnesses to skip the guard entirely (four of five Codex eval sessions had burned commands reading a file that binds nothing there). `getting-started.md`'s portability section — stale in both directions (said "still being validated" after the measurement; omitted the refusal) — now carries the measured named-limits summary, and the landing page's one unqualified portability phrase links to the monograph's named-limits section.

**What was deliberately not fixed:** the cold-read audit's editorial findings — undefined "round"/"baseline", the keep-the-clone gap, the review-batch claiming gap, the demotion evidence dead-end, and six lesser story items — need Wade's editorial voice and pair with announce copy; filed as one § Medium bundle with file:line coordinates rather than absorbed into this phase's scope.

**Two process notes the record should keep.** The audit's own cross-checking caught one finding before it shipped: the cold-reader flagged 71-vs-74 as a *contradiction*; the accuracy auditor's `REPORT.md` check downgraded it to *both-true-but-unreconciled*, which is what got fixed. And the build session caught itself mid-phase: the first draft of the one-rule reconciliation asserted the numbering gap came from "skipped numbers" — a cause the report doesn't state — and was retracted to the bare verified fact before commit. Same class as the round-attribution excerpt, one keystroke from shipping another one.

**Round.** Commit `e644ff5`, three independent fresh-context `general-purpose` reviewers in isolated worktrees, each given the SHA, told to read via `git show <sha>:<path>`, and required to open with the SHA reviewed — all three echoed it correctly. Lenses: claim verification, record truth, regression/coherence. Every surviving finding below was re-verified against the tree before being applied.

- **The claim lens found the phase's own new text overclaiming, 1 MEDIUM + 4 LOW.** The MEDIUM: the new blocking-checks parenthetical said a dead grep stage "on an install carrying those packs" would trip the gate — false, because all three blocking grep checks ship placeholder `paths:` and `grep.py:70` returns `SKIPPED (paths-unresolved)` before grep runs, while the gate keys on `FAILED` only; the sentence now carries the localized-install qualifier its own sibling PHASE_LOG correction had already stated. The LOWs, all fixed: the Phase-135 correction's "under *either* rule" half did not survive its own corrected premise (under the withdrawn draft rule the skipped blocking security checks are exactly what would have tripped); the §2.6 bundling parenthetical was off by one (item 5 bundles shared steps 6–9, not 5–9); the `configuration.md` caveat universalized falsely (local `served:` *extends* the default list, so `sonnet` alone passes); and `getting-started.md` attributed to "the two review skills" jointly what the ratified record attributes to a frontier *stack*.

All four fixed. It also caught Fig. 5's *central node* still labeling the promotion target as the shipped per-pack maps — contradicting the very lede this phase corrected, and hosting the tree's last round-attribution-over-pack-maps claim via node 4; the sublabels now say "your project's map · base + .project overlay". Two shipped skills (`auto-fix`, `auto-judge`) were found *authoring* the legacy `task_ids:` key the phase's new §6.6 text forbids — both now emit the modern two-key frontmatter (empty lists, behavior-identical through the shim). The corrected false blocking clause also survived verbatim in `tools/PRESCAN_ACCOUNTING_SPEC.md` (mirror-excluded but false; corrected with a dated note), plus: a "both skills" antecedent orphaned by the five-skill inventory fix, the shipped `pre-commit` hook's own comment pointing at the never-installed `examples/` path, a leftover *three*-stage pre-scan list at §2.5's Outputs block, and the Fig. 5 node-1 font-size override risking rect overflow (reverted to the default, which fits).

Corrected in the entry; **the phase's own commit message (`e644ff5`) carries the uncorrected form**, noted here rather than rewritten. Also fixed: two coordinate sets the phase's *own insertions* had shifted (`WORKFLOW.md:351`→`:352`; the checklist bundle's `install-and-update.md:241,255`→`:243,257` — the § Codex paragraph moved them); a mislocated correction-site label (main Phase-135 record, not its follow-up); the § Low entry's "four examples files" miscount (the directory holds four; WORKFLOW.md referenced two); two overstated fix descriptions ("now name … Step 9" — the shipped text names the skills, not the step; "with a link to the named-limits section" — the card has no link, the landing page does); an internal accuracy-clean/stale-in-both-directions tension on getting-started; a circular "full findings" pointer promising a record that does not exist; and two precision errors ("three sites" → two verbatim plus a same-claim row; "all eight `docs/*.md`" → seven).
