Rule 3 ran four ways: a real `install.sh` round-trip into a scratch repo (the `[''"]` YAML survives assembly byte-for-byte, and the installed registry fires on both styles with a live waiver), semgrep executed against a two-style fixture, the corpus measurement above, and a permanent test section that loads the **shipped** fragments and runs the real `run_check` rather than a retyped pattern.

Rule 1 ran 40 mutations — **4 of them reverts, labelled as such so they cannot pad the number** — plus 7 negative controls. **The first run reported 7 survivors, and two were real defects in my own guards.** The predicate's positive controls never exercised its escaped-quote branch, so `\"` could stop being flagged with the suite green. Worse, the executable section asserted on **line numbers**: gut the fixture's single-quoted forms and every `":2" in hits` still passed, because line 2 still existed and still matched in the *other* style — a fixture-vacuity of exactly the kind rule 3's own sub-rule warns about, in the tests written to satisfy rule 3. Both fixed: the assertions now read the matched source line, and a vacuity twin asserts the fixture carries both styles of every form.

The other five survivors were mutations I had written badly, and saying so is the point: three were inert (loosening the id regex to `*` still returns an empty group, which the `if part.strip()` filter drops) and **two were incoherent — I had mutated a test's own assertion to `pass`, which can only ever make a suite greener.** Deleting an assertion is not a mutation. They are replaced with mutations of the *subject*: a still-quote-agnostic pattern that drops a keyword (tests the zero-lost half) and a single-quote-only one (tests the widening half).

**Then the harness turned out to have been lying in both directions.** Several mutations here swap `'` for `"`, which leaves the file **byte-identical in length**. pytest keys its assertion-rewrite cache on `(mtime, size)`, so a restore landing in the same mtime granularity as the mutation makes the next run import the *mutated* module out of `tests/__pycache__`. The second run reported **40/40 killed and 7/7 negative controls red** — which is not a strong result, it is the signature of a baseline that was never green. `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` plus an explicit `__pycache__` rmtree fixes it, and the fix is documented in the harness because the trap is general: **any mutation that preserves file length can be invisible to pytest.** Final, trustworthy: **40 mutations / 0 survivors, 7 negative controls / 0 false alarms.** The controls are there because Phase 170's round caught a guard reddening on a legitimate rewrite — a new quote-free check, a new both-quotes check, a backtick pattern, a negated class, a notes reflow, a rename and a longer waiver rationale all stay green.

**Rule 2 found three defects in prose I had just written, all in the same paragraph-sized diff.** The `notes:` field claimed lowercase and multi-line SQL are "semgrep-sql-fstring's job" — but that rule's patterns are `$CONN.execute(f"...")` and `$CONN.execute(sqlalchemy.text(f"..."))`, so it covers only f-strings passed **straight to execute()**; one bound to a variable first is this check's alone, and the note now says so. The `WORKFLOW.md` waiver example used `_psql`, an identifier carried over from the corpus I had just been reading — a GDP leak in shipped content, in a phase whose own diff is three lines of YAML. And the same section cited `tests/test_check_pattern_quotes.py` bare, in a **consumer-facing** doc where that path does not exist; the house form (`WORKFLOW.md:1855`) qualifies such references as not shipped, and it now does.

**Suite: 2114 → 2165 passed + 4 skipped**, read off a run rather than derived from a count of what I added (Phase 171 wrote a derived number three times in one phase, twice in sentences about measuring). +51 across the two new modules.

### Phase 172's adversarial round

Three fresh-context reviewers, worktree-isolated, anchored to `a5a9368`, on distinct lenses — *does it execute* / *are its claims true* / *are its guards real* — with **one on a different model**, which `_shared/adversarial-review.md:29` requires and Phase 171's nine reviewers all violated.

**The claims lens found nothing live, and that is worth stating precisely rather than as a pass.** It re-derived every number independently against the same corpus — 21 → 33, 4 → 5, 123 → 182 with 59 single-quoted-only and no file using both styles; exactly three `metavariable-regex` uses across all shipped semgrep rules, all over identifiers; `semgrep-sql-fstring`'s `pattern-either` requiring a literal f-string at the call site — and enumerated the fragment population itself rather than trusting mine. Its one finding, the unqualified `tests/…` citation in shipped `WORKFLOW.md`, was **read off the intermediate commit**: rule 2 of the author-side pass had already fixed it at the tip, verified by `git show a5a9368:…`. A clean lens is weak information, not a ratification.

**The execution lens found two live defects in the waiver, and both were mine.**

**HIGH — "a bare `no-check:` waives nothing" was false on the file-level path.** `\s` matches newlines, and an `invert_file_check` check hands `waived_ids` the **whole file**, so a bare marker swallowed the next identifier-shaped token further down and waived whatever it happened to spell: `waived_ids("# no-check:\nimport os")` returned `{'import'}`. That falsified the rule in three places at once — the code comment, the shipped `WORKFLOW.md` bullet, and the test module's own docstring — and **both bare-marker tests were single-line**, so the one corner that breaks was the one corner untested. It is *latent* rather than live today (both shipped file-level checks are `*.ts`/`*.tsx`, so nothing hands the parser a `.md` or `.py` file), and it is fixed anyway: the marker is matched per line, with horizontal whitespace only, and `\b`-anchored so `xno-check:` is no longer a marker.

**MEDIUM — `--update-baseline` counted waivers in the header and printed none.** The `[waived]` loop existed only in `main()`. So the never-silent promise held on the ordinary run and broke on the one path a maintainer audits suppressions from. Also from that lens, and taken: **case-sensitivity was unspecified** — mutating the marker to `(?i)` survived all 51 tests — now decided (case-sensitive, like `# nosemgrep` / `# noqa`) and pinned.

Its remaining LOW findings were verified and dispositioned rather than absorbed. The `negative_pattern` short-hit branch really cannot be waived, and is unreachable defensive code for `grep -rn` output that has no second colon. Ids containing anything outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` really are unwaivable, and widening the class would eat the rationale (`no-check: x. Next` → `x.`) — so the constraint is documented instead. And **shipped files carrying live marker tokens is a real property with no "example" state**: the sweep found `WORKFLOW.md` (deliberate — a doc that teaches the marker wants real ids) and, accidentally, `grep.py` itself, where my own comment had minted a live waiver for a check called `x`. That one is now a placeholder, and the known set is pinned by a test so the day a file-level check covers `.md` or `.py`, the diff says so.

**Two corrections to my own mutation numbers, both in the direction of inflation.** The first "remove both cross-line defenses" mutation **survived and proved nothing** — it edited only the regex, while the per-line scan lives inside the function body, so it never removed the second defense. Re-anchored on the whole parser block, it kills. Then I labelled the two single-defense mutations *equivalent* and moved them out of the survivor column — and **one of them was not equivalent, only uncovered**: `\s` additionally accepts NBSP, vertical tab and form feed, which is a real behaviour change, and "declared equivalent" would have been *merely unattempted* wearing a residual's label. It is pinned by tests and graded. Removing the per-line scan alone genuinely is equivalent (`[ \t]` and the id class both exclude `\n`, so whole-text `finditer` finds exactly the per-line matches), and the harness reports that one apart rather than in either column.

**Final battery: 46 mutations = 45 graded (4 of them reverts) + 1 declared-equivalent, 0 survivors; 7 negative controls, 0 false alarms.**

**The guards lens is the one that earned the round, and it is the third phase running where an independent battery beats the author's.** It wrote 46 mutations of its own and **watched 38 survive**, against my 46/0 — and **3 of its 4 negative controls went red**, which is the direction I had been congratulating myself on covering.

**Its sharpest finding killed my predicate outright.** `bare_quote_literals` was a hand-rolled bracket scanner that recognised quote-agnosticism *only* when written as one character class holding both quotes. It therefore reported **false positives on four correct idioms** — `(?:"|')(SELECT)`, `[[:alnum:]"']` (it exited the bracket at the `]` closing `[:alnum:]`, so both quotes read as outside any class), `f["](S)|f['](S)`, and `("|')prod\1` — all verified by running it. A maintainer writing any of them is blocked by the guard, and the documented escape hatch **reddened its own pin**, because `_EXEMPT` was asserted equal to the empty set. So the guard punished its own procedure. The scanner is gone. `anchored_quote_style` now asks whether the regex *mentions* one quote style or both — no bracket parsing exists, so neither the POSIX bug nor the alternation class can. It admits one false negative, stated rather than left implied: a pattern mentioning both but anchoring them *mismatched*. Trading a rare false negative for a whole class of false positives is the trade, made on purpose.

**The headline assertion was vacuous and my own reverts hid it.** Five separate mutations — `and False`, `offenders[:0]`, inverting the `_EXEMPT` test, swapping its key to `(field, cid)`, keying on `(cid,)` — left `assert offenders == []` permanently true with the suite green. Reverting one of the phase's three fixes reds it, which proves only that it is live *today* against a site that already exists. The decision is now factored into `_offenders` and there is a **detection floor**: five planted violations, each required to be caught alone and again when mixed into the live population, plus a clean row required *not* to be caught. `_EXEMPT` stops being pinned-empty and is instead pinned *useful* — an entry must name a real field and that field must actually be flagged, so a stale exemption fails loudly and the key order is guarded.

**The doc half was pinned as one literal line** — assert one string present, one absent — which is exactly what this module's own docstring disclaims, and a *second* quote-anchored example added to § 6.5 stayed green. It is now swept as a class: every `pattern:`/`negative_pattern:`/`earlier:`/`later:` line in `WORKFLOW.md` is unwrapped as YAML would unwrap it and run through the same predicate, with a floor that pins the extractor sees each shape.

**Four more real gaps, all closed.** (i) *Line-scope was untested*: every fixture put the marker on the cited line **and nowhere else**, so nothing distinguished per-line scope from whole-file — and whole-file scope is the blanket marker the design rejects. (ii) *Id matching* was only ever paired against a lexically unrelated id, so substring, prefix and case-insensitive matching all survived; six near-misses now pin exact match. (iii) *Marker spelling* had eleven positive-and-exact cases and not one near-miss, so `no-?check:` and ids widened to `[^\s,]+` survived. (iv) *Waivers were only ever tested at N=0 and N=1*, so capping the list at one entry, de-duplicating, reversing it and counting distinct check-ids instead of findings all survived — the loudness claim was unverified for the case it exists for.

**Two of its mutations survived for a reason worth recording: they had silently retargeted.** `_run_position_check` and `_emit` each build the same `[id] SEV file:line — desc` message, and the position-check copy comes **first** in the file, so `replace(…, 1)` aimed at `_emit` landed there instead. That is Phase 170's rule 2 — *adding text to a file weakens every first-occurrence mutation over that file* — recurring one phase after it was written down. Both paths are now asserted.

**And its `>= 25` critique cut both ways, which changed the fix.** An exact count killed the mutations it named but **reddened four of the seven negative controls**, because adding any legitimate new check moved the number. A guard that punishes ordinary work gets deleted. The population test now **re-derives** the expected `(check_id, field)` set from the fragments and compares — no number to edit, no tolerance for a check escaping, and the four controls are green again. That duplicated extraction is the one deliberate re-implementation in the module: it is a differential control, where `_offenders` calls the production predicate for the opposite reason.

**Final battery: 70 mutations = 69 graded (4 of them reverts) + 1 declared-equivalent, 0 survivors; 7 negative controls, 0 false alarms.** The 24 added by the round are labelled `[lens3]` so the split between what I found and what an independent lens found stays legible. **A run of this harness went red-baseline twice more during these fixes** — once from my own broken test, once from a wrong expectation — and both times every mutation "killed" and every control "false-alarmed". That signature is now the first thing the harness's docstring tells a reader to check.

**Suite: 2114 → 2223 passed + 4 skipped**, read off the final run — not the earlier one. (An intermediate draft of this line said 2181, which was true of the run before the round's fixes landed and false by the time it was written. Same class as Phase 171's derived-number lapse, caught here by re-reading rather than by a guard.)

## Phase 173 (executed 2026-08-01 — Wave 2 item 7: the friction-log path, fixed twice before without a class sweep)

**The filing said "do not make it three." It was already three, and the round found the fourth.**
Phase 128 moved the friction log to `sysop/SYSOP_ISSUES.md`; Phase 147's rider found `/report-issues`
and `/share-wins` still reading the bare root; this phase found `/review-close`, `/intake` and
`/onboard` still asserting it — and its own adversarial round found the installer still *writing* it.

**The class, re-derived rather than adopted.** A whitespace-tolerant occurrence-level scan of the
shipped corpus found **31 bare references against 23 correctly prefixed across 11 files**,
independently reproducing the 2026-07-31 scout's count and per-file distribution. A round reviewer
re-derived the same numbers a third time from the object database. **My own first sweep was wrong in
the documented way** — a line-scoped `grep -v 'sysop/'` silently drops any line carrying *both*
spellings, so it reported 27 lines and hid `docs/install-and-update.md` and two of `add-task`'s
three. That is the scout's own "do not trust a sweep regex" bug, one variant over, caught only
because the occurrence count and the line count disagreed.

**The split that decided the work, and it is not "prefix all 31."** Across the whole corpus **5**
references assert a *location*: three false and bare (`intake:177`, `onboard:147`,
`review-close:1282`) and two already correct and **prefixed** (`report-issues:112`,
`share-wins:139`). **Of the 31 bare, therefore, only 3 assert a location** — a distinction the first
draft of this record got wrong, on four surfaces at once, by writing "5 of the 31" and deriving
"the other 26" from it. The round caught it; the true bare residue is 28. Everything else is a
display string, nominal prose, or — in one case — **correct precisely because it is bare**:
`docs/workflow.html:2489` is a leaf inside an ASCII tree whose parent node is `sysop/`, so prefixing
it would print the path twice and corrupt the diagram. A mass rewrite would have broken it. One
disposition the round overturned: `docs/install-and-update.md:14` was classed nominal, but the same
paragraph names the file correctly twice and then bare once, in the clause a reader skimming for the
contract files lands on. Prefixed.

**`/review-close` was the severe one, and the mechanism is worse than a wrong path.** Grep confirms
it named the correct path **nowhere in the file** (0 prefixed hits pre-fix; `add-task` likewise).
Step 7 step 1 looked at the bare root, found nothing, and emitted `note: SYSOP_ISSUES.md not present
— re-run bash install.sh to seed`, concluding the consumer "pre-dates Phase 13". **That diagnosis is
self-confirming:** `seed_friction_log()` tests `$TARGET/sysop/SYSOP_ISSUES.md` and returns early when
it exists, so the prescribed remedy inspects the real file, does nothing, and leaves the story intact
— while the cycle's friction capture silently no-ops and Step 8 reports success. Step 7 is explicitly
non-retroactive, so each occurrence is a permanent loss.

**Re-deriving a mode-dependent claim narrowed the scope instead of widening it.** I nearly swept the
"re-run `bash install.sh`" remedy as a second class. `LOOP_EXCLUDE_SKILLS` contains `review-close`
and `share-wins`, so they ship only in full mode, where re-running the installer *does* seed. The
remedy is false at exactly one site — the loop-shipped `report-issues:116` — which already has the
correct path. **The first draft of this record then blamed Phase 162 leg (c) for that over-breadth,
and the round showed leg (c) had scoped itself correctly all along** (to loop mode, to
`report-issues:116`, citing `install.sh:4666`). The over-broad reading was mine. Three phases running
(169, 170, 172) the *filed* reasoning was wrong; here it was right and the phase misread it.

**The adjacent-population sweep found the same failure one directory over.** Of the other three paths
`_ns_old_to_new()` migrates, `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md` is clean (same-directory siblings are unaffected by a
move that takes both). Two real defects, both verified before acting:

- **`security_map.md:9`'s section header still read `` `scripts/*.sh`, `scripts/hooks/*` ``.** Both
  review skills derive scan roots by parsing `##` headers (`security-audit:235`/`:255`,
  `codebase-review:221`/`:241`), so that section resolved to a directory no post-128 install has: the
  Shell-Scripts-&-Git-Hooks OWASP checklist attached to nothing and `sysop/scripts/` reported as
  uninventoried. **Phase 130 fixed the byte-identical header in `convention_map.md` and left the
  twin** (verified at `b7ea435`) — the fix-one-and-move-on failure this phase exists to close, live
  inside its own adjacent population. A round reviewer confirmed no third sibling exists.
- **`WORKFLOW.md:812`**, § 6.1's `## Task Workflow (pointer)` row, is boilerplate copied into a
  consumer's `CLAUDE.md` and said "follow the workflow in `WORKFLOW.md`". The same document's § 8
  manifest was updated at Phase 128; the template row was missed. Loop mode ships no `WORKFLOW.md`
  and the installer never emits that section, so full mode is the only mode that reads it.

## What the round found — and it is most of this entry

Four lenses, fresh context, one on a different model, all worktree-isolated. **The isolation put every
reviewer on `main` rather than the branch under review** — the caveat `_shared/adversarial-review.md`
records — and one of them caught it and stopped rather than reviewing the wrong revision. They were
redirected to `git show <sha>:<path>`, the portable form the same section prescribes.

**1. The installer writes the false claim into the artefact itself (the miss).** `seed_friction_log`'s
heredoc seeded every consumer's log with a header reading *"This file lives at repo root by design"* —
wrapped across a line, in the single most authoritative place the claim can appear. My corpus was
`core/ packs/ docs/ README.md CONTRIBUTING.md`: I swept every place the documentation *talks about*
the file and missed the place that *creates* it. `install.sh` is now in the population, and the
module asserts the seed destination and the migration mapping directly rather than assuming them —
an independent battery had rewritten both to the bare root with all tests still green.

**2. A regression I introduced (the worst finding).** Prefixing `/report-issues` and `/share-wins`
Step 5 turned a harmless ambiguity into a hard contradiction: Step 1 documents a fallback to a
pre-128 bare-root copy, so a Step 5 that *re-asserts* `sysop/SYSOP_ISSUES.md` targets a file that
does not exist on that path — **after** the issue or comment is already published, and the status
flip is the only thing preventing a re-run from double-posting. Pre-change the bare token was merely
ambiguous; post-change it was wrong. Write steps now bind to what the read step resolved *and* still
name the canonical path. The same shape inside Step 7 (`review-close:1286`, `:1294`) went with it.
**Self-initiated scope additions are the highest-risk part of any change, and this was one.**

**3. An independent battery beat mine 33-to-0 — the fourth phase running.** I reported 53 graded
with 0 survivors; a fresh lens wrote 39 of its own and watched **33 survive**, and **5 of its 11
negative controls reddened**. The survivors were not exotic:
- **Polarity blindness, both directions.** The predicate matched the *nouns* of a location claim and
  could not tell "is at the repo root" from "used to live at the repo root" / "moved it out of the
  project root" / "may have left it there; migrate it". Every correct migration note in this repo is
  phrased the second way, so the guard punished true sentences — the direction that gets a guard
  deleted rather than fixed. Worse, my own control for this passed **incidentally**: in the three
  skills it checked, the neighbouring token is prefixed, so no bare span exists and the predicate was
  never exercised. A vacuous control, exactly the class this project keeps finding.
- **Wrong directories were invisible.** `bare_spans` tested `endswith("sysop/")`, so `.claude/sysop/`,
  `vendor/sysop/` and `.sysop/` scored as *correct* — worse than a miss, because it marks a wrong path
  compliant. (I had found the `mysysop/` variant of this myself, and fixed only that variant.)
- **Six ordinary rewordings** walked through what I had called a structural check: `base of the repo`,
  `the repository's top folder`, `outermost directory of your project`, `top directory of the
  checkout`. "Structural" had meant "not a fixed phrase list" while leaving the *nouns* enumerated.
- **An asymmetric window.** All three historical defects put the claim *after* the token, so the
  30-character look-behind was untested, and a claim placed ahead of the reference survived.
- **A magic floor.** `>= 6` against an actual population of 7 let one skill drop its mention silently.

The rebuild answers each structurally rather than by extending lists: a **path-expression check** that
reads the path and needs no English (it catches every wrong directory, `./`, `/`, `$REPO_ROOT/`), a
**polarity guard** with its own anti-blanket control, a **symmetric window**, a **derived population
set** instead of a floor, and a corpus that subtracts binary suffixes instead of enumerating text ones
— which is what had silently excluded the shipped extensionless git hooks.

**4. Four false claims in this record, found by the different-model lens.** "Only 5 of the 31 assert a
location" (it is 3 of 31, or 5 of 54) on four surfaces; blaming Phase 162 leg (c) for an over-breadth
that was mine; a mutation headline that counted negative controls as mutations; and "12 changed across
9 files" conflating the occurrence changes (7 files) with the whole footprint. All four are corrected
above. **The record was written before the round precisely so the round could audit it, and this is
the fourth phase where that caught something the code review would not have.**

**Two lenses reached opposite verdicts on `install.sh` and the minority was right.** One declared it
clean after checking all 15 `SYSOP_ISSUES.md` occurrences; the other found the seed body, which
contains no such token because it writes the file's *own* header. Never weight findings by agreement.

**Residuals, named rather than counted as covered.** Implied location claims ("sits alongside
`CLAUDE.md`") carry no location noun and need a judgement no pattern encodes; the exotic tail of
phrasings is open-ended and widening it further trades false negatives for the false positives that
get a guard deleted; and verbatim pins constrain what a step *says*, so prefixing one with "SKIP this
entire step" keeps every pinned byte and inverts it. Property 2 and the path check are the backstops.
Filed separately: `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.7's port checklist states no destination for the doc copies while
§ 8.4's Day-1 checklist does.

**Counts, and which corpus they describe.** Over the sweep's original corpus (`core/`, `packs/`,
`docs/`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` — the boundary the round showed was wrong for excluding
`install.sh`): **31 → 18** bare occurrences, **23 → 34** prefixed, 13 changed across **8** files.
The guard's corpus now also reads `install.sh`, over which the same sweep is 71 total / 28 bare / 43
prefixed — a different denominator, stated because the two are easy to conflate. **18 bare references
ship unchanged and are the deliberate residue**, including the one that is bare *correctly*. Ten
files touched in all, counting the two adjacent-class sites and the installer.

Final battery: **61 mutations (12 reverts + 49 assumption) + 14 negative controls — 0 survivors,
0 false alarms, 0 no-match**, run after the predicate was rebuilt; every one of the independent
lens's 33 survivors is in it. **That is still an author's number**, now for the second time in this
phase — the first one was 53/0 and did not survive contact. Suite **2223 → 2256** passed, 4 skipped.

## Phase 174 (executed 2026-08-01 — the review governor: the count, the stopping rule, and the disposition tier the rounds never had)

**The trigger is a model release, and the first job was separating two things it changed.** Wade brought Anthropic's Opus 5 guidance — *"remove verification instructions carried over from earlier models ('include a final verification step,' 'use a subagent to verify'); they cause over-verification"* — after a week of post-cutover churn: sessions arguing with themselves, a fourth review round proposed and killed only by a one-off different-model adjudication (Phase 171's, whose verdict was "ship part A, do not run a fourth round"). The assessment that opened this phase: the warned class is **same-agent self-verification**, and the adversarial round is not that — it is the cross-agent writer-verifier shape the same guidance names as a strength, and the week's finding wave was real (the partial's own § model-upgrade bullets predicted it: a literal reader re-baselining a corpus written under a charitable one). But three pieces of the procedure compound with a model that self-verifies and delegates readily: a reviewer count with no stated number, a round with no stated end, and a finding taxonomy with nothing between fix-now and dismissed. Those are the phase.

**What ships is model-agnostic on purpose.** Every rule below is justified by evidence that predates the cutover — the count creep, the ~15% overlap, the author-zero-versus-independent-battery series — and the shipped prose cites that evidence, never the model. The model is the urgency, recorded here maintainer-side; consumers run heterogeneous models and the text serves all of them. The one model-facing addition is itself general: a new § model-upgrade bullet stating that newer models verify their own work unprompted, so instructed re-checks of an author's *own* output compound into churn while verification routed *across an agent boundary* does not — independence being the one thing a self-check cannot supply.

**The governor.** `_shared/adversarial-review.md` gains § *How many reviewers, how many rounds — the governor*: **two reviewers on distinct lenses default; a third lens when the change ships behaviour *and* a record making numeric claims; beyond three is the maintainer's decision, made outside the session that wants it.** **One round default, ending when every verified finding is dispositioned**; a second only when the fixes themselves produced substantial new material no fresh reader has seen; a session wanting more surfaces that to the human with the yield so far — never spawns it on its own judgment (that last clause is Phase 171's adjudication, made a rule). And **the latent tier**: a verified-real finding with no live path is *filed* — where the project parks demand-gated work, with the reason and a revisit trigger — not fixed inline, and it never fuels a further round. A § Scope carve-out keeps the single-reviewer-by-design and skill-sized flows honest — per-plan orchestrator reviewers (`/claim-task` 7b, `/auto-build` 6b), skill-sized fan-outs (`/review-close` 2b, the audit skills' own dispatch rules), the maintainer-side audit briefs, and § Compound findings' per-finding second pass are all outside it. (An earlier draft of this sentence said "the eleven shipped … sites" — a sweep sub-agent's integer copied instead of counted, the Phase-170 lapse; the round's claims lens caught it, along with "shipped" covering two `tools/` briefs that never ship.) This resolves the Phase-166 filing in `## Decisions to revisit later` **as ratified by Wade in-session** — Phase 166 held the count was the maintainer's call, and the maintainer made it; entry moved to `REVIEW_ARCHIVE.md` § Resolved — Phase 174. `CLAUDE.md`'s gate paragraph names the governor and the ledger row as steps, because Phase 166's round showed a rule with no invoker does not run.

**The one-battery bound, and the number that had to be corrected before it shipped.** Rule 1 of the author-side pass gains: write the battery once, close what it catches, re-run to confirm, report the fraction with survivors named — **do not keep authoring fresh batteries in pursuit of an exhausted zero.** The first draft of its evidence sentence said "three times… 28, 38, and 33", derived from memory of three entries; re-extraction of Phases 161–173's round records showed the true series is **five consecutive phases (169–173) reporting an all-killed author battery against independent batteries finding 33 to 99 survivors** — plus Phase 156 before them. The correction is the rule's own § *"derive the population from the source of truth"* applied to this phase's headline number, caught author-side before commit.

**The ledger.** `tools/ROUND_YIELD_LEDGER.md` — the prerequisite Phase 166 filed with the count decision — now exists: one row per round (a recorded skip rows too), 161–173 backfilled from `PHASE_LOG.md` with `unrecorded` cells left unrecorded rather than estimated (only 165, 169 and 170 have token figures, and 165's are flagged unverifiable by their own source). `tests/test_round_yield_ledger.py` enforces pace-keeping mechanically from this phase forward: a numeric `CLAUDE.md` Phase-log row ≥ 174 with no ledger row fails the suite, with a fabricated-phase negative control and public-mirror skips stating their reason (the Phase-160 lesson).

**The mirror sweep, run before the round rather than left to it.** A fresh-context sweep of every count-bearing instruction site found the sharpest contradiction *inside the file being edited*: the section opener said "usually wants **several reviewers**" — the exact ratchet phrase the governor diagnoses, 28 lines above it, met first by every reader. Fixed to defer to the governor. Also fixed: `WORKFLOW.md`'s partial-inventory enumeration (the rule-listing mirror, which would otherwise summarize a numbered policy without its numbers); `tools/SKILL_AUDIT.md` + `tools/LIFECYCLE_AUDIT_BRIEF.md`, whose hard-coded three lenses are now stated as the brief's own sizing under the governor's scope rule (the brief sets the count; the session running it does not raise it); and three claims in the gate test module that described the count as "unratified" / the section as "requir[ing] several reviewers". Checked and left: `docs/workflow.html:1387` (a different measurement, not a contradiction — monograph currency is its own standing work), README/CONTRIBUTING ("reviewer" there is the human merge gate), and the public docs, which carry no count language.
