## Phase 175 (executed 2026-08-01 — Wave 2 items 8 + 9: two recovery claims `/review-close` made that the tree did not support)

**Both items are the same defect wearing different clothes: a claim whose truth was checkable against a shipped artefact, and nothing checked it.** Item 8 promised a hook rescue for commands the hook has no matcher for. Item 9 licensed skipping gates with a sentence about consequence that was really a sentence about file extensions. Neither needed judgement to falsify — item 8 needed the hook executed, item 9 needed the extension list read against the thing it classifies.

**Item 8 — the `PermissionDenied` over-promise, and the site that made it plausible.** `permission_denied_hook.py` iterates exactly three matchers and returns 0 with no output otherwise. Executing it settles the class in one command: `gh pr merge …`, `mkdir -p … && cp …` and a bare `cp` all produce **empty output**; the three `git` shapes produce guidance. So `review-close:34` (Step 3b's pending-docs collect) and `:1181` (a denied `gh pr`) both promised a rescue that never arrives, and `:1181` sits on the `pr`-policy mainline — every protected-`main` consumer, this repo included. Both now state the recovery the reader actually has (relay the literal `!`-prefixed command, the Step 3 route) and say plainly that nothing arrives on its own. **The pre-phase sweep added a third site the filing did not have:** `:432`, recorded by the audit as "correctly hedged", limited the hook's coverage to *"the well-known git patterns in Steps 4c/4d/6"* — and Step 4d under `pr` runs `gh pr`. The hedge was a true statement about `direct` that reads as a coverage promise about `gh pr`, which is very likely where `:1181`'s author got it. Coverage is now stated as the three shapes at every site, never as a step range, and `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.2a says so as a rule. **`:1063`/`:1077`/`:1245` ship unchanged — verified sound, matcher by matcher.** The audit's own grep line was also wrong: it reported *"6, all in `review-close`"* where the command it quotes returns 9 across two files, having silently dropped `WORKFLOW.md`, which is where the authoritative description lives.

**Item 9 — the skip, and the gate that should never have inherited it.** The licence was *"a doc-only diff can't regress code-level lint/typecheck"*, and it is false twice over: the extension test classifies as documentation every file a build consumes (`pyproject.toml`, `tsconfig.json`, `.eslintrc.json`, lockfiles, CI workflows, semgrep rules, `checks.yml`) — so such a diff regresses lint and build *directly* — and `### Always` is a full test suite, which can assert on prose. The clause was live at five sites plus two in the spec. **The one that mattered was not the one filed.** The filing named Step 3; Phase 170 had already established that Step 3's green is explicitly *not* a verdict, so a skip there forfeits only a fail-fast. `4a-post` is the gate the skill itself calls the one "whose green means something", and it inherited the skip by reference — while its own ran-nothing rule is conditioned on *"while the list still contains a code file"*, **vacuously false on a doc-only diff**. That made the doc-only path the single route through the merged-tree gate that executes zero commands and reports green unchallenged, and Step 8's report vocabulary had no arm to say so: it offered `ran on <merge target>` or `not reached`, so the skip rendered to the human as a completed verification. `4a-post` no longer inherits it, the report can say `ran nothing`, and the zero-commands-on-a-doc-only-diff case **reports rather than stops** — halting every docs cycle after the merges would be the Phase-167 always-halt regression in the other direction.

**A contradiction inside one numbered list, which nobody had filed.** Item 3 arms each auto-detected command on its own surface appearing in the changed-file list; item 4 then cancels them. Three of item 3's four bullets can fire on a diff item 4 calls doc-only — a path under `frontend/` (`package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, a stylesheet), any surface's non-code manifest (`go.mod`, `Dockerfile`, `pubspec.yaml`), and the airtight one: **`Cargo.toml`, which item 3 names by name while `.toml` is absent from the code set six lines later.** Item 4 now never cancels a command item 3 armed.

**Two skips gain the conjunct the sound one already had.** Step 2b's skip was sound and ships unchanged — it requires *both* no code files *and* no `## Prevention Conventions` rule governing the touched types, and `tests/test_review_close_diff_basis.py` records that its first version shipped the bare claim and was disproved by Sysop's own maps. Step 2d and Step 3c had no such conjunct. Step 2d now skips only when the record is a `no-test`; a record naming a test is verified whatever the extensions say. Step 3c now runs its signal detection **first** — a `manual_smoke: true` task or a smoke heading beats the extension test, because the list cannot tell a docs commit from a task implemented in a `docker-compose.yml`, a feature-flag `.json` or a k8s manifest, and this is the gate whose miss is a human never being asked. `### Always`'s definition — *"run unconditionally"*, thirteen lines above the item that made it conditional — now says which gate keeps the promise, which makes `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md:222` and `docs/getting-started.md`'s *"runs it on the merged tree on every merge"* true rather than aspirational. Both spec sites moved with the skill (Phase 170's precedent): `WORKFLOW.md:345` had dropped Step 2b's saving conjunct entirely.

**The filed *consequence* did not survive re-derivation. The filed *number* did — and this phase got that wrong first, in the paragraph announcing it had caught the pattern.** The record's *"31 test modules in this repo assert on `SKILL.md` prose"* is **exact**: the filing quoted its own method, `grep -rln "SKILL\.md" tests/*.py`, and at the filing's own commit (`2ffe923`) that returns 31. It returns 37 at this phase's base and 38 now, because seven test modules were added in between. A pre-phase scout re-derived a *different* population — instrumented runtime reads over a full suite run, giving 44 / 39 / 26 depending on where you draw the line — against a *later* revision, and I wrote the divergence up as the filing being unprincipled. **It was not; the drift was the tree's, and the comparison was mine to get right.** The round's claims lens caught it by doing the one thing I had not: running the filing's own command at the filing's own revision. The 44/39/26 triple is separately unreproducible — the scout never stated its population rules — so it is recorded here as unverified and used for nothing. What the episode is actually evidence for is narrower and worth keeping: **a measurement is only comparable at the revision it was taken.** More consequentially, **fixing item 4 alone would not make pytest run in this repo**, and the first draft of this entry implied it would. Three mechanisms block it independently, and item 4 is the *last* of them: item 3's pytest bullet requires `pytest` declared in `[project.optional-dependencies]`, and this repo's `pyproject.toml` has no `[project]` table at all, so the bullet never arms; even armed, the surface gate needs a Python file. So the fix binds for consumers with a **declared** list (items 1–2) and leaves auto-detect exactly as it was — which the shipped text says, and which this record now says too. **This repo is covered by CI, not by the skill:** `.github/workflows/tests.yml` runs `pytest` on every PR with no path filter and `main` requires it. The gap bites consumers without that.

**That a doc-only diff can break the suite is demonstrated, not argued.** Three scratch-clone experiments: adding one extension token to item 4's list fails `test_all_three_doc_only_skips_share_one_code_file_set`; a meaning-preserving reword of **one sentence** turns 8 tests red; and a one-line `pyproject.toml` edit — a `.toml`-only diff, doc-only by item 4 — produces **30 collection errors** on this tree (29 at the phase's base; the round re-measured, and the extra one is this phase's own new module), so the suite cannot even collect. The class also already shipped: of the last 120 commits exactly one was doc-only by item 4's rule *and* touched `core/skills/` — Phase 161's `02ee0f5`, which also carried `core/companion/git-hooks/pre-commit`, an **extensionless shell script**.

**Filed, not fixed** (each verified, each a distinct change with its own blast radius): the code-file set misses **extensionless shell scripts** — `git-hooks/pre-commit` and `pre-merge-commit` are `file`-verified bash and classify as doc-only, and widening the set touches three sites plus a guard that asserts exactly 11 extensions; item 3's pytest bullet keys on `[project.optional-dependencies]` while the common modern shape is `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` alone, so auto-detect never arms for repos like this one; this repo has **no `## Merge policy` header**, so `/review-close` would default to `direct` against a protected `main`; and `_shared/adversarial-review.md:106` carries the same config-only-is-harmless premise one skill family over, where `/review-close`'s own `:368` has now been qualified.

### The author-side pass

**Rule 3 first.** The change prescribes two escape commands with substituted operands; both were checked against the invocations they stand in for — `! gh pr merge "<PR>" --squash --delete-branch` matches Step 4d's literal at `:1155`, including the quoting `:1142` explains is load-bearing (unquoted, `<PR>` is a shell redirection and `gh` silently merges the current branch's PR), and the `mkdir -p … && cp …` form matches Step 3b's at `:617`. The hook's behaviour itself was established the same way rather than by reading: five command shapes piped through the shipped script, exit codes checked.

**Rule 1, one battery — and it found three defects in the guards before any reviewer saw them, all in the over-strict direction the rule names as the one that hides.** (i) The unbacked-promise screen split sentences on `;` as well as `.`, on the reasoning that over-splitting only makes a guard stricter — it does not: the semicolon inside Step 4c's parenthetical separated the promise from the `git commit` that backs it, and the guard went **red on a sound site**. (ii) One of my three known-positive fixtures was wrong: I filed the step-numbered hedge as an unbacked promise, and it carries *"only surfaces"*, so the screen correctly passes it — its defect is a different one, and it now sits under the guard that actually covers it. (iii) My own corrected prose quoted the retired phrase verbatim to explain it, which tripped my own screen; the quote belongs here, not in the skill.

**Then 20 mutations, 0 survivors — and that number was the weak evidence this project's ledger says it is**, so I ran the three shapes I actually suspected. **Two survived, both "where it looks":** a *fourth* doc-only skip added elsewhere in the file carrying its own bare harmlessness claim, and a contradiction of the non-inheritance planted **outside** the `4a-post` slice — the exact hole Phase 174's round found one rule over. Both closed in kind by screening the claim *shape* file-wide rather than the sentence section-scoped, and both closures then needed two corrections of their own: the merged-gate screen first accepted the planted contradiction (whose sentence ends *"runs no verification at all"*, so a whole-sentence negation search excused it) and then rejected the shipped *"no diff-shape heuristic skips a list the consumer declared"* — fixed by binding the negation to the verb and the verb to the mention, and by excluding fenced blocks, since Step 8's template contains `skipped` as a slot rather than an assertion. **Final: 23 mutations, 0 survivors, 6 negative controls, 0 false alarms**, re-run after the closures. Both survivors ship as permanent regression tests.

### Phase 175's adversarial round

**Three fresh-context reviewers, one round, distinct lenses — *are the guards real* / *are its claims true* / *does it execute* — worktree-isolated, read-only outside their own trees, two of the three on a different model than the author.** Governor accounting: the third lens was bought under the escalation condition (a guard module ships; the record makes numeric claims), recorded here as the call rather than left implicit. All three worktrees landed on `6ac41d1` rather than the branch — the Phase-173 trap, now three rounds running — and all three detected it themselves, two reading through `git show e69182d:<path>` and one detaching its own worktree onto the commit.

**The guards lens is the phase's headline, and it is not flattering: 20 of its 31 mutations survived, and 4 of its 9 negative controls went red.** Both defect classes were reintroducible at their original filed sites in wording an ordinary editor would produce — `can't` → `won't`, "the merged-tree pass" for "4a-post", the promise in passive voice, a claim split across two sentences, a bullet with no terminal period merging into the sound sentence below it. The worst single one: `unbacked_promises()` excused a sentence if **any** backticked span in it matched the hook, so a false `gh pr` promise laundered itself by mentioning `git push origin main` in the same breath — at the exact filed site, on the `pr` mainline, with the corrected sentence still pinned three lines above. And the screens were wrong in the other direction at the same time: they reddened two sentences that are **true of the shipped hook**, including an accurate description of its own venv-prefixed output. **A screen wrong in both directions is not a screen**, so the screens were replaced rather than patched — `tests/test_review_close_screens.py`, six layers, each one a named survivor: a forbidden-verb zone in the two paragraphs where any coverage claim is false; paragraph scope instead of sentence scope (which is what punished the true sentences); a pinned mention census making a new hook paragraph a review event; predicate-scoped harmlessness screening (the old regex fired on `doc-only … never` whatever followed, so it reddened *"A doc-only cycle never bypasses this gate"* — prose strengthening the rule it guards); negation truncated at the clause boundary, because a 60-character window let *"`4a-post`, whose surface gate cannot arm anything, inherits item 4's skip"* pass; and the gate's synonyms plus its fenced `#` instruction comments, both previously invisible. All 20 survivors ship as permanent cases in that module.

**The claims lens found the round's sharpest single finding, and it is against this phase, not the filing.** This entry's first draft said the filed *"31 test modules assert on `SKILL.md` prose"* matched **no principled definition**. It is exact — the filing quoted its own command, and at the filing's own commit it returns 31 — and the lens established that by doing the one thing I had not: running the filing's command at the filing's revision. Four phases of "the filed reasoning was wrong" had made the fifth assume it. Corrected at all four record sites. The same lens found **a live contradiction of the fix**: `:389` said item 3's surface gate and item 4's doc-only skip *"both read the list this prints"* under a heading scoped to **each pass** — the propagation the phase's headline removed, in a sentence that never names `4a-post`, which is exactly why the new screen missed it while a *planted* mutation had convinced me the hole was closed. Also: two wrong numbers of my own (`eight lines` → six; `29 collection errors` → 30 on this tree), `gh` described as never *entering* the matcher loop when it enters and matches nothing, an absolute quantifier (`every file a build consumes` — `vite.config.ts` is code), and a false parallel between Step 2b's and Step 2d's second conjuncts, which share a reason but not a predicate.

**The execution lens walked all six consumer shapes on both diff kinds and found neither feared failure mode** — no always-halt, no green-having-run-nothing — which is the finding I most wanted and could least establish myself. Its four MEDIUMs were: a stale sentence at `:340` claiming step 0's skip *"is the only thing that spares one"*, false under this phase's own step 0 (and falsifying a clause **Phase 167 pins**, so that pin and its mutation were updated deliberately and inverted rather than worked around); `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md:222`'s unscoped *"runs unconditionally on every review pass"*, which this entry had claimed the phase made **true** while never touching the file — the Guide defines "pass" as each of the two runs, so it stayed false; Step 2d's conjunct written per-*branch* while the gate iterates per-*task*, which would silence a record naming a test because a sibling task's record did not; and the red-at-tip suite this record reported as green. Its LOWs retired Step 3c's now-vacuous skip computation (with detection first, that rule cannot change an outcome — it stays *stated*, because the coupling it forbids is a real regression, but no longer instructs work), gave `4a-post` a disposition under `NO_ORIGIN_MAIN`, and fixed a dangling relative clause in the spec.

**Post-round battery: 44 mutations, 0 survivors, 6 negative controls, 0 false alarms** — including all 13 of the guards lens's own surviving shapes re-run against the rebuilt screens, plus a declared **census tripwire**: adding a new correctly-limited hook paragraph *does* go red, on purpose, because the guard cannot judge a claim nobody has written yet and the census exists to make writing one a review event. That is the one false-positive direction kept deliberately, and it is recorded rather than left for a later reader to trip over.

**No second round.** The governor warrants one when the fixes produce substantial new material no fresh reader has seen, and a guard module rewritten wholesale is exactly that — but the material's verification was bounded and mechanical (the lens's own 20 survivors, executed against the replacement), which the governor assigns to the caller rather than to a new round. Recorded as a decision, not an omission.

**Suite: 2287 → 2344 passed + 4 skipped**, read off full runs before and after, not derived from the count of new tests. The tip was **red between the record commit and this one** — `test_round_yield_ledger.py` fails while a `CLAUDE.md` phase row exists without its ledger row, and the ledger row records the round's yield, so it cannot precede the round. The ordering is structural to Phase 174's gate meeting the commit-before-the-round rule; it is named here because the first version of this line reported a pass count with a failing test underneath it.

## Phase 176 (executed 2026-08-02 — Wave 2 item 10: the halt arm its only binding caller ignored)

**`_shared/adversarial-review.md` § Classification Rubric defines `blocker` as "Action: halt — do not call `ExitPlanMode`, do not execute, surface the question to the human." `/plan-review` gave `blocker` the *`fixable`* action at four sites and then called `ExitPlanMode` anyway.** It is the only rubric consumer that reaches `ExitPlanMode` **while a classification is still live**, so the prohibition was violated at the only site where it binds. It is *not* the only skill that reaches `ExitPlanMode` at all — the round killed that wording at four sites, including the shipped skill: `/auto-build:696` instructs the call outright in its Phase 6e executor prompt, and the sentence asserting exclusivity had `/auto-build` reaching it in its own second clause. `/claim-task:12` never enters plan mode; `/auto-build:515` parks every blocker and skips execution before `:696` can run, so the prohibition is vacuous there rather than absent.

**The contradiction was created by an extraction, and the commit that created it edited the file.** `/plan-review` never carried a classification rubric of its own. Step 5's "For each **blocker** finding" was authored at **`94dc48e` (2026-04-11)**, the commit that added the skill; Phase 26 (`2a360e8`, 2026-05-20) then pointed Step 3 at a shared rubric defining `blocker` as halt — in a diff that touched `core/skills/plan-review/SKILL.md`, removing the inline prompt from Step 3 and leaving Step 5 alone. It has shipped contradicting itself for ~2.5 months. **The first draft of this paragraph dated the text to `5076074` and was wrong in the way this phase is about:** `5076074` is a *pure rename* of the file — `1 file changed, 0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)` — and a path-scoped `git log -S` without `--follow` reports the commit that added the *path*. The claims lens caught it by running the command correctly. Eleven lines below that sentence the same entry lectures about re-deriving a filed number against the source it was filed in.

**The filed count depends on which filing you read, and the brief is the one that undercounts.** `tools/FIX_WAVE_BRIEF.md`'s Wave-2 row names three sites (`:86`, `:93`, `:102`). The checklist leg it derives from — § High, Phase 164's audit, leg (d) — names **four**, adding *"`:118`'s table reports 'Blockers incorporated' as diligence"*. All four are real and all four are fixed. A phase working from the brief alone ships `:119` unfixed.

**The filed coordinates did not drift, and saying they had was this phase's second instance of the same error.** The first draft asserted *"every coordinate in both filings had drifted, as Phase 167's rule 1 predicts"* — an assumption dressed as a measurement. Re-derived at `288a0b7`, the revision the checklist leg names as its own corpus: `:86`, `:93` and `:102` are **byte-exact there and still exact at the pre-phase tip**. The fourth was filed as `:118` and was `:119` at `288a0b7` — an off-by-one in the filing, not drift. The sibling coordinates fared no better under the same treatment: `auto-build:472` was **exact** at the filing revision and has since moved 35 lines to `:507`, which is not "hundreds"; and `claim-task:458` does not exist any more at all — Phase 171 deleted the reviewer-executor prompt it sat in, so `:806` is different text in a different step rather than the same site relocated. The sibling *verdict* holds; the drift framing described something that did not happen.

**`:102` is the worst site, and not for the reason filed.** The filing's reason is that it makes "zero blockers" the only clean-exit path and proceeds regardless — true. The unfiled half is the word *instead*: the clean-pass line is appended **in place of** the `## Adversarial Review — Incorporated Changes` section. Since `fixable` is the rubric's default arm and `blocker` its exception, the dominant path — findings returned, all `fixable`, all incorporated — is precisely the path on which the skill replaced its own audit record with "no blockers found". The condition is now the absence of *findings*, which is what § *Recording a clean pass* says. The recorded sentence is the rubric's, reproduced with the skill's pre-existing terminal period — "verbatim" was overstated, and the guard now accepts the rubric's own "no findings" phrasing as well as "zero findings", because a check that reddens when the skill converges on the ground truth is punishing the right answer.

**The class sweep found a fifth site and settled a discriminator; a sixth was fixed after the round asked why it was not discussed.** `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md:250`'s catalogue entry names the `fixable`/`blocker` split and then describes the outcome as uniformly *"a revised plan presented for approval before anything executes"* — the same defect one altitude up. The line the sweep settled on is that **a site which names the classification owes the halt; a site which never names it does not**, which is why the skill's frontmatter `description:` ships unchanged. The claims lens pointed out that `docs/workflow.html`'s `/plan-review` entry is the same shape on the *public* surface and the record was silent on it: licensed by the discriminator, but silence leaves a reader unable to tell examined-and-passed from never-looked-at. It said "presents a revised plan for approval before any execution" unconditionally, so it is fixed rather than merely disclosed. **`docs/workflow.html` is HTML and is outside the guard's population, which is `.md` only** — stated because it is a real hole, not a boundary.

**Siblings verified clean, by reading the shipped text rather than trusting the brief.** `claim-task:806` ("If any finding is `blocker` — park. Do not spawn the executor.") and `auto-build:507` ("halt and park") are correct, and `claim-task:743`'s definition bullet correctly states no action because its halt is 60-odd lines later.

**The class had no guard, underneath a test whose name covers it.** `test_the_procedure_does_not_contradict_the_skills_that_consume_it` (`tests/test_adversarial_review_gate.py:1266`) reads general; its docstring and body are scoped to the `isolation: "worktree"` carve-out. (It is one of *two* consumer-facing tests in that module, not one as the first draft said — `test_compound_findings_heading_resolves_for_its_citers` also derives a citer population. Neither touches a disposition.) `tests/test_blocker_halt_contract.py` is the new owner.

### What the round did to the guard, which is most of this phase

**The first guard was a regex screen, and an independent battery ran 21 defect mutations through it with a 100% survival rate.** Reported author-side: 19 mutations, 0 survivors. The gap is the one `adversarial-review.md` rule 1 describes exactly — my 19 were overwhelmingly reverts of my own edits, which measure *wiring* and say nothing about coverage. A whitelist of determiners and verbs loses to ordinary English: `"For **`blocker`** findings, modify the relevant plan step"` reintroduces the `:86` defect one comma from the shipped string. Worse, `/auto-build`'s halt inverted to absorb-and-continue with **nothing in the entire suite** going red, and `/claim-task`'s inverted with nothing in *this module* going red (it was caught, incidentally, by `test_claim_task_orchestrator.py` — coverage existed, but not where this module's name claims it lives). Six of the battery's eight negative controls also reddened, including `"For every `blocker`, surface its one-line question to the human"` — pure halt-side prose — because the shape keyed on a determiner and a token with no reference to any action at all.

**So the guard was rebuilt on two mechanisms rather than patched.** (1) **Verbatim disposition pins** — eleven load-bearing clauses across the rubric, both siblings, `/plan-review` and the guide, pinned byte-for-byte, so any *rewording* trips a pin even when no shape matches it. Phase 168's precedent, and its cost is deliberate: a legitimate reword reddens and is re-pinned on purpose. (2) **A narrow absorb screen over a wide population**, because a pin cannot see an instruction *added* alongside it — six of the reviewer's mutations worked that way, one of them by planting the literal shipped defect string in `README.md`, which the first population (`core/skills/` + `core/companion/docs/`) never read. Plus a **softener screen** on the halt arm and the Step 8 note, because two mutations neutralised the gate with a conditional rider carrying no absorb verb and touching nothing pinned.

**A general screen was tried first and abandoned on measurement.** Any clause naming a blocker near an absorb verb, minus a halt word: run against the tree it produced **eleven hits, all eleven correct prose** — `/auto-build`'s instruction to a human resuming a parked task, `/claim-task`'s "do not decide whether the work proceeds", the guide's `/next-task` entry using the *dependency* sense of the word. The separation between those and a real defect is semantic, not lexical. **The screen's narrowness is therefore declared, not implied:** an absorb instruction in a construction it does not list is caught only if it replaces a pinned disposition rather than joining one.

**Re-run of the reviewer's own 21 mutations against the rebuild: 21 killed, 0 survivors; 8 negative controls, 1 red.** The red is NC4 — reordering the rubric's two prohibitions, semantically neutral, trips the ground-truth pin. That is the pin's contract rather than a defect, and it is recorded here as the declared cost of the mechanism rather than netted out of the count. The one mutation that survived the first re-run was a plausible *fourth* consumer (a `plan-lint` skill citing the partial, writing `**blocker**` unbackticked); it is closed by deriving the consumer population from the tree and requiring every member to carry a pin, so a fourth consumer cannot arrive unnoticed.

### What the execution lens found in the skill

**A malformed reviewer return exited through the clean-pass stamp — and this phase made that load-bearing.** Nothing checked that `RAW_FINDINGS` was a findings list, so an error, a refusal or a rewritten plan yielded nothing classifiable, the zero-findings arm fired, the plan was stamped "Adversarial review: no blockers found" — whose stated purpose is telling future reviewers the step ran clean — and Step 8 called `ExitPlanMode`. A review that never ran was indistinguishable from a clean one: the #220 shape, which this repo has now fixed twice elsewhere. `/claim-task:721-732` requires an explicit `findings: []` / `verdict: CLEAN` for exactly this reason and `/plan-review`'s reviewer emits no verdict token, so a new 5a arm is the only thing standing in the way. Fixed here on Wade's call rather than filed, because hinging the record on "zero findings" is what made the predicate load-bearing.

**Four smaller live defects, all in prose this phase wrote.** The Notes rule *"every finding must be incorporated or explicitly rejected in the revised plan"* is unsatisfiable on a mixed blocker+fixable path where 5b forbids producing one — it now states its halt-path form, and says the `fixable` findings are deferred rather than dismissed. The 5b template's `Question:` line had **no producer**: the Prompt Template returns a prioritized issue list with no question field, so the template was asking the executor to invent the human's question where `/claim-task:808` hedges with "if one is present" — now hedged, with "do not invent one". The rubric requires a planner to have *tried revising* before classifying anything a `blocker`, which 5b then forbids — the arm now distinguishes the 5a attempt (scratch) from emitting a revised plan (forbidden). And "Still proceed to Step 8" read as a jump that skipped Steps 6–7, losing the file-mode write-back of the clean-pass annotation; it now says continue through 6–8. The recovery instruction is also mode-aware now: in conversation, Step 2 prefers the most recent plan-mode tool call over a newer chat message, so "update the plan and re-run" as first written could re-select the same unrevised plan and halt forever.

**Filed, not fixed** (each verified, each with its own blast radius): `plan-review:55`'s preamble-rejection message cites `claim-task` Step 6, which is now the plan-review-preference step — the `## Constraints & Risks` contract lives in Step 7a; the preamble check accepts only `- ` bullets and only an H2 heading, and is undefined when the section is last; Step 6's `K` row counts a verification total the Prompt Template never asks for, so it can essentially never fire; the Step 3 reviewer carries no do-not-mutate instruction, shared by all three consumers; and `adversarial-review.md:79`'s "five consecutive phases … 33 to 99 survivors" is understated against its own log — Phase 174 measured 30 and Phase 175 measured 20, making it six phases and 20 to 99 — but the sentence sits in a subsection Phase 168 pinned verbatim after a 19-character softening killed a ratchet, so re-pinning it is a change that should not ride along here.

### The author-side pass

**Rule 3 is out of scope and that is stated rather than skipped.** The change prescribes no command whose operand it computes or substitutes; the halt arm's product is a printed block.

**Rule 2 killed a claim I had just written, and left it in the tree.** The fix's first draft called `/plan-review` *"the caller the prohibition was written for"*; `git log -S` dates the prohibition to Phase 26, before Phase 171 removed plan mode from `/claim-task`, so it is an unverifiable provenance claim and probably false. I rewrote the shipped sentence and the module docstring — **and missed the assertion message sixteen lines below the docstring, which still carried the killed phrase until the claims lens found it.** The record then said "it now states the present-tense fact instead", which was false of the tree.

**Rule 1: one battery, and the useful number was the first one.** 17 mutations + 6 controls: **5 survivors, 1 false alarm.** All five survivors were one root cause — a file-level assertion satisfied by an incidental occurrence elsewhere in the same file (the Notes section re-cites the partial; Step 8 re-says "halt"; Step 3 re-uses the token). Closed by slicing each assertion to the clause that must carry it. The two guard defects the controls found were both **over-strictness**: generalising the quantifier to `a`/`an` reddened `adversarial-review.md:173`'s own referential *"`BLOCKER_QUESTION:` for a blocker discovered during implementation"*, and the `blocker`…`accepted` shape reddened a control that *narrated* the retired wording — ordinary work, since this repo does keep historical notes inside shipped files. Final author-side: 19 mutations, 0 survivors, 8 controls, 0 false alarms — a number the round then showed to be worth nothing, which is the point of reporting both.

**Two process notes.** The ground-truth assertion — the one pinning the rubric's definition, on which everything else depends — was **wrong twice in the same function**, both times because `[^.]` cannot span the sentences between a token and its action clause. It failed red, so it was cheap; the same bug pointed the other way is a guard that passes while measuring nothing. And a background `pytest` was reported by the harness as **exit code 0** while its output was an argparse usage error — Phase 173's false-green, arriving from the harness rather than from a `127`.

**One self-initiated scope addition, flagged rather than defended.** Step 5b forbids `EnterPlanMode` as well as `ExitPlanMode`; the rubric names only the latter. Step 8 is unreachable from 5b either way (the first draft of this sentence had that inversion backwards), so the addition is harmless — but it goes beyond the source of truth and is recorded as such.

### The round

**Three lenses, one round, per the governor** — the phase ships behaviour *and* a record making numeric claims, which is the stated escalation condition. Two of three reviewers ran a different model from the author. **All three worktrees were cut from `main` rather than from the phase branch**, and the guards lens detected it on its mandated first check and stopped rather than reviewing the pre-phase tip; the other two were redirected to `git show <sha>:<path>` and read-only clones. `adversarial-review.md` § *Worktree isolation* already warns that isolation "does not guarantee the revision you expect" — this round is a second instance, and a sharper one: the worktree was cut from the default branch while the main checkout sat on the branch under review.

**No second round.** The governor licenses one when the fixes produce substantial new material no fresh reader has seen, and a guard module rebuilt on two new mechanisms is exactly that. It is declined because the verification available is bounded and mechanical — the reviewer's own 21 mutations, re-run against the replacement, 21 killed — which the governor assigns to the caller rather than to a new round. Recorded as a decision, not an omission.

**Suite: 2344 → 2451 passed + 4 skipped**, both endpoints read off full runs rather than derived — the commit that opened this phase reported "2344 → 2411 (+67)" with the second figure computed from the count of new tests, which is the practice Phase 175's entry declared it had stopped, and the claims lens caught it repeated one phase later. The 107-test delta happens to equal the new module's size; that is a coincidence of this phase, not the method. The tip was **red between the record commit and this one** on `test_round_yield_ledger::test_every_phase_from_174_has_a_ledger_row`, which is structural: the row records the round's yield and cannot precede the round.

**One red run is recorded rather than dismissed.** The first full run of the phase failed `test_install_lock_timestamps.py::test_noop_update_leaves_tree_clean`; it passed in isolation immediately after, and passed in all four subsequent full runs including an independent reviewer's on a clean clone. No mechanism was found and none is claimed — it is logged here because "flake" was the working diagnosis and a disposition reached without evidence should be visible to whoever meets it next, not asserted in a status line and left out of the record. That omission was itself a round finding.

## Phase 177 (executed 2026-08-02 — the pre-push bundle: monograph currency for 172–176, the figures that still drew a retired architecture, and the two mirror gates nobody wrote down)

**The mirrors were five phases behind, and the last push proved that the gate list is not the same as the gate procedure.** `git rev-list --count b7b4f4d..HEAD` is **12** commits since the 2026-07-31 snapshot (public `b850b42` PR #23, tester `56098f5`), carrying Phases 172, 173, 174, 175 and 176. A push at that point would have shipped a stale public monograph for the second time and would have repeated two gates that were invented ad-hoc during the last cut, used, and never written down. Both halves are fixed here; **the push itself is staged, not taken** — it is outward-facing and needs Wade.

**Leg 1 — the monograph has no changelog section, and that is the constraint the pass has to work inside.** `docs/workflow.html` narrates phases inline, grouped by *failure class*, never by phase number; the only phase-*number* surfaces are the masthead, the hero stat and two colophon stamps. So five phases became three grafts onto arguments that already existed, following Phase 146's precedent (eleven phases → three prose blocks, none organized by phase) rather than appending entries.

- **The author-vs-independent battery series** in § I's pull-quote gained a second paragraph. Five more phases ran the comparison and none came out the other way: independent batteries found **38, 33, 30, 20 and — in Phase 176 — 21 of 21 survivors**, that last against an author-reported zero. The paragraph gives the survivor counts and the cause the numbers make legible — it names no phase numbers, and an earlier draft of this entry said it did: most of the author's counted mutations were reverts of the edit just made, which measure whether a guard is *wired to a file* and say nothing about coverage.
- **A sixth shape** in § III's *"The failure that looks like a clean result"*. The first five shapes are reviews that did not run; the new one is the same silence one layer down — a check that ran on half its subject (Phase 172's `sql-fstring` check — a `severity: critical` entry, not the only one; see the correction at Phase 172's record above — anchored on a literal `"`, and its sibling positional check disarmed on 59 of 182 files), a merge-time gate whose skip rule was vacuously false on a doc-only diff so it executed nothing and reported success (Phase 175's `4a-post`), and a plan reviewer whose malformed return fired the zero-findings branch and stamped the plan *"no blockers found"* (Phase 176). *A miss and a real zero are the same output* is the thesis, and the answer in all three was the same pair: derive the population from the source of truth instead of trusting an anchor to find it, and give the reporting vocabulary a word for **ran nothing**.
- **A new § *How many reviewers, and when a round ends*** — Phase 174's governor, the only one of the five that ships a policy an outside reader can adopt. Written to include the measurement that makes the obvious correction wrong: on one four-lens round the overlap between lenses was ~15% and each lens produced its sharpest finding alone, so the case for two-by-default is about *who decides*, not about reviewers being redundant. The latent-disposition tier is given the most space, because it is the piece that stops a round becoming a loop. **The ledger is described as something the project keeps, never as something a consumer gets** — `tools/` is mirror-excluded, and an implied deliverable there would have been a false claim on the public surface.

**"Six consecutive" was not extended to "eleven consecutive", and the near-miss is worth recording.** The existing sentence reads *"Six consecutive phase records…"*, and adding five looks like arithmetic. It is not: Phase 174's own record establishes the unbroken run as **169–173**, and Phases 161 and 164 are a different class, so the series is not consecutive across the join. The new paragraph therefore states *"five more phases"* and names their numbers, with no consecutive-count claim to falsify. Phase 175's rule — re-derive the filed number at the revision it was filed against — applied to a number already sitting in the shipped text.

**Leg 2 — the filed two figure labels were four stale sites in the monograph, plus a class of four in the shipped skills.** The filed coordinates `:1331` and `:2286` were **byte-exact at HEAD, measured before use rather than assumed stale**. The class sweep then found:

- `:1332`, the twin `<text>` in the *same* `<g>` as `:1331` — *"sub-agent · phase 29"*. Fixing `:1331` alone would have left the retired provenance dangling under a corrected label.
- `:1366`, the `/claim-task` glossary `<dd>`, ending *"a single sub-agent owns the adversarial review, the implementation, the verification, and the commit"* — the retired shape stated in the present tense as the reader's **definition of the skill**, and the most load-bearing of the four.
- `:2287`, in the figure being edited: *"emits envelope at top of message"*. False, and false for the pre-171 shape too — `parse_subagent_envelope.py::_find_envelope_block` returns `candidates[-1]`, the **last** fenced block, and every shipped prompt says so. It is the `REVIEW_REPORT:` block that is read first.
- **Four `§` citations in shipped skills** (`claim-task:466`, `auto-build:888`, `plan-review:190`, `WORKFLOW.md:214`) pointing at *§ "Reviewer-executor variant"*. `git show 3cbb684^:core/skills/_shared/adversarial-review.md` confirms the heading **was** `## Reviewer-executor variant — /claim-task Step 7` and that Phase 171 renamed it to `## The reviewer-executor variant is retired…`. Same phase, same fallout, and a citation whose truncation reads as a live section about a live variant. The section *body* still records collapsed self-classification as a known compromise, so three of the four sentences around those citations are unchanged. **The fourth was not, and the round caught the claim that they all were.** `auto-build:888` attributed a verbatim "handoff guidance" quote to the cited section — a quote that lived in the *pre-171* section and is absent from the renamed one — and its conclusion ("bundle the collapse only into `/claim-task` for now") had been inverted by the very phase that renamed the heading. That entry is now closed-by-events rather than deferred. My own check of this nearly missed it: a case-sensitive grep for the quote returned 0 because the original begins "Validate".
- **A second Phase-171 renumbering class:** the convention-loop figure cited `step 6 · pre-impl check` / `step 7 · post-impl re-check` and the prose beneath it *"read on every `/claim-task` Step 6"*. Post-171 Step 6 is *"Resolve the plan-review preference"* and Step 7 is *"Orchestrate"*; the map read moved to the planner at **7a** and the post-impl pass to the executor at **7e**.

**The re-layout was verified by rendering it, not by arithmetic.** Fig. 2's annotation grew from 170×56 to 240×76 (x 225–465, still centred on the existing arrow at x=345, with 15px clearance to both neighbours) and now reads *three cold sub-agents / planner → reviewer → executor / the orchestrator classifies · phase 171*. Measured in a headless browser via `getBBox()` across all **52** diagram nodes: every label fits, every viewBox contains its contents, and the new labels carry 16–59px of slack per side. That check also surfaced **three pre-existing overflows** in the same figure — two labels centred at `x="125"` inside a 170-wide box (an obvious typo against the two sibling boxes at `x="85"`), and `sysop/runtime/pending-docs/` at 178.7px in a 170px box. Confirmed pre-existing at `HEAD` before touching them; fixed, because leaving a visibly off-centre label beside a fresh re-layout reads as the re-layout's fault.

**My own sweep regex was wrong, in the documented way, and I nearly published the wrong conclusion.** A first pass for the `§` citations used an over-constrained pattern, returned nothing, and I ran it under an unconditional `echo "(none — clean)"`. The second pattern returned four hits — printed *above* that line — and the class exists. `tools/FIX_WAVE_BRIEF.md` § Things not to do says *"do not trust a sweep regex without verifying it — a class sweep's regex is itself a claim"*; it was a sub-agent's finding that survived my own bad regex, which is a live argument for not weighting a lens by whether the caller can reproduce it on the first try.

**Leg 3 — the two gates, plus the runbook's own drift.** Both are now numbered steps in `tools/TESTER_MIRROR_RUNBOOK.md` (4 and 5; the trailing steps renumbered **6–10** — the push step moved 4 → 6, and an earlier draft of this line said 7–10 — and nothing anywhere in the repo cites a runbook step by number, checked before renumbering).

- **Gate 1, run the suite inside the sterilized tree.** The mirror deliberately removes files the suite reads, so a test that reads one passes here and errors there — `tests/test_adversarial_review_gate.py` read `CLAUDE.md` and failed 3 tests in the sterilized tree that the source repo passed (Phase-160 follow-up, `ade2e1e`). The step states why it and the public branch protection are **not** the same check: public `main` requires `pytest` on the snapshot PR, so a failure surfaces in public at the worst moment, while the tester repo has no CI at all, so without this step a broken suite ships to testers unobserved.
- **Gate 2, scan public *history*, not the built tree.** **The command was executed against the live public repo before being written down**, per author-side rule 3: a full clone, `git rev-list HEAD` = **17** commits, per-commit token-scoped Pass 1a → the two most recent clean and **15 carrying one leaking line each** (14 at `PHASE_LOG.md:1121`; the oldest, `cb6b4f4`, carries the same line at `:1115` — an earlier draft of this entry gave the one coordinate universally) — reproducing the 2026-07-31 finding exactly, which is what makes the prescribed command a verified one rather than a plausible one.
- **A scope correction the brief's framing glossed.** Gate 2 is a *public*-repo gate: the public repo accumulates history through snapshot PRs, while the tester repo is force-pushed to a fresh root, so `git rev-list HEAD` there only ever shows one commit. But force-push **unreferences; it does not erase** — anything that shipped stays retrievable by SHA and is already in every tester's clone. The step says so, so the tester repo's exemption is not read as safety.
- **The `## Refreshing` section was a documented bypass.** It is the block actually used for a re-push and it went build → remote → force-push, routing around every verify step above it. It now names steps 3, 4 and 5 inline as running on the rebuilt tree. This is Phase 170's rule — inserting a step means auditing what routes *to* it — applied at authoring time rather than found by the round.
- **The tester announcement is bound in the same section**, with both prior failures named (144–145 unannounced; then 147–160 pushed 2026-07-29 against a thread last updated 2026-07-24). The brief records the binding; the runbook is where an operator stands.
- **The step-3 pass list had drifted from the script it wraps** — it enumerated 1a/1b/2/3 while `make_public_mirror.sh` emits 1a/1b/**1c**/2/**2b**/3, and Pass 2 has been a diff against the published snapshot rather than an eyeball-everything since Phase 120. The list is corrected and now says the script is the source of truth for it, which is the failure mode a hand-maintained copy has.

**What leg 3 does *not* close.** `REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md` § Medium's sterilized-tree item asks for a CI job or `self_check` target that builds the mirror and runs its suite **on every phase rather than every cut**. Writing the gate into the cut-time runbook is a different thing and a weaker one; the item stays open with a note saying so. Recorded because ticking it here would have been the overclaim this project's rounds keep finding.

**Guards, because the whole leg exists as work nothing caught for five phases.** Three modules, two new:

- `tests/test_monograph_figure_labels.py` — no SVG `<text>` may name the retired architecture, and every `/claim-task` step a diagram cites must be a step the **shipped skill defines**, with the defined set read from `SKILL.md` rather than transcribed. **The structural scoping is the load-bearing property:** Phase 176 built a general prose screen for this family, measured it, and got eleven hits of which all eleven were correct prose. A figure label has no room for a tense marker, so a retired term in one is unconditionally a defect — and the module's control pins the other direction, requiring that the monograph's correct past-tense pull-quote stays green, so the guard can never push the project to delete honest history to go green.
- `tests/test_mirror_runbook_gates.py` — a **declared** reversion guard, said so in its docstring rather than implied. It asserts structure (a pytest invocation against the built tree, a `git rev-list` commit walk, the refresh-path pointer, the announcement binding) rather than sentences, so an ordinary rewrite stays green; that direction has its own negative control. Two further controls: a gate moved out of the numbered Steps into `## Notes` must still report missing, and each gate removed *alone* must be detected.
- `tests/test_doc_currency.py` extended. The masthead's `Issue N` and its `YYYY.MM.DD` date had **never been in the guard's population**, so a currency pass could bump the hero stat and both colophon stamps and leave the masthead silently behind. **The first draft of this bullet then claimed that was "exactly the state the tree was in when this phase opened", and it was not** — at `4eadd99` all four sites read 159 together, and a reviewer ran the new module against that exact file and got six passes. The entry also contradicted itself four paragraphs later ("Stamps: 159 → 177, across all five sites"). What the extension actually buys is **partial-pass detection**, which is real and smaller than claimed; uniform staleness is out of scope by Phase 118's ruling that the monograph is a dated snapshot allowed to lag. All four number sites and both date notations must now agree, and the population control mutates **each site alone** so a guard reading three of four cannot pass.

**Stamps: 159 → 177, 2026-07-28 → 2026-08-02**, across all five sites.

**Adversarial round: run — three lenses (guards real / claims true / does it execute), two of the three on a different model than the author.** Sizing recorded, because the governor requires it: this bundle **ships behaviour** (three guard modules are code) **and** its record makes numeric claims a reviewer could falsify, so both terms of the escalation condition hold and the third lens is licensed by the rule rather than by preference. Reviewers were given the revision-verification-first instruction with an explicit stop, read-only lenses were told to use `git show`, and the guards lens — which must mutate — was given its own `git clone --branch` under `/tmp`. All three confirmed the correct revision; the worktree trap that landed all of Phase 176's reviewers on `main` did not recur.

**The author-side battery was worth nothing again, and this is the sixth phase in a row.** Reported: 20 defect mutations, 0 survivors, 5 controls, 0 false alarms. The guards lens wrote **46 mutations and watched 21 survive**, plus **18 negative controls of which 12 reddened** — the false-alarm direction I had barely probed, and the one that gets guards deleted rather than fixed.

**The three findings that mattered most were all in a guard's *premise*, not its wiring.**

1. **A "declared reversion guard" that could not detect deletion of its own subject.** Renaming or deleting `TESTER_MIRROR_RUNBOOK.md` made all six of its tests **skip and exit 0** — the mirror-exclusion skip, which I had copied deliberately from the Phase-160 lesson, swallowed precisely the failure the module exists to catch. The fix distinguishes "sterilized mirror" from "source repo, file deleted" using three *independent* markers, none of them the runbook.
2. **The runbook guard's announcement and command never had to co-occur**, though its docstring said they must. Deleting the suite step and re-homing its command under step 9 — *"Enable Discussions on `wade-cms/sysop-tester`"* — passed, because `suite|test` matched **5 of 10 steps** in a document about a *tester* repo. Two of my own predicates had the same over-breadth for the same reason (step 10's first line contains "no history"), which is why titles are now the bolded lead rather than the whole line.
3. **The site my own record calls "the most load-bearing of the four" was covered by no guard at all.** I fixed `:1366` and then guarded everything except it. It is prose, so a screen is the wrong instrument; it now carries a *positive* assertion — the entry must name planner, reviewer and executor — which a reversion to the retired sentence cannot satisfy.

**Six more survivors were ordinary authoring, not adversarial input:** a non-breaking hyphen, an en dash, an HTML entity, and a two-line wrapped `<tspan>` label all walked through a vocabulary matched as raw substrings. Labels are normalized now. Six more were population holes — `aria-label`, SVG `<title>`, `<desc>`, `<figcaption>`, and `docs/index.html` were all unread. A **commented-out** command satisfied the history gate, and so did `git rev-list -n 1 HEAD` and `git rev-list HEAD -- README.md`: a tree read wearing the command's name, which is the exact defect gate 2 exists for.

**One survivor is declared rather than closed.** A label can still evade by paraphrase — *"the sub-agent grades its own findings"* names the retired property using none of the vocabulary. Closing that needs semantics, not a pattern, so it is out of reach *in kind* rather than unattempted; the positive assertions are the partial answer, since a paraphrase of the wrong shape cannot satisfy a check that the right shape is stated. A second is declared **by design**: drifting every stamp back together still passes, because Phase 118 ruled the monograph a dated snapshot allowed to lag and a never-behind ratchet was deliberately not built.

## Phase 178 (executed 2026-08-02 — Step 4a's shared append files: the conflict Sysop prescribes and then aborts on, and the unmerged branch three later steps treat as merged)

**Upstream #307, filed 2026-08-02 and picked as the next phase because it is the only open item with unrecoverable data loss on a path this repo runs daily.** Every coordinate in the filing verified byte-exact against the tree before use — the rule Phase 176 broke while citing it, and the first batch-4 entry where nothing had drifted.

**The bundle premise did not survive the sweep, and dropping it is this phase's first product.** The filing said to bundle #307 with **#237** as *"one unit, Step 4a's shared-file conflicts."* #237 reports that Step 7 allocates `ISSUE-NNNN` **per-worktree** so parallel branches collide, and that *"Step 4a presents it as an ordinary content conflict."* Neither half holds here. `WORKFLOW.md`'s § 8.2b friction-log paragraph states the in-flow capture mechanism **is** `/review-close` Step 7, which runs on `main`; of the four skills that execute inside a worktree — `/claim-task`, `/document-work`, `/auto-fix`, `/auto-judge` — the friction-mention counts are **0, 0, 0, 0**, and `/auto-build`'s single hit is a speculative "the first cycle will surface friction" line. More decisively, **Step 7 contains no `git add` and no `git commit`, and no `git add` site anywhere in the skill names `sysop/SYSOP_ISSUES.md`** — so nothing commits the file, and Step 4a rebases commits. #237's cheapest-first fix ("one sentence in Step 4a") would have shipped a sentence about a conflict Sysop's own skills cannot produce: Phase 155's disqualifying shape, caught before it was written rather than by a round. **The round narrowed this and the narrowing matters:** `sysop/SYSOP_ISSUES.md` is a *tracked* file that Step 7 leaves dirty, and nothing stops a human committing it on a branch — the reporter's own incident describes a real conflict-resolution event. So the correct claim is "through no Sysop-prescribed command", not "never", and calling the reporter's fix flatly inert overreached. The ID collision is real, but it reaches a merge through the *uncommitted-file* path that **#311** already describes, so #237 is re-filed onto #311. **Fifth phase running where the filed defect was right and the filed reasoning was wrong** — and the first where the reasoning error would have changed which file got edited.

**The corruption reproduces exactly as filed, and this phase's "worse than filed" correction was itself the error.** A two-branch repro confirms the mechanism: git splits the entry into two hunks and leaves every field the two entries **share** outside the markers as common context, so a marker-strip union starves one entry and still parses under `yaml.safe_load` with unique ids. But the *count* is fixture-dependent, and the phase's first draft published its own fixture as a correction to the reporter. With **identical titles** the starved entry keeps `id:` alone — 1 of 10. With **different titles** — the realistic case for two unrelated follow-ups, and evidently the reporter's — the first hunk carries `id:` + `title:` and the union leaves **2 of 10, exactly as filed**. The round caught this; the filing was right and the correction was wrong. The same applies to the shipped field list, which named `surfaced_by`/`effort`/`blast_radius`/`depends_on` as always-outside: `surfaced_by` lands *inside* the markers whenever it differs, which it typically will. What is not fixture-dependent, and is the load-bearing part: **any** marker-strip union corrupts, parses, keeps ids unique, and is caught by `validate_tasks.py` with the errors the skill quotes — all four verified verbatim.

**Leg 1 — Step 4a routes conflicts instead of aborting.** `:807` said *"If rebase has conflicts: `git rebase --abort`, report the conflict, skip that branch"* unconditionally, four lines above prose telling the reader to resolve rather than abort. A new § names the two files every branch appends to as a matter of workflow — `tasks/index.yml` (whose `/document-work` carve-out is quoted verbatim, after the first draft cited a `§ *Do NOT modify*` heading that **does not exist**; asserting the ground truth instead of citing it is Phase 173's rule and this phase broke it once) and `review_tasks.md` — and prescribes structural resolution from the merge stages. **Stage numbering was verified by execution, not recalled:** stage 2 is the merge target, stage 3 the commit being replayed. `git rev-list --count <branch> ^HEAD` replaced `git merge-base --is-ancestor` after both were checked to agree on all three cases (merged, merged-sibling, never-merged), because `_shared/permission-guard.md` enumerates `rev-list` in the documented auto-approved read-only set and does **not** enumerate `merge-base` — and that file is explicit that treating an unlisted subcommand as read-only is an inference.

**Leg 2 — Step 4c filters on merge containment before it routes.** Wade's call between a 4a-side rollback and a 4c-side filter; the filter wins because it covers every skip path rather than the one 4a produces. Step 3b copies each approved branch's pending-doc to main *before* the merge is attempted (deliberately — it is what stops `git worktree remove` destroying it), so a branch that fails at 4a leaves a doc that Step 4c would route, flipping its `roadmap_ids` to `done`, `git mv`-ing the body to `archive/` and dropping the task's lock and parked markers **with the code never merged**. Step 3b's own rollback covers only its own skip and says so. The enabling fact for the filter is that **Step 6 is the only step that deletes feature branches and it runs after Step 4c**, so at filter time every branch this close merged still has a local ref — which makes a missing ref an unexplained state rather than a legacy quirk, and the step stops and asks rather than guessing in either direction.

**Leg 3 — the `pr` force-delete is gated on containment.** `:1261` iterated *"each **approved** feature branch"*, asserted it *"reached `main` through a squash"*, and ran `git branch -D` with safe `-d` **explicitly bypassed as meaningless against a squash**. A 4a-skipped branch is still approved, is not Step 2a `dirty`-SKIP'd, is not rejected — so it fell through every carve-out, and Step 3b had already removed its worktree, making the ref the last reference to the work. `direct` never had the hole because its list iterates *merged* branches and safe `-d` refuses; **the bypass is what removed the backstop**, which is why the guard is stated on the licence rather than added to the list. A `4a-SKIP` block now preserves branch and lock under both policies, and Step 8's report gained a line for it.

**The specs moved with the skill.** Phase 170's finding was that `WORKFLOW.md` was the root cause and the skill was implementing it faithfully; the same held here. § 2.8's close-out steps 5, 7 and 10 each carried the identical gap — no conflict routing, no consolidation filter, an unqualified force-delete — and all three were corrected.

**The guard found a defect in this phase's own prose, and it was the right kind.** The first draft of Step 4a step 3 read *"resolve it per the next section, then `git rebase --continue`"* — so a reader who stopped at step 3 was told to continue with nothing checked. The ordering property caught it; the fix was the prose, not the guard.

**Two defects in this phase's own mutation battery, both the classes prior phases wrote down.** (1) A `str.replace` whose anchor did not match is a silent no-op that scores as a **survivor** and indicts an innocent guard — Phase 172's *"a battery can lie about its own baseline"*, now refused explicitly by comparing the mutated text against the original. (2) An unscoped `_swap` aimed at Step 4a's validator command hit the **allow-rule line at the top of the file** instead, left the step untouched, and again scored as a survivor — Phase 170's first-occurrence retargeting rule, biting the battery written to honour it. Both are fixed in `tools/phase178_mutations.py`, and the region-scoping helper carries the reason.

**The author-side battery reported 15/15 killed and 6/6 controls green at commit time, and BOTH numbers were false.** Re-run on the committed tree it is **14/15** — the survivor (`index.yml dropped from the conflict context`) appeared because the last prose edit before committing, swapping the fabricated `§` citation for a verbatim quote, added `tasks/index.yml` mentions into that guard's 400-character proximity window. **Phase 170 wrote the exact rule this broke** — after adding text, re-run the *neighbouring* guards and read the survivors — one phase after this project last paid for it. And one of the six "controls" was `replace("FEAT-", "TECH-")` against a file containing **zero** `FEAT-`: a no-op scoring green, so the real control count was **5**. The no-op refusal this phase wrote for exactly that class was wired to `MUTATIONS` and never to `CONTROLS`. Two survivors in the *first* run were also battery bugs rather than guard gaps (a no-op `replace`, and an unscoped `_swap` retargeting onto the allow-rule line at the top of the file). **Final, after the round's fixes: 20 mutations / 20 killed / 0 survivors, 6 controls / 6 green / 0 false alarms** — with the dead control replaced, the stale anchors re-resolved, and four new mutations covering the polarity class the round showed was entirely unguarded.

**Suite: 2479 → 2510 passed + 4 skipped + 0 failed**, read off a full run on the final tree rather than derived, with the two new modules' test counts measured (23 prose + 8 executable = 31) rather than assumed: 2479 + 31 = 2510, and the arithmetic closes exactly. **The number in this sentence has been wrong twice already and both errors are worth keeping.** The first draft claimed **2498 passed, 0 failed** — wrong on the count *and* on the failure — and was measured on a tree that straddled the edits to `CLAUDE.md` / `PHASE_LOG.md` / the checklist, so it described no single revision (Phase 177's sterilized-tree defect, one file over). The second draft corrected it to **2497 passed + 1 failed** on the pre-squash working commit `0d12397` (a branch commit, so **not reachable from `main`** — the phase squash-merged as `443b1f0`, and that is the hash a reader can resolve), where the failure was the structural `test_round_yield_ledger` red — the ledger row records the round's yield and so cannot precede it. That row now exists, so the suite is green. **A third defect surfaced only on the final run:** the `"$TMPDIR"` scratch-file fix tripped `test_every_skill_guards_tmpdir_with_a_fallback`, because Phase 153's finding has a live drift guard requiring `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}` (`TMPDIR` is unset on most Linux shells). Fixed; the guard did its job on a change made by the phase citing it. The arithmetic closes and is worth stating because it names the red: 2479 baseline + **19** new guard tests = 2498, **minus 1** for `test_round_yield_ledger`, which flips from green to red the moment a `CLAUDE.md` Phase log row exists without a ledger row. That red is **structural and expected** — the row records the round's yield and so cannot precede the round — and it goes green when the round's row lands. It is named here rather than netted out, per the same rule Phase 177's record set. **The first measurement was also taken on a mixed tree**: a background run straddled the edits to `CLAUDE.md` / `PHASE_LOG.md` / the checklist, so its numbers described no single revision — Phase 177's sterilized-tree defect, one file over, and the reason this figure names the commit it was measured on. New guard: `tests/test_step4a_shared_file_conflicts.py`, 19 tests, asserting **ordering and structural properties** rather than token presence — the check that first-occurrence ordering held while the prescribed command moved out of its fenced block is the one that caught the battery's mis-target.

**Gate: the round ran, three lenses (guards / claims / behaviour), one on a different model, over `f55e44d`** — a pre-squash working commit, cited because it is what the reviewers actually read; it does not survive into `main`, where the phase lands as `443b1f0`. **It disqualified the phase as committed and the fix pass below is most of the work.** No reviewer got `isolation: "worktree"` — the filed defect that it builds from the *default branch* would have handed all three a tree with none of this work in it, since the phase lives on a feature branch.

**The guards lens is the headline: 52 mutations, 3 killed, 49 SURVIVED**, against my reported 15/15. My battery was not wrong so much as unrepresentative — every one of its mutations deleted or inverted a string the guard literally pinned. **Two of the three legs could be deleted wholesale with the suite green:** the reviewer replaced the entire Step 4c filter with a note saying it *"was dropped as unnecessary; consolidate every pending-doc"*, retaining only the pinned phrases, and all 19 tests passed. **Every polarity in the change was unguarded** — flipping *"`0` means merged"* to *"`0` means NOT merged"* passed, which inverts leg 2 into dropping exactly the merged docs and consolidating exactly the unmerged ones; so did a cross-file variant where the skill and the spec disagree. The ordering guards measured a 46-character gap inside one clause while the *prescribed command* sat 2,815 characters later, so relocating it — the actual defect — passed. **This is the sixth phase running whose round beat the author's battery**, and the first where the ratio was this bad.

**The behaviour lens found four HIGH defects by running the recipe, none of which any prose guard could see.** (1) **Union-by-id silently discards branch-side *modifications*** — a retriage or a `deferred` move on a branch is dropped wholesale and the validator goes green, because the merge target's file is internally consistent on its own. (2) **Two branches filing the same auto-numbered id annihilate one task**, and the companion `tasks/open/<ID>.md` `add/add` conflict commits its `<<<<<<<` markers, since neither `validate_tasks.py` nor the shipped `pre-commit` scans for them. (3) **Step 6's `pr` containment check can never return its pass value** — `rev-list ^origin/main` *is* an ancestry test and a squash breaks ancestry, so it scores non-zero for a correctly merged branch and a 4a-SKIP'd one alike: an inert cleanup and every clean close reported as suspect. My own paragraph two lines above says the branch is *"**not** an ancestor"*, so the change contradicted itself. **It was also a self-initiated scope addition** — #307 asked for a carve-out on the skip path, which had already shipped correctly — and the addition was the broken half. (4) **Unquoted `^HEAD` is a negated glob under zsh `extended_glob`**, so the exclusion is silently dropped, the operands become pathspecs, and a *merged* branch classifies `NOT-MERGED` on every close; measured `0` quoted against `2` unquoted. The one case an author would spot-check — an unmerged branch — returns non-zero either way and looks correct.

**The claims lens found the phase re-entering the data loss it exists to close.** Step 4c's **own** cleanup item said *"Delete all remaining `sysop/runtime/pending-docs/*.md` files"*, five items after the new 1b deliberately holds one back; the worktree is already gone and the doc is untracked, so that delete is unrecoverable — BeanRider ISSUE-0050 again, re-entered by the fix for it. It also caught `:450` still asserting an invariant this change breaks (and which its own next clause had always contradicted), `WORKFLOW.md` step 10's `direct` arm still unqualified, and the two false battery numbers above.

**And it retired this phase's own headline as an error.** The "1 of 10 fields, worse than filed" correction is fixture-dependent; with differing titles it is **2 of 10, exactly as filed**. Five phases of "the filed reasoning was wrong" made the sixth assume it — the reporter was right and the correction was the mistake. Corrected at all four sites.

**The guards lens also found a population gap the phase's own rule should have caught:** `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md` is a **third** restatement of these steps, shipped to every consumer, still describing the old behaviour — and the new guard's spec-agreement block did not include it. Precedent for guarding all three files already existed in three sibling test modules.

**Disposition — everything fixed, nothing deferred.** Step 6's containment check **deleted** rather than repaired (keyed on the 4a-SKIP verdict the phase already introduced); Step 4c's cleanup scoped to what it consolidated; `^` operands quoted in both files; the union rule given explicit modify / duplicate-id / outside-`tasks:` clauses with the stage-1 diff that makes them detectable; `git add` stated on the resolve path; exit 1 and exit 2 split to different actions; the gate's coverage scoped to `tasks/index.yml` (`validate_tasks.py` has zero knowledge of `review_tasks.md`); scratch files moved to `"$TMPDIR"`; `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md` brought into the population.

**The guard layer was rebuilt, and the rebuild is the phase's real product.** `tests/test_step4a_shared_file_behaviour.py` (8 tests) builds real git repositories and *runs* the recipe: it pins the corruption and the validator's exact error strings, asserts the stage numbering against git rather than against a sentence, drives the full resolution through `rebase --continue`, proves the containment test separates merged from unmerged pre-squash **and is invalid post-squash** — that test exists specifically to stop Step 6's defect returning — and pins the zsh quoting hazard. The prose module keeps the ordering properties and gained polarity, cross-file-agreement and cleanup pins. `_section` now fails with a named diagnostic instead of erroring all 19 tests when a heading is renamed, which was one of five over-strictness false alarms the round measured.

**CI then found a vacuity hole in the new fixture — the same class the round had just spent three lenses on, in the tests written to answer it.** All eight executable tests passed locally and failed on the PR. Cause: `_init` ran a bare `git init`, and the runner's git has no `init.defaultBranch`, so it defaulted to `master` while every fixture names `main` — each `main` reference erroring. **The fixture did not notice, because its conflict check was `assert r.returncode != 0`, and `fatal: invalid upstream 'main'` satisfies that exactly as well as a conflict does.** It reported "expected a rebase conflict" while nothing had conflicted. Fixed at both levels: the branch name is pinned with `git symbolic-ref` (portable across git versions, unlike `init -b`), and the check now asserts the conflict **state** — unmerged index entries, naming `tasks/index.yml` — rather than an exit code. Verified by planting the defect back under a `master`-defaulting git and confirming the fixture errors with the named diagnostic. A second CI-only defect went with it: `zsh` is absent from the runner, and a missing binary raises `FileNotFoundError` rather than returning non-zero, so the skip guard never fired. **The lesson is the phase's own, arriving one layer down:** an exit code is not evidence of the state you wanted, which is the identical shape as Step 6's containment check being an ancestry test — and this repo's rule that a green from a run that did nothing must never read like a green from a run that did.

**A recorded defect repeated verbatim — the `✓` the same commit denied.** `f55e44d` committed the `CLAUDE.md` row as `| _pending_ | ✓ |` while `PHASE_LOG.md` in that same commit said the round had **not** run, against a gate whose own words are *"a phase is not done until an adversarial round has run."* This exact defect is already written up in this file for an earlier phase, including the observation that the table supports partial states (row 60b: `rubric ✓ · dogfood ☐`), so it was expressible and simply was not done — **twice now**. Reading the log is not the same as applying it, and a `✓` is the one cell in that table that asserts the gate.

**One over-strict guard of my own, caught by my own re-run:** the post-squash test first asserted `rev-list --count` appeared nowhere in Step 6, and reddened on the blockquote *explaining why the check is wrong*. Scoped to prescriptive lines. That is the failure direction Phase 175 named, and it took one iteration to hit it.

## Phase 179 (executed 2026-08-02/03, squash-merged as `d0de051` (#320) — upstream #280: the placeholder section that authorises a skip, the remedy a consumer cannot reach, and the replacement remedy that was also wrong)

**Upstream #280, filed 2026-07-30 by GDP through `/report-issues`, picked because it is a wrong result inside a *security* gate and because its cheap half is separable from its expensive half.** The installer coordinates were verified before use and all hold: `apply_substitutions()` is hard-gated to `*/checks.yml` at `install.sh:1573-1578`, the installer says so in its own output at `:1690-1691`, and both review skills ship in **both** install modes (`install_skills` / `install_convention_map` / `install_security_map` are unconditional in `run_install_pipeline`; neither skill is in `LOOP_EXCLUDE_SKILLS`).

**The reported number reproduces exactly, and reproducing it found something the report did not contain.** A python+postgres+nextjs+llm install assembles **26** sections whose header globs are still in `<…>` form — verified by running the installer, not by summing sources. 25 are pack sections (10 python + 2 postgres + 7 nextjs-react + 6 llm), every one *wholly* placeholder; the 26th is core's `` ## `Dockerfile`, `<datajobs Dockerfile>`, `.dockerignore` — Container Build ``, which is **mixed**: it resolves through `Dockerfile` and its Check/Skip lists legitimately bind that file. GDP's planned mitigation (`TECH-MAPS-CHECKS-REGISTRY-COVERAGE`) pins a derived structural test — *"no `## ` header contains a `<…>` token"* — and that predicate condemns the mixed section too. GDP's tree has a root `Dockerfile` **and** `.dockerignore` (checked in the clone at `~/Projects/gdp-query-system`), so as designed the mitigation drops real coverage of files it actually has. The derived-not-authored instinct was right; the predicate is one token too broad. The corrected form is **"no section whose globs resolve to zero tracked files carries a `Skip:` line"** — same discipline, and mixed sections exempt themselves. That is the correction owed on the issue, and `test_mixed_glob_sections_exist_so_the_last_sentence_stays_load_bearing` pins the premise it rests on.

**The fix is authority, not assembly — and the phase deliberately declined the assembly half.** The report's proposed fixes (extend substitution to markdown; suppress pack sections superseded by an overlay) are not two changes but three interlocking ones, and fix 1 alone makes the file *worse*: a substituted section carries a real glob, so it reads as authoritative and duplicates the consumer's localized section — precisely the double-cover `SKILL.md:190` forbids. Suppression is computable only *through* the substitutions map, so it depends on substitution; and any placeholder a consumer never mapped still needs an omit rule. All three mutate the artifact every consumer's security gate reads, on every update, and reopen Phase 55's deliberate revert (`PHASE_LOG.md:458` — whole-file substitution rewrote headers into junk like `## __disabled_no_op__/*.py — Auth`). Parked, with the trigger recorded as **fired, hazard defused, structural fix still demand-gated**.

**Leg 1 — the § Scope note.** A byte-identical paragraph in all six `security_map.md` **pack sources**: a section binds only the files its globs actually match, so a placeholder section scopes no checks and authorises no exclusion; a mixed glob list binds exactly what its concrete globs match. It ships through the existing concat with **zero installer change** (zero installer change is verified directly — `git diff <parent>..HEAD -- install.sh` is empty. Round 1's record offered a `1 file changed, 6 insertions(+)` measurement as its evidence; that number was **borrowed from a reviewer's differently-packed run** and does not reproduce for the pack set the paragraph is about, which is 10 insertions across 8 changed files.
