The conclusion held; the evidence was not measured here), and it reaches every reader of the assembled file rather than only the skills. **Scoped to the security maps on a measured premise:** `Skip:` lines appear in the six security maps (36) and in **zero** convention maps, so the negative-routing hazard is security-map-specific; `test_convention_maps_carry_no_skip_lists` pins that premise so the scoping self-invalidates rather than outliving its reason.

**Leg 2 — the Skip-authority sites, and the count was wrong by eight.** The phase filed two; the class is **ten**, all ten now scoped. Round 1 found seven more and round 2 found the tenth — `WORKFLOW.md:278`, which round 1's fix pass *listed as scoped and never touched*, in § 2.6, earlier in the document than all three sites that were scoped, so a linear reader met the unqualified version first. Beyond the Step 4 dispatch line and the do-not-report guard: `security-audit/SKILL.md`'s dispatch list item 4 (*"Instructions to **SKIP** checks the map says are irrelevant"* — the line that literally enters each sub-agent's prompt), the skill preamble at `:11` that invites agents to substitute placeholders mentally, `/auto-fix` (a fourth consumer of the same lists, `SKILL.md:189-193`), `WORKFLOW.md` at `:278`, `:437`, `:1110` and the blank security-map template at `:1057-1063` that a new project copies — **four** sites in that file, not three; round 1's record listed the template separately from "`WORKFLOW.md` ×3" and so double-counted it, which is how an enumeration of ten came to assert nine. And `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md:144`. **The filed count being smaller than the real class is now the rule, not the exception** — Phases 169, 172, 173 and 175 each recorded it, and this is the fifth.

**Leg 3 shipped a false remedy, and then shipped a second false remedy in its place.** `security-audit/SKILL.md:204` and `codebase-review/SKILL.md:190` (both Phase 141, `8083e2c`) said *"The fix there is localizing that section's glob (or its `substitutions.project.yml` token) — never a new duplicate section"*: the token has zero effect on markdown and the in-place edit is reverted on update, so the only reachable action was the overlay the same sentence called *"never."* **The replacement was wrong in the opposite direction.** It routed to the `.project.md` overlay as *"the only durable write target for map content"* — and `_shared/promotion-write-target.md` has a section titled **"Why not overlay-only"** stating that skills read the **base** maps at review time, so an overlay-only write *"would be invisible until the next `sysop-update.sh` re-ran the concat."* The same partial names `.claude/security_map.project.md` as staged by the **Step 2a coverage commit** — the exact step being edited. A consumer following the replacement would have localized a section and seen nothing change: #280's own symptom, re-shipped as its fix. The canonical answer already existed in the tree and the phase did not consult it. Both sites now prescribe the **dual-write**, gated on `.claude/sysop.lock` because a source repo has no overlay at all — the consumer-install guard every sibling rule in that step already carried and this one lacked.

**The same overlay-only error was already shipped, and it is part of #280's root cause.** `packs/python/companion/convention_map.md:11` — the preamble the reporter quoted — said *"Localized sections belong in the never-managed `.claude/convention_map.project.md` overlay."* That is the instruction they followed. It now states the dual-write. So the reporter did not merely hit a dead end; they hit a documented path that was itself inert for the round that used it.

**A public page still described the behaviour this phase retired.** `docs/packs.md` — the "Anatomy of a pack rule" page Phase 120 wrote *specifically* to explain placeholder-map semantics, i.e. the canonical public answer to #280's question — said *"`/security-audit` resolves placeholders by inference … so it works against the maps as shipped."* Both skills now treat a placeholder section as binding nothing, so the page contrasted the two skills in the direction that matters and was false on the security side. Rewritten, and it now carries the dual-write rule to the surface a consumer would actually read.

**Gate: the round ran, three lenses (guards / claims / behaviour) over `d1ee973`** — a pre-squash working commit, cited because it is what the reviewers actually read; it is **not reachable from `main`**, where the phase lands as `d0de051`. Round 2 read `853f4d0` and the final fix pass is `f64bbef`, both likewise branch-only. The round over `d1ee973` and it disqualified the phase as committed.** The third lens is licensed by the governor's condition — the change ships guards *and* a record making numeric claims. No reviewer was given `isolation: "worktree"`: Phase 178 recorded that it builds from the **default branch**, which would have handed all three a tree without this work. Reviewers were told to copy the repo to `/tmp` before mutating and to leave the working tree alone.

**The guards lens is the headline: 79 mutations, 32 of 62 defect mutations surviving (52%), against my reported 10/10.** Its decisive result was a single simultaneous mutation reversing **all three legs** — the note told to honour unlocalized Skip lines, dispatch told to *"let a placeholder Skip stand as the reason a category went unaudited"*, the remedy gutted to *"editing the assembled map in place works fine in practice"* — with the entire suite green. The guards detected deletion and nothing else. Leg (b) was effectively unguarded (12 of 14), including the deletion of its **only operational sentence**, which nothing pinned. The dead remedy was revivable by dropping its parentheses or swapping one ASCII apostrophe for a curly one — the guard written specifically to prevent #280's defect, bypassed by typography. And **nothing guarded the artifact #280 is about**: a plausible dedup filter in `install_security_map()` stripped the note from every consumer install with the whole suite passing.

**My own author-side pass had already caught a weaker version of this and I still under-corrected.** Battery 1 was ten mutations, 10/10 killed, and worthless — every one deleted text a guard literally pinned, which measures wiring, not coverage, and is the exact failure `_shared/adversarial-review.md` § *Before you spawn anyone* describes. Battery 2 (bypass-shaped, 8 mutations) found **5 survivors** plus 2 more that died only on Phase 141's parity guard, meaning a symmetric two-sided edit would have passed. I strengthened the pins to whole sentences and reported 20/20 — and the independent lens then ran 79 and watched 32 through. **The round beat the author's battery, as it has in every phase since at least 167** — the exact ordinal is unstateable, because this file's own numbering collides (Phases 177 and 178 both claim "sixth"), and round 2 was right to refuse the count rather than inherit it. What `tools/ROUND_YIELD_LEDGER.md` does support: 167, 172, 175 and 176 each ran a corrective author pass and were beaten anyway. So did this one.

**The claims lens found the record asserting a green suite that the commit does not produce.** `PHASE_LOG` said *"2510 → 2520 passed + 4 skipped + 0 failed, measured on a full run of the final tree."* The commit is **red**: `test_round_yield_ledger.py::test_every_phase_from_174_has_a_ledger_row` fails because a `CLAUDE.md` Phase log row exists for 179 with no ledger row. The 2520 was measured *before* the `CLAUDE.md` row went in — derived, not measured on the final tree, which is the discipline Phase 178's record claims for itself one entry earlier. All five prior phases (174–178) landed the ledger row in the same commit as the table row; this one broke that shape. It also found: an invented reader (`claude-security` was named as reading the assembled map — it has **zero** references to `security_map`, and Sysop's relationship with it runs the other way through Phase 144's ingest; real non-`/security-audit` readers include `/test-audit` and `/auto-fix`), the *"two Skip-authority statements"* undercount above, a `test_convention_maps_carry_no_skip_lines` that pinned one spelling while the record claimed a self-invalidating premise, and three overstatements — *"discovered by glob rather than authored"* (core is named explicitly), *"three of the ten are anti-vacuity guards"* (one was a string pin), and a claimed authority for *"editing the assembled map is forbidden by the pack preamble"* that exists only in the convention map's preamble, not in any security map's.

**And it found two corrections I claimed to have made and had not.** The parked Phase-120 entry carried **two mutually exclusive bolded dispositions** — *"TRIGGER FIRED — un-park."* and *"STILL PARKED"* — and my STATUS paragraph asserted that the `install.sh:1218-1221` citation drift was *"applied above"* and the *"works as shipped"* assessment *"struck"*, when neither edit had been made. Worse, the § High entry carrying the **correct** `:1573-1578` citation moved to the archive in the same commit, so the checklist's only surviving citation for that mechanism was the stale one. Fixed: one disposition, the citation corrected in place, the assessment struck with #280 named as what refutes it.

**The behaviour lens ran the thing and confirmed the delivery while finding the dual-write contradiction above.** Verified by execution: the full install (5 note copies, each the last preamble paragraph before its pack's first `---`, no mangling under `od -c`); loop mode (both maps and both skills ship, note present); idempotency (`git status` empty after re-install *and* after `--update`, so Phase 148's content-anchored lock is unaffected); the real upgrade path from the parent commit; and the substitution path — installing with `<api module>: myapi` yields **0** replacements in either markdown map — and a pack-set-dependent count in `checks.yml` (14 for python alone, 23 for the four-pack set; round 1's record quoted 17 with no pack set named, matching none of them) — so the note's own literal `` `<api module>/` `` cannot be corrupted. It also established that **nothing machine-parses these maps** — the only non-test consumer is `concat_files`, a byte-level append — so a `>` blockquote containing the strings `Skip:` and `<api module>/` cannot be mistaken for a section, a glob or a Skip list.

**One reviewer disagreement was resolved by measurement rather than by averaging.** The behaviour lens reported four suite failures and diagnosed three as pre-existing (`test_install_concat` ×2, `test_install_runtime_migration` ×1), root-caused to a system `python3` without PyYAML. The claims lens reported one. Re-run under the canonical invocation those three **pass** in 33s: the behaviour lens had verified them "at parent" in a throwaway clone, which has no `.venv`, so its diagnosis was correct about its own environment and wrong about the repo. Only the ledger red is real. *Reviewer agreement is not evidence — and neither is reviewer disagreement.*

**The guard module was rebuilt — and round 2 retired the claim that the rebuild is this phase's real product.** `tests/test_placeholder_section_authority.py` (13 tests) now pins **whole sentences inside the block that governs them** rather than fragments anywhere in a 1,100-line file; reads `_rendered()` text with HTML comments and fenced blocks stripped; folds typography before the dead-remedy absence check; matches a Skip *list* by shape (`**Skip:**`, `**Skip**:`, `- **Skip**:`, bare `Skip:`) rather than by one spelling — and deliberately **not** by bare `Skip\b`, which reddens on *"Skip generated migration files…"*, ordinary prose in a conventions document; carries a `_DEMOTION` check for the class where a rule is left byte-perfect and framed as non-authoritative (*"Superseded — do not follow:"*, *"Editorial aside, not an instruction:"*, *"Historically … no longer required"*); and **installs into a temp consumer and asserts the note survives into the assembled `.claude/security_map.md`** — the artifact the whole issue is about, which no guard previously read.

**The rebuilt battery reported 28/28 on a red baseline before it reported 28/28 on a green one.** The first run scored every mutation as killed *and* reddened all three controls, because the dual-write rewrite had removed the phrase Phase 141's `test_2a0_guards_partial_localization_and_routes_to_localizing` pinned — so the suite was already failing and every result was a false kill. This is Phase 172's *"a battery can lie about its own baseline"*, and the harness now refuses to run without asserting a green baseline first. Corrected, the honest first number was **24/28 with four survivors**, all one class: the pinned sentence present but reframed by a neighbour. `_DEMOTION` plus a line-start assertion closed them — and the line-start rule then had to be **scoped**, because the remedy legitimately sits mid-paragraph inside 2a-0 and asserting otherwise was a false alarm of exactly the kind the round counted three of. **Final: 28 defect mutations, 28 killed, 0 survivors; 3 controls, 3 green, 0 false alarms** — measured after the baseline gate, on the final tree.

**Suite: 2510 → 2525 passed + 4 skipped + 0 failed**, 2529 collected, measured on the final tree with the ledger row in place. The structural `test_round_yield_ledger` red — a `CLAUDE.md` Phase log row with no ledger row — was live through both rounds by construction, since the row records the round's yield and cannot precede it; it is named here rather than netted out, per the rule Phase 178's record set and this phase's first draft broke by claiming a green it had not measured. The guard module carries 15 tests: 13 from the round-1 rebuild plus the two reversion pins round 2 required.

**What the phase does not fix, stated plainly.** This ships a *rule*, and the failure mode is a reader ignoring prose. The guards can now pin the rule's presence, its position, its containment, its polarity and its delivery into the consumer's artifact — but none of that makes an agent honour it. The mechanism that would is a deterministic check flagging any assembled section whose globs resolve to zero tracked files while carrying a `Skip:` line; `run_checks` dispatches by check-id prefix (`semgrep-`, `lint-`, `pip-audit-`, `coverage-`, `pyright-`/`tsc-`) with everything else falling through to grep, so that check needs a new stage prefix and a new runner module — a phase, not a rider. Filed rather than built.

**Round 2 ran three lenses over `853f4d0`, and the guards verdict is the phase's most important result: the rebuild did not fix the failure mode it was built for.** 74 mutations, **56 surviving (76%)**, and round 1's disqualifying finding **reproduces verbatim** — three one-sentence insertions, one per leg, every pinned sentence left byte-perfect, full suite `1 failed, 2522 passed`, byte-identical to a clean tree. I reproduced it in a scratch copy before accepting it. The reviewer's diagnosis of the reported 28/28 is correct and worth stating flatly: **the mutation families were drawn from round 1's reviewer's own list, and the module was built to match that list**, so the number measured my list, not coverage. The rebuild turned a deletion detector into a byte-exactness detector over a few sentences — better at catching edits *to* those sentences, no better at catching **reversal**, which is the failure mode #280 is about.

**Polarity detection by string matching is abandoned deliberately, not overlooked.** `_REVERSALS` and `_DEMOTION` caught **0 of 21** out-of-vocabulary reversals — *"remain binding"* evades `still binding`, *"treat any Skip entry"* evades `treat every`, *"carries exactly the same authority as a localized one"* evades everything — while false-reddening on legitimate prose containing `deprecated`, `do not assume`, or `regardless of` near `skip`. Two rebuilds failed for one structural reason: a blocklist encodes the last round's vocabulary and the next reviewer picks new words. Filed as debt with the 74-mutation battery attached rather than chased a third time. **A third round was not spawned** — the governor puts that past the session's authority, and the pre-stated stopping condition (another ~50% survival on the rebuilt guards) was met.

**What round 2 did close is the guard gap under the sweep.** Round 1's fix pass scoped nine sites and guarded three; both round-2 lenses independently reverted every swept site to its pre-phase wording and watched all of them pass — including `packs/python/companion/convention_map.md:11` and both `docs/packs.md` corrections the commit message names as its fix. Reversion pins now cover all ten swept sites plus the two public-doc corrections; a 13-reversion battery kills 13. They are **reversion pins, not rule guards** — they catch the clause going away, which for a doc site is the drift that actually happens, and they do not catch reversal. Naming the tier is the point: round 1's record claimed coverage it did not have.

**The behaviour lens verified the remedy end-to-end, which is the result that matters to a consumer.** Following the new 2a-0 dual-write literally in a fresh install and then running `--update` leaves base and overlay at **exactly one copy each** — reproduced in two independent trees, for both maps — because `install.sh:1755` truncates the base and re-concatenates before appending the overlay. `promotion-write-target.md`'s "no duplication results" holds, and this phase had cited it without running it. The `.claude/sysop.lock` gate is real (present after install, absent in this source tree); install, loop mode, re-install and `--update` are all clean with an empty `git status --porcelain`.

**And it found a false claim shipped in both skills that one grep falsifies.** The first dual-write sentence justified itself with *"no skill reads the `.project.*` siblings"* — universally. `test-audit/SKILL.md:48` reads `security_map.project.md`; `contribute-convention/SKILL.md:141-142`/`:161` parses all three overlays. The canonical partial states it correctly and **scoped** — *"Skills read the base maps **at review time** — Step 2 / Step 2a parse …"* — and this phase universalised it while citing it. The prescribed action was right; the reason given was falsifiable in one grep, in a phase whose whole subject is claims that cannot be checked. Now scoped to the review-time parses.

**Three more contradictions the fix pass created or left, all corrected.** (1) `packs/python/companion/convention_map.md:11` — the preamble #280's reporter actually followed — ended with sentence 2 forbidding (*"Do not edit them into the assembled `.claude/convention_map.md`"*) what sentence 3 prescribed (*dual-written … into the assembled map*): round 1 rewrote half the line. (2) `docs/packs.md` was rewritten at `:72-95` only, so its own summary still said maps are localized *"by inference for the security audit"*, and the section headed **"What you own — and where localization lands"** still said *"Don't localize there"* and routed to the overlay alone — the inert remedy, on the public page, in the section named for the question. (3) The map-hygiene rule at `security-audit:306`/`codebase-review:313` (Phase 78) routed dead-citation and stale-glob fixes to the overlay *"not the regenerated base copy"* — which, once every localized section is an overlay section, leaves stale content live in the file Step 2a parses for the whole round: the identical failure the new 2a-0 forbids 120 lines earlier in the same file. Hygiene now dual-writes too.

**A self-inflicted one, also corrected:** round 1's `(c)` clause said the disposition *"records what still has to be localized rather than discharging the invariant"*, two lines above the unchanged sentence *"An entry in none of the three is an unmapped top-level entry"* — so `(c)` demonstrably does discharge that class. Reworded to what is true: it keeps the entry off the unmapped list and is still not coverage.

**Round 2's claims lens found round 1's own defect class recurring in the file it was found in.** The parked Phase-120 STATUS paragraph still read *"`/security-audit`'s **two** Skip-authority sites"* and *"both skills now route to the `.project.md` overlay"* — the **disqualified overlay-only remedy**, still shipping in the checklist — while the fix-pass commit message said "All corrected." I had corrected the two items round 1 named and never re-read the paragraph containing them.

**Known limits, recorded rather than implied.** (a) The guards do not detect reversal at any site: a shipped rule can be left byte-perfect and contradicted by an adjacent sentence. (b) The ten swept sites carry reversion pins only. (c) `/auto-fix` is in `LOOP_EXCLUDE_SKILLS`, so one of the ten does not reach loop-mode consumers. (d) A consumer who follows the dual-write gets a permanent and **incorrect** `⚠ committed local edits in managed paths … will be lost` warning on every later `--update`, because `reconstruct_old_install` builds its shadow tree without the overlay — pre-existing installer behaviour (Phase 24a/78) that this phase promotes from a Step 9 special case to the standard 2a-0 remedy. (e) `docs/configuration.md:20-37` still frames the overlay as *the* place to author map changes — incomplete rather than wrong; it is a durability table. (f) The monograph's `(c)` framing at `docs/workflow.html:1791` is now behind the skills. All filed.

**The mechanism that would actually close this** — a deterministic check flagging any assembled section whose globs resolve to zero tracked files while carrying a `Skip:` line — remains the honest answer to a prose rule nothing enforces. `run_checks` dispatches by check-id prefix (`semgrep-`, `lint-`, `pip-audit-`, `coverage-`, `pyright-`/`tsc-`) with everything else falling through to grep, so it needs a new stage prefix and a new runner module. A phase, not a rider. Filed.

## Phase 180 (executed 2026-08-03, squash-merged as `ad75ab0` (#335) — upstream #329 + #322: the two Step 7/8 contracts that lost a durable artifact silently, and the correct contract sitting in a file the actor never reads)

**Bundled on the Phase-30/43a precedent, and the bundle earns itself.** Both issues are `/claim-task` Steps 7–8, both came out of the same GDP burn-in of the Phase-171 orchestrator, and both are the same shape one layer down: **the contract is stated correctly in a file the actor never reads, and stated wrongly — or not at all — in the prompt the actor does read.** #329's correct message layout was already written in `_shared/adversarial-review.md:178` (*"sealed `REVIEW_REPORT:` at the TOP + `TASK`/`STATUS`/`BRANCH`/etc. block at the BOTTOM"*), in § *Envelope receipt*, which is **not** part of the Prompt Template the reviewer is handed. #322's write target was already asserted by `/review-close` Step 2d (*"the executor writes it into the body during implementation, inside the worktree"*) as its stated reason for reading the record at the branch tip — a sentence describing a mechanism `/claim-task` never implemented.

**The filed diagnosis of #329 was wrong, and it is the correction that sizes the fix.** `REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`'s entry called the two asks **mutually unsatisfiable**: `:710` declares the `TASK:` envelope the LAST fenced block and `:721` requires a further one, so *"a reviewer obeying `:710` literally must drop the sealed block."* That does not hold. Emitting the sealed block **first** satisfies both requirements exactly — the asks are jointly satisfiable in one order, which the prompt's own **layout** inverts and never names. A reviewer reading top-to-bottom meets a contradiction that is not in the requirements, which is precisely what GDP's did. The distinction is not academic: an unsatisfiable pair forces a *requirement* change, a mis-ordered layout is fixed by **stating the layout**, and only the second lets the fix land on a shape another file already documents. The reporter's own framing ("two co-equal, unemphasized asks") was wrong in the other direction — `:710` carries bold `**Then**` and capitalised `LAST`, verified — so both the report and the triage that corrected it were wrong about the mechanism while right that the mechanism was broken. **Six phases have now recorded the filed reasoning being off while the filed defect was right (169, 170, 172, 173, 175, 176); this is the first where the *correcting* record was off too.**

**The hook was indifferent all along, which is what made the ordering free to choose.** `_find_envelope_block` returns the **last** fence carrying `TASK:` + `STATUS:`; `_find_review_report_block` returns the **first** whose head is `REVIEW_REPORT:`. Either order parses. So the fix is not a compatibility problem, and the only reason to prefer one order is that a shipped partial already names it.

**#329's fix, both halves.** The tail now carries an explicit layout — *"Your final message must carry two fenced blocks, in this order, with no content after the second"* — sealed report first, envelope last, and the `review.md` instruction no longer claims to home the sealed block, so the block has exactly one required home. The silent half becomes a **post-review transport check**: a prescribed `python3 - <<'PY'` block at the end of Step 7b, modelled on Step 7a's post-plan integrity check and carrying its argument verbatim (the verdict is a *file*, not a line of transcript), which reads the review envelope and classifies the return `OK` / `EMPTY_TRANSPORT` / `NO_ENVELOPE`, writes `review-transport.md`, and routes each. It is mechanical for the reason the skill already gives one step earlier: an orchestrator that has to remember to open a JSON file and notice a `null` is the attention decay the reshape exists to remove.

**The filing put the assertion at Step 8 and Step 8 is too late for the remedy it names.** The entry (following the report) proposed the null arm at `:1025`, with *"re-spawn once (`:973` already allows it)"* as one disposition. `:973` fires at 7b; `:1025` runs **after the executor has already implemented**, where re-spawning the reviewer would re-review a plan that has been executed. So the *actionable* check went to 7b, where re-spawn is meaningful, and Step 8 got the **reporting** arm it was owed. `EMPTY_TRANSPORT` re-spawns once and then **proceeds on `review.md` rather than parking** — stated as a deliberate asymmetry with the reviewer failure row, because a review that demonstrably ran and left a durable artifact is worth more than a claim discarded over a channel failure, and the receipt is what stops the degraded case reading as the healthy one. **Class sweep:** the `BLOCKED` arm reads the same field and the filing named only `EXECUTED`; it gets the same arm, and the failure table gets a row for parsed-but-null.

**#322: both filed negatives verified, and the reporter's proposed remedy for the untracked case was refuted by execution.** Nothing else in the skill names a worktree copy for the body (the other references are Step 2's `body:` resolver and its validator heredoc, Step 2's full read for context, Step 4c's `validate_tasks.py` run, and Step 6's option-C discussion — none of them a write target; the enumeration in this entry's first draft named the wrong step numbers and was incomplete, which the round caught while confirming the load-bearing negative), and Step 8 carries no clean-tree assertion, so the mechanical catch is new work rather than a wiring change. The downstream mechanics reproduce exactly in a scratch repo: `git mv` on a modified-but-unstaged tracked file stages **`HEAD`'s** content, the body contributes `0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)` to the consolidation commit, and the edits survive as ` M tasks/archive/<ID>.md` — so the reporter's account **and** their recorded self-correction (Step 6's reset does not destroy them; the Phase-167 gate shipped) both hold and both survive into the record. But the report's untracked-body remedy — *"copy it into the worktree first and `git add` it"* — makes `/review-close`'s merge abort with *"The following untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge"*, reproduced in a scratch repo and now pinned by a test. That is the finding the report does not contain, and it is what the shipped untracked arm says instead: the body is on no branch and cannot be put on one, so write the main-checkout copy and **report it**, because it will not reach the PR and needs committing before `/review-close` runs.

**#322's fix.** The write rule sits directly beside the read rule in the Planner Prompt — their separation is the defect — plus the location in plan item 4, the write target and a licence to *correct a wrong plan step* in Executor Sequence item 3 (GDP's executor complied with a plan step naming the main checkout; complying was not the error, but nothing licensed correcting it), and a prescribed `python3` probe in Step 8's `EXECUTED` arm. The probe resolves the main checkout via `--git-common-dir` rather than trusting the CWD — a CWD drifted into the worktree would report a tree that is **clean by construction** after 7e's commit, i.e. a false green on exactly the run that is broken — diffs **tracked** modifications under `tasks/` only, names the files, and routes to *refuse and report*: the human moves them, this skill does not, because which copy is authoritative is their call. `STRANDED` joins the auto-mode chain's skip list. The untracked carve-out is deliberate and tested: `git diff HEAD` ignores untracked files, so the one case the executor is told to write on main does not report as a defect.

**Two shape decisions worth recording.** The Step 8 probe was first written as bash (`git -C "$(dirname "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)")" diff …`) and rewritten as a heredoc: `git -C` binds no seeded allow-rule, the compound splits on `&&`/`||` (Phase 152/153), and Phase 126 converged every prescribed block in this file on a single `python3 - <<'PY'` idiom precisely so one rule covers them. And the transport check went in as a *subsection of Step 7b* rather than a new numbered step, matching the post-plan integrity check's placement, so nothing renumbers and no forward pointer can route past it (Phase 170's rule 3).

**Guards, and what tier each one is.** `tests/test_claim_task_step7_contracts.py` (51 tests). The #329 ordering property is read off the **fence sequence** of the reviewer tail using the hook's own predicates — not off any sentence about ordering — so a rewrite that moves the blocks fails and one that reflows the paragraphs does not. The #322 probe is `ast.parse`d and asserted on the **git argument vector** it composes, so renaming locals, changing string style or rewording the arms stay green while widening past `tasks/` or going untracked-inclusive does not. Three guards **execute** rather than read: a final message composed from the tail's own two fences is driven through the shipped `parse_subagent_envelope.py` and must fill `review_report_raw` (with the envelope-only message kept as a control that still reports `parsed: True`); both prescribed blocks are extracted verbatim and run against real git repos; and the untracked-merge abort is reproduced rather than asserted. The sentence pins are a **reversion detector**, named as one (Phase 176's rule), not a coverage guard. Two checks have external populations (`_shared/adversarial-review.md`, `review-close/SKILL.md`) that no skill mutation can reach, so their predicates are exercised directly as pure functions rather than by writing to the tree.

**The author-side pass found one hole in its own battery and two in the neighbours', and the neighbours' were the serious ones.** Mutation M16 — inverting the planner's operative write sentence while its bold heading stood — **survived the first battery**, which is the exact class the fix-wave brief names ("keep every pin verbatim and invert what the step *does*"); closed with a pin on the operative sentence plus a `FORBIDDEN` for the inverted form. Then, per the brief's rule that adding text weakens every neighbouring guard: (1) `test_claim_task_orchestrator.py`'s `artifact dir back in the worktree` plant anchored on a bare `main_root = Path(common).resolve().parent`, and this phase added two more blocks resolving the main root identically — one **below** the park block — so `_last_sub`'s `rindex` retargeted the plant onto a block no check inspects and it survived while the park block sat untouched. That is Phase 170's first-occurrence class one index over: `rindex` fixed the direction, not the ambiguity. Anchored on the park block's own next line, in all three copies of the plant. (2) The Step 7b *"reviewer asked to classify"* check tested negation at `n7b.lower().index("classify")` — the first occurrence of the **word**, not where the regex matched — and scanned fenced text; once the reorder put the envelope fence directly above `Report findings only.`, its `ERROR: <… if you could not complete the review …>` line dropped a `not` into the negation window and the check went blind to a planted self-classification instruction **with the whole mutation table green**. Both bugs were pre-existing; the edits only exposed them. Now per-match and prose-only. A third neighbour, the orchestrator's `CONDITIONAL_ALLOWLIST`, fired on the new `skip the auto-mode chain` clause — that is the review checkpoint it exists to force, and the clause was added to the list narrowly.

**A known-false claim in a maintainer record was corrected rather than left standing.** `tools/ROUND_YIELD_LEDGER.md`'s batch-5 triage row asserts #329's two asks are *"mutually unsatisfiable"*. That was the triage session's own unreviewed claim — the row says so — and this phase's re-derivation refutes it. Corrected in place with the correction named, because leaving a claim known false in the ledger is what Phase 179's round punished.

**Gate: the round ran — two lenses (guards real / claims true), one round, over `49f7821`.** Governor: this ships behaviour plus guards and no numeric record beyond its own battery, so two lenses is the default and no third was licensed. One reviewer ran on a different model from the author. Both were told to verify their revision before reading: **the claims lens landed on `4f290d5` — the pre-phase tip — and correctly fell back to `git show 49f7821:<path>` and a `--no-local` clone.** That is the isolation hazard `_shared/adversarial-review.md` records, firing on its first use here; without the verification instruction that lens would have reviewed the wrong tree and reported it as this phase's.

**The guards lens beat my battery, for the sixth phase running.** It wrote 22 blind-spot mutations; **all 22 survived the new module alone**, 13 survived the full four-file suite (59%), and the 9 caught were caught by the *pre-existing* `test_claim_task_orchestrator.py`, not by anything this phase shipped. Four were structural and are now closed, each kept as a permanent regression (R1–R4): (1) **the whole transport subsection relocated above the reviewer spawn** — every marker present, every pin byte-perfect, every section still slicing, and the check would then read an envelope that cannot exist yet or, on a re-run, the *previous* run's; a placement check now pins the order 7b → end-of-tail → transport → 7c. (2) The failure-table row's disposition inverted to *"parks immediately"* while the transport section's own `**This does not park**` pin stood, leaving the file asserting both terminals for one scenario. (3) A **decoy waiver clause** satisfied the auto-chain's bare `STRANDED in section` test — and, once planted, kept satisfying it after the real clause was deleted, so one token disarmed detection of a separate worse regression; the clause is pinned verbatim and the occurrence count is now exactly one. (4) The probe's pathspec widened by *adding* a path (`"--", "tasks/", "docs/"`) passed a required-token test; the pathspec is now asserted **exactly**. It also flagged a methodology trap worth carrying: **a full-suite run is not a reliable mutation oracle here**, because several modules' mutations assert their own anchor text is present, so an unrelated edit removing that anchor raises and reads as a catch — two of the lens's own verdicts were false positives from exactly that, and it said so.

**The remaining nine survivors are all one class, and it is already filed rather than re-litigated.** Every one softens a mandatory verb in an unpinned sentence beside a pinned one ("where practical", "discretionary", "you needn't"). `REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md` § Medium item (c), filed by Phase 173's round, records it: *"Verbatim pins constrain wording, not behaviour … the one survivor class the phase could not close in kind."* Phase 179 then abandoned polarity-detection-by-string-matching after two rebuilds, measuring 0 of 21 out-of-vocabulary reversals caught while false-reddening on correct prose. Chasing it a third time is the thing that record exists to prevent. The module's docstring now states this, states that coverage is per *pinned sentence* rather than per section, and states that some Step 7–8 defects die only in a sibling module it does not reference — three claims its first draft left implied. **One negative control reddened for real** (renaming `out` → `outcome_path` in a Step 8 block trips `chain_problems()`, keyed to the literal local name), and it is pre-existing over-strictness this phase did not introduce and did not fix.

**The claims lens found two HIGH defects in the fix itself, both of the class this phase is about — a shipped sentence asserting something the tree refutes.** (1) **`NO_ENVELOPE` → park made an unregistered hook fatal to every claim.** Step 8's read-order contract names *"an unregistered hook or a failed write"* as supported configurations and falls back to regex-parsing the return text; my disposition parked on exactly that. The verdict now falls back the same way and **must not park**, pinned. (2) **"`main` is never committed to directly" is false in this very file** — Step 4d commits the claim flip on `main`, and under `pr` policy `/review-close` Step 4-pre *cherry-picks local-only `main` commits onto the integration branch*. The conclusion survives and the reason did not: what the sweep moves is **commits**, and a stranded body edit is uncommitted, so nothing stages it and it reaches no branch. Rewritten to say that. The same lens found the two failure-table rows could both fire with opposite terminals, and that the transport block computed its verdict from the envelope alone — so a run that lost `review.md` classified `EMPTY_TRANSPORT` and its disposition routed 7c at a file that does not exist. A fourth verdict, **`NO_REVIEW_MD`**, now outranks both envelope verdicts and is the arm that parks; the table row is scoped to `review.md` present, making the two rows disjoint by construction.

**It also caught the mailbox-staleness hole and a spec population this phase had not swept.** The transport check reads `<CLAIM_ID>.review.json` from a mailbox keyed by claim and phase with **no run component** — the exact class Step 7-pre's move-aside exists to close — so the `EMPTY_TRANSPORT` re-spawn now moves the stale envelope aside first, and the receipt is documented as a report rather than a freshness proof. And `WORKFLOW.md` restates these steps for every consumer: item 7 described 7b with no transport, item 10 described the executor persisting the record with no location, item 11 described Step 8 with neither new arm, the runtime table omitted `review-transport.md`, and **`:346` still attributed the `## Test decision` to *the planner*, contradicting `review-close:340` and this phase's own rule.** Five sites updated, plus `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md`'s consumer-facing instruction, which had the same silence about *where* to write it. Phase 170's rule — both spec sites move with the skill — caught by a reviewer rather than by me, again.

**Six smaller record defects, all real, all corrected:** a claim that this was the *first* phase whose correcting record was wrong (Phase 178's round retired its own headline correction, and Phase 175's did the same — two entries in this same file); a six-phase enumeration wrong at both ends; a wrong line number for the `BLOCKED` arm; a body-reference enumeration with the wrong step numbers and two omissions; *"all four verdicts"* against a test covering three (now four); and `1 file changed, 0 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)` stated of the whole consolidation commit when it is true of the body's contribution to it. **Also narrowed:** the `CONDITIONAL_ALLOWLIST` entry this phase added was the bare phrase `skip the auto-mode chain`, which would have exempted that phrasing anywhere in the file; it is now bound to its own sentence.

**Final battery: 24 defect mutations + 4 negative controls against 10 checks, 0 survivors, 0 false alarms** — measured after the fixes, on the final tree, with the round's four structural survivors included as permanent regressions and the softening class excluded by the filed disposition above rather than counted as killed.

**Suite: 2522 → 2584 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed** — measured on the final tree with the ledger row in place, not derived. The `test_round_yield_ledger` red that Phase 179's record predicts for this moment (a `CLAUDE.md` Phase log row with no ledger row) was live from the phase commit until the round's yield existed to write, which is the ordering the convention forces rather than an oversight.

## Phase 181 (executed 2026-08-03, squash-merged as `3c4b5f7` (#339) — upstream #337 + #334: the metadata field with six readers and no stated writer, and the size gate whose only remedy could not answer the condition that tripped it)

**Bundled because they edit the same step regions of the same three files** — `/triage` Step 1, `/auto-fix` Step 1, `/auto-judge` Step 1, under ten lines apart in `auto-fix/SKILL.md` — so they could not be separate branches without conflicting. The sequencing inside the phase was #337 first: it makes the classification predicate trustworthy, and #334's scoped read then keys on it. That was a fix-scoping preference, not a gate, and the batch-6 triage round had already struck the "hard prerequisite" framing from the filing.

**The defect, and why it is worse than a wrong tag.** `> **Flag:**` is read by six shipped surfaces — `/triage`, `/auto-fix`, `/auto-judge`, `/sitrep`, `review_index.py`, `sitrep_survey.py` — and written by one, with nothing anywhere stating that. `triage/SKILL.md:62` carried the load-bearing inference (*"If a batch has a `Flag:` tag from Step 1, it was flagged by a prior run … do not re-analyze its tasks"*), and a `Flag:` line is plain markdown with nothing in it that supports the inference. On the reporter's queue a review generator's emitting agent, pattern-matching the metadata of batches already in the file, produced 19 `Flag:` lines about its own findings; `/triage` read them as prior verdicts, skipped 18 of 25 pending batches unread, read 41 of 385 tasks, and printed a confident complete classification. **A healthy run and a degraded one produce identical evidence** — the class Phases 143, 157 and 180 all sit in, here in the review loop's own router.

**The fix put provenance in a second key rather than reshaping `Flag:`, and that decision is the whole reason the blast radius stayed small.** `> **Triaged:** <YYYY-MM-DD> <auto|flag> [TASK-…, …] — <note>` is the verdict record. `Flag:` keeps its exact prior shape and meaning — presence is still the *pool* predicate, `/auto-judge` takes the batch and `/auto-fix` skips it — so no reader had to change how it parses `Flag:` or what that field means. **All six readers did change**, and the round's claims lens was right to say so: five gained a `Triaged:` test (the two Step 0.5 prereqs, `/triage` Step 1a's candidate rule, `/sitrep` priority 4a, `sitrep_survey.py`'s P4 split) and `review_index.py`'s `Flag:` pattern itself was harmonised. What did not change is the field's meaning, which is what kept each of those a one-line predicate swap instead of a re-parse. The filed entry anticipated reshaping `Flag:` and touching two unshared regexes; both parsers still changed, but to **learn a new key** rather than to re-parse an old one, which is strictly less risk on six readers. The two `Flag:` patterns were harmonised while they were open (they genuinely diverged — `^> \*\*Flag:\*\* (.+)` refuses a bare tag, `^> \*\*Flag:\*\*\s*(.*)$` accepts it and discards it via `bool()`), and both keys are pinned character-equal across the two files by a test. **They stay duplicated rather than shared through an import on purpose:** `review_index.py` ships in both install modes and `sitrep_survey.py` only in full, so a sibling import would give `/sitrep` a failure mode it does not have today, to buy a cosmetic.

**The record does work neither issue asked for, and it is the same defect one layer up.** With no durable home for an *auto* verdict, "classified as auto" and "never read" were the same observable state. So an all-auto queue made `/sitrep` priority 4a recommend `/triage` forever, and made `/auto-fix` and `/auto-judge` Step 0.5 re-invoke it on every run — while the skill's frontmatter has claimed idempotence since Phase 44. `Triaged:` records both verdicts and 4a keys on the record; pre-change it held in *output* terms — a second run on an auto batch wrote nothing — but not in *cost*, because the batch was re-read and re-classified every time. The record is what makes it hold for the work as well as the diff. **A legacy `Flag:` with no `Triaged:` sibling is treated as untriaged**, which re-opens every batch tagged before the record existed. Correct direction — re-reading a flagged batch costs one pass, skipping an unread one costs the batch — and named in the shipped skill text rather than left to be discovered.

**Task granularity landed, and not where the filing put it.** The entry specified `/auto-fix` consuming *batch minus flagged tasks*. That breaks an invariant neither the issue nor the entry states: **a batch is the claim unit** — one `Branch:`, one `batch_work.sh` lock, one worktree — and `auto-judge/SKILL.md` declares the two pools disjoint (`:13` pre-change, `:15` after this phase's own two-line insertion moved it) precisely so they can run concurrently. Splitting one batch across both skills puts two agents on one branch. The payload is delivered inside `/auto-judge` instead: the `Triaged:` list is the **judgment set**, and everything else in the batch is a **mechanical remainder** the same agent fixes prescriptively, without adversarial re-reading. That removes the cost the report measured (~305 tasks in the expensive lane by association) and leaves pool membership untouched. Splitting batches at triage time was considered and rejected: it renumbers batches, rewrites `Scope`/`Overlap`, and destroys "a batch is a coherent review scope". **Stated here as a deviation from the filing, because it is one.**

**Three stale attributions the filing did not name, all the same retired writer.** `WORKFLOW.md:1385` — the site the entry called the one that proves its case — asserted the field is *"present only if `/auto-fix` classified the batch"*. So did `WORKFLOW.md` § 2.7's steps 2–3, describing a classify-and-persist-flags flow Phase 44 extracted; § 2.7b's trigger sentence; and `auto-judge/SKILL.md:165`/`:170`, which told the Opus agent **in its own prompt** that the flag came from `/auto-fix`. The writer-side contract also went to the **generators**, in the section whose template an emitting agent copies: `/codebase-review` § 5c and `/security-audit` § 5c now say neither key may be emitted, and give the reason.

**#334: the gate is gone from all three sites and the read is two-pass.** `triage:34`, `auto-fix:51` and `auto-judge:53` each became a § 1a index pass (`grep -n -E '^## |^### Batch |^> \*\*(OWASP|Scope|Branch|Verify|Overlap|Flag|Triaged):\*\*'`), a § 1b scoped body pass (`sed -n '<START>,<END>p'`) over only the batches that skill will act on, and a § 1c advisory. On the shipped guard fixture the index pass returns **1,289 bytes against a 3,863-byte tracker**, and the ratio improves with queue size because the index grows with batch count while the file grows with task count. (The first draft of this record said 1,222 / 4,065 — real numbers, measured on a scratch fixture that never reached the repo; the round's claims lens re-ran the shipped one and got neither. A number nobody else can reproduce is not evidence, however honestly it was obtained.) The advisory states the thing that made the old halt a dead end: `archive_review_tasks.py` relocates whole Rounds by **merge status**, not by size, so it reclaims nothing from a queue of `Pending` batches — which is exactly the state these skills exist to clear.

**Running the prescribed commands found a live data-integrity defect neither issue mentions, in shipped code.** `review_index.py` had four closers — round header, next batch header, `## Statistics`, and an EOF fallback — but the `in_deferred_section` branch early-`continue`s every line once `## Deferred` has been seen, so the `## Statistics` closer was **unreachable** on any tracker whose Deferred section precedes it. That is the canonical order, so in practice the **last batch ran to EOF** and its `--range` output covered every trailing standalone section — `## Deferred`, `## Statistics`, and the `## Convention fire ledger` that `/codebase-review` § 5e parks there on purpose so the archiver cannot move it. `close_batch.sh` feeds that range to `CLOSE_AWK` as `-v s -v e`, and `mode=flip` rewrites every `- [ ] **TASK-…**` inside it. **Reproduced by driving the shipped awk over the shipped indexer's range: closing the most recent batch marked every deferred task `[x]`.** `close_batch.sh`'s own grep fallback (`grep -n '^##'`) already bounded correctly, so the two paths disagreed and the preferred one was the wrong one. Fixed at the source — any `## ` heading now closes an open batch — and guarded end-to-end rather than by assertion. **This is rule 3 of the author-side pass earning itself:** the defect surfaced as a range mismatch in a test I wrote to prove my own prescription worked, not from reading the file.

**The `:1566` permission row had a third error the entry did not name.** It attributed the archiver to `/codebase-review`, `/auto-fix` and `/auto-judge` "when `review_tasks.md` exceeds 125KB". **No skill invokes it at all** — verified across the tree: the three queue readers name it in an advisory addressed to the operator, and the two generators only *stage* `review_tasks_archive.md` when it already exists. The row now says so; the rules stay in the template as headroom, because removing a template rule never removes it from an installed consumer. `codebase-review:28` and `security-audit:30` were reworded off the same false framing.

**Loop mode was filed, not folded** — on the batch-6 entry's own instruction to treat it as a distinct defect sharing the same root. It ships no gate (`install.sh:88` excludes all three skills), so nothing there is blocked; what it has is unbounded growth, because it ships the two skills that *write* `review_tasks.md` and excludes `close_batch.sh`, the **sole** writer of `Merged` — the write is the `sed -e "${BATCH_START}s#...#\`Merged\`#"` at `:401-403`. (The triage entry cited `:12`, `:270`, `:375`; the round's claims lens showed those are a file-header comment, an equality *read*, and a dry-run `echo`. The conclusion held and the citation set was an index of lines containing the string — the exact failure that same entry criticises an earlier draft for. Corrected in the filing too.). The fix is a design decision, not a mechanical one, and this phase was already across three skills, two parsers and five doc surfaces. Filed as a § High entry with the cheapest next step named.

**Guards: `tests/test_flag_contract.py`.** Three tiers, named as such. **Executed, not asserted:** the index-pass command is extracted from the skill file and run against a fixture hand-transcribed from the shipped generators' § 5c templates (transcribed, not derived — nothing reads the skill files to build it), and its derived batch ranges must equal the indexer's; the prescribed `sed` is run and must return exactly one batch; the shipped `CLOSE_AWK` is extracted from `close_batch.sh` and run over the shipped range, and `## Deferred` must survive. **Behavioural:** the `/sitrep` cascade is driven through `_recommended_next` for untriaged / stamped-flag / all-auto / mixed queues. **Reversion detectors, labelled as such:** the § 1c advisory clause and the merged-only clause, pinned verbatim. One pre-existing module moved with the behaviour: `test_sitrep_survey.py`'s flagged-batch tests now model a *stamped* verdict, and the unstamped case joins them as its own test.

**The author-side pass: one battery, 29 mutations across six assumption classes plus four negative controls. First run 25/29 with four survivors; final 29/29, 0 false alarms.** The four survivors were one class and the fix was structural rather than more vocabulary: three re-added the size halt in wordings outside the pattern corpus ("halt and ask", "abort the run", "stop; the tracker is above the ceiling") and one gutted the merged-only advisory down to two incidental tokens. Pattern-matching prose for a halt is the class **Phase 179 already measured losing** (0 of 21 out-of-vocabulary reversals caught), so the guard now constrains **where** the ceiling may be discussed — every `125KB` mention must sit inside a subsection whose heading and operative sentence are pinned — and the population of skills carrying a ceiling is **derived from the tree** rather than from the module's own list, so a fourth reader cannot be silently uncovered. **An author's zero measures self-consistency; the round is the measurement.** *(Both batteries were also run without clearing `__pycache__`. Round 1's guard lens showed CPython validates a `.pyc` on `(int(mtime), size)`, so a same-size revert inside one second can reuse stale bytecode and report a kill that never ran. Treat 29/29 and 23/23 as upper bounds; the cold re-run after the round is the number that means anything.)*

**Gate: the round ran — three lenses (does it execute / are its claims true / are its tests real), one round, over `79b67a3`.** Governor: this ships behaviour **and** a record making numeric claims, which is the condition licensing a third lens. All three were told to verify their revision before reading; all three landed on `e8490c1` (the pre-phase tip) in their worktrees and correctly fell back to `git show 79b67a3:<path>` — the isolation hazard `_shared/adversarial-review.md` records, firing on all three at once. Without that instruction the whole round would have reviewed the wrong tree.

**The execute lens found a regression this phase introduced, and it is the worst finding of the round.** Widening the batch closer from `## Round N` to any `## ` had **no fence awareness**. A task *about markdown* quotes the tracker's own shapes, so a fenced `## Deferred` truncated its batch: `close_batch.sh` flipped the tasks above the fence and left the rest at `- [ ]` under a `Merged` header — the "a failed task closes as a done one" class Phase 157 fixed, arriving from the other direction. The lens built the fixture that shows it (a docs batch whose remediation quotes a tracker section) and drove the shipped script through it; I had built four fixtures and none of them contained a fence. **The older half of the same hole was already there and unnoticed:** a fenced `> **Flag:**` was attributed to the enclosing batch as a real verdict, which is #337's own failure mode arriving from *inside* the file. All three parsers are now fence-aware, and the `_fence_marker` helper is pinned identical across them.

**The operator half of that hole cannot be closed the same way, and the fix says so instead of pretending.** `grep` cannot see fences, so the prescribed index pass will keep reporting fenced lines. All three skills now carry the caveat naming both consequences and telling the operator to open the region with the scoped read — a fence is obvious on sight and invisible to `grep`. A `review_index.py --range` "second opinion" was drafted and dropped: it binds no seeded allow-rule, so under `dontAsk` it would be denied, and prescribing a command three skills' guards do not declare is the Phase-152 defect.

**Three more from that lens, all live.** One **trailing space** voided a `Triaged:` record — the pattern was `$`-anchored with no slack while rule 4 of the contract invites hand-editing, and because the grep index pass cannot see the difference, `/sitrep` would recommend `/triage` forever while `/triage` reported nothing to classify: exactly the loop this phase claims to remove. A `Triaged: … flag` with **no `Flag:` line** failed toward the *cheap* lane, since `/auto-fix`'s pool test is literally "no `Flag:` line" — now routed back to `/triage`, asserted at both layers rather than trusting one. And the bound fix had landed in `review_index.py` **only**: `sitrep_survey.py` still counted `## Deferred` tasks into the last batch, so `done == total` could never hold and `/sitrep` priority 2 never fired for it. The lens noted that the phase's own harness already contained the file shape that catches this, two functions away from the assertion pointed at the wrong fixture.

**A fourth site was mine to find and I had not swept for it.** `next_task.py::parse_review_batches` has the identical unbounded-last-batch shape, so `## Deferred` task lines counted into the last batch's `open_count` and severity totals — inflating exactly the batch `/next-task` ranks. Fixed with the same two changes. Three parsers, one class; the record's "fixed at the source" now means all three.

**The claims lens found 21, and the ones that mattered were in my own record rather than in the code.** The upstream-count sentence said *"26 … after Phase 181 fixed and closed #337 + #334"* while **both issues were still open** — a decrement for closes that had not happened, inside the sentence announcing that decrementing had been replaced by measuring. It caught that by *running the command the sentence cites*. **"1,222 bytes against a 4,065-byte tracker" does not reproduce**: real numbers, honestly obtained, measured on a scratch fixture that never reached the repo; the shipped one gives 1,289 / 3,863. A number nobody else can reproduce is not evidence. I invented a cross-reference to **`WORKFLOW.md` § 2.7a**, a section that does not exist. And **the stated mechanism for the data-integrity defect was wrong**: there were four closers, not two, and the cause is that the `## Deferred` branch early-`continue`s so the `## Statistics` closer is unreachable — premise wrong, conclusion right, and now pinned by a permutation test over all six trailing-section orders rather than by one fixture that happened to have the failing order.

**Two findings are the same failure this phase exists to punish, committed by this phase.** The `Merged`-writer citations I carried forward — `:12`, `:270`, `:375` — are a **file-header comment, an equality read, and a dry-run `echo`**; the write is `:401-403`. That is a set of lines *containing* the string, i.e. an index rather than a population, which is the exact error the same checklist entry criticises an earlier draft of the triage for making. And the **duplicate-don't-import rationale was inverted** — `install.sh:97` excludes `sitrep_survey.py` from loop mode while `review_index.py` is kept, so `sitrep_survey.py` only ever exists alongside it and the failure direction I described cannot occur. The decision stands on the house duplicate-and-pin idiom; the reason given for it was false, and it shipped in a source comment.

**Ten smaller record defects, all real, all corrected:** *"the six readers of it are unchanged in what they route on"* (all six changed — what did not change is the field's meaning); *"every reader treats it as untriaged"* at two new `WORKFLOW.md` sites (two do); a stale `**Checks:** Classification gate (auto vs flag)` left in the § 2.7 block this phase rewrote to say classification is not that skill's job; stale routing prose inside `sitrep_survey.py` itself, at the docstring and at the P4 comment; an archiver population **assumed** at five skills when six mention it, in the one place this module did not apply its own derive-the-population rule; *"two pre-existing modules moved"* (one); a fixture described as built from the shipped writers that is hand-transcribed from them; three post-change line citations that this phase's own insertions had moved; and an idempotence claim that read stronger than the delta (it held in output terms before, not in cost).

**Regression evidence on real data, because six parser edits deserve more than a fixture.** Over GDP's live 326 KB `review_tasks.md`, the pre-phase and post-fix parsers are identical — 25 batches, every line range, every task id, `deferred`, `rounds`, `grand_total` and `summary` — re-measured at the final revision rather than at the commit where the fix landed. **The corollary is that the real tracker never had the bug**, and the first draft of this paragraph said the two parsers *now agree where before they did not*, which is false there: GDP's `## Deferred` section precedes its Rounds, so no batch is followed by a trailing section and both parsers already agreed. The disagreement is real but lives in the other shape — a tracker whose last batch is followed by any `## ` section, which is what `/codebase-review` § 5e's end-of-file ledger placement produces as soon as one stale verdict is recorded. So the fence and bound rules are a no-op on the corpus they will actually meet today; what they change is the corpus a consumer gets the first time a ledger, a Statistics table or a Deferred list lands after the last batch.

**Round 2 ran, on the governor's one stated condition: the round-1 fixes replaced a mechanism.** Closing the fence hole meant adding fence state to three shipped parsers, in the path `close_batch.sh` uses to decide which checkboxes to flip — new material no fresh reader had seen, and in the same class as the defect it was fixing. Two lenses (does it execute / are the new guards real and the new claims true), scoped by prompt to `git diff 79b67a3..c9d63c7` only.

**It found that my fence fix was worse than the bug it replaced.** The loop honoured an **unterminated** fence, so one unbalanced ``` disabled structural parsing to end-of-file: the batch's `line_end` ran to EOF and `close_batch.sh` flipped every checkbox in it, including a trailing `## Deferred` section's. Measured on one file — pre-phase `[11, 27]`, round-1 `[11, 16]`, round-2-subject `[11, 27]` again, `5 tasks → [x]` where the batch has three. A mid-file unbalanced fence made every *later* batch vanish outright, flagged work included, with `/sitrep` reporting no discrepancy. The fix is a two-pass **balanced-only** mask: you cannot know a fence is balanced until you have read the whole file, and an unterminated one is now ignored rather than honoured — failing toward structure, which is the safe direction.

**Three more from the execute lens, all live.** The fence rule could not see `> ``` `, which is the **one form that matters**, because tracker metadata is `> **Key:**` and an example of it is quoted inside a blockquote — so #337's from-inside-the-file half was still open in exactly its realistic shape. `review_index.py`'s Deferred trigger tested `line.strip()`, contradicting the `startswith("## ")` closer three lines above, so an *indented* `## Deferred` in a task's detail lines diverted every following task into `deferred` while the batch stayed open and the three parsers gave three different answers. And the `[—–-]` tolerance accepted `auto-fix will handle these` as a durable `auto` verdict, because `\s*` before the dash permitted zero whitespace — failing toward the cheap lane.

**The § 1a caveat I had just written was a false universal, in shipped operator guidance.** It said a disagreement between the operator's boundary and a parser's *is* a fenced example. On an unbalanced fence the operator is right and the parser is wrong; the caveat would have had them discard real flagged batches. It now says to read the region and names the three causes that are not fences, including a batch header whose dash is not an em dash — a genuine grammar divergence between `next_task.py` and the other two that the lens surfaced.

**The guard lens wrote 119 mutations to my 29 and found 56 genuine escapes — 47%, against my reported 29/29.** The fifth phase in a row where that gap appears, and this time the single worst escape was a **one-keyword change that restores #337 in full with all 2,674 tests green**: `has_triage_record=bool(flag_reason)` in the `ReviewBatchState` construction. `_classify_review_batches` was tested only on its output strings and `_recommended_next` only on hand-built states, so **nothing fed one into the other**. That seam now has eight tests that start from bytes on disk and end at a recommendation. It also caught my `test_review_index_ignores_fenced_metadata` as **vacuous** — the fenced heading truncated the batch before the fenced metadata was reached, so it passed with fence handling deleted outright, meaning the older half of the defect had no working guard at all.

**And it found a fourth and fifth structural reader.** `archive_review_tasks.py` — the script this phase's own size advisory tells the operator to run — parsed a fenced `## Round` / `### Batch … \`Merged\`` as structure and **split a real merged round in two at the opening fence line**, both halves reporting `all_merged: True`, relocating both with unbalanced fences and a real `- [x]` task carried into the wrong archive block. Fixed, and the population is now **derived from the tree**: any module compiling a pattern anchored at `^### ` must be fence-aware. That predicate immediately flagged a sixth candidate, `ingest_security_report.py`, which turned out to be a *writer* whose only mention is a docstring about stopping a finding forging a batch header — so the predicate was tightened rather than the module changed, and the boundary is now stated. The two **shell** fallbacks (`close_batch.sh`, `batch_work.sh`) are still fence-blind; that is filed with its reproduction rather than fixed, because fence-awareness in bash is another new mechanism and the path is degraded-mode only.

**Four claims lens B falsified, all mine.** *"The `_fence_marker` helper is pinned identical across them"* — only the **regex** was pinned, and it broke the close rule in two of three copies with the pin green; the mask **body** is now compared as source. *"An archiver population assumed at five skills when six mention it"* — I fixed the docstring and left the hard-coded five underneath it, which the lens proved with an archiver invocation in `review-close`; it is derived now. *"F21 … `/triage` still carried the unqualified `$`-to-EOF licence a bulk edit had missed in the other two"* — at `79b67a3` **all three** carried an unqualified licence in two different wordings, and my negative assertion was pinned to one parenthesised variant, so a "Shortcut: `$` for the last batch" line passed; every unqualified form is now rejected. And the GDP parity sentence, already corrected once before the lens read it.

**Where the guards ended up.** Every escape from both lenses that I could close in kind is closed and re-verified cold: the ceiling guard is line-indexed rather than substring-sliced (a `#### 1c.` demotion and a verbatim copy pasted into another step both walked through the first version), § 1c must stay **inside** Step 1 rather than merely after § 1b (it was relocatable to end-of-file with zero characters edited), the section-order fixture varies the section **vocabulary** rather than only the order, an **empty** batch must still bound, and the `sed` and the shell fallback are read out of the files that ship them instead of restated in the test. What is not closed is the one class Phase 179 already measured string-matching losing: a halt phrased with no number at all. That is recorded as a residual, not as coverage.

## Phase 182 (executed 2026-08-03, squash-merged as `adbf0cf` (#343) — upstream #321 + the Phase-165 filing: the bare-`python3` PyYAML probe, and the bootstrap held up as its precedent that could not fire where its callers run)

**Trigger.** GDP's `/claim-task` died on its **first command**. `bash sysop/scripts/claim_task.sh --entry-state <ID>` exited 3 on a PEP-668 host — every modern distro, and Homebrew macOS, where `pip install` into the system interpreter is an *error*, so PyYAML lives only in `.venv`. `claim-task/SKILL.md:134` defines a non-zero exit there as "the question could not be answered at all … surface stderr verbatim and **stop**", so followed literally the claim never starts, and the error text named no remedy. The `--release` half had been filed by Phase 165's own round on 2026-07-29 and deliberately parked; upstream #321 widened it and is the demand event that overturned the park.

**Two claims in the inbound material were false, and both mattered.** #321 asserted the `--entry-state` gate had *"**zero** coverage against a bare system `python3`"* — `tests/test_claim_task_sh.py:585` pins exit 3 under a yaml-less shim exactly as `:228` pins `--release`, so the two halves were one defect with one blocker rather than "one parked, one cheap". That correction was already in the checklist entry and is why this landed as one phase. The entry's *own* load-bearing rationale was the second: it carried Phase 126's finding that a `$PY_BIN` variable command word "binds no static allow-rule" as the reason the fix had to keep a literal `python3`. True of a *skill heredoc*, and irrelevant inside a bash script — the permission matcher only ever sees `bash sysop/scripts/claim_task.sh …`, as Phase 126's own out-of-scope note recorded for `claim_task.sh:187`. The literal form was kept anyway for consistency with the shipped idiom, but the record now states the honest reason rather than the inherited one.

**The fix is one helper, not four edits.** `resolve_yaml_python()` probes `$MAIN_REPO_ROOT/.venv/bin`, `$MAIN_REPO_ROOT/venv/bin`, then the same pair under `$REPO_ROOT`, and **prepends the winner's bin dir to `PATH`** — so `:157`'s gate, `:170`'s heredoc, `:291`'s preflight and `:342`'s flip heredoc all keep a literal `python3` command word and all receive the same interpreter, and `:409`'s `validate_tasks.py` call rides along. It **probes rather than assumes**, which is not decoration: the blind `PATH=.venv/bin:$PATH` prepend that both the report and the entry describe would shadow a *capable* system interpreter with an *incapable* venv one, trading the reported failure for its mirror image — the hazard `self_check.sh:61-66` names from the probe side — *"a yaml-capable system python is no comfort if run_checks picks a venv python without it"* — which the first draft mis-described as "the other direction" when it is the same one. Anchoring on the main checkout before the current one is what makes it right from a worktree (`--entry-state`'s routine caller) and from any subdirectory (`--release` may be run from anywhere). Only when nothing can `import yaml` does either path refuse, and both refusals now name `python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install pyyaml`.

**The two deliberate tests were revised, not deleted**, per the filing: `test_no_pyyaml_degrades_without_mutating` → `test_no_pyyaml_anywhere_degrades_without_mutating` and `test_missing_pyyaml_exits_3` → `test_missing_pyyaml_anywhere_exits_3`. Each now asserts its own fixture carries no venv — so it is still the fail-closed case it always claimed to be — and each gained a sibling proving the venv path is found.

**The hostile fixture was built before the fix, and it earned that ordering twice.** `tests/test_claim_task_venv_python.py` covers no-python3-at-all / python3-without-yaml / venv-only / venv-absent / from-a-worktree / from-a-subdirectory, and its `python3`-without-yaml shim is a **real interpreter with `yaml` shadowed via PYTHONPATH**, not the suite's existing `exit 1` shim — against that cruder shim a "fix" that merely deleted the probe and let the heredoc crash would still have looked green. It was red in exactly the ten right places before the fix and green after.

**The class sweep is where the phase grew, and the filed count was again low.** Derived from the tree rather than from the entry (Phase 173: filed 2 → 31; Phase 179: filed 2 → 10), the population was not four sites but four more *scripts*, each reaching PyYAML through whatever `python3` PATH produced: **`sitrep_survey.py`** — so `/sitrep`, whose only Bash call it is, was **entirely dead** on a PEP-668 host; **`next_task.py`** and **`backfill_completed_dates.py`**, both with a completely unguarded module-level `import yaml` (a raw `ModuleNotFoundError`, the latter on step 4 of the documented roadmap migration); and **`scope_overlap.py`**, which degraded to `exit 0` with `overlaps: []` on the advisory that exists to stop wasted parallel work. **The round corrected this one, and it was the phase's own worst claim.** The first draft called it "the worst of them", "**silent**", and "indistinguishable from *could not look*" — at four sites including two shipped test docstrings. Running the pre-fix script proves otherwise: it prints `· note: no readable tasks/index.yml (or PyYAML unavailable) — candidate scope could not be inferred`, and `--json` carries the same string in `notes`. What *is* silent is narrower and was not the thing named: `_parse_lock_file` returns `{}` on `ImportError` while `_read_locks` still back-fills `task_id` from the filename, so in-flight locks are **counted** (`in_flight_count: 1`) with their `workspace`/`branch`/`paths` empty and **no note at all**. The headline line still leads with `✓ No declared overlap`, which is misleading — but misleading-with-a-note is not the Phase-135/146 shape, and the severity ranking built on it does not survive.

**The precedent the entry cited was itself half-inert.** `validate_tasks.py`'s bootstrap globbed only `.venv/` — not `venv/`, which `install.sh::pick_python_with_yaml`, `run_checks.sh` and `self_check.sh` all support — and globbed **CWD-relative**, so it resolved nothing from a subdirectory and nothing from a **worktree**, which is where `/claim-task` builds. So the fix widened it (the file's ancestors → the main checkout via git-common-dir → and only then the CWD, across both layouts) and put the identical block in all five scripts. **That ordering is stated here in the direction the code implements it, which this entry originally got backwards** — the first draft wrote "CWD → the file's ancestors → …", contradicting two later sentences in this same entry (the round paragraph's *"orders script-anchored roots ahead of the CWD"*, and Phase 183's restatement). Phase 184 found it still standing on the public mirror, one entry after the round that fixed four sibling sites. **Cited by name rather than by line on purpose:** Phase 184's first draft of this correction wrote `:4258` and `:4284`, and its own header paragraph then shifted every line by two — reproducing the exact Leg-C defect it was correcting, in the one file its citation guard excludes. **Inline rather than shared, by necessity:** it must run before any import can be trusted, so it cannot itself depend on one, and `_log.py`'s header records `validate_tasks.py` and `next_task.py` as deliberately standalone for pre-commit. `tests/test_venv_pyyaml_bootstrap.py` pins the five copies identical **modulo indentation, and only the resolution loop** — it normalizes with `re.sub(r"\n\s*", "\n", text)` and matches a regex over the loop alone, because the surrounding `try`/`except` and the error text differ legitimately per script. The first draft said "byte-identical" at three record sites; that is the same overstatement Phase 181's round caught ("only the *regex* was pinned"), and it is corrected rather than repeated. `scope_overlap.py`'s copy is deliberately **non-fatal and gated on a probe**: every yaml use in it is a local import on a documented degrade path, and running the resolution unconditionally would reorder `sys.path` on hosts that never needed it.

**`:409` is confirmed a non-instance, and the entry's reason for it was incomplete.** `validate_tasks.py` does self-bootstrap and the `cd "$MAIN_REPO_ROOT"` does put a CWD-relative glob on target — but the load-bearing reason is that `:291`'s guard has already hard-exited on that path, so `:409` is unreachable in the broken state regardless. After the fix the exported `PATH` reaches it directly.

**The author-side pass found the phase's own worst claim.** The first draft of the bootstrap comment said the ancestor walk meant "a run from a subdirectory **or a worktree** still finds the venv". The fixture falsified it on the first run: a linked worktree's ancestors are the worktree, which never carries a `.venv`. That is what produced the git-common-dir arm — a fix that exists because a *test written before the code* contradicted the code's own comment. It also caught a battery-harness hazard worth recording: an interrupted run left a mutation in the tree between write and restore, and only the new drift guard caught it; the harness now snapshots every target and restores in a `finally`.

**Author-side mutation battery: 29 mutations, 18 killed, 11 survivors — and the honest number is lower than the first one measured.** Run with `__pycache__` cleared between every mutation. The first pass reported **13/14**; re-run with the *shape* guard excluded from the selection it was **9/14**, because `test_all_five_copies_are_identical`'s regex reddens on any edit to the block whatever the edit does — a reversion detector reading as a coverage guard, the Phase-176/178 shape. Four survivors were then closed by new tests (run-from-outside-the-repo, a non-git tree, per-script `venv/` layout, and per-script error text). One property — the git probe's `cwd=` — had **zero** behavioural coverage and was masked by the ancestor walk; the test that closes it needed all other arms exhausted at once (a *worktree's* script, invoked by absolute path, from a CWD that is not a git repo). **Declared residuals:** the `[[ -x ]]` executable check in `resolve_yaml_python` is redundant — a non-executable candidate fails the `import yaml` probe anyway — so no mutation can distinguish it; and three properties (git-probe anchor, `venv/` arm, ancestor walk) are proven behaviourally at least once but **not once per script**, resting on the byte-identity guard to propagate. That is stated rather than netted out.

**Declined, and named in the #321 close** rather than dropped, both filed § Medium: the hardcoded `.venv/bin/python3` command words — the **mirror-image** class, Phase 125's Concern 6, which breaks non-venv consumers rather than venv-only ones. **The round caught this filing under-counting its own class 5×**, two paragraphs after this entry congratulates the phase on deriving populations from the tree: it named `next-task/SKILL.md:15` and `claim-task/SKILL.md:251` and the grep returns **ten sites across eight skills**, five of them with no fallback prose at all. The filing now carries the grep output; and `document-work/SKILL.md:215-224`, whose in-heredoc bootstrap is CWD-relative while that skill runs in the task worktree, so it cannot fire where it lives. Six sibling heredocs carry the identical glob and are inert only because they run from the main checkout, so porting the git-common-dir arm there is a seven-site change with its own drift-guard update, not a one-liner.
