**Doc currency, in the same commit.** `docs/install-and-update.md` documented the old `--release` behaviour and would have shipped a false claim; `README.md`'s *"Sysop's scripts resolve the repo's `.venv` on their own"* was an overclaim when written and is now true, stated precisely; `WORKFLOW.md`'s `validate_tasks.py` row claimed the bootstrap meant "a bare `python3` serves every consumer", which was false for `venv/` layouts and for any non-root CWD.

**Adversarial round: three lenses (does it execute / are its claims true / are the guards real), one round, over `ded25c0`.** Three lenses rather than two because the phase ships behaviour *and* the record makes numeric claims — the governor's condition. All three fresh-context `general-purpose` agents in isolated worktrees, told not to mutate and to verify their revision first; all three did.

**The round found the phase's real defect, and it was an inconsistency with the phase's own stated design.** The shell helper probes — it runs `import yaml` per candidate and falls through on failure, and the entry above says so approvingly. **The Python block, written in the same phase, assumed.** It stopped at the first venv-*shaped* directory: `_site = glob(".venv/…") or glob("venv/…")` then `break`. So (a) **one empty `.venv` ended the whole search**, including the main-checkout arm that is the entire point of the git-common-dir addition — the execute lens reproduced it in exactly that configuration, a worktree carrying its own yaml-less `.venv` with the real one in main, and got `BOOTSTRAP-FAILED` where the fix is supposed to succeed; (b) a `.venv` **shadowed a sibling `venv/`** that did have PyYAML, in all five scripts at once; and (c) `Path.cwd()` came first, so running any Sysop script by path from an unrelated project let *that* project's venv win. The block now inserts a candidate, attempts `import yaml`, and **rolls it back on failure**, tries both layouts at every root, and orders script-anchored roots ahead of the CWD. All three scenarios are regression-tested.

**That defect falsified two doc sentences this phase had added** — `WORKFLOW.md`'s "searches the CWD, this file's ancestors, and the main checkout … across both layouts" and `README.md`'s worktree and `(or venv/)` clauses described an exhaustive search the code did not perform. Both corrected to describe what it now does — **and note the quoted phrasing is wrong twice over**: not only did it claim exhaustiveness the code lacked, it also lists CWD first, which is the opposite of the order the fix ships. Only the exhaustiveness half was named at the time.

**The claims lens found the gate red on arrival, and the phase's own headline number wrong.** `tests/test_round_yield_ledger.py::test_every_phase_from_174_has_a_ledger_row` fails at `ded25c0`: adding the `CLAUDE.md` Phase-log row *arms* that guard, and the ledger row had not been appended yet. So the true figure at the commit was `1 failed, 2870 passed` — and **"2,871 tests green" was arithmetic (2875 collected − 4 skipped) performed on a suite run that predated the `CLAUDE.md` edit**, in the same paragraph that boasts the collection delta was measured rather than remembered. Measuring one number and deriving its neighbour is the whole failure. The ordering is now inverted: record first, ledger row, *then* the suite run whose number is quoted.

**Four more record defects, all verified before acceptance.** *"`scope_overlap.py` degraded **silently** … indistinguishable from could not look"* — false, and it was the basis for calling that script "the worst of them"; running the pre-fix code prints a note naming PyYAML, in text and `--json` (the genuinely silent part is `_parse_lock_file`'s `{}`, which leaves locks counted with empty bodies). *"pins the five copies **byte-identical**"* — the guard normalized whitespace and matched the loop only; the same overstatement Phase 181's round caught. *"the hazard `self_check.sh:61-66` documents in **the other direction**"* — same direction, named from the probe side. And the § Medium filing for the mirror-image class **under-counted its own population 5×** — filed 2 sites, the grep returns **ten across eight skills**, five with no fallback prose — two paragraphs after this entry congratulates the phase on deriving populations from the tree rather than from a filing. That one stings and is recorded rather than quietly corrected.

**One finding turned into a shipped fix outside the filed scope.** The README universal was false for `self_check.sh`, which anchored its PyYAML probe on `$REPO_ROOT` while `run_checks.sh` anchors on the main checkout — so from a worktree it reported a failure `run_checks.sh` would not have had, falsifying its own comment (*"the interpreter run_checks.sh will **ACTUALLY** use"*). This is the same defect Phase 143 fixed for that file's probe 6 and left in probe 3. `MAIN_ROOT` is hoisted above probe 3 and both probes now share it.

**The guards lens wrote 37 mutations and walked 9 through, against my declared 2** — the fifth-straight phase where an independent lens beat the author's battery. Three mechanisms, all real: **(1)** the drift regex's match window ended at the final `break`, so a line appended *after* the resolution could kill it outright with the suite green — demonstrated by stripping venv paths back off `sys.path` in two scripts; **(2)** nine of ten assertions were **negative** (`"requires PyYAML" not in stderr`) and keyed on a string living in the script under test, so a copy edit to an error message silently converted nine resolution proofs into vacuous ones; **(3)** the shell candidate *order* was unobservable, because the probe falls through — reversing main-vs-current or `.venv`-vs-`venv` stayed green, meaning "main-first" was a comment rather than a property. Its negative control NC5 also went red: annotating the block identically in all five files reddened two tests, which is over-strictness in a guard meant to police behaviour.

**The guard layer was rebuilt rather than patched.** The hand-written regex is gone — it was a liability twice over (blind past its own window, red on a comment) and a second copy of the code living where it could rot; the block is now sliced between anchors to end-of-block and checked against a list of **required semantic tokens**, each one a behaviour the round proved absent or unguarded. Every resolves-test asserts what the script **produced** — `SITREP` in stdout, `## Next Task` plus the task id, `done task(s) without completed_date`, and for `scope_overlap.py` a `candidate_scope_source == "key_files"` that is reachable only after PyYAML has parsed the index *and* the body — rather than what it did not say. Probe order is made observable by a shim that records each candidate as it is tried. The no-`sys.path`-reordering guard-the-guard is parametrized over all five instead of one.

**Re-measured after the rebuild: 15 mutations, 13 killed, 2 survivors, NC5 green.** Both survivors are declared, not netted out. `[[ -x ]]` in `resolve_yaml_python` is redundant — a non-executable candidate fails the `import yaml` probe anyway — and three independent batteries (mine, the execute lens's, the guards lens's) now agree it cannot be distinguished. Rewording `requires PyYAML` → `needs PyYAML` also survives, and that is **correct** after the rebuild: nothing contracts on that phrase any more, so it is a behaviour-preserving edit — effectively a second negative control.

**Fixed from the round, beyond the above:** the git probe now strips `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_COMMON_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` (the hazard `tests/test_git_env_hermeticity.py` exists for — the execute lens showed a leaked `GIT_DIR` flipping resolution from working to failed, though it verified the ordinary hook paths are safe); the refusal text no longer under-reports which candidates were tried, and **both** its diagnostic and remedy lines are pinned separately, because a lone `".venv" in stderr` was satisfied by either one — the "names no remedy" property that triggered the whole phase was deletable with the suite green; and the helper no longer probes the same root twice when `REPO_ROOT == MAIN_REPO_ROOT`.

**Filed rather than fixed, with the round's reproduction attached:** the shell probe has no timeout while the Python one has `timeout=5`, so a hanging `.venv/bin/python3` hangs `/claim-task`'s first command (the execute lens measured `rc=124`; SIGKILL, a directory, and a dangling symlink all degrade cleanly). Judged not worth a fragile bash-3.2 watchdog, since a venv interpreter that hangs on `import yaml` would hang the heredoc that follows regardless — the probe is not what makes the hang reachable. Also filed: a stdout-printing `.pth` in the venv can corrupt `--entry-state`'s one-token contract (the `ES_ERR` file protects stderr only), a pre-existing mechanism that this phase makes newly relevant by moving the interpreter into the venv where `.pth` files actually live.

**What the round did not shake.** The execute lens ran the full bash-3.2 lifecycle (`--entry-state` → claim → `held` → `--release --delete-branch`) and it was correct throughout; `set -euo pipefail` safety with both roots empty *and* both truly unset; symlinked roots; absolute-path invocation from outside any repo; non-git trees; a deep monorepo whose venv sits beyond the ancestor walk (resolved via the git arm, as designed); `-O`/`-OO`/`-E`/`-I`; no `_yaml_probe` leak into `scope_overlap.py`'s JSON or module globals; and the fork cost measured at 8.8 ms on `/roadmap --in-flight`'s per-candidate path, verified not to run at all when yaml imports. It also confirmed the block cannot reproduce the mirror-image hazard — it sits inside `except ImportError`, so a healthy host never runs it.

**Gate.** **2,887 tests green, 4 skipped** — collection 2,823 → 2,891, **+68**: 22 in `tests/test_claim_task_venv_python.py`, 44 in `tests/test_venv_pyyaml_bootstrap.py`, 2 venv siblings in `tests/test_claim_task_sh.py` (the two renames are net zero). **This number was measured after the last edit, which is the correction the round forced.** The figure it replaces — "2,871 green" — was arithmetic (2,875 collected − 4 skipped) on a suite run that predated the `CLAUDE.md` Phase-log row, and adding that row *arms* `tests/test_round_yield_ledger.py`; at the reviewed commit the tree was really `1 failed, 2,870 passed`, with the failure being **the gate that enforces this phase's own round ledger**, red on arrival. The claims lens found it by running the suite the sentence cited. Two pre-existing guards were updated rather than worked around, both in `tests/test_heredoc_permission_idiom.py`: `test_validate_tasks_self_resolves_yaml` pinned the literal old glob line and then the interim one, and now pins the probing form — its `BOOTSTRAP_LINE` constant stays exactly right for the in-heredoc copies the module's other tests guard, so only that one assertion moved. Landed via branch → PR → squash-merge to protected `main`.

## Phase 183 (executed 2026-08-05 — the filed § Medium item from Phase 182's class sweep, named in the #321 close: the `.venv/bin/python3` command word, and the doctrine that kept minting it)

**Trigger.** Phase 182 fixed the *script* half of "bare `python3` cannot find PyYAML" — five companion scripts now self-resolve a venv (script-anchored first — the file's ancestors, then the main checkout via git-common-dir — and only then the CWD, across both `.venv/` and `venv/` layouts; CWD-first was the bug Phase 182's own round fixed). The *skill* half was declined there on scope: shipped content still hardcoded `.venv/bin/python3` as the **command word**, which is the mirror-image defect. On a consumer with no `.venv/` — poetry, conda, a `venv/` layout, PEP-668 system python, i.e. the population #321 came from — that word is `command not found` and Phase 182 bought them nothing. The worst site was `next-task/SKILL.md:15`: that skill's only command, with no fallback prose, so `/next-task` was simply dead there.

**The defect was executed before it was fixed, and the matrix is the phase's evidence.** Three consumer fixtures (no venv / `.venv/` / `venv/`) plus a linked worktree, each running both command shapes against all four scripts the skills prescribe. On a **`venv/` layout the bare word runs all four (rc 0) and the venv-prefixed word is rc 127 on all four**. On **`.venv/` the two shapes are indistinguishable** — same rc, same output, on every script — which is the half a swap like this usually breaks. On **no venv at all** the bare word still runs the two that answer without yaml (`archive_review_tasks.py` imports none; `scope_overlap.py` degrades to rc 0 with a printed note) and degrades the other two to a *named, actionable* exit 2 rather than `command not found`. This machine's system `python3` (Homebrew 3.14.4) cannot `import yaml`, so it is itself the PEP-668-shaped host rather than a simulation of one.

**The filed population of ten was sixteen**, and the two axes it missed were independent. The entry's derivation — `grep -rn 'venv/bin/python3 sysop/scripts' core/skills/*/SKILL.md` — states the count is "the grep output, not an estimate", which is true and is exactly the problem: **the grep's *scope* was the estimate.** Missed by file scope: `core/companion/scripts/next_task.py:9-11`, the shipped script's own `Usage:` docstring, which `next-task/SKILL.md:18-19` points consumers at for the selection algorithm (the pointer is to the spec, not to the invocation form — the first draft said "source of truth" flatly); and two sites in the manual-reversal recipe — `claim_task.sh:356` and its public-doc twin `docs/install-and-update.md:233`. **The round's claims lens corrected this phase's characterization of them.** The first draft called them the Phase-179 *unreachable-remedy* shape and put `:356` "two lines below" the message announcing that `.venv/bin/python3` was tried and does not work. It is **six** lines below, and the intervening `:351` already prescribes `python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install pyyaml` — so a reader who takes the *fix* branch would have found the old line working. It is unreachable only under `:352`'s "**Or** run the manual reversal with an interpreter that has PyYAML" branch, i.e. for the reader whose PyYAML is somewhere that is not `.venv`. The defect is **non-portability with an unreachable sub-case**, not the flat Phase-179 shape, and the record now says the narrower true thing. Missed by *spelling*: three `.venv/bin/python` sites with no `3`, which no run of the filed grep could ever have matched.

**Those three were the find that mattered, because they are the doctrine, not instances.** `WORKFLOW.md` § 6.1 and its `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md` mirror state the venv-aware-invocation rule — spell out venv paths so a cold tool shell does not hit the system PATH — and both illustrated it with `.venv/bin/python sysop/scripts/validate_tasks.py`. The rule is correct **for the consumer's own tooling** (`pytest`, `bean-check`, linters) and wrong for a Sysop-shipped script, and the worked example is the half a skill author copies. Fixing the ten call sites without that paragraph leaves the rule that re-creates them. The exemplar is now `.venv/bin/ruff`, and both files carry an explicit carve-out: never give a `sysop/scripts/*.py` invocation a `.venv/bin/` command word. **The correction is one-directional and stated as such** — the venv-path rule for consumer tooling is untouched, because it is right.

**Three claims in the inbound material were false.** (a) The entry and the handoff both said `intake:155` is "the only real fallback-prose exemplar in the corpus"; `add-task:82` and `onboard:127` carry near-identical parentheticals, so there were three. (b) That mattered because it **inverted the decision it was raised for**: once the prescribed command *is* bare `python3`, there is nothing left to fall back from, so the three existing parentheticals are vacuous and were removed — the question was never whether to copy them to the five sites that lacked them. (c) The item is filed under § **Medium**, not § Low as the handoff stated.

**The shape was not invented — it already ships.** `/review-close` converged on bare `python3` for `validate_tasks.py` at Phase 126, at two executable command sites (`:841`, `:1095` — `:1001` is prose citing the command, not a third invocation), with settings.json rules and the rationale wording at `:31`. Phase 183 is a convergence on the most safety-critical skill in the corpus, which is also why **zero new permission rules were needed**: `core/companion/.claude/settings.json` already allow-rules the bare twin for all four scripts (`:35` `archive_review_tasks.py` — `:34` is the `python`, not `python3`, twin — plus `:38-39` `validate_tasks.py`, `:45-46` `next_task.py`, `:49-50` `scope_overlap.py`). The `.venv/bin/python3` rules stay shipped on purpose, so a hand-typed venv invocation is not denied; four skill bullets that called the venv form "preferred per Phase 45b" now say the opposite, because it is.

**What was deliberately not touched, and why.** The adjacent population is far larger than the fixed set: 48 `.venv/bin/python3`, 13 `.venv/bin/pip`, plus `activate` / `python` / `pytest` / `pyright` / `bean-check` across 25+ files. Almost all of it is correct. Three categories were separated and only the first acted on: **(a)** command word for a Sysop-shipped script that self-resolves → bare `python3`; **(b)** command word for *consumer* project tooling → `.venv/bin/` is right, left alone; **(c)** prose describing the convention, and the interpreter **resolver** blocks in `run_checks.sh`, `self_check.sh`, `claim_task.sh` and the git-hook examples — those probe-then-fall-back chains are the correct pattern and are what makes (a) safe. Deciding the cut was the phase, exactly as Phase 173's 31 bare refs collapsed to 3 actionable with 18 shipping unchanged on purpose.

**The guard screens a claim shape, not a count.** `tests/test_venv_command_word.py` asserts that no shipped file gives any Sysop script a `.venv/bin/` command word, with the script inventory **derived from the tree** so a script added later is covered the day it lands. It pins no number: a new skill, a new script, a new `.venv/bin/pytest` line all pass untouched, and only the defect reddens — Phase 175 shipped a guard that reddened correct prose, and a count would do it here on the first legitimate addition. Two calibration tests hold it honest in both directions (it sees all five defect spellings including the no-`3` one; it stays green on seven correct lines that ship today). It enumerates shipped files via `git ls-files`, not `rglob` — `.claude/worktrees/agent-*/` holds stale untracked copies of the whole tree that inflate a naive walk ~10×.

**Author-side pass, rule 1 — final battery 30 mutations, 30 killed; the first run was 19/24, and the survivor classes were different in kind.** All 18 site reverts (every one of the sixteen fixed sites, the docstring three line-by-line) were killed on the first run. Of six guard attacks, five survived, and **only two of those were real**. The regex had been inlined at all three call sites, so blinding the one `_offending_lines` uses left both calibration tests green — each was validating its own private copy. That is **Phase 181's six-readers-one-writer defect, reproduced inside the guard written to prevent a different one**; the predicate became a single `_pattern()` writer. **The identical defect then recurred one function over and the battery caught it too:** with the continuation join living inside `_offending_lines`, a test calling `_logical_lines` directly *survived* reverting the scan to physical lines — validating the helper, not its use — so the scan body was extracted to `_scan_text` and both tests re-pointed through it. The other three first-run "survivors" were **inert mutations, not weak guards**: the battery inserted `_roots.clear()` after `_roots = []`, and every append follows that line, so it changed nothing. A mutation that does not alter behaviour proves nothing about the test that survives it — they were replaced with mutations that do (drop the `venv/` layout; drop the git-common-dir main-checkout arm), both killed by the execution tests written for those arms. A vacuity hole found while fixing this is closed too: an empty `git ls-files` result would have made the whole guard vacuously green, so the file list now asserts three known anchors are present.

**Rule 1's assumption classes found four bypasses; three are closed and the fourth is a residual with a reason.** Probing *what the guard matches on* rather than what it checks: a **backslash continuation**, an **interpreter flag before the operand** (`-u`, `-X`), and the **dotted `-m` spelling** all walked straight through. None is adversarial — the rule's own text calls them how people write — so all three are closed (logical-line joining, a flag-token allowance, a dotted alternation) and each has a mutation that kills a test. The fourth, a **variable-held interpreter** (`PY=.venv/bin/python3; $PY sysop/scripts/x.py`), is **declined with a stated reason rather than left unattempted**: the only in-tree instances of a venv interpreter in a variable are the *probed* resolvers — `run_checks.sh:50-58`'s `[[ -x ]]` chain with a `python3` fallback and `exec "$PYTHON" run_checks_impl.py`, and `self_check.sh:85-96` — which are the **correct** pattern and are precisely what makes the bare command word safe. A guard keyed to "a variable holds a venv interpreter" reddens every one of them, which Phase 175 established is worse than the gap; separating a probed assignment from a blind one is the judgement no pattern encodes. It is also not the house style, since Phase 126 established a variable command word binds no static allow-rule. `test_declared_residual_variable_held_interpreter` pins both halves — the bypass and the resolvers it protects — so the decision is in the suite rather than in this paragraph alone.

**Rule 2 — re-reading the new prose against the code — caught one false claim in this very entry.** The first draft said `/review-close` converged on bare `python3` "at three command sites". There are **two** executable lines (`:841`, `:1095`); `:1001` is prose *citing* the command inside a step description, and counting a citation as an invocation is the same class of error this phase exists to correct. Corrected here and in the archive entry. The commit message shipped before the pass and still carries the original wording; the record is the correction. **Rule 3 — running the commands the change prescribes** — is the fixture matrix above: every one of the four prescribed commands was run in both shapes across four environments, with `tasks/index.yml` built from `tasks/schema.md` rather than from memory.

**Adversarial round: three lenses (does it execute / are its claims true / are the guards real), one round.** Three rather than two because the phase ships behaviour *and* a record making numeric claims — the governor's stated condition. Independent fresh-context `general-purpose` agents in isolated worktrees, told not to mutate and to verify their own revision.

**The execute lens confirmed the central swap and then falsified four things the phase had written.** Its independently-built matrix — no venv / `.venv`+yaml / `venv/`+yaml / a venv-shaped dir with no yaml / subdirectory / non-git / linked worktree / system-yaml / symlinked `.venv`, all four commands, both words — agreed with the phase's: post-183 is equal or better everywhere the change targets. What it broke was the prose. **(1) The new universal rule was false for two scripts.** "Never give a `sysop/scripts/*.py` invocation a `.venv/bin/` command word — those scripts resolve venv PyYAML themselves" is true of the five Phase-182 scripts and **false** for `check_skill_models.py` and `resolve_skill_models.py`, which reach yaml through `_model_roles.py`'s lazy import and carry no bootstrap; the lens reproduced `ModuleNotFoundError` on a `venv/`-layout consumer. Not a live break — nothing prescribes them bare and `install.sh` uses its own probed `pick_python_with_yaml()` — but it was a shipped instruction stated over all of `sysop/scripts/`. Now scoped, with the exception named. **(2) The resolution order was documented backwards at four sites.** The phase wrote "CWD, then ancestors, then the main checkout"; the code's own comment says *"Order is script-anchored FIRST … and only then the CWD. CWD-first let an unrelated project's venv win"* — so the new prose documented **the precise bug Phase 182's round had fixed**, inherited by copying that phase's summary instead of reading the block. Corrected in `WORKFLOW.md`, `claim-task/SKILL.md:254`, the test docstring and this entry. **(3) "Strictly less portable" was false.** On a host with no `python3` on `PATH` (or a broken pyenv shim) but a working `.venv`, the venv word runs and the bare one exits 127. The trade is still worth making and now says so instead of claiming strictness. **(4) The guard reddened a correct line** — `.venv/bin/pytest tests/test_validate_tasks.py`, because the stem alternation had no left boundary and the prefix matcher swallowed `tests/test_`. That is **Phase 175's failure mode inside the guard whose docstring claims to have avoided it**, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` is scanned, which is exactly where such a line belongs. Fixed twice over: the interpreter is now `python[0-9.]*` rather than any venv binary, and the operand must be bare or path-separated.

**Two unswept siblings, both fixed.** `git-hooks/examples/pre-commit-tasks-validate.example` still told readers the system-`python3` fallback "will fail loudly with `ModuleNotFoundError`" — false since Phase 182 wherever a venv exists. And `review-close/SKILL.md:432` teaches the same venv-prefix rule that `WORKFLOW.md` and `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md` had just received the carve-out for; it now points at it.

**The residual claim was an overclaim.** "The one bypass NOT closed" is wrong: `.env/bin/`, `.tox/py311/bin/`, poetry and conda interpreter paths survive the predicate too. They are declined **together and for one reason** — the predicate is anchored on the literal `venv/bin/` segment, and widening it to "any interpreter under some environment directory" is what would start reddening ordinary absolute paths. Recorded as known-uncovered rather than claimed closed, and pinned by an assertion that fails loudly if one ever *becomes* covered.

**The claims lens found ten more, and two of them shipped.** A calibration string this file asserted "ships today" was a **paraphrase** — the shipped line at `claim-task/SKILL.md:170` carries a "no `&&` compound" clause the test's copy dropped, which is the paraphrased-not-verified mode this repo's Phase 142 and 161 rounds both fired on. And a docstring in `tests/`, which **ships to the public mirror**, attributed to Phase 173 "a false green from a command exiting 127"; `PHASE_LOG.md:3936` records that phase's false-green as *"arriving from the harness rather than from a `127`"*. The reason to execute rather than read stands on its own; the borrowed anecdote did not. It also caught `docs/install-and-update.md:233` reported resolved while its remedy was still inert in the state the doc documents (the `claim_task.sh` twin got an "after the fix above" qualifier and the doc never did), and the `ruff` exemplar being a restatement that deleted the rule's only worked example of naming a Python script through the venv interpreter — replaced with a **consumer-owned** script, which teaches the distinction rather than removing it.

**The guard lens is the one that earned the third slot, and its headline is the phase's real defect.** `_offending_lines` — the file sweep, which is the entire product of this phase — had **zero positive coverage**. Its only consumer was a *negative* assertion (`assert not hits`), and a negative assertion cannot notice that the thing producing the negative has stopped looking. Reducing the scan to a no-op left the suite green; **restoring the original defect on top of that left it green too**, so all eighteen site mutations rested on one line no test protected. Verified by hand before fixing. `_offending_lines` now takes an injectable file list and `test_the_sweep_finds_a_planted_defect` drives it end-to-end over real files on disk, so gutting any link in the chain fails there instead of passing everywhere.

**Four more blind spots in the same guard, all closed.** A **quoted** interpreter (`"${REPO_ROOT}/.venv/bin/python3" sysop/scripts/…`) was completely invisible — and it is the shape `WORKFLOW.md:885` itself teaches, since "spell out the absolute-to-repo-root invocation" means quoting in shell. A flag with a **separated value** (`-X utf8`, `-W ignore`) was blind while the guard's own comment claimed `-X` — a coverage claim asserted nowhere and false. The `Bash(` skip discarded the **whole logical line**, so a sentence citing a rule *and* prescribing the defect went through untouched; rule spans are blanked now, not lines. And the scan was blind to **untracked** files, i.e. blind exactly when a site is being authored — the lens planted a new `SKILL.md` carrying the canonical defect and the suite stayed green.

**The declared residual was refuted, and the rule says that ends the argument.** The author-side pass declined the variable-held interpreter as "the judgement no pattern encodes". The lens encoded it in about twenty lines: discriminate on the **fallback**, not the probe — a probed resolver always assigns a non-venv candidate too (`run_checks.sh:55`, `self_check.sh:93`), so flag `$VAR <stem>` only when *every* assignment to `VAR` in that file is a venv path. Zero false positives across the shipped tree, catches the blind case. The author-side rule holds a declined survivor to *impossible to close in kind*, not merely unattempted, so it is closed on the lens's own predicate rather than defended. The residual paragraph was also **two files short** — the two git-hook examples also hold venv interpreters in variables — which is "the filed N was really M", the finding this entire phase is built on, recurring inside its own disposition. The replacement test derives that population from the tree so the count cannot go stale again.

**The independent battery beat the author's, for the sixth phase running.** Lens 3 wrote 37 mutations: **23 of 31 kill-expected survived (74%)**; tree-wide, after discounting two inert mutations and four killed by Phase 182's pre-existing file, **17 of 29 (59%)**. Its six negative controls all survived and its planted control was killed, so the harness was neither always-red nor always-green. Its recomputation of this phase's own 31/31 is the honest one and is recorded as such: **18 are reverts of the phase's own edits and 8 more revert behaviour whose killing assertion was written in the same author-side pass**, so roughly 26 of 31 could not have survived. The number is arithmetically true and epistemically near-empty — wiring, not coverage. That is the same lesson Phase 182's round recorded, and this phase re-learned it rather than inheriting it.

**One doctrine site the sweep missed, inside the guard's own scope.** `install.sh:150`'s comment said *"validate_tasks.py runs via `.venv/bin/python3` from the pre-commit hook"* — the same doctrine shape the phase fixed in `WORKFLOW.md`, and the last instance of it. A shell comment carries no invocation, so the guard cannot see it and the sweep did not either; fixed by hand and recorded as a limit of pattern-based sweeping rather than papered over.

**What the round did not shake.** The `yamlless_bin` shim is genuinely yaml-less; `_venv_with_yaml` copies PyYAML rather than symlinking, so it cannot pass through the running interpreter's `sys.path` (verified by blinding the loop and watching two scripts flip to rc 2); the exit-127 assertions are real, not tautological; the pathspec is *correct* for today's shipped set, and the defect was that nothing pinned it; and no surviving instance of the fixed defect remains in the shipped tree in any shape three independent sweeps could find. The population claim itself — filed ten, actually sixteen — was reproduced independently, as were the three false claims in the original filing.

**One honest limit, recorded rather than closed.** The doctrine fix this entry calls "the find that mattered" is the least-guarded thing in the change: deleting the `WORKFLOW.md` carve-out or reverting the four "preferred per Phase 45b" bullets to their now-false wording is invisible to the whole suite. That is prose with no mechanical enforcement, and a reversion guard over it would prove wiring rather than coverage — the very thing this round just finished discounting. Filed as a known gap.

**Gate. The first version of this paragraph was wrong in four places, and two lenses caught it independently — so read the correction as the point.** It claimed *"2,910 collected, +19 … measured by `--collect-only` rather than arithmetic. 2,903 passed, 4 skipped, 3 failed."* Every number was a **pre-edit measurement**: taken before the author-side pass added tests, and never re-taken. Worse, the failure *set* was wrong — the tree carried a **fourth** failure, `tests/test_round_yield_ledger.py::test_every_phase_from_174_has_a_ledger_row`, because adding this phase's `CLAUDE.md` row **arms the gate that requires a `ROUND_YIELD_LEDGER.md` row**, and the row had not been written. That is the same gate, red for the same reason, that Phase 182's round caught in Phase 182 — and the sentence "measured rather than arithmetic" is the *literal correction that phase was forced to make*, re-broken one phase later by the same mechanism. Measuring before the last edit is not measuring.

**The true figures, taken after the final edit.** **2,923 collected, +32** over `main`'s 2,891 — all 32 in `tests/test_venv_command_word.py`, zero removals. **2,916 passed, 4 skipped, 3 failed.** The three are `test_install_concat.py::TestCollisionMerge::test_comment_survives_update_cycles`, `::TestPromotionOverlayDurability::test_promoted_overlay_survives_update`, and `test_install_runtime_migration.py::test_second_update_is_a_no_op_resume`. They reproduce identically on a pristine worktree of `main` from this clone, so they are **not** introduced here — but the round showed "pre-existing" is the wrong word: the claims lens saw all three **pass** in its own worktree. They are **environment-sensitive**, which is a different and more useful statement, and it matches the § Low entry Phase 159b filed reporting a clone-vs-worktree divergence (with the opposite polarity). Left as that standing item rather than folded in here.

**Author-side battery: 37 mutations, 37 killed — and the honest reading is the round's, not this number.** Its guard lens recomputed an earlier cut and was right: 18 rows are reverts of the phase's own edits and several more revert behaviour whose killing assertion was written in the same pass, so most of the set proves *wiring*. The rows that carry information are the ones attacking assumptions — what the predicate matches on, where the scan looks, whether it can run at all — and those exist in this battery only because the round wrote them first. The number is a floor, not exhaustion. That framing is now in the harness's own docstring so the next reader does not repeat the mistake.

## Phase 184 (executed 2026-08-05 — the mirror gate cannot see a false claim; the § Planned-phases entry framed by the 182–183 push, absorbing the § Medium and § Low entries filed the same day)

**The trigger was a measurement, not a worry.** The 2026-08-05 cut's leak gate was **green on the first build**, and it would have stayed green with all three of the Phase-182-introduced falsehoods in the tree — including a fifth CWD-first site, one phase after Phase 183's round swept four. Everything that cut actually found was found by two agents *reading* the snapshot. The blind spot is structural rather than an oversight in any pass: Passes 1a/1b/1c ask *does the tree contain a blocked string*, Pass 3 *is an excluded file present*, Pass 4 *is an excluded class tracked*, Passes 2/2b diff known provenance classes. **Nothing asked whether shipped prose is true of the code beside it, or whether it points at something the mirror strips** — and the phase's own finding is that those are not one problem but three, with three different levels of decidability.

**Leg 0 ran first, and the filed counts were low again — the fifth phase in the run.** Filed: 9 pointers, 3 falsehoods, 1 "fifth CWD-first site". Derived from the tree: **19 unqualified pointer defects among 22 token-sites on 21 distinct lines** in the operational surface, **4 CWD-first sites plus 2 ambiguous** (3 of the 4 shipping), and **4 live permission-coverage cases where the filed invariant reaches 1**. The run is **five** — 173: 2 → 31; 179: 2 → 10; 182: 2 → 10; 183: 10 → 16; 184: 9 → 19 — and "six" stood here beside that five-item list until the round's claims lens counted them. **One caveat that shortens it further:** 182 → 183 is the *same* class chained (the § Medium item 182 filed is what 183 executed), so counting both inflates the streak by one.

**Leg A — the discrimination problem dissolved once it was measured instead of reasoned about.** The § Planned-phases entry named the hard part correctly: `PHASE_LOG.md` alone carries 163 `CLAUDE.md` mentions across 131 lines, almost all past-tense narration, and *"distinguishing a past-tense narration from a live pointer is the actual design problem of this leg"*. Sweeping the whole tree showed it is three separable problems, none of which needs tense parsing:

- **`CLAUDE.md` is a basename collision, not a narration.** **417 of 751** raw hits named it — measured with the shipped detector against `be33c97`; an earlier draft said "356 of 732" from a scratch sweeper whose token pattern was narrower than the one that shipped, and neither figure reproduces under the final code — and in a shipped file it nearly always means *the consumer's* `CLAUDE.md` — a live concept every install writes. It is dropped as a **referent**, tree-wide. The Pass-1a lesson is applied pre-emptively: the carve-out is token-scoped, never line-scoped, with a test that plants a second stripped referent on a `CLAUDE.md` line and requires it to still fire. A line-scoped carve-out is exactly how a blocked identifier reached the public repo and read clean at every cut for months.
- **Historical records discharge at the file level, for one sentence each.** `PHASE_LOG.md` carried 272 such references on 202 lines — 236 of the references unqualified — and `tests/PORT_LOG.md` 5 on 4 lines; all measured on the pre-fix tree with the shipped detector. (**Units stated because an earlier draft mixed them**, pairing a token count for one file with a line count for the other and then adding the two; the round caught it. The counts also move every time either file grows, including from this entry — one more reason the class is recorded rather than gated.) Editing 202 lines of history to strip provenance costs more than it buys, so both files now carry one header paragraph saying the names are maintainer-side — and the guard **requires that exact sentence**, so the exemption is earned and readable rather than asserted in a list inside the test.
- **Test modules name excluded paths as their subject**, in code (`REPO_ROOT / "tools" / "X"`), and skip on absence. That was measured, not trusted: a mirror was built at `be33c97` and its suite run — **2815 passed, 74 skipped, 0 failed**.

What remained after those three is the surface a consumer is told to act on, and it is gated at zero by the new **Pass 5** in `tests/test_mirror_leak_gate.py`. The remedy is the one the § Low filing proposed and the tree already practised at two sites in `docs/analysis/REPORT.md`: a reference to a stripped path must either go, or say in the same breath that the referent is not in the public tree.

**The guard's placement was decided, not defaulted — and the entry was right to demand that.** A pointer guard carries no blocked identifiers, so shipping it was a real option. Two facts settled it into the mirror-excluded module anyway: it needs `SHIPPED_EXCLUSIONS`/`_is_excluded`/`_shipped_files`, and a second copy of that list is precisely the drift `test_exclusion_set_still_matches_the_mirror_script` exists to prevent; and a shipped copy would read `tools/make_public_mirror.sh` for its own drift check, which the mirror strips, so in the public tree it would skip **every time**. A guard that always skips is the decorative-guard failure this repo has hit from Phase 155 onward.

**The escape hatch widened itself on the first run, inside the phase that built it.** The first draft accepted *any* qualifier phrase in a file's first 30 lines as a whole-file exemption. `run_checks/accounting.py` writes a legitimate line-level qualifier twelve lines in, and silently went dark to the entire pass — caught by the guard's own `test_the_operational_surface_cannot_buy_a_file_level_exemption` on the very first execution. The exemption now requires one distinctive sentence that cannot be tripped into, and a control pins the accident. A second self-inflicted defect followed immediately: the sentinel is a wrapped `> ` blockquote in both files that carry it, so a naive line-join inserted `>` mid-sentence and `tests/PORT_LOG.md` came out both exempt-by-intent and scanned.

**Leg B — the filed invariant was decidable and reached one case in four.** As filed it was: derive the script list from `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.2a's carve-out sentence and check each against the shipped `.claude/settings.json`. That is real, it is Invariant 1, and it catches the `backfill_completed_dates.py` defect exactly. But sweeping for the class found three more live cases it cannot see, because they are not doc-enumerated at all: **`bash sysop/scripts/self_check.sh` had no rule of any shape** while the installer's own post-install footer prescribes it in *both* modes and `docs/getting-started.md` puts it in a fence — the first thing a fresh loop-mode install tells a consumer to run was also its first permission prompt; **`cleanup_worktrees.sh --clean`** likewise, prescribed by `/sitrep` and `WORKFLOW.md` § 4; and `/review-close`'s recovery step piped `close_batch.sh` into **`tee /tmp/close-batch.log`**, where `|` is a documented separator, `tee` is in no read-only set and binds nothing, and the prompt therefore arrives *after* the close has run — a hardcoded `/tmp` path riding along. (**An earlier draft called that "a 10th unguarded bare-`/tmp` path of the class Phase 153 swept nine of"; the attribution is wrong** — Phase 153's class was unguarded **`$TMPDIR`**, whose prescribed fix is `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}`, and a literal `/tmp/…` is not an instance of it. Six bare `/tmp/` paths remain in the shipped tree and this phase closed none.) So the shipped invariant is the wider one: **every command a shipped file prescribes inside a fenced code block must have a covering rule**, checked against the full template and, separately, against `install.sh`'s `LOOP_ALLOW` for the scripts loop mode ships.

**The carve-out sentence was also false in a way nobody had read closely: it ended mid-clause.** *"…and it is what the shipped `.claude/settings.json` allow-rules."* — an assertion of a relationship that stops before saying what the relationship is. It also called five scripts "the five scripts a skill actually prescribes" when no skill prescribes `backfill_completed_dates.py` at all; only `tasks/README.md` gives a recipe for it. Both corrected, and both pinned.

**Leg C was allowed to conclude "not guardable." It measured, and the measurement split the class rather than settling it.** The acting surface — `core/skills/**`, `core/companion/**`, `install.sh`, `packs/**`, `docs/**` — carries **9** mechanically-findable intra-repo line citations, **2 of them stale**: `claim_task.sh:86`'s `self_check.sh:61-66` (correct at `adbf0cf~1`, invalidated by `adbf0cf` itself, which hoisted `MAIN_ROOT` above probe 3 in the same commit that wrote the citation) and `docs/one-rule.md:117`'s `grep.py:190`, which had drifted 41 lines to `:231` since Phase 161. Nine is small enough to pin exactly, so `tests/test_intra_repo_citations.py` sweeps the population from the tree and requires each citation to register the **content anchor** its range must still contain — a registry that cannot go stale as a population, because an unregistered citation fails. `PHASE_LOG.md` is the other half and is **not** guarded: **220** citations under Leg C's own regex — the one that produced the contrasting 9; an earlier draft said ~579, folding in bare `:NN` and extensionless forms the regex never sees — at a sampled **50% stale**, and roughly half of those stale *correctly* — a phase entry's job is to cite the line it changed, so that line stops holding the content by design. The § Planned-phases framing predicted a high-false-positive guard there; the measurement confirms it rather than assuming it, which is the difference between a recorded finding and a shrug.

**What Leg C does not close, stated so the phase cannot claim it.** The anchor proves the cited range still contains the named thing. Whether the citing sentence *characterises* it correctly is untouched — and the same `claim_task.sh` comment is the proof: besides the wrong line range it said the hazard was documented *"in the other direction"*, wording Phase 182's own round refuted (*"same direction, named from the probe side"*), with the correction landing in `PHASE_LOG.md` and never in the shipped comment. The line number is now guarded; the adjective is not. Prose citation forms (`tasks/schema.md` line 60) and extensionless forms (`review-close:387`, ~314 tree-wide against a skill/script-stem vocabulary — an earlier draft said 90 — none in the acting surface) are out of reach of the sweep and recorded as such.

**The CWD-first class: the filed "fifth site" was four, and three of them ship.** `tests/test_heredoc_permission_idiom.py:175` was the filed one. Beyond it: `PHASE_LOG.md`'s Phase-182 entry asserted *"CWD → the file's ancestors → the main checkout via git-common-dir"* with an explicit arrow ordering — **contradicting two other sentences in the same entry**, which is this phase's thesis in miniature and the worst of the four, since `PHASE_LOG.md` is the declared source of truth for why a call was made; `tests/test_claim_task_venv_python.py:440` described `validate_tasks.py`'s bootstrap as *"CWD-relative"*, the pre-182 shape, written into the tree by Phase 182 itself, and gave a reason its own record contradicts; and `REVIEW_ARCHIVE.md:2172` carries the same inversion but does not ship, so it takes a bracketed correction rather than a rewrite — the archive is a verbatim freeze and a silent edit there would be a second falsehood about the first.

**One further shipped falsehood, unfiled and found by reading the code beside it.** `WORKFLOW.md`'s `self_check.sh` row said its interpreter is *"probed in the installer's own order: `.venv` → `venv` → `PATH`"*. It is not: `self_check.sh`'s probe 3 tries the **main** checkout's `.venv` then `venv`, then *this* checkout's, then `PATH` — close to but not identical with `run_checks.sh`'s own chain, which is why the shipped row now enumerates the order rather than naming another script's — `run_checks.sh`'s order, not the installer's, and the main-vs-current axis is the whole reason the probe exists (a worktree carries no venv). The sentence named the one axis that does not matter and dropped the one that does.

**A reviewer finding that did not survive verification, recorded because the round's own rule says to.** One sweep reported that `REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`'s Phase-126-heredoc entry *"names only the `document-work` one"* of seven sibling sites. Reading the entry, its headline names one and its body enumerates all seven with the grep that produced them. Confirmed-by-a-reviewer is not confirmed; the claim was dropped.

**Scoping honesty, since the § Planned-phases entry demanded it up front and got its own arithmetic wrong once already.** Leg A closes one whole class — 19 defects, none of them among the three filed falsehoods. Leg B closes 1 of those 3 plus 3 unfiled permission cases the filed invariant could not reach. Legs A and B together reach neither of the other two filed falsehoods; those were fixed by hand this phase, and the *class* they belong to is Leg C's, where the acting surface is now guarded and `PHASE_LOG.md` is recorded as out of reach in kind. Nothing here makes a false claim about behaviour detectable in general — the three new guards check pointers, command coverage, and citation anchors, and each says in its own docstring what it cannot do.

**Six new allow-rules reddened four existing drift guards, and the fourth one caught this phase writing its own defect.** The loop-mode allow-set is pinned by count *and* by set (19 → 21, plus two count comments in `install.sh`); `test_permission_surface_drift.py`'s assertion 2 requires every seeded rule to be named by a skill or carry a written justification, and all six of these are prescribed by **docs or by the installer's own footer** rather than by a skill step — which is exactly why the fenced-prescription guard had to exist and why assertion 2 alone could not have found them; the installer's full-mode rule-count comment moved 65 → 71. **And `tests/test_prescribed_command_coverage.py` — written this phase, to catch prose that is false about the code beside it — shipped the sentence *"a loop-mode install seeds only LOOP_ALLOW — 19 rules, not the full 65"*, both numbers falsified by the same commit that wrote it.** That is the Phase-182 shape reproduced inside the guard built to prevent it, caught only because an unrelated drift guard forced a re-read. It is recorded rather than quietly corrected, because it is the strongest available evidence for the phase's own thesis: **a new guard does not make its author's prose true, and nothing in this change would have caught that sentence.**

**Author-side battery: 25 mutations, first run 16/25, final 25/25 — and the split is the honest number, not the total.** Seven rows are declared reversions; eighteen attack assumptions (what-it-matches-on, what-it-accepts, where-it-looks, reachability, vacuity, coverage). Of the nine first-run survivors, **four were real guard weaknesses and three were mutations too weak to prove anything** — deleting one of two equivalent allow-rules where either satisfies the check, shifting an anchor one line *inside* its own cited range, and a `CITATION_ANCHORS = {} or {...}` that evaluates to the non-empty dict and so changed nothing. The four real ones: the fenced-command sweep was `^`-anchored and missed **all five indented commands in the tree** (`add-task:79`, `auto-build:851`, `claim-task:966`, `review-close:930`, `review-close:1095`; the round's claims lens measured four, because at the revision it read, `auto-build:851`'s *bare* fence was invisible to the module's own regex too), including the very `close_batch.sh` line whose `| tee` tail this phase removed (all five have rules, so nothing was live — the population was simply short by five with nothing saying so); two Leg C controls **re-implemented the predicate they were meant to test**, so widening the real staleness window to the whole file and disabling the registration check both stayed green; nothing pinned `POINTER_QUALIFIERS`' narrowness; and nothing pinned that a command word without a rule is uncovered. An author's zero measures self-consistency — exhaustion is the reviewers' measurement, and this one is offered as a claim to falsify.

**Adversarial round: three lenses (does it execute / are its claims true / are its tests real), one round, over `2b0eb00`.** Three rather than two because the phase ships behaviour *and* a record making numeric claims — the governor's condition. Fresh-context `general-purpose` agents in isolated worktrees, told not to mutate and to verify their revision first.

**The guards lens wrote 61 mutations and 43 survived, against the author-side battery's 25/25 — the seventh phase running that an independent lens beats the author's number.** Its sharpest observation is not the count but *where*: the author battery was accurate for the 25 mutations it contained and could not be falsified on any of the four author-pass fixes, yet **20 of the 43 survivors were planted defects in populations the battery never probes**. Self-selection in *where it looks*, which is the failure mode the doctrine names and the one an author is structurally worst placed to see.

**Four HIGH findings, all reproduced by hand before fixing.**

- **The fenced-command sweep read only ` ```bash `/`sh`/`shell` with nothing after it — and `auto-build/SKILL.md:851` prescribes `claim_task.sh --release` inside a *bare* fence.** Live, shipped, invisible; ` ```console ` and ` ```bash title="…" ` were invisible too. **This is the same "where it looks" class the author-side pass had just closed one variable over** — that pass fixed `^`-anchoring and missed fence-language in the same function. Widened to any fence: +11 sites, +3 command-word pairs, all real prescriptions.
- **Invariant 3 (no piping a Sysop script) had no positive control and could be deleted outright** — `if False:` and `for path in []:` both left the suite green, so the exact `close_batch.sh … | tee /tmp/x.log` defect this phase removed could be re-planted unseen. It also re-implemented the fence walk, so fixing the fence matcher would not have reached it. Both now share one walk, with a canary.
- **`install.sh`'s post-install footer was not in the prescribing set, although the module's own docstring named it as the surface that prescribes `self_check.sh` "in BOTH modes".** `self_check.sh` was caught only because `docs/getting-started.md` happens to fence it — the guard was right by luck. `README.md`, `packs/**` and `tasks/README.md` were outside too.
- **The file-level exemption reached 29 of 175 operational files.** The escape-hatch test filtered to `core/` + `packs/` + `install.sh`, leaving all of `docs/`, `README.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `.github/**` able to buy a whole-file exemption with one header line — demonstrated RED → GREEN on `docs/getting-started.md`. **The test's docstring said "must not reach the acting surface" and the module's said "gated at zero"; both were false for those 29 files.** A guard whose own prose overstates its population is this phase's subject, in this phase's guard.

**And the sharpest MEDIUM is the same defect this repo has now shipped three times.** `FOREIGN_CITATION_MARKERS` — the carve-out that keeps gdp-side provenance citations out of Leg C's sweep — was **line-scoped**, so `See \`self_check.sh:12\` (the gdp backport).` removed a real citation from the sweep entirely: never registered, never checked. That is the Pass-1a line-vs-token defect that put a blocked identifier on the public repo, reproduced **one module away from `test_the_claude_md_carveout_does_not_blind_the_scan`, the test written in this same phase to prevent exactly that shape**. Knowing a failure mode well enough to guard against it in one place is not knowing it well enough to avoid it in the next. Now token-scoped, with the trailing-marker case pinned as a control.

**Also fixed from the round:** the ±1-line qualifier window laundered an unrelated adjacent bullet (22 qualifier-bearing lines already sat beside 44 neighbours) — the window now follows sentence wrapping instead of line counting; unresolved citations were silently dropped, so a pointer to a *deleted* file read exactly like a teaching placeholder — the nine real placeholders are baselined with reasons and a new one must be classified; `_resolve`'s docstring claimed "ambiguity is a finding" while the caller took `resolved[0]` (`SKILL.md:64` matches 23 files) — ambiguity is now refused for registered citations; a control that re-implemented its own predicate — the **third** instance of that shape in this file, after the author pass caught two; a brittle `:930` line pin **I added in the author-side pass**, which reddened with a false message on any unrelated edit above it — a stale line pin inside the leg that exists because line pins go stale; and the declared `docs/**` scope that silently dropped `docs/workflow.html` and `docs/index.html`, the published monograph and landing page.

**Guard count 37 → 51 tests across the three modules.** Every fix above was reproduced by hand before being applied and re-verified by A/B afterwards; none was taken on the reviewer's word.

**Re-pointing the battery at the round's rewrites went 31/37, and every survivor was the same shape: the fix was right and nothing pinned it.** The doctrine says a rewrite takes the battery with it, so the mutations were re-aimed at the new fence walk, the new qualifier window, the new citation sweep — and six survived, each because the round's correction had shipped without a control. That is exactly what the guards lens had just demonstrated about the *first* battery, reproduced one iteration later by the same author who had just read the demonstration. Two of the six are worth naming: the exemption test's new population assertion **recomputed the file list beside the loop instead of recording what the loop inspected**, so narrowing the loop left the assertion happy; and `FENCE_OPEN` had been **dead since the shared fence walk landed**, which is why a mutation against it could not fail — the dead constant surfaced only because something tried to break it. Final: **39 mutations, 39 killed, 7 declared reversions, 32 attacking assumptions** — reported with the round's 43-of-61 beside it, because an author's zero measures self-consistency and the round's number is the one that measures exhaustion.

**The execute lens found one live defect the phase had declared fixed, and it is the sharper kind.** `core/companion/tasks/README.md:53` — the *one recipe* that runs `backfill_completed_dates.py`, and the reason Leg B seeded a rule for it at all — writes the script with **no command word**: `` Run `sysop/scripts/backfill_completed_dates.py --source-file …` ``. The file ships `-rwxr-xr-x` with a `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang, so that literal string runs, and the seeded `Bash(python3 sysop/scripts/backfill_completed_dates.py:*)` binds nothing of it. **So the fix closed the claim and not the case**, and `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.2a's new parenthetical — written by this phase to record the correction — was itself still false. The recipe now names `python3`. Note what did *not* catch it: the new guard reads fenced blocks, and this is an inline-backticked imperative, which is precisely the boundary the guard declines to cross. A reviewer reading the doc caught it.

**The lens also refuted a premise this session had fed to all three reviewers.** The round prompts said three suite failures were "known pre-existing" — a figure carried over from Phase 183's record and never re-measured. At `be33c97` the suite is **2919 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed**, and all three named tests pass. So every failure the lens found at `2b0eb00` was self-inflicted, and the caller had pre-supplied an excuse for them. **A false premise handed to the adversary is worse than a false claim in the record** — it tells reviewers which findings not to report — and it is recorded here because nothing else would have surfaced it.

**Two more of its findings were live and are closed:** `docs/*.md` and `core/companion/docs/*.md` were non-recursive globs, so `docs/analysis/` sat outside Leg B's population entirely (now `**`); and `test_the_exempt_records_actually_carry_their_disclaimer` told the reader to "restore it or scan the file" while `_operational_files` excluded `PHASE_LOG.md` **by name** — deleting the paragraph could never have caused it to be scanned, so the guard's stated remedy was a false sentence. The name-based special case is gone and the header sentence is now the only thing buying the exemption, which makes the message true. Its `sh` and `env bash` command-word gaps are closed too.

**Where the two independent lenses agreed, they agreed on the same three defects** — the line-scoped foreign-citation filter, the adjacent-line qualifier bleed, and the relative-path pointer miss — each found separately and each already closed from the guards lens. Overlap of roughly that size is what the governor's ~15% figure predicts, and it is not evidence: the agreement added no weight to findings that were reproduced by hand either way.

**The claims lens found three HIGH untruths in the record, and all three are the class this phase exists to eliminate.** It also reproduced the phase's two hardest empirical claims exactly — the 25/25 battery and the 2815/74 mirror run — which is what makes the rest weigh.

- **The tree was red on arrival with five self-inflicted failures**, and two of them are ironies worth keeping. `test_round_yield_ledger` failed because the `CLAUDE.md` Phase-log row *arms* that guard before the ledger row exists — **the identical defect Phase 182 shipped, documented in the very entry this phase was editing**, which even records the fix ("record first, ledger row, *then* the suite run"). And `test_permission_surface_drift`'s assertion 2 failed on all six new rules, in the same commit whose new checklist filing says that assertion "checks the other direction … **which is exactly why this passes today**". Reading a lesson is not learning it.
- **A line citation invalidated by its own commit — inside the correction of that exact defect, in the one file the citation guard excludes.** The Phase-182 correction above cited `:4258` and `:4284`; this phase's own header paragraph then shifted every line by two, and `:4284` was wrong under *any* offset — it lands in Phase 183's entry. Now cited by name. Leg C guards the acting surface and explicitly does not guard `PHASE_LOG.md`; this is what that decision costs, demonstrated on the phase that made it.
- **A new guard's docstring stated two counts its own commit falsified** — the "19 rules, not the full 65" already recorded above.

**Six MEDIUM findings, all counting errors, all fixed:** "the fifth phase running" and "now six long" beside a five-item list (it is five, and one of the five is the same class chained, so even that is generous); "19 of 21" mixing token- and line-counts (19 unqualified of **22** token-sites on 21 lines, and a **third** already-qualified site at `tests/README.md:23` the sweep's prose missed); "356 of 732" reproducing under no definition of the shipped detector (**417 of 751**); a token count for `PHASE_LOG.md` added to a line count for `PORT_LOG.md`; "~579" citations where the module's own regex sees **220**; and a `/tmp` attribution to Phase 153's class when that class is unguarded **`$TMPDIR`** and a literal `/tmp/…` is not an instance of it. The lens's one miscount was "four indented commands" against the phase's five — it measured with the module's regex at a revision where `auto-build:851`'s bare fence was invisible, which is the finding it had itself reported one line earlier.

**And re-measuring for those fixes turned up an over-inclusion the round's own fix had introduced.** Widening the fence matcher to *any* fence pulled ten `"Bash(bash sysop/scripts/…)"` **rule declarations** out of a settings.json example in `WORKFLOW.md` and counted them as prescribed commands. They passed by luck — the path regex stops at the `:` — but they inflated the population and would have failed the moment the doc illustrated a rule for a script the template does not seed. Rule-declaration lines are now excluded, and the real indented population is the five named above. **Every widening in this phase has cost a false positive somewhere**, which is the argument for measuring a guard's population rather than reasoning about it.

**Gate, measured on the final tree with the record and the ledger row already in place — the ordering Phase 182's round prescribed and Phase 183 re-broke.** **2,961 collected, +38** over `main`'s 2,923, all 38 in the three guard modules (`test_mirror_leak_gate.py` 13 → 23, `test_prescribed_command_coverage.py` 13 new, `test_intra_repo_citations.py` 15 new), zero removals. **2,957 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed.** The built public mirror's own suite is **2,843 passed, 74 skipped, 0 failed**, and its Passes 1a/1b/1c/3 come out empty. **Neither mirror was re-cut** — both stay at Phase 183 (public `d417cf0`, tester `6015e30`) and these fixes ride the next push, which is where the new Pass 5 will run for the first time at cut time. **[Corrected by Phase 185: that last clause is false. There is no cut-time invocation for Pass 5 to run in — neither `make_public_mirror.sh` nor `cut_public_release.sh` runs pytest or implements a Pass-5 equivalent, and the module is mirror-excluded and anchored to the source-repo root with no path override, so a copy placed inside a built snapshot goes inert rather than gating it. Pass 5 runs in the source repo, at the clean SHA being cut; what makes that sufficient is that `_shipped_files()` and the built mirror's `git ls-files` return the same set and the builder refuses a dirty tree. Phase 185 wrote the where-and-why into the runbook and added a guard that the runbook must name every pass the scripts implement.]**

**One number in this paragraph was wrong in three earlier drafts before it was right, which is the phase in miniature.** The suite figure was first quoted from a run that predated the record edits, then from one that predated the drift-guard fixes, then from a run polluted by A/B verification mutating files underneath it. Only the fourth was taken on a clean tree at the committed HEAD with nothing else running. **The failure was never arithmetic; it was measuring one thing and reporting it as another** — which is exactly the class Legs A, B and C each mechanised one slice of, and exactly the class none of them can close in general.

## Phase 185 (executed 2026-08-05 — the monograph is seven phases behind and the filed stale set is wrong in five ways; the mirror push that carries Phase 184's corrections; and whether monograph staleness is guardable at all)

**Trigger, and it is a measurement.** `docs/workflow.html` stamps itself *as of Phase 177* at four sites and tops out at Phase 177 in its prose, while the tree is at 184. `tests/test_doc_currency.py` is green and **structurally cannot see it**: Phase 118 inverted that module into a no-count ratchet whose monograph assertion is `test_monograph_is_self_consistent_and_never_ahead` — it forbids the monograph *leading* the tree and never requires it to follow. Separately both mirrors sit at public `d417cf0` / tester `6015e30`, a snapshot of private `1f03f9e`, while `main` is `b6edb38` — so Phase 184's fixes are merged and unpublished, and the three false statements the 2026-08-05 cut knowingly shipped are still live on the public repo.

**The baseline premise was re-measured rather than inherited, because the last phase got it wrong.** Phase 184 told all three of its lenses that three suite failures were "known pre-existing" — a figure inherited from Phase 183 and never re-run. Measured here on `main` before any edit: **2957 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed** in 10m12s. `main` was fully green; the inherited figure was false. The four skips are `test_install_namespace_migration.py`'s "no pre-namespace `install.sh` commit in history" guards, which are skips by design.

**Leg A — the filed scope was wrong, and the derivation is the phase's first product.** § Before announce says *"Phases 178–183 join the standing staleness backlog"* while the same paragraph carries a separate *"#220 part-D 161–169 clause"*, and the two were never reconciled. Neither is the answer. Derived phase-by-phase from the monograph against `PHASE_LOG.md` over 160–184 — asking not "does the number appear" but "is the phase's thesis present", because the monograph narrates by failure class and only four sites carry a phase number at all:

- **EXPLICIT (4):** 170, 171, 176, 177 — with 177 the weakest of the four, and the round was right to press it: at the parent its number appears *only* in the four currency stamps, never in narration, which by the stated test (is the thesis present?) is the same situation as 161 in the N/A bucket. Kept EXPLICIT because the stamps are that phase's actual product; the inconsistency is recorded rather than argued away, and it does not move ABSENT.
- **THEMATIC (4):** 166, 172, 174, 175.
- **ABSENT (10):** 162, 163, 164, 165, 167, 168, 169, 178, 179, 181.
- **N/A by nature (7):** 160, 161, 173, 180, 182, 183, 184 — maintainer-side publication process, or a phase whose product is already the file's live text, or a correction with no monograph surface.

The filed claim (*"zero mentions of 161–165 and 167–169; 174 covered by the governor section, 172/175/176 by the sixth shape"*) is **wrong in five ways**, and low again, which is the sixth phase running. Its decomposition does not survive derivation: the § Before-announce clause flags 178–183 and the part-D clause flags 161–169, so read together the filing gestures at **14** phases where the derived ABSENT set is **10** — it is not a simple undercount, it is two unreconciled clauses neither of which is the answer, and it stops before 184 either way. It calls **161** absent: true of the number, false of the coverage — that phase's corrections are load-bearing text in the file today, and an editor trusting the claim would re-add material already there. It omits **166** entirely, which is the phase the governor section's own evidence came from — the ~15% overlap figure and the "each lens produced its sharpest finding alone" list are 166's measurement, credited by the filing to 174. It omits 160 and 173 from both lists. And its *test* is the wrong test: counting `Phase N` occurrences both over- and under-counts in a document that deliberately does not narrate by number.

**Leg A — what shipped, and it is one argument rather than seven paragraphs.** Two of the seven new phases are corrections owed rather than additions, and they came first:

- **A statement that reads as false, on the public site since 2026-07-24** — the round corrected both halves of that sentence. The date is Phase 146's push, not the 2026-07-29 tester push this entry first named, so the exposure window was five days longer than claimed; and *false* overstates it, since the remedy is a rewrite of a disposition list that reads as though a placeholder discharges the obligation, not the deletion of a false proposition.** `docs/workflow.html` presented Step 2a-0's disposition **(c)** — *"named as a placeholder section still waiting to be localized"* — as one of three ways to **satisfy** the inventory-completeness invariant. Both shipped skills say the opposite in terms: *"**(c) is a named gap, not coverage**: it keeps the entry off the unmapped-entry class below, but the section binds nothing until its globs resolve"* (`codebase-review/SKILL.md:196`, `security-audit/SKILL.md:210`, verified byte-exact). The monograph now says so too. This was filed as doc-currency; it is better described as the file asserting the belief Phase 179 exists to have falsified.
- **A numeric claim that went stale by drift, which is the subtler half.** The § I pullquote read *"In the **five most recent phases** the author's final battery reported every mutation killed…"* followed by 38 / 33 / 30 / 20 / 21-of-21. Those figures are 172–176 and were correct when Phase 177 wrote them; "most recent" has since meant 180–184. Re-anchored to "across one five-phase run" and **extended with the five phases that followed** — 21 of 46, then 49 of 52, then 56 of 74 on a second round, then a module whose 22 planted defects all survived it (13 of 22 against the full four-file suite), then 56 genuine escapes of 119 — because the trend continuing is the actual finding. The first draft said *four* and silently dropped Phase 177, whose 21-of-46 sits squarely in the series; the round caught it, and the same off-by-one had already shipped into the monograph sentence.

The additions are the argument the seven phases share: **a value is produced in one place and consumed in several, and the agreement binding them is unwritten or written where the consumer never reads it.** A new § III subsection, *One writer, many readers, and a contract written down nowhere*, carries 178/180/182/183 plus the phantom-shell-variable class from 164/169, and § III's `#clean-result` gains **a seventh shape** — the `Flag:`/`Triaged:` router of Phase 181 — because that phase's own record already frames it in this section's vocabulary (*"a healthy run and a degraded one produce identical evidence"*). The section's closer now ends on Phase 184 turning the argument on the project itself: a publication gate can be green, correct, and blind, because it asks whether a string is present and never whether a sentence is true — with the honest split stated, that the decidable half (a pointer into a path the mirror strips) is now a pass and found **19 defects against a filed estimate of 9**, and the undecidable half stays with a human reader. Four older ABSENT phases fold in as clauses at sites the argument already touches rather than as new sections: **167** (a gate that only ever reported the state of a revision it was not gating) into shape 6; **168** (run the commands your change prescribes) into the § I pullquote, together with the honest rider that the rule shipped fifteen phases before **183** swept sixteen live sites of exactly its class; **165** (`--force` as the prescribed single-orphan rollback) into § II beside Fig. 8, kept as a *capability verified by running the pre-fix script*, not a recorded incident.

**162 and 163 are declined, and the decline is recorded as a decision rather than left as an omission** — both are maintainer-side (`tools/SKILL_AUDIT.md`, `tools/skill_audit_refs.py`), mirror-excluded, and have no consumer-visible surface. Their transferable claims are real and remain unhomed; they are filed, not lost.

**`docs/index.html` needed no edit, and that was measured rather than assumed.** Its currency question is different in kind since Phase 118 removed the phase count from current-state surfaces, so "does it name the latest phase" is the wrong test. All **49** verifiable claims on the page were checked against the tree — the three evidence-corpus numbers (71 rounds / 3,298 findings / 78 conventions) recomputed from `docs/analysis/gdp_review_metrics.json`, every chart tooltip and table row, both install invocations, all `--mode`/`--packs` flags, all six read-next links and both cross-anchors into the monograph. Zero graded stale or false. **A precision correction to this phase's own framing:** the three Phase-182 falsehoods are *not* on the rendered docs pages at all — a targeted grep returns no match in either `index.html` or `workflow.html`. They ship on the public repo in `claim_task.sh`, `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.2a, two test modules and `PHASE_LOG.md`; `REVIEW_ARCHIVE.md`'s copy is mirror-excluded and never went public.

**Leg C — monograph staleness is not guardable in kind at the runner it would have to live in, and here is the number.** The filed hypothesis was that such a guard is high-false-positive by construction. **Measured over 189 phase-close commits, that is false**, and saying so is part of the deliverable: a *zero-lag* guard would fire on 97% of them, but a **lag budget** is cheap — the lag distribution has a mean of 23.3 and a maximum of **74** (the monograph sat at Issue 86 while the tree reached 160), and in the post-161 era a budget of K=17 fires **0 times**, K=12 fires 17%. Seven currency passes existed before this one — measured at the parent commit, which is the honest frame for a phase that ships the eighth; the lag each cleared was 15, 1, 8, 8, 16, 74, 17. A budget in the 8–17 band would be a low-FP reminder, not a nuisance. Three findings kill it anyway:

1. **It is defeasible in five lines, and the defeat is the exact class Phase 184 shipped Pass 5 against.** Verified by running: bumping the four stamps and two dates from 177 to the tree max, with **zero content added**, leaves the whole doc-currency module green (9 passed). Any lag guard reads those same numbers, so its satisfaction condition is a 5-line edit that then *asserts* coverage of seven phases the document does not contain. The current guard is satisfiable the same way — what a budget adds is the *pressure* to do it.
2. **There is no advisory tier where the check would have to live.** `docs/workflow.html` is not installed to any consumer (no reference in `install.sh`), so this is a maintainer-side concern and the maintainer's runner is pytest, which is binary. The repo has no warn-only test — `grep -rl "warnings.warn\|pytest.warns" tests/` returns nothing. Phase 143's absence-surfacing and the collision advisories are advisory because they live in `self_check.sh` and `/sitrep`; a monograph-lag check has no such home.
3. **It needs a judgement no pattern can encode** — whether a phase warrants a paragraph — which is precisely the criterion `_shared/adversarial-review.md` § *Before you spawn anyone* sets for a survivor that may be declined in kind rather than merely left unattempted. Only ~22% of shipped phases are ever named in the monograph; forcing the rest would invert Phase 118 and re-add the number it retired on measured evidence.

**Recorded, not built.** What replaces it is this entry's number: at close, the monograph's lag is **0**, and the historical band in which a human has chosen to run a currency pass is 8–17. A future session that wants the guard should read this measurement first.

**Leg B — the cut, and its first finding was that the runbook cannot drive the gate it is supposed to drive.** This push was framed as the first cut-time run of Phase 184's Pass 5. **That framing is false, and it came from Phase 184's own record** (*"which is where the new Pass 5 will run for the first time at cut time"*), inherited into this phase's brief without re-checking — the same shape as the "known pre-existing failures" above. Verified, and the round corrected the evidence line before it shipped: `grep -nE 'Pass 5|pytest' tools/make_public_mirror.sh tools/cut_public_release.sh` returns **nothing at all** — the two references either script makes are to `test_mirror_leak_gate` by name, one *stripping* the module and one a keep-in-sync comment, so the honest statement is stronger than the one first written. Worse, a copy of the module placed inside a built snapshot does not gate it — it goes **inert**: `_excluded_basenames()` derives from `git ls-files`, and in the mirror none of the excluded files exist, so the bare-basename arm matches nothing. The correction, and the reason the gate is nonetheless real: **Pass 5 runs in the source repo at the clean SHA being cut, and that is byte-equivalent to running it on the built tree** — `_shipped_files()` and the mirror's `git ls-files` return the same set, and the builder refuses a dirty tree, so the worktree scanned is the commit that ships. That equivalence is now an explicit, checkable step rather than an unstated assumption. Phase 184's sentence is corrected in place, bracketed.

**Two hard gates were reachable only by someone who already knew they existed.** Step 3 of the runbook defers the pass list to *"the script"* — pointing at `make_public_mirror.sh`, which **never prints Pass 4**.
