and the run exits 1 having cleaned nothing. The half nobody had filed is the inverse: the
worktree the caller was told to stand in is crowned MAIN and therefore **skipped**, so the
prescribed cleanup could never do the one thing it was invoked for.

And it is the *prescribed* path, not an edge case: `batch_work.sh:1185` prints
`cd ${WORKTREE_DIR}` and `batch_work.sh:1190` names this script five lines later.

### What shipped

**`cleanup_worktrees.sh`** resolves the primary via `--git-common-dir`, anchoring the query
and the absolutisation to the same directory (`self_check.sh:70-75`'s shape, not
`batch_work.sh`'s — the latter is correct only because its query and its `cd` share the
ambient cwd, and measured from a subdirectory of the primary the answer is the CWD-relative
`../../.git`). It **fails closed**: `claim_task.sh:208-211`'s precedent, because a fallback
to `$REPO_ROOT` puts one empty answer behind two meanings and this phase's whole subject is
that shape.

**`batch_work.sh`** anchors `$INDEX_SCRIPT` (the READ side — `review_index.py` resolves
`review_tasks.md` from its own location, `review_index.py:47`), `$TASKS_FILE` (the WRITE
side), and `$WORKTREE_DIR` at the primary; and its claim commit becomes the repo-anchored,
pathspec-scoped shape with a rollback that `--release`'s sibling has carried since Phase 151.
`Q-020`'s structural note (a) is exactly this — *the class recurs at call-site granularity,
not file granularity* — and `--release` versus the claim path was one of the four pairs it
named.

**`validate_tasks.py`** loses Invariant 13. `Q-022` offered two shapes and they collapse to
one. Shape (a) is *"scope the check to bodies whose task has **no live lock**"* — check
only the unlocked ones, so a claim in flight is exempt. This phase's first draft glossed
that backwards ("exempt tasks with no live lock"), inheriting the inversion from its own
brief, and the round caught it. Read correctly it is not merely near-vacuous but **fully**
vacuous: Invariant 9 (`validate_tasks.py:559-570`) makes a missing lock a hard *error* for
every `in_progress` task, so on a validator-clean tree no unlocked `in_progress` task
exists for the check to look at. What remains is shape (b), and `/review-close` Step 2d already reads the
branch tip and blocks. The retirement is carried through `schema.md` (the numbered list ends
at 12; § *Test decision* now names where enforcement lives), `WORKFLOW.md`'s count, and
`review-close`'s three citations — including `:506`, which said "Invariant 13 already warned
at validation time" and is now the *first* notice rather than a second one.

### Three defects this phase introduced into its own fix

1. **A worktree is removable while it IS the current directory** — git exits 0 and deletes
   it. Anchoring MAIN correctly therefore made the removal modes reach a directory the
   pre-fix code never could, and the bare `git worktree prune` closing each mode then died
   `fatal: Unable to read current working directory`, exit 128, under `set -e` — after the
   removals, so the run reported nothing it had done. Fixed by anchoring the process at the
   primary; the caller is told when its own directory was the one removed.
2. **The claim commit landed on the wrong branch.** Anchoring the paths without anchoring the
   *precondition* split them: `claim_batch` asked the CALLER's HEAD while the rewrite and the
   commit went to the primary. With the primary on a feature branch and a worktree holding
   `main`, the claim committed to `feat/x` and printed `✅ Claimed Batch 1 on main`; `main`
   gained nothing. Not reachable before this phase — everything used `$REPO_ROOT`, so the
   write followed the same HEAD the check had read. **A fix for a wrong read opened a wrong
   acceptance**, which is Phase 233's rule ("check both directions of the predicate, always")
   arriving from the other side.
3. **The bare `git pull --ff-only origin main`** was safe only while that precondition
   guaranteed the caller *was* on main. Moving the check to the primary removed the guarantee
   without moving the pull, so a caller on any branch behind `main` would have had it
   silently fast-forwarded.

None of the three was found by reading. (1) came from driving the prescribed sequence; (2)
and (3) came from the mutation battery's own survivors.

### The round: the fix was wrong in three git layouts, and the battery was wrong about itself

Three lenses (execution, guards, record), fresh-context `general-purpose` agents in isolated
worktrees. The governor's third lens applies — behaviour plus a numeric record.

**The execution lens disqualified the first resolution.** It resolved the primary as
`dirname "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)"` — the idiom five shell siblings use for the
*lock* path — which is the repo root only when the git dir is literally `<root>/.git`. It is
not, in three layouts, and all three were reproduced:

| layout | `dirname` yields | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| submodule | `<super>/.git/modules/<name>` | `cd` re-rooted the script at the **superproject**; `--clean` removed its worktrees and `--force` destroyed uncommitted work in one |
| `git init --separate-git-dir` | the git dir's **parent** | a read-only `list` run died exit **128**, where it had exited 0 |
| bare repo + worktrees | a non-worktree path | same crash |

Each is a real directory, so the `-d` check passed and the wrong answer was used — the
fail-closed arm guarded a probe *failing*, and the probe was succeeding. **A new cross-repo
blast radius, introduced by a fix for a within-repo one.**

The shipped resolution narrows to the case the defect actually lives in: `--git-dir` and
`--git-common-dir` are equal exactly when the caller *is* the primary — in a plain checkout,
a submodule and a separate-git-dir layout alike — and differ only inside a linked worktree.
Only then is the primary someone else, and it is `git worktree list --porcelain`'s first
entry, which git documents as the main worktree and which is the same list the classifier
compares against. A first entry marked `bare` means there is no main working tree, so the
caller's own is protected as before. Measured after: **byte-identical to pre-phase in all
three exotic layouts, and correct in the linked-worktree case.**

**The guards lens falsified the battery's number.** (Not an instance of the register's 47/47
all-killed series — this battery reported a survivor, so `ledger_stats.py` does not count it
there. The weaker claim is the one that holds: *nearly* clean, with a healthy `pre` column, is
not independent either.) It ran 40 mutations disjoint from the author's and **16 behaviour-changing ones
survived** — against an author battery reporting 19 of 20. Two fixture assumptions did most
of that damage, and neither is exotic:

1. **Every worktree in the author's fixtures was a *sibling* of the primary. Sysop's never
   are** — `claim_task.sh` and the agent harness put them under `<primary>/.claude/worktrees/`.
   Against a sibling fixture, a MAIN test that prefix-matches is indistinguishable from one
   that compares equal, and `$REPO_ROOT/..` is indistinguishable from `$MAIN_ROOT/..`. So the
   two mutations that reinstate this phase's own defect both survived — including the one the
   author's `A6` row exists to catch, which the prefix variant walks straight past.
2. **The commit-failure arm was declared "UNEXERCISED — no fixture makes `git commit` fail
   after a successful rewrite."** That was false: a three-line rejecting `pre-commit` hook
   reaches it, and **Sysop ships pre-commit hooks.** Both lenses reached it independently.
   That single missing fixture is why the rollback's anchor and its `return 1` were both
   unguarded — and anchored at `$REPO_ROOT` the rollback **destroys the caller's uncommitted
   `review_tasks.md`** while leaving the primary half-applied. A survivor declined as
   impossible-in-kind has to actually be impossible.

**The claims lens found eleven record defects**, of which two were live falsehoods in shipped
prose rather than in the phase's own account: `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.4 still advertised
*"13 invariants; 12 and 13 are warn-only"* — a **second** count site — and
`review-close/SKILL.md:467` still called the record *"warned by the validator"*. The phase's
guard could not see either, because it asserted `"enforces 13 invariants" not in workflow`,
a literal string neither site contains. **A guard keyed to one phrasing is a guard keyed to
the author's memory of where the fact lives**; it now derives the count from `schema.md`'s
numbered list and sweeps every shipped `.md` for any disagreeing figure. Mutation-verified
against both sites. It also caught this phase quoting `Q-022`'s shape (a) **backwards** —
the shape scopes the check to bodies with *no live lock*, and the phase glossed it as
exempting those, inheriting the inversion from its own brief. The conclusion (vacuous) held;
the reasoning as written did not.

Four citations were stale or wrong when written, three of them moved by this phase's own
edits after they were checked.

**Final: 31 mutations, 30 killed, 0 false kills, one declared survivor** (`A3`, a
resolved-but-nonexistent `MAIN_ROOT`; the guards lens independently could not construct an
input reaching it either). `pre: killed 7, of which 0 only by pre` — nothing this phase
guards was already guarded, which is what a genuinely new surface looks like.

**Read that 30/31 as wiring, not coverage.** The first battery reported 19/20 and an
independent lens found 16 behaviour-changing survivors of 40. A battery cannot escape the
fixtures its author designed, and the two that did the damage here were *ordinary* — the
project's own worktree layout, and a hook the project ships.

## Phase 235 (executed 2026-08-27 — the schema cluster that was two-thirds someone else's work, and the exclusion that outlived its reason)

**Members:** `Q-235`, legs #436 and #437 — closed. Leg #435 rerouted into the orchestrator
group. One filing out: `Q-313`, § Medium. Wade's call at the session's open, made against four
measured slices rather than the two the brief offered.

### The brief was wrong about the shape of the choice, and that was the phase's first product

The brief framed the Track D remainder as "four § High in two clusters, and they still do not
compose", and asked that the choice between them be brought to Wade rather than assumed. The
clusters compose at exactly one seam, and it is the seam the brief proposed cutting on.

**`Q-235` leg #435 is not a schema addition. It is the orchestrator's unbuilt option C.** Two
shipped files state its blocker in the words the filing was written in:

- `core/skills/claim-task/SKILL.md:501` — option C *"is specified but not built … it needs a
  `## Plan` body section that `tasks/schema.md` does not yet define and a release ordering this
  skill does not yet carry."*
- `core/skills/_shared/plan-review-preference.md:63` — the same claim, reworded (*"It needs a
  `## Plan` body section `tasks/schema.md` does not define and a release ordering the skill does not
  carry"*). Not the same sentence; the round caught this file calling it one.

The filing's own evidence pointed at this and was read backwards. `git grep -n 'Execution Plan'
core/` returns zero — and the brief took the zero as proof of an **empty surface**, which is what
made "#435 and #436 are pure additions" look true. The zero is a **vocabulary miss**: Sysop's name
for the artifact is `## Plan`. Grepping the name the tree actually uses finds the design already
settled — write-back target, second-run rule, the batch asymmetry, and a rider that option C's
write-back must also carry `## Test decision`. Building the field alone would have shipped a
schema section with no writer and no reader, which the brief's own dead-weight test forbids.

**Method note, and it generalises past this phase.** A grep that returns zero has two readings —
*the surface is empty*, or *I searched for the wrong name* — and only one of them is ever checked.
Phase 234 paid for the same class in the opposite direction (`--show-toplevel` answers a question
nobody was asking). The cheap discriminator is to grep for the **thing** as well as the **word**:
here, `'## Plan'` and `plan.md` both hit immediately.

**So the remainder is now the orchestrator group alone** — a cleaner statement of it than "four
§ High in two clusters" ever was, and one fewer entry to reconcile at the next Track D open.

### #437 measured smaller and sharper than filed, and the filing's headline claim did not survive

The entry reports `user_action` "overloaded across three different meanings" and cites three
sites. Two of the three are one predicate:

| filed | what is actually there |
|---|---|
| `auto-build/SKILL.md:120` — *not-executable* | line has moved to `:136`; `if t.get("user_action"): return False` |
| `auto-build/SKILL.md:142-143` — *a reason* | `:158-159`; the **same** predicate re-tested in the `EXCLUDED` chain to render a message. Not a distinct semantics — one bit, one reading, rendered twice |
| `roadmap/SKILL.md:126` — *blocked-on-human*, ordering at `:166` | exact. Same reading of the bit as `auto-build`, different *disposition* |

So the three readings measure at about 2.5, and a field split keyed on them would have been
keyed on a miscount. **The defect underneath is real and is a different one: a timing
contradiction, fixable with no schema change at all.**

| says pre-work | says post-merge |
|---|---|
| the heading itself — `## User ops (do these first)` | `tasks/schema.md:97` |
| `_shared/decomposition-rubric.md:77` | `review-close/SKILL.md:591` |
| `add-task/SKILL.md:57` | `review-close/SKILL.md:754` |
| `intake/SKILL.md:101`, `:111` | `validate_tasks.py:185` |

**Three independent lines of evidence settle it against the post-merge reading**, and none of
them is the heading's wording:

1. **Every runtime reader gates on the flag**, which is a pre-work semantics by construction.
   `/auto-build` drops the task from its executable frontier; `/roadmap` classes it 🔒
   blocked-on-human and *orders* on it; `/next-task` keeps it out of the agent pool and surfaces
   it separately to the human who can act. Nothing in the tree defers it.
2. **The rubric's own exemplars skew pre-work.** The clearest is *"only the user knows their actual
   spreadsheet categories / which dump folder is canonical"* — knowledge the agent cannot begin
   without. An earlier draft called it "unambiguous"; the rubric files it under
   **Legitimate-but-softer** (`:78`), opposite "Strong", so the word was the draft's and not the
   rubric's.
3. **The four post-merge sites are one claim, repeated** — all four are the justification for a
   single decision, excluding the heading from `/review-close` Step 3c's manual-smoke phrase list.
   There is no independent assertion of post-merge timing anywhere.

**The decision those four sites justify is correct and is unchanged.** Their *other* stated
reason — `user_action: true` is a large routine class, and firing the gate on all of it would
train the operator to waive wholesale — is sound and timing-independent. Retiring the false half
leaves the exclusion standing on the half that was always load-bearing. Same correction shape as
this repo's `Q-212` and `Q-023` notes: the position holds, the stated reason does not, and a false
reason in the document that records a decision is how the next reader re-derives it wrongly.

### The falsehood was self-insulating, which is why four sites carried it

Two of the four cited **`tasks/schema.md § "User ops"`** as their authority —
`validate_tasks.py:185` and `review-close/SKILL.md:754`. **No such section existed.** The only
`## User ops (do these first)` occurrence in `schema.md` was `:158`, a line **inside** the
` ```markdown ` body-template fence (opened `:141`, closed `:163`). A reader following the
citation to check the claim landed on a template line that asserts nothing, so the claim could not
be falsified at the place it pointed to — and the two remaining sites were free to cite each other.

The fix therefore **creates the section** rather than repointing the citations: `schema.md`
§ *User ops* now states the timing once, canonically, with the exclusion's two reasons and the
`manual_smoke` boundary. That converts a false citation into a true one and removes the
contradiction at its root instead of at four leaves.

### #436 shipped with a reader, and with the collision stated rather than elided

`solo: true` declares that a task mutates state shared **outside the filesystem view** — a global
lockfile, a singleton registry, a live schema, a shared fixture corpus — so it must not batch with
anything, even work whose paths are disjoint. That is the property `scope_overlap.py`
structurally cannot grade, which is the filing's actual point.

**The collision the brief flagged is real and needed answering:** `schema.md:86` already says
`architectural` *"usually wants to run alone"*, and `/auto-build` already solos on it. The
non-overlap, now written into `schema.md` § *Solo*: `blast_radius` grades **surface area** (a wide
change conflicts with almost anything), `solo` grades **serialization** (a narrow change corrupts
shared state regardless of paths). Neither implies the other — a `single-file` task can be
`solo: true`, and an `architectural` task solos already via invariant `a.` and gains nothing.

**Two build decisions worth recording:**

- **Appended as invariant `d.`, not inserted as `b.`.** The K=12 provenance note cites `a.` and
  `b.` by letter and `schema.md` § *Solo* cites `d.`; renumbering would have silently repointed
  two prose citations at different rules. Cheaper ordering was available (`d.` reads an index
  field, `b.` opens a file) and was declined for that reason.
- **Invariant `b.` stays.** It is the hardcoded special case of the same property — SQL migrations
  found by body-text grep — and retiring it as "superseded by `solo:`" would silently unprotect
  every existing task that relies on it and never declares the field. The drift guard asserts this
  directly, because it is the tempting refactor.

The validator type-guards the field and nothing more, and the docstring says why: the meaning is a
claim about runtime state no static check can confirm, and the one reader fails safe on absence.
The type guard is the part that earns its place — `"yes"` is truthy in Python, so an unguarded
string would silently solo every batch it landed in, with no error anywhere.

Scoping used two fresh-context agents. Both returned findings that did not survive checking, and
both are recorded because the failure mode is repeating a plausible claim, not missing one.

- **"`WORKFLOW.md:108`'s relax-once fallback is documented but no shipped code implements it."**

- **"`/onboard`'s Leg-B 'non-negotiably carries' list omits `user_action`, which the validator

A third was **downgraded, not refuted**: `next_task.py:537-538`'s ready-then-partition against

### What this phase filed

**`Q-313`** (§ Medium) — **nothing declares post-merge operator steps.** Retiring the false claim

already done by then. Verified absent by sweep rather than assumed. The entry names the cheap shape
(a `## After merge` heading surfaced in Step 8's existing report — no gate, because the failure

**A record repair that was not one, and the round caught it.** This phase's first draft reported

rather than quietly dropped because that is the whole point of the class.

### The adversarial round

**Three lenses, one round, per the governor** — the phase ships behaviour (`solo:` with a
reader and a validator check) *plus* a numeric record (the battery fraction), which is the
governor's stated condition for a third lens. Independent fresh-context `general-purpose`
agents, each in its own worktree, none permitted to mutate the shared tree. Every surviving
finding was re-verified by me against the tree before it was acted on, and three were
refuted or downgraded in the process.

**The author-side pass paid for itself before any reviewer ran.** It found four real guard
holes — a rationale guard covering only one of the two files that state the reason; a sweep
whose population was a `core/`-only directory walk, missing `install.sh`, `packs/` and
`docs/`; a guard prefix-matching so `Example I-disabled` passed as `Example I`; and a
`b.`-stays assertion reading one of two files. It also caught the battery's own docstring
declaring two rows "expected survivors" when both were killed.

#### Lens 1 — the claim. The phase replaced a false universal with a weaker one.

The sharpest finding of the round, and it lands on the phase's central product. The new
`schema.md` § *User ops* asserted *"By close time these steps are already done."* **Nothing
guarantees that.** `/claim-task` gates on `status` alone, so a `user_action: true` task can
be claimed, worked and closed with the human step outstanding — and the rubric's own
exemplars include a *"go/no-go judgment at a rollout boundary"* (`:73`) and the
`Low/architectural` *"done-except-for-human-sign-off"* pairing where *"the code landed"*
(`:51`). Neither is pre-work.

The evidence offered was weaker than stated too: all three runtime readers are frontier
filters over `status: open`, so they establish *an agent may not start it* — a claim about
dispatch — and are silent on the post-claim window where Step 3c's gate actually lives.

**The fix narrows the claim to what the tree enforces.** The section now states that the flag
gates *dispatch*, that **nothing verifies the steps were performed**, and that the
do-these-first timing is a **convention rather than a guarantee**. The Step 3c exclusion is
unchanged and now rests entirely on the routine-class reason, which is timing-independent and
was always the load-bearing half. Same narrowing at `review-close` (two sites) and
`validate_tasks.py`.

The same lens caught `§ Solo` claiming `solo: true` means the task *"must run alone"* while
only `/auto-build` Step 2 enforces it — `scope_overlap.py` has **zero** `solo` references, so
every in-flight advisory is blind to it. Scope narrowed to what ships, gap filed.

#### Lens 2 — the guards. 41 of 64 mutations survived, against my reported 17/17.

The fifth consecutive phase in this log where an author's battery reported everything killed
and an independent one did not. **The finding was one shape repeated seven ways:** every prose
guard was `assert "<literal>" in <whole file>`, which is satisfied inside a negation, by an
incidental hit elsewhere, or from a neighbouring section. The reviewer restored POST-merge
timing in two shipped files, declared `solo` an alias of `blast_radius` in ten places, and
declared invariant `d.` inert — with all 110 module tests and all 4,922 suite tests green.

Concretely: `assert "waive" in body` passed with the whole rationale deleted, because
`review-close/SKILL.md` uses the word twelve times for unrelated reasons. The `"stays" or
"Retained"` disjunct was satisfied by invariant **c.**'s *"Retained for correctness/headroom"*
— a rule the guard is not about. The `### User ops` slice ran to the next `## ` and so
swallowed the whole of `### Solo`, 6,382 characters. The suffix filter omitted shipped
extensionless git hooks and `.fragment` files. And the two authoring surfaces that carry the
`solo` contract to consumers — `add-task/SKILL.md` and `tasks/README.md` — had **nothing**
reading them.

**All seven classes were closed in kind**, which the rule requires of any survivor one
declines to close. `tests/_prose_guard_helpers.py` ships `states()` (refuses a negated
occurrence), `section()` (slices to the next heading of the same-or-higher level, and asserts
the heading is unique — a decoy duplicate had silently redirected a guard) and `normalize()`
(folds unicode dashes, emphasis and hard wrapping before matching). The sweep lost its suffix
filter entirely and now reads every tracked text file: **181, against 155 filtered and 82 for
the original `core/`-only walk**. Four crash-not-assert anchors now assert with their own
message.

**The honest reading of the post-fix number.** The battery is now 34 rows including the
round's seventeen classes, and reports **34/34 killed, 2 controls green, 0 false kills,
reverts an 11% minority**. That is a much better number than the 17/17 it replaces, because
it covers attacks the author did not invent. It is still an author's battery against
author-designed mutations, and the round's own lesson is that such a number measures
self-consistency. A fresh independent battery against the hardened guards has not been run.

#### Lens 3 — the record. One fabricated discovery, one convention violation.

**The `Q-241` "record repair" was not a repair.** The phase reported that the entry carried a

This is the Phase-153 class exactly.

**`Q-235` was recorded closed in three places while still unticked and absent from

Plus a dense tail, all verified before acting: `schema.md:88` was wrong when written (`:86`);

The lens also **verified clean** what it could not fault: the `#437` core evidence (its own

Three claims this phase made did not survive it: that these steps are done by close time,

**Track D's last cluster opens.** `Q-235` closed in Phase 235, leaving the orchestrator group
(`Q-028` + `Q-029` + `Q-030`, plus `Q-107` from § Low) as the whole Track D remainder. Wade's
calls at this session's open, taken against the four slices put to him: take **spec repair +
part B leg 3 + `Q-030` legs (b)/(c)/(d)**, take `Q-107` at its **cheapest+** depth, **defer
`Q-314`** to the next orchestrator phase, and **hold the mirror-push slot** to the end of the
remainder for the fourth consecutive time.

### The spec was substantially discharged and had been saying otherwise since Phase 171

Wade ratified at Phase 235's open that `tools/CLAIM_TASK_ORCHESTRATOR_SPEC.md` is repaired
**inside** the first orchestrator phase rather than speculatively beforehand — the phase that
must read it is the one that pays to fix it. Phase 171 recorded its own pre-build spec pass as
*"most of this phase's product."*

All five verified-stale sentences reproduced exactly, and one of them was worse than filed:

- **`:3` said "the orchestrator reshape is not [built]".** Phase 171 built part A. That sentence
  stood for **64 phases** after it became false, at the top of the file, in the § *Status* line
  a reader meets first.
- **The § *Migration surface* row said `claim-task/SKILL.md` is "562 lines today".** It is
  **1200**. The row now refuses to state a line count at all rather than restating a fresh one —
  it rots on every touch, and both prior readers of that row budgeted against the wrong file.
- **The `/sitrep` insertion point was sited at `sitrep_survey.py:514`.** The real
  `state = "planning"` is `:857`, inside `_classify_task`.
- **The same paragraph called the `sitrep` SKILL tables "not drift-guarded … zero `SKILL`
  references".** That is **half-false**, and the halves matter in opposite directions:
  `tests/test_sitrep_survey.py` now opens `core/skills/sitrep/SKILL.md` and asserts every state
  the survey emits appears in the § *Classification states* table — but the § *Recommendation
  routing rules* table is still opened by nothing. The correction is scoped to the routing table
  only, because adding a second guard over the states table would duplicate a shipped one, which
  is how a roster comes to read as coverage it does not have (Phase 204).
- **§ *Q3* prescribed copying `## Test decision`'s validator treatment "exactly … warn-only in
  `validate_tasks.py`".** **Phase 234 retired that invariant**, and its companion citation
  `validate_tasks.py:655` now points at blast-radius code. Copying it would have rebuilt the
  exact defect the retirement removed — and the argument applies to `## Plan` with *more* force,
  since there is no status at which a missing `## Plan` is an error, so a warn-only invariant
  would fire on nearly every task in the queue rather than merely on claimed ones. The spec now
  says **ship Part C with zero validator change** unless a status can be named where absence is
  wrong.

**A finding the brief did not carry: the two `sitrep/SKILL.md` line ranges had not merely rotted,
they had TRANSPOSED.** The spec cited `:64-77` as "classification states" and `:89-96` as
"routing rules"; today `:64-77` *is* the routing-rules table and the classification-states table
sits below it. A reader trusting the numbers would have edited the wrong table and found the
right one already correct. A transposed range is worse than an absent one because it looks
checkable.

**And the A/B/C/D cut Wade ratified had ZERO hits in all 515 lines** — it existed only in
`REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`, in a paragraph carried identically by **both** `Q-028` and `Q-029`, which is
not where a builder reading the spec would look. It is now a
table in a new § *What is built, what is not*, with each part's state named.

### Part B leg 3 — the reaper is two owners, because the close path has no list carrying both

`/claim-task` claims batches as well as roadmap tasks, and since Phase 171 a claim of either kind
writes `sysop/runtime/claim/<CLAIM_ID>/<RUN_ID>/` and, on a park,
`sysop/runtime/parked/<CLAIM_ID>__<RUN_ID>.md` — both in the main checkout so they outlive
`git worktree remove`. **Nothing removed either of them, for either claim kind.**
`WORKFLOW.md` § 8.6 said so in the shipped tree (*"Nothing removes it yet"*), and
`claim-task/SKILL.md` said *"Nothing does, yet."*

The fix is deliberately **not** one owner. `/review-close` Step 4c's `closed` list is built from
`roadmap_ids` only — `review_task_ids` are excluded there by design, and the skill says so — so
no batch id can reach it, and teaching it one is a step-order change to the close. So:

- **Roadmap half — `/review-close` Step 4c**, beside the lock and park-marker cleanup it already
  does: `shutil.rmtree` of `sysop/runtime/claim/<tid>/`, with a resolve-and-re-check containment
  guard before the remove (this is the only `rm -rf`-shaped operation in the close path) and a
  symlink arm that unlinks the link rather than following it. A new `CLAIM_ARTIFACTS_REMOVED`
  row is printed and carried through to Step 8's report, because Phase 219's lesson is that a
  heredoc which computes a fact and does not print it hands Step 8 a value the agent supplies
  from memory instead.
- **Batch half — `close_batch.sh`'s new `remove_claim_artifacts()`**, sited beside
  `remove_batch_lock()` and wired into both of its gated loops (the `CLOSED` arm and the
  already-finished `MERGED_UNLOCK` arm — two distinct call sites, and the second is the recovery
  path for the first). `tests/test_close_batch_sh.py` is ~950 lines of real-subprocess coverage,
  which is the argument for putting the mechanism here rather than in prose.

Both are gated on `close_landed_on_main`, for the reason the lock already is: under `pr` policy
the close commits on an integration branch while `main` still reads the work open, and removing a
park verdict before the merge lands destroys the one record of why the work stopped. **Deferring
is the safe direction; releasing early is a double-claim.**

### `Q-030` (b) is sharper than filed — there is no revised plan at all

The filing says Phase 140's recording mandate has no durable target on `/auto-build`'s dominant
path. Reading Phase 6d, the defect is one level worse: the all-fixable arm does not build a
revised plan *anywhere*. It hands the executor `PLAN_TEXT` + `RAW_FINDINGS` raw and lets it
absorb inline (§ *Out of scope for v1* says so explicitly), so the orchestrator's 6c
classification — which findings it absorbed, which it rejected, and why — **is never expressed,
in context or on disk**. The named readers could not reach it because there was nothing to reach.

`/auto-build` had **zero** `REVIEW_REPORT` references before this phase — the only one now is the
new 6d block quoting the mandate — so the mandate's "record it in the sealed report" arm has no
target either, and its single destructive gate fires at Step 4 —
*before* planning — so there is no plan-approval moment for a human to read it at.

6d's all-fixable arm now writes `classification.md` into `sysop/runtime/claim/<TASK_ID>/<CYCLE_TS>/`
— the same namespace `/claim-task` Step 7c uses, and the one leg 3 now reaps, so no new runtime
directory and closed work does not accumulate. It carries a per-finding disposition and, for each
rejected finding, the **per-clause** rationale `_shared/adversarial-review.md` requires, with an
explicit instruction for the empty case because an empty section is indistinguishable from a lost
one. It is stated as **not** an input to Phase 6e — v1 still absorbs inline, so the executor's
reading and this record are two independent readings of the same findings and may differ. A
record that implies it bound execution when it did not is worse than one that says what it is.

### `Q-030` (c) — the TOCTOU was ~207 lines and two git operations wide

The existence guard is `claim_task.sh:585`; the write was `:792`. Branch creation and
`git worktree add` sit between them, so the window is wide in wall-clock terms, not just in
theory — and the write was a plain `cat > "$LOCK_FILE" <<EOF`, which **truncates**. Two claimants
that both passed the guard both reached the write, and the second silently overwrote the first's
lock: two agents, two worktrees, one lock naming only the winner.

The write is now `( set -C; printf '%s\n' "$LOCK_CONTENT" > "$LOCK_FILE" )` — noclobber opens
O_EXCL, so the create either wins or fails with no truncate outcome, and the subshell scopes the
option. Building the content first also removes a second failure the heredoc had: a death
mid-heredoc left a **partial** lock, which parses as a lock with missing fields rather than as no
lock. Probed both directions before shipping.

**The recovery message deliberately does not name `--release`.** That path refuses on an *absent*
lock; here the lock exists and belongs to the winner, so `--release` would either refuse or
release someone else's claim. It names the two objects this run actually created —
`git worktree remove` and `git branch -D`.

### `Q-030` (d) — the tooling that never existed

`claim_task.sh:775-776` justified its `date` fallback chain by saying a blank `expires:` is what
*"downstream lock-validator tooling treats as malformed"*. **No such tooling exists and none ever
has**: `sitrep_survey.py` parses `expires:` into a `Lock` dataclass field that nothing reads, and
staleness is decided from `started:` and mtime. A reader who believed the sentence would go
looking for a validator to satisfy, or would conclude the field is load-bearing for the wrong
reason.

The chain stays, on the two reasons that are real — the lock is a human-readable record surfaced
by three commands, and the field is pinned by two test files, so blanking it is a contract change
rather than a cleanup. **Pin the reason, not the fact** (Phase 235's method note): the guard
asserts both corrected halves and the absence of the retired parenthetical, because a guard that
only checked the fallback still exists could not tell a stated rationale from a stripped one.

### `Q-107` — the asymmetry is deliberate, and `/auto-build`'s "verbatim" was a retype

Two different problems wearing one entry.

`/claim-task` Step 7b inlines `plan.md` while 7e hands the executor the same file by path. That
asymmetry is **right** and was unexplained, which is how the next reader "optimises" it away: a
reviewer *told to read a file* can skim it, read part of it, or not read it, and nothing
downstream can tell — the same undetectable-omission shape this whole reshape exists to remove,
one level down. The executor has no such failure mode available, because it cannot implement a
plan it did not read. Recorded in one blockquote at the site, with an instruction not to
"fix" it and a pointer to the shared contract as the only correct place to revisit it.

`/auto-build` is not the same case and the shared word hid it. Its Phase 6a agents return plans
into **orchestrator context**; the only `Write` of `plan.md` is in Phase 6d, *after* the reviewer
spawn and only on the park arm. So there is no file, and "verbatim" describes a **retype**. The
measured harm on a real 3-task cycle: all three plans abbreviated, and on one the retype dropped
a clause about a test fake's differentiated return values, so the reviewer returned a finding
describing *the transcription* rather than the plan. The failure is **bidirectional and leaves
identical evidence** — dropping a clause manufactures a phantom finding the executor is
dispatched to fix; smoothing one hides a real finding. Both spawn sites now say "re-emitted in
full", with the mechanism and the honest instruction: if you cannot emit it in full, say so in
the prompt rather than abbreviating silently. Pass-by-path is the durable fix and needs 6a to
write the plan before 6b; filed, not built.

### The author-side pass, and what it cost

Run per `_shared/adversarial-review.md` § *Before you spawn anyone*, and reported because Phase
166 showed the rule otherwise has no invoker. **Eight findings, one of them a live defect in this
phase's own change:**

1. **The `/auto-build` classification block's `mkdir -p` was ungated.** `mkdir -p` is the one
   command in that skill which does *not* fail on an unsubstituted placeholder — it would have
   created a directory literally named `<TASK_ID>`, returned 0, and written the record to a path
   no reader will ever open, which is indistinguishable from never writing it. The park block
   twenty lines above gates its own `mkdir` for exactly this reason and I walked past it. Caught
   by a **shipped** guard (`tests/test_phantom_shell_vars.py`), not by inspection. Now
   `case`-gated on a shell builtin (no new permission rule), verified fatal unsubstituted and
   clean substituted.
2. **This phase's own prose weakened a shipped guard.** The Phase-171 check that Step 7b hands
   over the shared template was `adversarial-review.md` *anywhere in Step 7b*. The `Q-107`
   rationale blockquote names that file, so the mutation stripping the real citation from the
   `prompt:` line began passing. **The weakness pre-dated the prose; the prose exposed it.** The
   guard is now anchored to the spawn instruction rather than the section.
3. **Five of this phase's first-cut guards were `assert "<literal>" in <whole file>`** — the exact
   shape Phase 235's round put 64 mutations through with 41 surviving — and **all five failed on
   contact**. The instructive one: a guard asserting the retired lock-validator phrase is absent
   from `claim_task.sh` **fails on the fix and passes only if the record of the fix is deleted**,
   because the correction must quote the phrase to retire it. It now pins the retired
   *parenthetical assertion* and separately requires the phrase to be absent outside the
   paragraph retiring it.
4. **Three shipped sites assert "part B is unbuilt."** Leg 3 makes that *partly* false. Re-scoped
   to legs 1+2 rather than deleted — and when the Step 8 guard was re-anchored, a loose
   `does not exist` search was satisfied by the new paragraph's own heading ("What still does not
   exist"), so the mutation inverting the readers claim went green. Anchored to the clause naming
   the legs.
5. A Phase-171 mutation anchor went stale on rewritten text — a silent no-op, caught only because
   that module asserts on no-ops separately from survivors.
6. The `close_batch.sh` insertion shifted a self-citation's line range at **two** sites.
7. The new test module read a mirror-excluded `tools/` path with no `pytest.skip` — it would have
   reddened the required check on the public snapshot, as a collection error.
8. `"Locks kept"` is pinned by a shipped test. The message was reworded to **preserve the
   literal** rather than edit the test to fit the new code — editing a test to match code is how
   a guard gets weakened, and the direction matters more than the effort.

### The adversarial round — three lenses, and the third measured 54% survivors

Governor: three lenses, because this phase ships behaviour **and** publishes a numeric record.
Three independent fresh-context `general-purpose` agents, each in its own worktree at the phase
commit `24ef0c9`, told not to mutate the primary checkout. **All three ran on the author's own
model — a recorded gap**, not a decision: `_shared/adversarial-review.md` calls model diversity a
review dimension and this round did not buy it.

**Lens 1 — does it execute (2 HIGH, 4 MEDIUM, 2 LOW). Every finding came from RUNNING things,
and the two HIGH were both in code this phase wrote.**

- **`shutil.rmtree` was a new abort point inside a loop whose own contract forbids aborting.**
  Step 4c's cleanup loop opens by stating that "an abort mid-loop must not have already destroyed
  an earlier task's records (the parked marker below is unrecreatable)". Every prior operation
  there is non-raising by construction; `rmtree` over a user tree is the first that realistically
  raises. Reproduced with one unremovable claim directory: **exit 1, an earlier task's
  unrecreatable park marker already gone, a later task's lock never cleaned, the index staged —
  and none of the six report rows printed**, which puts Step 8 straight back to supplying them
  from memory, the Phase-219 failure that block exists to have fixed. Now wrapped, with the
  failure recorded in a new `CLAIM_ARTIFACTS_FAILED` row rather than raised or swallowed.
- **The containment re-check governed only one of the two removal arms.** The comment claimed
  containment was re-checked "before removing anything"; the `elif claim_dir.is_symlink()` arm
  never consulted it. Demonstrated with `tid = "../../../escaped_link"`: a symlink at the repo
  root, outside `sysop/runtime/claim/` entirely, was unlinked and **reported as a claim
  artifact**. `inside` is now the first branch of the chain and every removal is an `elif` of it.
- **`remove_claim_artifacts()` printed `✅ Removed` when the `rm` had failed** — both echoes were
  unconditional and `set -e` is disabled by the call sites' `|| true`, so a read-only `parked/`
  lost nothing and reported success. Directly falsified the function's own header promising it
  "reports either way".
- **Any lock-write failure was reported as "claimed by another agent"** — `2>/dev/null` discards
  EACCES/EROFS/ENOSPC along with the noclobber message, so a read-only locks dir sent the operator
  hunting for a rival that did not exist. Now discriminated on `[[ -e "$LOCK_FILE" ]]`.
- **The race-loser's recovery advice re-minted a trap this same file already guards.** It printed
  `git worktree remove "$WORKSPACE_PATH"` with no mode branch — and in `--branch` mode
  `WORKSPACE_PATH` *is* the main checkout, so it handed the operator `fatal: is a main working
  tree`. `claim_task.sh` already branches on mode at its PyYAML-missing reversal, with a comment
  saying why. Now a three-way `case` on `$MODE`.
- **And the sharpest finding of the whole round: the fix for the author-side defect was itself
  defective.** The author-side pass caught an ungated `mkdir -p`; the `case` gate written for it
  put the placeholders in the `case` subject **and again** in the `mkdir`, so an agent that
  substituted only the first passed the gate and created the literal `<TASK_ID>` directory anyway
   — verbatim the outcome the gate exists to prevent. **Nothing pinned it**: the guard that caught
  the original matches `line.startswith("mkdir -p")`, which the `case` form no longer does, so the
  pattern could be neutered entirely with 81 tests green. The path is now substituted **once**,
  into a variable the gate tests and the `mkdir` uses, with a parametrized executed test over all
  four substitution states. A rider: the gate's comment claimed it worked "for the reason the park
  block above gates its own `mkdir -p`" — that block's `mkdir` is ungated, and the two that are
  gated use a `git rev-parse` probe, not a `case`. Corrected.

**Lens 2 — are the claims true (3 HIGH, 5 MEDIUM, 2 LOW).**

- **The phase's own "0 failed" was false at the commit it names.** The suite was measured *before*
  the ledger row was appended, and `tests/test_round_yield_ledger.py` refuses draft cells — so the
  commit the number is attributed to was red. The brief's instruction was explicit ("**measure it
  after the record**") and this phase did it backwards. The figure below is re-measured after the
  record, at the commit stated.
- **The spec still asserted, in the present tense, that a batch park "is removed by nothing and
  accumulates forever"** — 120 lines above the migration row this phase had already marked
  RESOLVED. Repairing a file's § *Status* line while leaving its body carrying the retired claim
  is precisely the class the repair exists to close.
- **`Q-316` described `/claim-task` Step 7b as passing the plan by path**, contradicting the
  `Q-107` close in the same commit, whose whole point is that 7b **inlines** deliberately.
- **A fabricated mechanism shipped into a consumer-facing comment.** The corrected lock-validator
  rationale added "staleness is decided from `started:` **and mtime**". Locks use `started:`
  alone; the only `st_mtime` reads in `sitrep_survey.py` are pending-round markers and round
  receipts. Writing a new falsehood while correcting an old one is the Phase-153 shape.
- **Three more stale citations survived inside the file being repaired** — `562 lines` and
  `:514-519` as live assertions, plus three more in the very sentence whose new blockquote claimed
  "every line number in the sentence above was wrong", having corrected two of five. All are now
  symbols.
- **The tree still said what the record called misleading:** `auto-build/SKILL.md` continued to
  read "the orchestrator builds a `REVISED_PLAN`" under a heading saying *Write Revised Plan*,

**Lens 3 — are the guards real. 78 mutations, 42 survived (54%). 21 negative controls, 5 falsely
red (24%).** The project's standing condition, one more time. The worst were not exotic:

- **Both tests in `TestBatchReapingIsGuarded` were inert.** The early-return check asserted
  `any("return 0" in ln for ln in lines[resolve:rm])` — and that window also contains the *numeric
  guard's* `return 0`, so replacing the main-root return with `main_root=""` left it green while
  `rm -rf` ran against an absolute `/sysop/runtime/...` path. **The incidental-hit failure the
  test's own docstring claimed to have closed, committed in the same file.**
- `shutil.rmtree(claim_dir)` → `rmtree(claim_root)` walked through — every close would have
  deleted other claims' in-flight artifacts. So did dropping `shutil` from the import (a
  `NameError` after the index rewrite), and deleting the `CLAIM_ARTIFACTS_REMOVED` **print** while
  leaving the token in a comment, because the guard counted mentions.
- **Every retired falsehood could be restored in new words.** All five WORKFLOW mutations
  survived, and `claim-task/SKILL.md` could be made to say *"A review batch's marker is removed by
  nothing"* again — the exact claim this phase exists to retire — because the guards pinned the
  old **sentences** rather than the claim. Fixed by adding positive `states()` assertions
  alongside the negative ones: a negative check can always be rephrased around, a polarity-aware
  positive one cannot.
- The retired lock-validator justification could be re-asserted **400 characters after** the
  retirement, inside the guard's own character-offset exclusion window. Replaced with `states()`,
  which needs no window — and the shipped retirement sentence reworded to carry an explicit
  "incorrectly" so the helper can tell a retirement from an assertion.
- **All five over-strict controls failed as a bare `ValueError: substring not found`.** Renaming a
  python local or a shell variable is a legitimate rewrite; these guards extract by anchor and
  cannot follow a rename, which is defensible — reporting it as an unexplained stack trace is not.
  Every slice now goes through a `_find()` helper that names the anchor and says what to do.

**Disposition.** All lens-1 and lens-2 findings verified against the tree by me and fixed.
Lens 3's survivors were closed **by class**, and **fifteen representative mutations were re-run
against the rebuilt guards and all fifteen now fail the suite** — that is a weaker claim than
re-running all 42 and is stated as one. The guard module grew from 29 to 43 tests. **Nothing was
filed out of the round**; `Q-316` was filed before it, out of `Q-107`'s close.

**Residual, declared rather than hidden.** Prose *optionalising* — turning a MUST into "where
practical" — remains partly open in the spec and in `/auto-build`'s prompt guidance. This is the
class Phase 179 abandoned polarity-by-string-matching on at 0/21, and Phase 180 recorded nine
survivors of it as an already-filed known limitation. The load-bearing claims are now
polarity-guarded by `states()`; the softening class is not, and is not claimed to be.

## Phase 237 (executed 2026-08-27 — the readers, and the flag nobody could clear)

**Scope, on Wade's call at the open.** Three units, put to him as a scoping question before any
code was written: **part B legs 1+2** (the orchestrator group's readers) plus **`Q-314`**, with
`Q-314`'s shape chosen from four options and the mirror-push slot re-put for the fifth
consecutive phase. His calls: **B** (legs 1+2 + `Q-314`), **shape (iv)** for `Q-314`, and **hold
the push**. Part C (option C, plan-only) and part D stay open, which is the same remainder the
runway named minus this phase's two legs.

### Part B leg 2 — `/sitrep` stops being park-blind (`Q-030` leg (a))

A parked claim and an unstarted one produced **identical evidence**: lock present, branch present,
zero commits ahead, therefore `planning`. That is the Phase 135/143/146 shape — a dead thing and a
healthy thing indistinguishable — and it had been true for `/auto-build`'s parks since Phase 65a,
which is a **pre-existing gap the orchestrator reshape did not create**. `sitrep_survey.py`
contained zero occurrences of `parked`.

`_claim_stall()` is the probe, inserted immediately before `_classify_task`'s `state = "planning"`
assignment because anything later is swallowed by it. Two new states: **`parked`** (a park marker
at `sysop/runtime/parked/<ID>__*.md`, or a newest run whose `classification.md` reads
`verdict: BLOCKED` with no marker, reported as the park it is with the missing marker named) and
**`awaiting approval`** (no marker, newest run carries `verdict: PROCEED` and no `outcome.md` —
Step 7d's human gate, reached and unanswered).

**One glob covers both park origins**, because `/auto-build` Phase 6d and `/claim-task` Step 7c
were given the same `<id>__<stamp>.md` filename shape on purpose. So leg 2 pays off for
`/auto-build` even though part C may never ship.

**The spec's preferred mechanism was declined, and the reason is that its argument had gone
stale.** § *Park on absent human* prefers riding an unread lock field on a "zero new I/O"
argument. That argument predates Part A: Step 7c now writes a purpose-built marker carrying the
reason, the branch, and the `--resume` line, so a glob is both simpler and strictly more
informative — and the lock-field route would have required an orchestrator write to the lock that
appears on **none** of the spec's own lists of orchestrator-level writes.

**Report unknown, never "did not run".** Every arm of the probe returns `""` when it finds no
positive evidence, and `""` leaves the existing classification untouched. This is the whole
design, not a defensive detail: `sysop/runtime/` is gitignored, the `SubagentStop` envelope is
Claude-Code-only, and a `--resume` onto a rebuilt worktree legitimately carries nothing — so
absence is *unknown*, and a reader that called it "not run" would accuse honest consumers on three
separate paths. The probe only ever **upgrades** a classification on positive evidence.

**Plumbing: six sites — the spec's count was right and the substitution was not.** This phase's
first record said "four, not six", and its round showed that arithmetic wrong in both directions:
`render_text`'s active-work loop genuinely needed **no change** (it renders `ts.state` generically,
and `awaiting approval` at 17 characters fits the 30-column field), but `run_survey` did — it
passes the new `main_root=` argument, and the phase counted that nowhere. Six minus one plus one is
six. The sites are `_classify_task`, `run_survey`, `_recommended_next`, `_suggested_order`, and the
two `sitrep/SKILL.md` tables. (The spec does still contradict itself on the number: § *Migration
surface* says five, § *Park on absent human* says six and enumerates six.)

**Routing rank, and why it is not higher.** `6a` parked / `6b` awaiting approval / `6c` planning —
*below* `5 in progress`, not above it. The cascade's consistent logic is "further along ranks
higher", and both new states have **zero commits ahead**: they are specialisations of `planning`,
which is exactly why `planning` swallowed them. Ranking a park above live in-progress work would
send a human to answer a question while a build sits half-finished. **Visibility is not what the
rank buys** — the ACTIVE WORK table renders every task with its own state and notes, so a park is
legible there whatever the cascade names.

### Part B leg 1 — `/review-close` Step 2e, the claim-artifact report

Per-branch: which of `plan.md`, `planner-integrity.md`, `review.md`, `classification.md` and
`outcome.md` exist for that branch's claim, plus the hook envelopes and the recorded verdict.
**It never changes a disposition**, settled in the spec's Q1 on a stated argument: a *rejecting*
gate must know whether it applies, and getting that wrong is a false FAIL on work already done —
which is how Phase 155 died (inert on the batch claims it was reported for, false-FAIL on the
dominant path, 41 of 53 mutations surviving). A reporting step that mis-resolves prints "no
artifacts found" beside a branch that has them: wrong, visible, self-correcting.

**Three things the spec left unspecified, decided here:**

- **Branch → claim id comes off the lock, not the branch name.** Branch names are not reversible —
  `--branch <name>` and `tasks/index.yml`'s `branch:` both override the generated name, and a batch
  branch comes from `review_tasks.md`. The lock records `branch:` against its own `task_id`, and
  locks are still on disk at Step 2 (Step 4c removes them). One code path serves both claim kinds
  here — `batch_work.sh`'s `write_batch_lock` writes `task_id:` and `branch:` too — so **Step 2e is
  genuinely batch-capable**, which keeps it clear of the failure that disqualified Phase 155's gate.
  **That is true of leg 1 and NOT of leg 2**; see the round below and `Q-317`.
- **Which run:** the newest, by *lexical* sort — run ids are `<UTC stamp>-<hex>`, so lexical is
  chronological. Deliberately not mtime: this directory is gitignored, so a clone or a copy, both
  of which reset mtime, are ordinary things to happen to it.
- **Six artifacts, not the spec's four.** Q1's list already carries one correction ("**Four**, not
  three — an earlier revision … was not swept") and the same failure had recurred: Part A shipped
  `planner-integrity.md` and `outcome.md` as **first-class routing artifacts** that Step 7-pre's
  own resume table routes on. A report built from the four would be blind to the two files that
  answer *was the plan re-gated?* and *did the executor already run?*

**Containment before it was needed.** Phase 236 shipped a containment gate over one of two removal
arms and its round found the other; here a symlinked run directory is refused up front. The blast
radius was disclosure rather than damage — this step only reads — but reporting an arbitrary
directory's contents as this claim's artifacts is a false report either way.

The Step 8 line is **`Orchestrator artifacts:`**, not `Claim artifacts:`. The first draft used the
latter and collided with the line Phase 236 added one screen below for Step 4c's *removal* tally —
two identically-labelled rows in one report, meaning different things.

### `Q-314` — `user_action` was set-once, and `/roadmap` promised otherwise

Every occurrence of `user_action` in the shipped tree was a reader or a template default. Nothing
cleared it. So once the human supplied the credential the task was fully agent-executable and yet
stayed out of `/auto-build`'s frontier, out of `next_task.py`'s agent pool and 🔒 in `/roadmap` —
**permanently** — while `roadmap/SKILL.md` promised that "clearing it early converts a serial stall
into parallel progress". The only escape was a hand edit the tree never instructed, and which
`tasks/schema.md` then contradicted by scoping the `## User ops` section *"present only when
`user_action: true`"*: following the schema, a human who performed the step had to delete the
record of having performed it.

**Shape (iv), chosen by Wade over the filing's three.** One field with a named mechanism, not two
fields. The filing's `user_action_done:` companion would encode one fact as two booleans that must
stay in sync forever, and — decisively — `user_action` is a **step** property, not a task property:
the rubric's own list includes steps that are not prerequisites at all (a go/no-go at a rollout
boundary, a done-except-for-sign-off pairing), for which "done" is not well defined. The filing's
`/review-close` arm was rejected on timing: close runs *after* the work, and the promise being
repaired is about clearing **early** so the rest of the queue parallelises — circular for the
ordinary prerequisite case.

`clear_user_action.py` ships with `--dry-run`, never commits (the `claim_task.sh` contract), and
**copies `claim_task.sh --release`'s `yaml.safe_dump` kwargs verbatim** so the two writers of
`tasks/index.yml` cannot reformat it differently — pinned by a test, because they live in different
languages and nothing else compares them. `tasks/schema.md`'s scoping sentence is retired and the
section now says the record is kept; `/roadmap`'s promise names the command that keeps it.

  `FATAL` would have bought the drift checks and no resolution proof at all — the Phase-204 shape.

  literal `state = "…"` assignments; the new states arrive through a module constant, so both were

  appear in the table — and renaming `_PARKED_STATE` to `_PARKED_LABEL` walked straight through it:

### The round — three lenses, one round, pinned to `fbf3ee9`

Governed by `_shared/adversarial-review.md` § *How many reviewers, how many rounds*: the change
ships behaviour **and** a record making numeric claims, so the third lens is licensed. Each
reviewer got its **own detached worktree at the phase commit** — an `isolation: "worktree"` agent
is created from the *default branch*, which under this repo's `pr` policy would have handed all
three the pre-phase tree, deterministically. Each was told to gate on a symbol the change
*introduced* (`_claim_stall`, `clear_user_action.py`) before reading anything. **Model diversity
bought**: lens 3 ran on a different model from the author, which Phase 236 recorded as a gap.
Containment held — the primary tree was clean and at the right HEAD after the round.

**Lens 1 (does it execute) — 2 HIGH, 4 MEDIUM, 7 LOW, every finding from running something.**

- **The HIGH is the one that mattered, and it killed a state this phase shipped.** `/claim-task`
  Step 7c — the *only* writer of `classification.md` in the tree — emits
  `json.dumps(report, indent=2)` inside a ```yaml fence, so the verdict on disk is
  `  "verdict": "PROCEED"`. Both new readers scanned for a line *beginning* `verdict:`. **So
  `awaiting approval` was unreachable in production**, as was the BLOCKED-without-marker arm, and
  Step 2e printed "not recorded in this run" every time — indistinguishable from a genuinely
  pre-7c run, which is precisely the invisibility the leg exists to remove. Verified by
  reproducing the writer and feeding its exact bytes to the reader: `''`. **Every fixture in the
  new test module hand-typed a flat `verdict: PROCEED` that nothing in the tree emits**, so the
  guards were green over a dead mechanism — and the correct idiom already existed two files away
  in `tests/test_claim_task_heredocs_execute.py`. Both readers now parse the fenced body, with a
  drift guard on Step 7c's writer shape so this cannot silently recur.
- **The second HIGH: the suite was red at the commit**, on `test_round_yield_ledger.py` — the
  `Q-272` structural gap between the `CLAUDE.md` row and the ledger row. Not new, but the record's
  "0 failed" was **false at the commit it named**, because the measurement was taken before the
  record was written. That is Phase 236's finding, repeated one phase later.
- MEDIUM: the atomic write diverged from the writer it claimed parity with — `mkstemp` creates
  0600, silently narrowing `tasks/index.yml` from 0644, and `os.replace` onto a **symlinked**
  index replaced the link while leaving the canonical file untouched *and reporting success*. Both
  fixed (resolve first, preserve mode). Step 2e aborted the whole report on one unreadable claim
  directory, losing the healthy branches' rows — now per-branch. A comment asserted `/sitrep`
  reports duplicate lock branches as drift; it does not, so Step 2e reports the ambiguity itself.
- LOW: the lock parser was last-wins where `claim_task.sh` is first-wins (a `notes:` tail with a
  column-0 `branch:` hijacked the resolution); `fields.get("task_id", lf.stem)`'s fallback was
  dead for a present-but-empty key; envelope absence was attributed to the harness even when an
  unparseable envelope was sitting in the mailbox; a malformed index raised a traceback; duplicate
  ids flipped the first and left the rest reporting success; buffered output landed after the
  validator's through a pipe; and **the bare permission rule bound no valid invocation** — the
  positional is required, so it always exits 2. That last is Phase 152's defect, and this phase
  had written a *justification* for it. Dropped.

**Lens 2 (are its claims true) — 2 HIGH, 4 MEDIUM, 6 LOW.**

- **"The two writers of `tasks/index.yml`" is false: there are six.** Asserted at five sites. And
  the new `TestTheTwoWritersOfTheIndexAgree` class justified itself with *"nothing else compares
  them"* — falsified **by an edit in the same commit**, which registered the new script in
  `tests/test_index_writer_class.py`, whose `test_every_index_writer_carries_the_canonical_kwargs`
  has pinned all six since Phase 201. A two-member roster over a shipped six-member guard is the
  Phase-204 shape this phase congratulated itself on avoiding elsewhere. Class deleted;
  `core/companion/tasks/README.md` (five → six, and it had gone stale unnoticed) corrected; and
  the guard that checks that README now derives its roster from `INDEX_WRITERS` instead of
  hand-listing it, since a hand list is how it came to say "Five" over a population of six.
- **`/sitrep` is batch-blind for the new predicate, and this phase's own test hid it.**
  `run_survey`'s lock loop `continue`s on a `BATCH-`/`TASK-` prefix *before* `_classify_task`, so
  `_claim_stall` is unreachable on the batch path — and `test_a_batch_claim_takes_the_same_path`
  passed because it called the helper **directly**, bypassing the path that would have shown it
  inert, while its docstring invoked Phase 155 by name. Phase 155's failure mode, reproduced
  inside a test named after it. `Q-030` leg (a) is still correctly closed — it reported a parked
  `/auto-build` task, and `/auto-build` works roadmap tasks — so this is filed as **`Q-317`**, the
  test is rescoped to what it proves, and a new test pins the gap so closing it reddens.
- **A park older than `--stale-days` classified `stale`**, whose `next_action` is *"confirm dead
  and rm the lock if abandoned"* — destructive advice about a live claim, since a park is by
  construction long-lived. The stale check `return`s before the classification arms, and **every
  integration test built `Lock(started="")`**, which short-circuits it. The probe now runs first.
- The `RECOMMENDED NEXT` text asserted a marker on disk and a held worktree, neither of which the
  probe checks — and contradicted its own detail line on the BLOCKED-without-marker arm, where the
  marker is absent by definition. Reworded to what the evidence supports.
- Corrected in the record: the plumbing was **six** sites, not four (`render_text` genuinely
  needed no change, but `run_survey` did, and the phase counted it nowhere); "eight shipped
  guards" was eight *failures* across six modules; the third declined `Q-314` shape was never
  written down; and Step 2e's cross-reference named the wrong `/sitrep` step. **Lens 2 also
  reproduced the +60 delta exactly** and confirmed nine other claims true, including the runway
  rider and the routing-table gap.

**Lens 3 (are the guards real, on a different model) — 54 mutations, 12 survivors (22%); 12
negative controls, 0 falsely red; 0 mis-anchored.** Better battery discipline than the author's:
its builder asserted every anchor existed in the pristine file *before* the mutation entered the
battery, and re-verified occurrence counts at apply time — three hand-copied anchors failed that
check during construction and were fixed before anything ran. **The author's own battery, by
contrast, produced fourteen meaningless cells** on its first pass (a shell-variable assumption
made every `pytest` invocation match no tests, and every cell read "no tests ran") and separately
recorded one mis-anchored mutation as a survivor. Check the instrument before the result.

**The headline: Step 2e had no coverage of any kind.** Lens 3 confirmed by exhaustive grep across
all 65 files that mention `review-close` that **zero tests referenced any of Step 2e's output
strings**, and that — unlike Phase 236's `close_batch.sh` and `claim_task.sh` blocks, which this

runs it against real fixtures — 22 tests, and a re-run of lens 3's six mutations plus four of my
own kills 9 of 10, the tenth being the verdict fence-parse whose fallback regex handles the same
input (verified behaviour-preserving, not a gap).

**One of the phase's own guards was vacuous by construction**, and lens 3 root-caused it exactly:
`test_the_schema_no_longer_scopes_user_ops_to_the_flag` compared a needle containing `user_action`
against a body run through `normalize()`, which strips `_` — so the count was 0 on *every* input,
the `if occurrences:` branch holding all the assertions never executed, and the test passed

normalizing the needle — and fixing it exposed a second hole the round had not reached: deleting

**Of the remaining survivors, three were real and are closed** — the marker glob's `__` separator
was pinned nowhere, `re.IGNORECASE` bought nothing any test exercised, and `_suggested_order`'s
