## Phase 243 — the round's own instruments (`Q-241` + `Q-239`), and four record repairs

Two § High, both maintainer-side, both about the machinery a round runs on rather than
anything a consumer touches. Neither was in a track that demanded it now; the routing was
Wade's, taken on the ground that these two are the cheapest open § High and that both
remedies were already decided in shape, so nothing here waited on a design call.

### The defect that had already corrupted a measurement

`Q-241` was filed when a baseline clone run went red. `test_real_consumer_corpora_produce_no_residue`
parametrized over `REPO_ROOT.parent.glob("*/review_tasks.md")` — every sibling directory
holding a tracker — and scored each one against a **zero-false-positive budget**, because
`archive_review_tasks.py` has no `--force` and one false positive makes the archive path
unusable. Nothing established that a sibling was a real checkout. A throwaway fixture left
beside the repo was therefore graded as a consumer corpus and hard-failed.

**Reproduced first, in an isolated export of `HEAD` with one scratch fixture beside it.**
The test collected the fixture and failed with *"2 false positive(s)"*. That is the filed
shape, unembellished.

### The filed remedy was disproved, and so was the one that replaced it

The entry prescribes a real-checkout marker — sample a sibling only if it carries `.git` or a
`sysop/` vendor dir. That was built. It closes the hard-fail on a *bare* scratch directory, and
it does **not** close the filed bug, which the round established by execution: this module's own
fixtures call `git init` **and** create `sysop/scripts`, because `archive_review_tasks.py`
resolves its repo root as `parents[2]` of itself and cannot be run from a fixture shaped any
other way. 28 test modules build that shape. **Any marker a real consumer has, a runnable
fixture has too**, so the filed case — a clone made beside the checkout alongside throwaway
fixtures — still reproduced after the fix.

The marker gate also did not reach the half that had actually cost a phase. All six real
siblings beside this checkout carry `.git`, so gating on the marker left the collected count a
function of where the checkout sits: **15 / 10 / 10** across a primary checkout, a scratch copy
with a fixture beside it, and a scratch copy with nothing. That is the environment read as a
delta, which is what corrupted the previous phase's measurement.

**So the mechanism is not a heuristic over discovered directories — it is declaration.** Nothing
is sampled unless a human names it in `SYSOP_CONSUMER_TRACKERS`. That closes the class in every
shape, including the reported one, because there is no inference left to get wrong; the marker
predicate is gone rather than tightened. The count is now invariant **by construction** rather
than by luck: **15 / 15 / 15** across the same three locations, and it stays 15 in a fourth where
a marker-perfect fixture sits beside the checkout — the exact case that reproduced before.

The cost is stated rather than buried: on a machine that declares nothing, the check skips, and
that includes CI and every fresh clone. It was **already** skipping in CI and in every clone; what
changed is that it now skips loudly, with the variable to set, instead of sampling whatever
happened to be adjacent.

### A lens that errors out is not a lens that finished

`Q-239` was observed on this machine rather than reported: a review lens died to consecutive
server-side errors and left its full-suite battery running, reparented, against a clone nobody
was reading. The round procedure never said to check.

**The first fix for it was disqualified by the round, and it was worse than nothing.** It
prescribed `pgrep -f "$ROUND_DIR"`. Three independent defects, all established by running it:

1. **It is blind to the process it was written for.** The orphan is the *child*. The shell whose
   arguments carried the round path dies with the agent; the surviving `pytest` was started after
   a `cd` and carries nothing to match. So the sweep misses the canonical case **and prints an
   affirmative all-clear** — the prescribed re-check manufactures a second one. A remedy that
   reports "no orphaned reviewer processes" while the battery runs is worse than no remedy.
2. **It destroys the round it exists to protect.** Every lens shares one round directory, and the
   text said to sweep *"after ANY lens reports an error, not only at the end"* — precisely when
   siblings are still running. A reviewer following it killed a healthy sibling's in-flight suite
   during this very round.
3. **The handle was reconstructed, not recorded.** It was rebuilt from `git rev-parse --short
   HEAD`, and a round's own fixes move `HEAD` — this phase is three commits — so by close-out the
   command names a directory that never existed. The block's own comment said to use the path you
   gave the reviewers; the code beneath it re-derived one.

The replacement asks the kernel instead of the command line: `lsof -a -d cwd` over **that one
lens's** directory, taken as the literal string handed to it at spawn. Verified both directions
by execution — it finds the `cd`-then-run orphan that `pgrep -f` misses, and scoped to the dead
lens it leaves a healthy sibling untouched, where the old `pkill` killed it. Kill by PID, never
by pattern. The limits are stated in the shipped text rather than left implied: a process that
chdir'd away is out of reach, and where the harness owns the reviewer's directory the check
cannot run at all — recorded as a gap, not papered over.

**The entry's ⚠ caveat is honoured.** Its load-average figure was a one-machine observation the
filing marked as motivation, not evidence. It was not re-derived and appears nowhere; the section
ships no number.

### The author-side pass, and why it changed the phase

Run after the commit, before spawning anyone. **Its first battery killed nothing: 0 of 4.**

The four mutations were the obvious ones — make the new marker predicate always-True,
always-False, drop its `sysop` arm, and neuter the residue assertion outright. All four left
the suite green **in this checkout**, and they did so for one reason: the sampling test reads
whatever sits beside the repo, and beside this repo every corpus is real and clean. **It
passes on a working check and on a dead one alike.** The demonstrations that closed `Q-241`
above were real, but they were hand-run in a scratch tree — they were evidence, not guards,
and nothing in the suite would have caught any of the four regressions.

That is the project's standing finding arriving on schedule, and this time before the round
rather than from it. Four guards were added, all building their inputs instead of finding
them, so they behave the same in CI, in a worktree, and on a machine with no siblings:

- the marker predicate is pinned against a bare directory, a `.git` **directory**, a `.git`
  **file** (a linked worktree — a shape `is_dir()` silently rejects), and a `sysop/` vendor dir;
- the zero-budget assertion moved into `_sample_corpora(trackers)`, taking its trackers as an
  argument. That seam is the point: a fixture can now hand it a corpus that IS dirty and
  require the failure, which no arrangement of the machine's own clean corpora can do.

**Re-run: 6 of 6 killed, 3 of 3 controls green, 0 false kills.** The sixth mutation is worth
naming because it is the one a fixture cannot reach — replacing the sampling test's body with
`list(trackers)` gutted the call and stayed green through every other guard. It is closed by
a **source-level wiring pin**, which is labelled as exactly that in its own docstring: it
asserts the call happens, and nothing whatever about whether the sampling is right.

**Rule 4 did not fire, stated rather than left implied.** Nothing here moves a delimiter,
predicate or state machine over text another writer produces — the residue machinery is
untouched, and the new predicate tests directories, not content. No hostile corpus was built,
because there is no boundary here for one to attack.

### Five record mutations — four intended, one an accident the round caught

Four were surfaced by the reading pass that opened this phase, and Wade's call was to fix
rather than file, so no `Q-` ids were spent. **The fifth was not intended and not noticed until
the round found it — it is recorded here because the heading said four and the record has to
match what happened.**

1. **A misfiled round record, in a file that ships.** The previous phase wrote its own 82-line
   round-findings section into **Phase 212's** entry, roughly 24,000 lines from its own, which
   has no such section at all. Its last line before the gap reads *"and the round proved that
   again, below"* — so the intended location was recoverable from the prose, and that is where
   it went. Both copies of Phase 212 now agree again, and Phase 212's own round section, which
   it always had, is undisturbed.
2. **An orphaned promotion block.** A Medium → High promotion written for a `core.hooksPath`
   entry outlived its entry: Phase 240 closed and archived the entry but left the block behind,
   indented under the next § High entry, where it read as *that* entry's amendment. It carried
   research the archived copy does not have — three upstream issues, one closed as not-planned,
   and the recurrence evidence — so it was **moved to the archived entry rather than deleted**,
   with a note saying why it was adrift. Its closing open question is decided (Wade,
   2026-08-29): the reproduction stays in-repo.
3. **A severity a ledger row got wrong.** The round ledger recorded `Q-308` as § Medium. It was
   filed § High and has never been anywhere else — checked against the filing commit, not
   inferred from where it sits today.
4. **A claim that repair 1 made true again.** The duplicate-`PHASE_LOG` entry asserts the two
   copies are byte-identical for their first **15,454** lines. That was **false** at the
   previous phase's commit, because repair 1's misfiled section landed inside the duplicated
   span. Moving it restored the divergence point exactly. The amendment records the transient
   rather than weakening the claim, and names the general hazard: **a duplicated region is
   load-bearing evidence for that entry, any phase writing into the span can silently falsify
   it, and no guard watches** — the citation guard excludes `PHASE_LOG.md` entirely.

Everything in repair 4 was re-derived by anchor after the move: **66** duplicated `## Phase `
heading lines across **63** entries, no heading appearing more than twice, copies identical
through line **15,454**. All four match the entry as amended. **The duplication itself was not
touched** — that is its own entry and its own phase, and it was not this phase's scope.

5. **A live tracker moved to the archive by accident — mine, and the round caught it.** The
   helper that lifted `Q-239` and `Q-241` out of § High terminated an entry at the next
   `- [ ] <!-- id:` or `## ` heading. A free-standing **blockquote** note sat between `Q-241` and
   `Q-015` — the inbound-issue triage tracker, ~27,000 characters recording which upstream issues
   are still open — and it matched neither terminator, so it was carried into the archive as part
   of `Q-241` and filed under a `## Resolved` heading. It is live: it names eleven individually
   re-confirmed open issues. Restored to § High in its original position. **The lesson is the
   narrow one:** a structural extraction over a hand-maintained file must be told what a record
   *ends* at, not just what the next record *starts* with, and the two are not the same in a
   document that also holds free-standing prose.

**And the class bit twice.** Writing repair 1's own account, I inserted this phase's round
section by anchoring on `"### What this phase did NOT do"` — which is a **prefix** of Phase 212's
`"### What this phase did NOT do, and why it is recorded rather than implied"`, so a
first-occurrence replace put it back into Phase 212's entry, roughly 25,000 lines from where it
belonged. Exactly the defect repair 1 exists to correct, committed by the repair. Caught by
checking, not by care: the duplicated-region identity check `Q-322` depends on is the canary for
any write into that span, and running it is what surfaced this. **Anchor on a whole line, or on a
position derived from the entry you mean — never on a heading prefix in a file that repeats its
own section names 63 times.**

### The round — three lenses, and it disqualified both mechanisms

Three fresh-context `general-purpose` reviewers in throwaway clones pinned at the commit under
review, on distinct lenses (*does it execute* / *are the claims true* / *are the guards real*).
The governor's third lens applies: behaviour plus a numeric record.

**It went badly for the phase, which is the point of running it.** Both mechanisms were
disqualified — the `Q-241` marker gate as unable to close its own filed bug, the `Q-239` sweep as
blind, misleading and destructive — and both were rebuilt rather than shipped. Details in the two
sections above; what is worth recording here is the shape of the round itself.

- **The guards lens wrote 52 independent mutations and killed 26.** Against the author battery's
  reported 6 of 6. It reproduced all six honestly — the author's number was self-selected, not
  wrong — and then found that **the fix's own wiring was the one thing unguarded**: removing the
  marker filter, i.e. reverting `Q-241` outright, left the module green. Both the execute lens and
  the guards lens found that independently.
- **The wiring pin I wrote was broken in both directions.** It matched the module's own source for
  a literal call. Its own string literal is a second occurrence of the token it split on, so
  **deleting the test it certified still passed** — a guard vacuous exactly when it matters. And
  four legal reformats (a keyword argument, a renamed local, a wrapped call, black's multi-line
  form) falsely reddened it. It is gone; the wiring is now tested by *calling the real test
  function* against a declared corpus, which has neither failure mode.
- **The execute lens proved finding H3 by triggering it**, killing a sibling lens's in-flight
  suite with the command the change prescribed. That reviewer disclosed it, which is why the
  finding is a measurement rather than an argument.
- **Four record numbers were wrong and are corrected here**, all found by the claims lens: the E1
  routing count (39 was the *pre-phase* figure, carried onto a page whose header forbids exactly
  that — it is **37** at this commit, and the two it lost are this phase's own); the collected
  count, stale the moment the guards landed; the `Q-322` divergence delta, which conflated a
  within-copy offset with an absolute file line; and a shipped-file count taken against a narrower
  strip list than the mirror builder's own.

**One author-side number stands and one does not.** The 0-of-4 first battery and the 15/10/10
measurement both reproduced independently. The "3 of 3 controls green" does not — the battery ran
inline and the record never named the controls, so nobody can re-derive it. Recorded as
unreproducible rather than repeated.

### Numbers

Measured **after** the record was written, on the phase's own final tree — the tree that carries
this paragraph. **5,216 passed, 162 skipped, 0 failed.** Nothing is red.

The suite grew by 5 tests across the phase, all of them in `tests/test_archive_accounting.py`,
and the arithmetic is worth stating because the module's count moved three times and one of the
moves was the defect being fixed. Before: **15** collected in the primary checkout and **10**
anywhere else — that spread *was* `Q-241`. After the first fix: **10** everywhere. After the
guards: **14**. After the round's rebuild: **15** everywhere, including beside a marker-perfect
fixture. The final 15 and the original 15 are the same integer for opposite reasons — the first
was six discovered corpora plus nine tests, the second is nine tests plus six guards and no
discovery at all.

**Two batteries, and only the second one means anything.** Author-side: 0 of 4, then 6/6 with
3/3 controls green. Independent guards lens: **52 mutations, 26 survived**. The gap is the
phase's own headline finding and it is recorded in the ledger row rather than softened here.

### What this phase did NOT do

- **The duplicate excision.** Repair 4 amends the record about it and restores its evidence;
  it removes nothing. The remedy there is a single contiguous cut whose boundaries move every
  phase, and it carries a decision this phase had no mandate to make — copy 2's Phase 234 draft
  holds lines that exist nowhere in copy 1.
- **The model-role gate tail.** Left for the next phase. The design question underneath its two
  § High is now answered — a preview states uncertainty and never a verdict it cannot stand
  behind — but the work was not opened.
- **The mirror push.** Three phases now sit unmirrored, touching seven shipped files. Not
  urgent at this cadence, and deliberately not bundled with a phase that edits the record.
- **A class sweep for other environment-parametrized tests.** `test_mirror_skip_discipline.py`
  parametrizes over `tests/test_*.py`, which is a *real* delta when a module is added and is
  not this class. No broader sweep was run, so nothing here should be read as coverage.

## Phase 244 — the model-role gate tail (`Q-345` + `Q-344` + `Q-346` + `Q-347`)

Four entries, one function, and a design question that had already been answered. `Q-345`
(§ High) and `Q-344` (§ Medium) are the same class — the model-role gate's `--config` and
`--root` are read **pre-update in the preview and post-update in the apply**, so `--dry-run`
reaches a verdict the apply does not. `Q-346` is the rest of that gate's exit-code vocabulary.
`Q-347` is a `producer | grep -q` under `pipefail`, filed rather than fixed because the
shipped `--help` is far under the pipe buffer.

Wade settled the underlying question on 2026-08-29: **a preview states uncertainty and never a
verdict it cannot stand behind.** The stated cost, accepted: a consumer loses early warning of
a genuinely bad mapping and meets it at apply, where the gate already refuses without touching
a pin. So this phase was execution, not a design pass — and the execution still moved three
things the filings had wrong.

### Reproduced first, all four, before anything was designed

An export of `HEAD` as a scratch source plus throwaway consumer targets, each with a
`.venv/bin/python3` carrying PyYAML. Every number below came out of that harness.

- **(a) a fabricated refusal.** The source adds a model to `served:`/`inline_models:` — the
  Phase 95 `fable` shape — and the consumer takes the documented one-key override. Preview:
  `⚠ would REFUSE the model-role mapping (invalid mapping)`, 30 FAIL lines, `served: opus,
  sonnet, haiku, fable` — the *target's* pre-update list. Apply, minutes later on the same
  tree: silent success, 30 pins across 20 files, `model: newmodel` written.
- **(b) Phase 223's original false negative.** The source *sunsets* a model and the consumer
  has a role mapped to it. Preview: the literal `no-op under default mapping`. Apply:
  `⚠ model-role mapping REFUSED`.
- **(c) an empty-population refusal.** `.claude/skills` present, Sysop's skills missing — the
  partial install `--update` repairs. Preview: `⚠ would REFUSE … (unreadable config)` over a
  config that parses. Apply: passes.
- **`Q-344`.** A fresh `--dry-run` prints `skipping: resolver, skills tree, or
  served_models.yml not present` two lines after announcing it would copy `served_models.yml`
  into the target. The apply on the same target records `model-roles: wrote …`.

### The filing's reason was half wrong, and the half that survives is the one that matters

`Q-345` says the preview cannot be repointed at the source because "the consumer's
`served_models.local.yml` layers on top and the merge is the thing being judged." That is
**false**: `--local` already points at the consumer's file, which Sysop never overwrites, so
the post-update merge is computable pre-update — the source's `served_models.yml` is right
there in the checkout.

`--root` is harder, and the first draft of this paragraph overstated it as impossible. The
round measured the truth: in **`full`** mode `install_skills` copies `core/skills` verbatim, so
the post-update tree IS the source tree — running the checker against it returns the apply's
exact verdict, and `diff -rq` on the two trees is empty. Only under **`--mode loop`** is it
filtered (`LOOP_EXCLUDE_SKILLS`), and there previewing it means a second copy of
`install_skills`' selection rules, the same class of silently-wrong-about-the-future the function
is being fixed for. So the honest statement is a **cost** argument plus a genuine loop-mode
blocker, not an impossibility. Whether the full-mode case is worth a mode-dependent preview is a
design question this phase had no mandate to answer; it is filed as `Q-348`. The entry's other
reason is corrected here rather than repeated.

### What the preview says now

`resolve_skill_models()`'s dry-run half moved into `_preview_skill_models`, which runs
**before** the target-side precondition — because that precondition tests for the three files
this run creates, which is `Q-344` exactly. It tests the **source** for the three pieces
instead, since what decides whether the step runs is whether this checkout ships them.

Two lines, no verdict:

    • would resolve skill model-role markers via served_models.yml (+ served_models.local.yml where present)
    • the mapping is NOT judged here — a preview would have to read the served_models.yml and
      skills tree that this update replaces. It is validated at apply, where a bad mapping is
      refused and every pin keeps its current value.

**One branch was kept, and the reason it survives is the reason the others did not.** The
no-PyYAML warning is a statement about the *consumer's environment*, which this run does not
change — so the preview's answer is the apply's answer. Everything else in the arm was a
statement about state the run replaces.

**The `source` mode is gone from `_model_role_checker_path`.** Its only caller was the
preview's judge. Leaving an unreferenced mode would leave a second way to point the gate at
the source stack — the exact repointing that measured `model: best` across 21 files with a
green install. The source copy remains as the `vendored` mode's fallback, so the partial-vendor
path is unaffected.

### Guarding the checker moved the crash into the executor

`Q-346` leg 1, reproduced: a consumer's own latin-1 `.md` under `.claude/skills/` — Claude
Code's standard *user* skill directory — made `check_skill_models.py`'s unguarded
`read_text(encoding="utf-8")` raise. Python exits 1; `install.sh` reads 1 as a verdict. A
consumer with **no override at all** got `⚠ model-role mapping REFUSED (invalid mapping)` with
a `UnicodeDecodeError` traceback indented beneath it.

Guarding the checker and re-running produced `model-role resolution reported an issue (skills
keep their default models)` with a traceback from `resolve_skill_models.py`. **The class is
wider than the filing**, and wider than this paragraph's first count of it. **Six** call sites
walk `iter_skill_files` with the same bare read: the checker's `--list` loop and its population
loop, `_model_roles.find_role_violations` (the loop that actually produces the verdict), the
resolver's survey and rewrite loops, and the migrator. The first draft said "four", omitting
`--list` and `find_role_violations`; the round counted them. So the helper went in beside the
walker (`migrate_skill_model.read_skill_text`) and all six use it — plus the config loader, where
a non-UTF-8 `served_models.yml` escaped the `YAMLError` catch the same way. **The first cut of
that catch guarded only the DECODE**, so an unreadable `served_models.local.yml` — the
documented, never-overwritten override file — raised `PermissionError`, exited 1, and printed as
`REFUSED (invalid mapping)` with a traceback: byte for byte the shape this phase claims to close,
still live on the file the docs tell a consumer to create. The round found it; both halves are
caught now.

**Skipping is correct, not merely safe**: a file this family cannot decode cannot carry a
discoverable `sysop:model-roles` marker, so it is a file Sysop does not own — the conclusion
the marker check already reaches, one step earlier. Every **script** reports what it skipped — two of the six
sites (`find_role_violations` and the resolver's survey loop) skip silently and disclose through
their script, so nothing is hidden, but "every caller" was the wrong granularity. The checker's
green line names the count, and the empty-population guard still fires when skipping is what
emptied the tree. **Two limits the round measured and this phase did not fix:** the installer
swallows both disclosures on the success path (`Q-349`), and an untraversable *directory* is
dropped by `rglob` before the guard ever sees it, so it is absent from the count (`Q-350`).

### The exit-code vocabulary becomes total

The apply arm tested `-eq 3` then `-ne 0`, so **only rc 1 was ever a real verdict and three
things were reported as one**:

- **rc 2 is four states** — config not found, root not a directory, `ConfigShapeError`, empty
  population — and none is a judgement on the mapping. `REFUSED (unreadable config)` asserted
  both halves wrongly at once, which reproduction (c) hit over a readable config. It now says
  the gate could not read what it needs and lets the checker's own diagnostic name the cause.
  **The control flow is deliberately unchanged**: rc 2 still declines to apply. Only the claim
  moved.
- **every rc outside {0,1,2,3}** became `REFUSED (invalid mapping)`. Measured at `da002b5`
  with a preserved checker patched to exit 5. It now degrades to "not one of its defined
  outcomes", applied UNVALIDATED. Unreachable with today's checker; surviving a future one is
  the fix's stated purpose.
- **the checker-absent branch wrote no `record`**, so the summary read `model-roles: APPLIED:
  …` with no trace that the gate was skipped. The warning scrolls; the summary is what a
  consumer reads back.

`Q-347` is a three-line change with a control: a 4 MB `--help` reports *unsupported* through
the pipeline and *supported* through capture-then-match, and both agree on the shipped 811
bytes.

### Guards a phase falsifies are replaced, not deleted

Six tests asserted the preview reaches a verdict. That was the right property under Phase 242's
design and is void under this one, so each was repointed at what now holds rather than removed
(the Phase 204 convention):

- `test_dry_run_previews_the_refusal` → the preview states the limit **and** the apply still
  refuses, asserted in the same test so the pair cannot be reduced to nothing.
- the two stale-checker preview tests → **equality** of the model-role block against a healthy
  tree. An absence assertion is satisfied by degrading to some other wrong thing; equality
  fails if the fixture perturbs the preview at all.
- `test_the_preview_and_the_apply_agree_…` → the preview emits none of five verdict tokens,
  and the apply's verdict still lands.
- the malformed-config classification → moved to the apply arm, where both inputs are final.

`test_phase223_derivations.py` asserted `_model_role_checker_path source` was present. Replaced
with the stronger property: the gate is invoked **exactly once** in the function, the dry-run
block names neither the gate nor the chooser, and no `source)` mode exists.

### Three fixture defects, all found by running

- `_inline_pins` — a test helper — had the same unguarded `read_text` the shipped code did, so
  it crashed on the fixture written to prove the shipped code no longer does.
- `_age_vendored_checker` asserted the literal `--managed-only` was absent after excising the
  argparse block, so it broke on a **comment** that merely named the flag. Tightened to the
  registration; the real control (`_assert_checker_is_really_stale`, which runs the aged
  checker and requires argparse's exit 2) was always the load-bearing one.
- Four new fixtures built their source tree with a plain directory copy, and `--update` aborted
  on all of them. **The first diagnosis was wrong and was going to be filed.** It read the
  abort as another preview/apply disagreement — the apply "escaping it" because its own
  snapshot commits the dirty paths first — and a new § Medium was drafted. Checked before
  filing: both arms abort, symmetrically, from a non-git source, and a git source passes both.
  There is no disagreement. The real answer was already in the tree — `_stale_source_tree`
  carried the same five lines (`init`, two `config`, `add`, `commit`) and a comment saying it had
  learned this the same way — so the step moved into `_source_copy` as `_commit_source` and the second fixture
  stopped rediscovering it. **A drafted filing that survives to the record is a fabricated
  finding**; this one is kept as a near-miss because the thing that caught it was running the
  claim, not re-reading it.

  **The mechanism this paragraph first named was ALSO wrong, and the round caught it.** It said a
  non-git source "records no `sysop_commit` anchor, so Phase 125's no-anchor fail-closed fires".
  Phase 125's fail-closed is **explicitly gated off** for exactly that population — `install.sh`
  requires the source anchor to be something other than `unknown`, and the comment above it says
  a non-git source yielding `unknown` is *normal, not corruption*, and that failing closed there
  would break the documented update flow. What fires is **Phase 24b's preservation guard**, and
  only on a **dirty** consumer tree: measured, a clean tree updating from a non-git source
  returns rc 0. The retraction's conclusion held; its explanation did not. Twice in one
  paragraph, the same failure — asserting a mechanism from the shape of a symptom. A correct
  retraction resting on an invented cause is still an invented cause.

### The author-side pass

Ran before any reviewer was spawned, per `_shared/adversarial-review.md` § *Before you spawn
anyone*. It found one defect and one omission, both mine:

- A vacuous assertion written minutes earlier —
  `assert verdict not in _model_role_block("\n".join(_model_role_block(preview.stdout)))`.
  The inner call returns a list, the join makes a string with no section header, and the outer
  call therefore returns `[]`, so every membership test passed against an empty list. The test
  would have been green forever. Fixed to compare against the joined block, with a
  non-emptiness guard above it.
- Dead code in the `Q-347` test: a first-draft `_probe` helper and a shadowed `probe` string,
  neither reachable.

### The round — three lenses, and it found the fix making a claim it could not stand behind

Three lenses, per the governor's escalation condition (this phase ships behaviour AND a record
making numeric claims). Execution, claims, guards. Each in a throwaway clone pinned to the phase
commit and gated on a symbol the phase INTRODUCED, because a reviewer handed the parent tree
reports no findings and that is indistinguishable from a clean pass.

**The § High is the phase's own fix overstating itself, and it is the sharpest finding.** The
preview's second line said, flatly, that a bad mapping "is refused and every pin keeps its
current value". **Three of the apply arm's six outcomes contradict that** — rc 3, an undefined
rc, and a checker absent from both trees all print `applying it UNVALIDATED` and *do* rewrite
pins. The execution lens built the rc-3 fixture, which is `Q-330`'s own population (a vendored
checker preserved-as-modified by the Phase 24b guard), and measured `model: best` landing across
21 files behind a preview promising the apply would refuse it. At the parent commit that same
fixture printed a TRUE warning with all 13 failing pins listed. **So the phase deleted a correct
early warning and replaced it with a false reassurance** — which is not the cost stated in this
entry and accepted by Wade, because on that path the consumer never meets the refusal at apply
either. A preview that states a limit and then overstates what happens next has not stopped
making claims it cannot stand behind; it has moved them one sentence along. The second line now
names the unvalidated outcome, and `--adopt` — which reaches this function under `DRY_RUN` and
never applies anything — stops printing the forward reference at all.

**The class this phase claims to close was still live on the file the docs tell consumers to
create.** `read_skill_text` guards `(UnicodeDecodeError, OSError)`; the config loader's first cut
guarded only the decode, and `load_roles_config` gates on `is_file()`, which a mode-000 file
passes. So an unreadable `served_models.local.yml` raised `PermissionError`, exited 1, and
printed as `REFUSED (invalid mapping)` with a traceback under it — byte for byte the reported
shape, on a config that parses fine.

**`Q-344`'s fix reversed the direction of its own defect rather than removing it.** The
precondition that decides whether the step runs is *(this source installs it) OR (the target
already has it)*. The filed bug was testing only the target; the fix tested only the source, so a
source clone missing one of the three made the preview announce a skip the apply did not take.
Demonstrated with `served_models.yml` deleted from a source clone. Neither half is the predicate.

**Two false claims in shipped comments, one of them a citation to a test this phase deleted.**
`install.sh` still said "Both arms now use it" of the source checker — false since Phase 242's
own round, and doubly false now — and cited `test_dry_run_previews_the_refusal` as holding one
end of the property. That test does not exist; the phase replaced it. A shipped file citing a
guard that is gone is the same defect class as a false sentence in this log.

**The impossibility argument was cost dressed as impossibility.** The comment said the preview
"cannot" read `--root`. In `full` mode `install_skills` copies `core/skills` verbatim, so the
post-update tree IS the source tree — the lens ran the checker against it and got the apply's
exact verdict, with `diff -rq` empty. Only loop mode filters. Corrected, and the design question
that opens (should the preview be mode-dependent?) is filed as `Q-348` rather than answered here,
because Wade decided the shape and a second honesty contract is not an execution detail.

**The record was wrong in eight further places, every one re-derived by the claims lens.** The
headline suite number said "0 failed, nothing is red" while `test_round_yield_ledger.py` was red
at that very commit — `CLAUDE.md` carried row 244 and the ledger did not, which is exactly the
close-out constraint the next-session brief spells out and this phase tripped anyway. The brief
asserted the `Q-322` anchors had moved when this phase's append left all three untouched. A
"fourteen briefs running have said this" counter turned out to be hand-incremented and carried,
on the page whose own header forbids carrying integers — three honest derivations give 29, 8 and
6. The same commit said four unmirrored phases in one file and five in another. "All four sites"
was six. "26 rows + 6 controls" was 27 + 6. Two more were granularity: "every caller reports"
is true per script and not per site, and "three `git init` lines" is five.

**Two limits the round measured that this phase did not fix, filed rather than papered over.**
The installer swallows the skipped-file disclosure on the success path (`Q-349`), and an
untraversable directory is dropped by `rglob` before the read guard can see it, so it never
reaches the count (`Q-350`).

**What the round checked and found sound**, stated because a clean dimension is information: the
rc vocabulary is total (stubbed at 0/1/2/3/5/42/127 through the real installer — rc 1 and rc 2
both decline, every `record` reaches the summary); `Q-347` is a real fix demonstrated both ways
with the `|| true` correctly labelled inert; `Q-346` leg 1's positive control (parent traceback,
HEAD clean); nasty files of six kinds under `.claude/skills/`; `--managed-only` vs full-tree
parity; every install mode including loop, adopt, `--ref` and `--check`; dry-run writing nothing;
the `source` mode having no remaining caller anywhere in the tree; the `Q-345` correction to its
own filing being materially right; and all six repointed guards being equal or stronger than what
they replaced — **a claim the third lens then contradicted for three of the six**, and it is
right. The three "a stale/absent checker cannot change the preview" tests now assert a property
that is **true by construction**: the preview reads no checker, so no checker state can reach it.
Their fixtures — aging a checker, deleting one, building two 3.5 MB source trees — are decorative
with respect to the equality assertion, which `assert baseline` guards only for non-emptiness.
Their predecessors were not tautological, because under the old design the preview really did run
a checker. The preview half of those three went from a real cross-arm property to a tautology
plus a five-token blocklist, and three of the guards lens's survivors walked through all of it.

**The guards lens falsified the author battery, which by then read 27/27.** 43 independent
mutations against the same seven verifier modules: **27 killed, 16 survived**, plus **2 false
kills of 18 controls**. That is the 56th time this project's ledger has recorded an all-killed
author battery being falsified by an independent lens, against 0 that survived the check — and
this round is the reason the ledger's guard refuses to let such a row stand unchecked.

**Five survivors were live and consumer-visible.** The sharpest re-armed the thing this phase
exists to remove: a preview judge in a **third** function, called from the preview, printing a
fabricated warning at a consumer whose override is perfectly valid. It defeated three guards at
once — the structural guard was scoped to two functions *by name*, the verdict blocklist knows
five tokens, and all three block-equality tests pass because the fabricated line is constant
across fixtures. That is `CH03`'s lesson unlearned one level out: widening a guard from one named
region to two is still a list of places, and a list of places is not the property. It now counts
gate invocations across the whole file, with comments stripped.

The other four: the § High's own guard was `"UNVALIDATED" in stdout`, which a sentence containing
the token and stating the opposite satisfies; the newly-created undefined-rc arm asserted two
strings and never the outcome, so adding a `return 0` made it silently decline while claiming to
have applied; the refusal's durable `record` could be rewritten to `model-roles: APPLIED` because
every other record string in the function was pinned and that one was not — the exact shape a
neighbouring test's docstring names as the worse of round 2's two mutations; and the new
capability probe could drop `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` and leave `__pycache__` in the consumer's
vendor dir, which is Phase 212's defect at a new call site ten lines above the comment explaining
the rule.

**Three more were the round's own fixes, guarded on one leg each.** `Q-344`'s disjunction has
three terms and the new test deleted only `served_models.yml`, so the filed defect reproduced
verbatim on either of the other two (now parametrized over all three). The no-PyYAML branch could
lose its `return 0` and print a warning *and* a contradicting continuation in one block. And the
preview could be handed the wrong argument and warn about an override file that does not exist —
the false-positive twin of the polarity class that test's own comment discusses at length.

**Three disclosure counts were pinned only at n=1**, because every fixture in the suite wrote
exactly one undecodable file; `len(unreadable)` could become a literal `1` at three sites and
nothing noticed.

**The two false kills were both on the structural guard, and both are fair.** Adding an ordinary
comment that *names* `_check_model_roles` or `_model_role_checker_path` reddened it — including a
comment asserting the very property the guard checks. The tree survived only by luck: the one
existing prose reference is followed by a backtick rather than a space. A guard that reddens when
someone writes a sentence about it is not a guard, so it strips comments before counting.

**And the lens found the tree RED on arrival, which the battery structurally could not see.** The
round's own fix commit added 41 lines above a registered citation into `install.sh` and did not
re-point it — the third recorded instance of the class that module exists for, and the first where
one phase both fixed and re-broke it. The battery's verifier list omitted
`tests/test_intra_repo_citations.py`, and `Battery.run` aborts on an already-red verifier, so
listing it would have refused the run outright. "27 of 27 killed, 0 false kills" was produced by a
verifier set narrow enough not to notice. The module is now a verifier.

**One gap the lens named and this phase did not close:** `resolve_skill_models` runs unconditionally
in `--mode loop` and no test exercises the model-role step there. The round checked loop mode by
hand; there is no guard. Recorded rather than papered over.

**Adding that verifier immediately taught something about the control set.** With the citation
module listed, a control that ADDED a comment line to `install.sh` scored as a false kill — and
the harness was right. In this repo a line-count change to `install.sh` is not semantically
neutral, because a citation from `cleanup_worktrees.sh` is anchored to a line number in it. So
the control was wrong, not the guard: a negative control has to be an edit that is neutral in
**this** tree, not in the abstract, and it is now an in-place reword. Two of this phase's three
citation repoints happened because the tree does not tolerate line drift there quietly; the third
would have, had the verifier been listed from the start.

**The author-side battery, first run: 25 of 27 killed, 6 controls, 0 false kills.** Both survivors
were real and both are closed. `CH03` added a second gate invocation inside the preview and walked
the whole suite, because the structural guard was scoped to `resolve_skill_models`' own body and
this phase had moved the preview into a *separate function* — a guard scoped to where the logic
used to live stops watching the moment it moves. `RC06` deleted the rc-2 `return 0` and survived,
because the rc-2 tests asserted the pins were still `opus`, which the resolver failing on the same
malformed config satisfies either way; re-oracled onto the absence of `model-roles: APPLIED`. The
battery also **refused one of its own controls as blind** — it edited a comment against verifiers
that import the target, so it measured nothing and would have reported as if it had.

**A process failure worth recording, because it cost a redo.** The second battery run was launched
in the background and then the tree was edited while it ran — the one thing the close-out
constraints name explicitly. The battery's restore wrote its own starting state back over five
code fixes. Nothing was lost that was not re-doable from the session, but the rule exists for a
reason and knowing the rule was not enough; the fix is to treat a running battery as a lock on the
tree, not as a background task.

  `Q-322`.
- **A sweep for other `| grep -q` pipelines under `pipefail`.** `Q-347`'s entry proposes one
  and this phase fixed only its own site. Nothing here should be read as coverage of the class.

### The settled remedy was wrong, and it was wrong in both directions at once

`Q-322` arrived as settled. Its figures reproduced exactly — **66** duplicated `## Phase `
heading lines across **63** entries, no heading appearing more than twice. Its boundaries
did not, and neither did the cut they prescribed.

The entry had been through five passes: the filing, an amendment, a re-amendment, a full
retraction, and a Phase 243 amendment. Every one of them derived the region with a `grep`
over headings, and every one landed in the same wrong place. The reason is a single fact
none of them could see with that instrument: **the paste began mid-way through Phase 171's
entry, before any heading at all.** A heading-anchored derivation cannot find a start that
is not at a heading.

**Two distances, and this record's first draft merged them into a false one.** It said the
paste began *"145 lines before its first duplicated heading"*. It does not. 145 is the
distance from the true start (3446) to the `**Mirror push (2026-07-31` **paragraph**
`Q-322` anchored on (3591) — which is not a heading. The first duplicated `## Phase `
heading sits at 19271 in copy B, **151** lines past that copy's start. The mechanism
survives the correction and is if anything worse than stated — a `## Phase ` grep lands
**151** lines late, not 145 — but the sentence asserted a causal link between the number
and the heading that the tree does not support. Caught by the round's claims lens.

Grown in both directions from the anchor instead of inferred from it:

| | copy A | copy B |
|---|---|---|
| lines | 3446–19044 | 19120–34718 |
| length | 15,599 | 15,599 |

Byte-identical, maximal in both directions, and the only such run in the file.

So the prescribed excision of `19265–34771` would have done two wrong things in one edit:

* **left 145 lines of the duplicate behind** — copy B's head, a second copy of Phase 171's
  tail, sitting inside what reads as Phase 234's entry; and
* **deleted lines 34719–34771, which are unique.** That block holds Phase 234's only suite
  figure anywhere in the file, its `A3` declared-survivor rationale, and the file's only
  reference to `Q-311`/`Q-312`.

The brief anticipated the second half of that — it flagged copy 2's Phase 234 as carrying
lines copy 1 lacks, and set up a splice to rescue them. **With the correct boundaries no
splice is needed.** The cut is `19121–34718`, keeping line 19120 (copy B's blank first
line) as the separator, and Phase 234's round section and its battery/suite/not-done tail
are both retained where they already were, in the right order. The rescue plan was an
artifact of the wrong boundary, not a real requirement.

### What the excision did, measured

A full self-similarity scan — 30-line windows grown to maximal runs — finds **exactly one**
duplicated region of >= 30 lines before the cut and **zero** after. All 66 duplicated
headings are accounted for by that single run. No third copy. The file goes **37,712 ->
22,122 lines** at the excision commit — net, because that same commit also added the
8-line superseded-figures marker. The excised range itself was **1,439,928 bytes (32.2%)**;
net of the marker the file lost **1,439,373 bytes**. Both bases are given because an
earlier draft put the net line count and the gross byte count in one sentence as though
they measured the same thing. **That byte figure was wrong in this record's first draft**, and wrongly in the
phase's own signature way: it read `1,395,337 / 31.2%`, measured over `Q-322`'s discredited
range `19265–34771` rather than the range actually cut. The author-side pass caught it. A
phase whose finding is *the settled boundaries are wrong* is exactly the phase that will
quote a figure derived from them.

Citation safety was checked before cutting, because `PHASE_LOG.md` ships and
`tests/test_intra_repo_citations.py` excludes it: of the external `PHASE_LOG.md:NNNN`
citations, the highest target is `19082` — which sits in the **unique block between the two
copies** (19045–19119), not in copy A as this record first said, and comfortably before the
cut at 19121. The conclusion held; the reason given for it did not. Nothing cited,
internal or external, points at a line >= 19265, so the excision shifts no cited line.

**One deliberate keep.** The `### The battery, and what it does not prove` block carries
**Phase 234's** pre-round `19/20` figures, superseded by the round section's `30/31` directly
above it. Wade's call was to drop the superseded block, taken when the block still had to be
spliced in. Once the boundaries were corrected it survives in place, so dropping it became an
active deletion of unique substance — the `R2`/`B5`/`A6` analysis and the `_check_partition()`
finding are in that block and nowhere else. It is **marked superseded rather than deleted**,
which satisfies both halves of the instruction: nothing is lost, and the stale number cannot
be read as current.

### The guard, and the battery that rewrote the thing it was scoring

An ordinary phase commit created this and nothing noticed for five phases, so it is guarded.
`tests/test_phase_log_no_duplicate_region.py` asserts two properties, and the cheap one is
not the load-bearing one:

1. no `## Phase ` heading line appears twice — legible, and what a reader would check by hand;
2. no contiguous run of >= 30 lines appears twice — **0.02s on the real file**, and the
   instrument that actually produced the true boundaries.

Both, because neither implies the other: a paste need not contain a heading, and this one's
start was invisible to the heading check.

**The author-side battery's first run scored 7/12 with five survivors, including the
flagship row.** Two attacked a cost optimization or what I then judged to be dead code; the
other three were real fixture gaps — nothing exercised the overlap filter (every fixture
used disjoint copies), nothing had *two* duplicated regions, and `RG09` survived twice
before a random search over 400 documents (**37 differ**) produced the shape that kills it.

**And the "dead code" judgement was wrong — that is this phase's sharpest finding about
itself.** I removed the backward-growth loop after the battery showed no change, and wrote
into this record that a window starts at every index so the loop could not matter. The
round's guards lens then *confirmed* it by brute force over 600 random documents: **zero**
missed run starts. Two independent measurements, one conclusion, and it was false.

Both had asked whether a run **start is lost**. Neither asked whether a **non-maximal run is
gained**, which is the thing the loop prevents. The round's execute lens asked that instead
and produced a seventeen-line counterexample in which the detector reports `(8,10,15,17)` —
a strict sub-run of the true maximal pair `(5,10,12,17)`. Three adjacent copies of a region
reported **eight** runs where two are correct. The function's own docstring promises *"every
maximal pair"*, so the contract was simply false, and `test_a_region_pasted_three_times`'s
`in runs` assertion was too weak to see it. The loop is restored, with a guard relaxed so it
also collapses the adjacent-copy case, and `test_reported_runs_are_maximal` now pins it.

**Two lenses agreed and the third was right.** The governing rule — *never weight findings by
how many reviewers agree* — earned its place here in the confirming direction rather than the
rejecting one: the majority had verified a narrower claim than the one the record made.

Two citation-guard rows had to be fixed before they measured anything — `{} or {...}`
evaluates to the *second* dict, so the row was a no-op reporting itself as a gap in the guard.
The battery then reported **16/16 killed**.

### The round — three lenses, and the author's 16/16 was worth 8/23

Three fresh-context `general-purpose` reviewers on distinct lenses (does it execute / are its
claims true / are its guards real), each in its own clone pinned to the round tag and gated on
a symbol this phase introduced. The governor's third lens applies: the phase ships guards *and*
a record making numeric claims.

**The guards lens is the product. It ran 23 mutations disjoint from mine and 15 survived** —
against a battery reporting 16/16. That is the sixth consecutive phase in this log where an
author's clean sheet did not survive an independent one, and the survivors were not exotic:

* **size-conditional inertness.** Every fixture in the module is under 200 lines and both
  real-file gates assert *emptiness*, so `if n > 2000: return []` passes the entire suite while
  making the guard permanently blind to the only file it protects. My claim that the fixtures
  distinguish an inert detector held only for *unconditional* inertness. Closed by planting a
  duplicate into the real file's lines in memory.
* **the threshold was free to drift.** The real-file gate is green for `min_run` anywhere in
  [5,59]; the fixtures pinned only an upper bound, so the documented 30 could sit anywhere in
  [5,32] with the suite green — a 30-line paste silently missed. Now pinned from both sides.
* **the citation sweep could read half the file** and still clear both non-vacuity floors
  (317/315 against >300/>250). Now pinned to the file's extent, not to a count.
* **existence resolved on a bare basename** would pass any citation whose *filename* exists
  anywhere. My non-vacuity fixture was over-fitted — its planted name failed under both
  readings — and the two tests I first wrote for this and the out-of-range bound *also* failed
  to kill their rows, because they poked the helper rather than running the gate's predicate.
  Both predicates are now extracted so a fixture can reach them.
* plus a duplicate heading on the final line, an over-accepting prefix, and an unasserted sort.

**The claims lens found seven record defects**, every one confirmed and fixed: the headline
causal claim (*"the paste began 145 lines before its first duplicated heading"* — 145 is the
distance to `Q-322`'s **anchor paragraph**; the first duplicated heading is **151** lines in);
"this phase's" 19/20 inside Phase 245's entry meaning Phase 234's; a misattributed edition in
the rewritten prompt, which **regressed a statement the previous edition had correct**, on the
page whose entire subject is mishandled integers; an overclaim that the page contains no
integers at all; net and gross figures in one sentence; and a "three of five" that listed two
and was refuted eight lines later in the same entry.

**Final battery: 25/25 killed, 5 controls, 0 false kills — with 9 of the 25 rows supplied by
the round rather than by me.** That split is the honest reading of the number, and it is
recorded rather than smoothed into a clean sheet.

**Filed, not fixed:** `Q-351` — nothing pins a test module's *existence*, so `git rm` on all
three new guards leaves the meta-guards green (78 passed). Repo-wide, ~90 modules, and the
remedy is one roster rather than a per-module pin, so it is a design decision this phase had
no mandate to take. It is the Phase 204 class recurring on a phase closing a different

### `Q-267`: the fold-in was authorised on figures that were wrong

The brief's instruction was to un-exclude `PHASE_LOG.md` from the citation guard. The
population was re-derived against the tree first, and the sibling module's own docstring
turned out to be the stale number the decision rested on: it claimed **220 citations at a
sampled 50% stale**; the tree holds **405 unique — 386 unambiguous, 15 ambiguous, 4
dangling**. That docstring is now re-derived in place.

**The 15 are a blocker, not a cost.** They cite a bare basename resolving to many files
(`SKILL.md` matches 23, `README.md` matches 4), and `test_no_registered_citation_is_ambiguous`
refuses to register an ambiguous citation *deliberately* — its own round added that, because
an ambiguous anchor would be validated against an arbitrary one of 23 files forever. There is
no legal registry entry for those fifteen. Un-excluding wholesale needs either editing fifteen
historical entries or weakening that refusal; neither was authorised and both are worse than
the gap.

So the sub-property that is both checkable and honest ships instead:
`tests/test_phase_log_citation_targets.py` asserts **the cited file still exists**. A phase
citing a deleted or renamed file is a broken pointer with no stale-by-design defence — the
content moved house, not just down the page. It needs no anchors, is untouched by the
ambiguity refusal, and was non-vacuous on arrival: 4 dangling citations and 2 pointing past
the end of the post-Phase-49 `run_checks_impl.py` shim, all named with reasons rather than
asserted away. **Line drift stays unguarded, and that is now a recorded decision with a
measurement behind it.**

### The cut was red before it started, and only one gate could have said so

The pre-cut build is runbook step 4 — run the suite *inside* the sterilized tree, not just
in the source repo. It failed.

| | passed | skipped | failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| source repo at `74f85f8` | 5281 | 164 | **0** |
| sterilized mirror, same SHA | 4835 | 389 | **1** |

The one failure was `tests/test_phase_log_citation_targets.py::test_every_cited_file_still_exists`,
shipped by Phase 245 two commits earlier. `PHASE_LOG.md` **ships**; part of what it cites
does not. Twenty-four citation sites across fifteen targets — `CLAUDE.md`,
`REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`, `REVIEW_ARCHIVE.md`, `tools/*`, `make_public_mirror.sh`,
`mutation_battery.py` — resolve against `git ls-files` in the source repo and against
nothing in the snapshot. `.github/workflows/tests.yml` ships too, so this was public
`main`'s required check going red on the snapshot pull request: the exact failure mode
`tests/test_mirror_skip_discipline.py` exists to prevent, arriving in a module that guard
could not see.

**It could not see it, and it says so.** `tests/test_mirror_skip_discipline.py:22-25`
states its own limit — *"a module that reaches an excluded file through a computed path …
is outside what this can see — it is a floor on the class, not a proof against it"* — and
`_reads_excluded_file` (`:91`) implements exactly that floor, matching literal path
construction in module text. Phase 245's module reaches those files through `git ls-files`
plus citation resolution and constructs none of them as a literal, so it sat in the guard's
*"builds no path to a mirror-excluded file"* skip bucket. **The limit was written down in Phase 221 and met for
the first time twenty-four phases later** — 37 commits, 2026-08-21 to 2026-08-30 — **by a
module shipped two commits before the cut that would have published the failure.** The
round caught this record's first draft saying *"nine phases later"*: nine is the number of
DAYS, and the phase merged a distance in days with a distance in phases while writing about
a defect that merged two distances. The tighter interval was the flattering one. A stated limit is not a mitigated
one.

**The fix had to have a shape of its own.** The house idiom keys the skip on the absence of
the file the module *reads* — `tests/test_round_yield_ledger.py:28-35`,
`tests/test_queue_entry_ids.py:48-55`. That is unreachable here, because this module's
subject file is the one that ships. So the sentinel is `CLAUDE.md`, following
`tests/test_skill_audit_refs.py:707-708`, in an autouse fixture
(`tests/test_phase_log_citation_targets.py:81-104`).

Three choices inside that, each of which could have gone the lazy way:

* **Module-wide, not per-test.** Five of the eleven tests are population-dependent; the
  other six would have gone on passing in the mirror while asserting a property about a
  tracked set that is no longer the one under them. Six green tests certifying a question
  nobody asked is the *inert rather than gating* shape `TESTER_MIRROR_RUNBOOK.md` names at
  Pass 5 — and it reads as coverage, which is worse than a skip.
* **Autouse fixture, not a `skipif` mark.** A mark is the tidier spelling and it fails two
  ways: a new test added later inherits the fixture but must remember the mark, and
  `pytest.mark.skipif` does not contain the literal `pytest.skip` that the discipline
  guard asserts on (`:128`) — so the tidier spelling would have left the module inside the
  guard's population and *reddening it*.
* **Not the allowlist.** Adding the fifteen targets to `ALLOWED_DANGLING` would have turned
  the mirror green by blinding the guard in the source repo, where it is the only thing
  checking them. The tempting fix was the one that destroys the instrument.

Constructing the sentinel path has a second effect worth stating, because it was not the
motive: it moves this module *inside* `test_mirror_skip_discipline`'s population. The
guard's `builds no path` skip count drops by one, and this file is now enforced rather than
merely correct — **for the one spelling actually written, and the round measured what that
is worth.** It wrote nine variants of the same sentinel differing only in spelling
(`REPO_ROOT.joinpath(...)`, single quotes, black's multi-line form, an f-string, a name
held in a variable, `os.path.join`, string concatenation): the literal form is caught and
**eight of the nine are not**. One is not hypothetical — five modules in `tests/` already
bind their root to `REPO` rather than `REPO_ROOT`, and the guard's line filter requires the
literal `ROOT`, `parents[N]` or `Path(`. That table is evidence *for* `Q-357`'s claim that
the remedy is not a wider regex, not against it.

**`Q-357` carries the class, and it is filed rather than fixed on purpose.** The remedy is
not a wider regex — a module can reach an excluded file through `git ls-files`, through a
helper imported from a sibling, or through a path assembled at runtime, and no static
matcher over module text reaches any of those. The instrument that would is running the
suite inside a sterilized tree *per phase* rather than only at a cut, which is precisely
the open half of `Q-072`. This is the second instance found **by a cut** — the first
was `tests/test_adversarial_review_gate.py`, shipped by Phase **154**, which reached
`CLAUDE.md` and raised `FileNotFoundError` instead of skipping, failing **three** tests the
source repo passed, and found by the Phase 160 cut. Both were found late. **A third instance
is not a cut's and is worth naming rather than scoped away:** Phase 221 shipped two modules
reading four excluded paths with no guard, and its own round caught them by building the
mirror and running the suite — which is the same instrument, bought at review prices instead
of at cut prices. That instance sits four lines above the docstring this phase quotes, and
this record's first draft walked past it. `Q-357` says to fold into `Q-072` rather than
solve it separately.

**The runway called this in advance, in the right words, and nobody was watching.** The
`Q-072` blockquote attached to this very push slot — written 2026-08-26, two prerequisites
Wade attached on his own call — reads: *"The open half is automation: nothing exercises the
sterilized tree **per phase**, so a defect introduced by any phase surfaces at the cut, where
fixing it is most expensive."* That is not a general worry that happened to fit. It names the
mechanism (no per-phase sterilized run), the actor (any phase), the symptom (surfaces at the
cut) and the cost (most expensive there), and all four came true four days later. The entry
was read at this phase's open as background; it was a prediction.

### The record the runway never got

`tools/ANNOUNCE_RUNWAY.md` § *The order* has not been amended since 2026-08-28, by Phase
239. Phases 240 through 245 are absent from it — six phases, one of them
(`Q-322`) sequenced by Wade specifically to precede this push, none of them recorded in the
file that is supposed to say what order the work is being done in. That is the same defect
the file has now logged against itself four times (Phase 234's amendment opens *"this file
was never amended for 233"*; Phase 237's, *"the previous amendment never…"*). Amended here
for 240–245.

**This phase does not write its own ✓.** `TESTER_MIRROR_RUNBOOK.md` step 1 cuts from merged
`main`, so a phase branch structurally cannot contain the record of its own push — the SHA
does not exist until the branch merges. Phase 239's first draft marked the push done while
filing its own record entry open in the same commit and its round caught it; Phase 230's ✓
was written by Phase 231 and Phase 227's by Phase 229. The push line here is written by
Phase 247, from the merged tree. **Not "the way every prior one was" — the round checked,
and the most recent one was not.** Phase 227's ✓ was written by Phase 229 and Phase 230's
by Phase 231, each by the following phase; Phase 239's was written by Phase 239 itself, in
a separate post-merge commit (`c688361`). Two patterns, and the runway distinguishes them

— the ✓ is written after the cut, from a SHA the phase branch could not contain — and the

### The author-side battery, and the column that is the finding

`tools/phase246_mutations.py`, two verifier columns:

* **`guards`** — the subject module plus `tests/test_mirror_skip_discipline.py`, in the
  source repo. What an ordinary `pytest` run sees, and what CI sees.
* **`sterile`** — the mutated module copied into a pre-built sterilized mirror and run
  there. **Nothing in CI or in any per-phase check does this.** It is reachable only by a
  cut.

Run 1: **8/8 killed**, one row `ANCHOR-STALE` — the battery aimed `A02` at the subject
module while `_resolve` is defined in the sibling it imports from. Re-pointed and recorded
in the row's own `note=` rather than quietly fixed; an unnoticed stale anchor reports a row
that never ran. Run 2: **9/9 killed, 2 negative controls both surviving, 0 false kills**,
2 of 9 declared reverts (22%, a minority — a set composed mostly of reverts reports wiring
rather than coverage).

**The split is the result, not the fraction.** Of the nine, **four are killed by `sterile`
alone**: `R01` (delete the fixture), `R03` (neuter its condition), `R04` (drop `autouse`),
`R05` (retarget the sentinel at a file that ships). Every one of those ships green through
a full local suite and through CI, and surfaces at a push. That is `Q-072`'s open half —
*"nothing exercises the sterilized tree per phase"* — restated as a count instead of a
worry, on a phase that met it. Four more (`R06`, `A01`, `A02`, `P01`) are killed by
`guards` alone, and `R02` by both — nine rows, not two sets of four; this record's first
draft said *"the complementary four"* of a four-element subset of nine, and left `R02`
in neither list.

**And the guards-only half of that split is partly construction, which the round had to
say out loud.** The `sterile` verifier copies *only* the subject module into the sandbox
and runs *only* that module. `A02` mutates `tests/test_intra_repo_citations.py` and `P01`
mutates `tests/test_mirror_skip_discipline.py`; neither file is copied and neither module
is run, so neither **could** have been killed by `sterile` under any construction. The
sterile-only direction is real evidence and the guards-only direction is half artefact.
Stated rather than left for a reader to notice, because the section was written as though
the split were symmetric.

**`R01` was expected to be killed by `guards` and was not, and the reason is a defect in a
shipped guard.** Renaming the fixture to `_source_repo_only_DISABLED` leaves the literal
string `pytest.skip` sitting in the now-dead function body, and
`tests/test_mirror_skip_discipline.py:128` asserts exactly `"pytest.skip" in text`. So a
module whose skip has been disconnected reads as compliant. This is rule 1's *"a check
satisfied by a substring is satisfied by an incidental use of that substring — worse than a
gap, because it marks a dangerous line compliant"*, found in the guard that was supposed to
be catching this phase's own defect class. **Filed onto `Q-357` rather than fixed here:**
distinguishing a reachable skip from a present one is static reachability analysis, which
is the same problem `Q-357` already says a wider matcher cannot solve, and the instrument
that answers it by execution is again `Q-072`'s.

**What the battery does not reach**, stated rather than left implied: every row is
unprobed (no `effect=`), so a kill is evidence the guard is wired to the file — with all
nine killed that is the whole population, but it would say nothing about a survivor. It
measures whether the skip fires in the right tree and not in the wrong one, and nothing
past that: not whether the fifteen stripped citation targets should have been cited that
way (a `Q-267` question), and not the eleven gates' own coverage (Phase 245's battery's
subject, not re-run here).

### The round — three lenses, and the author battery falsified for the seventh phase running

Governor: this ships behaviour **and** a record making numeric claims, so three lenses, one
round. Fresh-context `general-purpose` agents, isolated worktrees, distinct lenses, none of
them forks.

**The guards lens wrote 56 mutations. Twenty-two survived every column**, against this
phase's 9/9. That is the seventh consecutive phase whose clean sheet an independent battery
falsified, and the split says why the author's number was never going to be informative: nine
rows against one construction idiom measure wiring, not coverage.

**The finding that mattered was one the phase's own fix could not have caught, and both the
guards and execute lenses reached it independently: the over-skip direction, one level up.**
Three separate one-token edits to the fixture's *condition* — `if True:`, `is_file` →
`is_dir`, `CLAUDE_MD` → `CLAUDE_MD.parent` — leave the sentinel constant untouched, make the
module skip **in the source repo as well as the mirror**, and were missed by every column an
automated run performs. Eleven gates go inert in the only tree where they were meant to run,
and the suite reports green with a skip count nobody reads. None of the three is adversarial:
`is_file`/`is_dir` is a one-word slip, `.parent` is a refactor slip, and `if True:` is the
ordinary "disable this while I debug" that never came back out.

**The phase's new pin had the defect the pin was written to catch.** `_PIN_SENTINEL` was
guarded by nothing, so retargeting *it* at a path in neither tree skipped the pin in both
trees with zero new failures on a full suite — the exact silence the pin exists to break.
Its docstring claimed *"neither can be quietly retargeted"*, and that was true in one
direction only. The guards lens made the reachability concrete rather than theoretical: two
of the five `.md` entries in the guard's own fallback exclusion list (`HANDOVER.md`,
`PHASE_47_SPEC.md`) **do not exist in the tree**, so a maintainer picking a sentinel from
that list has a two-in-five chance of landing in this trap.

Both are now closed, and by different instruments because they are different properties. The
sentinel constant is closed by a **membership** assertion derived from the mirror builder's
own strip list — not hand-listed, and checked *before* the skip so a retarget cannot silence
it. The condition is closed **behaviourally**: `test_the_citation_guards_actually_RUN_in_the_source_repo`
runs the module and asserts its tests actually ran. No textual check reaches the condition
class; a guard that can be satisfied by skipping is not a guard, and skipping is precisely
how this failure presents.

**Two corrections to the battery itself, both of which changed the headline.** The `sterile`
verifier copied and ran *only* the subject module, so `A02` (which mutates the sibling) and
`P01` (which mutates the discipline guard) had their sterile cells scored against an
**unmutated sandbox** — both read "killed by guards alone" when neither could have been
killed by `sterile` under any construction. A verifier that cannot see its subject measures
nothing and reports that as evidence. And the interpreter was hardcoded to `.venv/bin/python3`,
which aborts from a linked worktree — where every round reviewer runs — so no reviewer could

**The claims lens found the record wrong in fourteen places**, and the corrections are made
above rather than listed here — every one of them moved *against* the phase. The load-bearing
ones: the headline statistic said *"a quarter of what it cites"* when the measured figures are
one citation site in twenty and one target in eight, at five sites including a **shipped** one;

— *"it gets mechanized or dropped — it does not get written a second time"* — in a paragraph
that was writing it a third time. `Q-359` files the mechanization the rule actually requires.

**One more closure, and its residual stated rather than rounded off.** The guards lens
showed the distinctness assertion was a tautology one token away: `!=` softened to `is not`
on two `Path` objects for the same path is **always** true, because they are never the same
object — and `is`/`!=` confusion is among the most ordinary Python slips there is. Ran as a
compound with `P01` (collapse both sentinels, then soften the comparison) the whole mechanism
went inert with the suite green. The assertion is now a set-cardinality check, which has no
comparison operator to soften: the same slip applied to `len({…}) == 2` is a **SyntaxError**
on this interpreter, not a silent pass. Each single edit is now killed — `P01` alone reddens,
the softening alone reddens. **The two-edit compound still walks through** (`len` becomes 1,
and `1 is not 2` is true), and that is left as a declared residual rather than chased: it
needs two deliberate edits inside one function, and the next instrument up is a guard on a
guard, which the governor names as the point where marginal product stops being defects a
consumer could meet.

existence, so renaming `test_a_skip_sentinel_…` to `_a_skip_sentinel_…` deactivates this
phase's product with four characters — the `Q-351` class, already filed, and the reason the

(a *comment* or a dead helper's *docstring* mentioning `pytest.skip`); its population misses

paths the mirror really strips. All are on `Q-357`. A sentinel spelled `claude.md` survives on
this machine and is caught on CI, because APFS is case-insensitive and `ubuntu-latest` is not
— half a finding, and the half that fails is the maintainer's own machine.

### The PR went red, and it was not this phase

The required `pytest` check failed on the first run —
`tests/test_install_model_roles.py::test_adopt_does_not_promise_a_step_it_never_takes`,
`install.sh failed (rc=1)` with an **empty stderr**. Worth recording because the first
instinct on a red check is that the branch did it, and here that was wrong in a way only
execution could settle: `install.sh` reads none of the files this phase touched, the four
preceding PRs passed on the same code, and the test passes locally.

**The mechanism, proved rather than argued.** `cmd_adopt` commits the lock with
`git commit … >/dev/null` under `set -e` and no empty-commit guard. `iso_now()` is
second-granular, and Phase 148 anchored both lock timestamps to content — so a lock deleted
and regenerated inside the same wall-clock second as the committed one reproduces it byte for
byte, git stages nothing, prints *nothing to commit* to the **stdout that redirect discards**,
and returns 1. Locally the two writes fell one second apart (`22:28:05Z` / `22:28:06Z`) and
the run succeeded; pinning the clock to a constant made the same sequence exit 1. The test
scripts install → commit → unlink → adopt back-to-back, so a fast runner lands both in one
second and the check goes red at random.

**Third recorded instance of the class here** — `/document-work` Step 4a/4d hit it twice and
was fixed by gating on `git diff --cached --quiet`; the idiom exists and this site never got
it. Filed as `Q-360` and **not fixed**, because a cut phase's stated non-goal is behaviour
change and this is pre-existing and unrelated to the subject. Consumer reach is real but
narrow; the live cost is a coin-flip red check on every future phase, which is why the entry
routes it to the next phase that opens `install.sh`.

### The push record Phase 246 could not write

`tools/TESTER_MIRROR_RUNBOOK.md` step 1 cuts from merged `main`, so the SHA of a push does
not exist inside the branch that triggers it. Phase 246's live order line designates this
phase as the writer.

**This phase's first draft asserted that the log holds *both* patterns for who writes such a
record — "Phase 227's ✓ was written by 229 and Phase 230's by 231" — and used that to
contradict Phase 246's claim that it goes *"the way every prior one was."* The round's claims
lens refuted it, and the refutation is the more interesting fact.** Every prior push record
was ticked by the phase that did the push: `Q-293` (215–226) by **Phase 227** in `7fee3db`,
`Q-301` (227–230) by **Phase 230** in `2f443bb`, `Q-320` (231–239) by **Phase 239** in
`c688361` — the last of those in a separate post-merge commit, which is the *mechanism* by
which a pushing phase can write its own record, not a second pattern for who writes it. There
is **one** pattern, Phase 246's sentence was right, and the correction of it was the false
statement. Phase 247 writing Phase 246's record is therefore a **new** precedent. It is
justified — 246's cut ran from its own merge commit, so the SHA did not exist while its branch
was open, and it did not take the post-merge-commit route 239 took — but it is justified by
mechanics, not by a precedent that does not exist. The error ran in this phase's favour, which
is why it is recorded at length rather than quietly amended.

Private `6607f09` → public `1d4a4d6` (squash-merged from a snapshot branch whose head was
`ef27890`) and tester `ff73f5d`, force-pushed to a fresh root — **0 parents, verified**.
Both remotes resolve to tree **`74857c6`**, **359 files**, confirmed on cold clones of both
repos taken from a third directory; the previous cut was 355 files at tree `0341ba9`.

**The gate on the exact pushed tree** was recoverable and is the number worth quoting: the
required `pytest` check ran against the snapshot head, whose tree *is* `74857c6`, and
returned **4803 passed, 404 skipped, 0 failed** in 9m13s. That is the **sterilized tree's
own suite** — `tests/` ships, so the snapshot's CI runs the mirror gates *in the mirror*,
and `tests/test_phase_log_citation_targets.py` skips there exactly as Phase 246's fix
intends.

**A hand-rolled Pass-1a grep over the clone was also run, and it is recorded because it
misleads twice.** It reproduces only the ratified public contact address, which the real
gate allowlists — and a `grep | head` pipeline reports `head`'s exit status, not `grep`'s,
so it reads clean whatever it found. The suite above is the gate; a grep beside it is not a
second opinion.

**One number left as it stands.** Phase 246's `CLAUDE.md` row and `PHASE_LOG.md` heading both
say *"the mirror push (240–245)"* while the window is **240–246** — the snapshot is of that
phase's own merge commit, which is the whole of the argument. **The supporting claim about
house style was wrong and the round caught it:** the first draft said *"the house style
elsewhere includes the phase's own number (Phase 230's row reads '227–230', Phase 214's
'202–214')"*, citing the two rows that support it and not the two that do not — Phase 195
reads "(190–194)" and Phase 227 "(215–226 …)", both excluding their own number. Excluding

close-out contract lets the next phase touch the previous row's **hash cell** and nothing
else, and a merged phase's heading is its own record of what it set out to do. The correct
